findings.title: The loop's terminal state is a human-only, event-blocking kill switch, specified in nine words buried mid-paragraph
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 (char ~1400 of a 3296-char line): "Nothing remains → write DONE + disable (create `$MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled` and note it), exit." This is the ONLY mention of the kill switch in all 155 lines (grep -n 'native-supervisor-disabled' returns exactly one hit). mr-native-tick.sh:123-127 implements it as `gate -1` — the FIRST gate, ahead of the pending-event fastpath at :181: `if [ -f "$MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled" ]; then ... log "SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: ${EVFILE:-none})"; exit 0; fi`. Contrast the `.blocked-on-human` path (tick :144), which the prompt gives a self-clearing wake_file (L81: "Cron ticks then stand down FREE until the wake file exists; events and manual runs still get through"). Armed 2026-08-10T05:00:52Z (mr-native-tick.log:2623 "DECISION standdown -- no mechanical slice launchable"); cleared only by a human at 2026-08-14T01:52:22Z (log:2837 `src=manual`). Armed duration 92.86h.
findings.impact: The routine, recurring, expected condition ("I can't see work right now") is routed to the most severe terminal state in the system — human-only, blocks completion events, no wake_file, no notification — while the exceptional condition (blocked on a human decision) gets the graceful self-clearing one. 92.9 hours of a 168-hour window (55%) spent in a state only a human could exit. Recovery path = a human happens to notice.

findings.title: The "no mechanically-launchable slice" judgment was factually wrong: 7 fully-specified slices were sitting in the queue
findings.evidence: Spec commit 45b9b6d, 2026-08-09T19:56:31-04:00 (= 2026-08-09T23:56Z), inserted specs/monster-realm-v2/M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md decomposing EIGHT slices, each with a full declared touches: set — 13r-a (:37), 13r-b (:69), 13r-c (:88), 13r-d (:111), 13r-e (:128), 13r-f (:157), 13r-g (:173), 13r-h (:185) — plus pre-computed disjoint fan-out pairs at :212. The same commit added them to PLAN.md §9 (`git show 45b9b6d:specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md` lines 463-484 name 13r-a..13r-h). 13r-c was launched FROM that spec at 2026-08-10T02:02 (log:2591) and merged at 04:02 (log:2617). Then log:2623 at 05:00:52Z: "DECISION standdown -- no mechanical slice launchable (M22-25 design-sketch, 13r-c-2/M21b-2 need heavy-ceremony spec scoping)" — it enumerated a hypothetical follow-on "13r-c-2" while overlooking the seven remaining lettered siblings. Proof they needed no further work: they were launched with zero additional spec commits — 13r-a at 2026-08-14T21:04:39Z (log:3147 "resumed after 5-day skip"), 13r-b/13r-f 08-14T23:23 (log:3185), 13r-d 08-15T02:03 (log:3247).
findings.impact: The 92.9h outage was not caused by an empty queue. It was caused by a recall failure inside a 3,296-char paragraph. ~14 slices of ready work (13r × 7 + 14r × 7) sat idle. This is a PRIMARY-priority failure (delivery of quality features stalled), not a cost failure.

findings.title: MR_FORCE bypasses the kill switch on entry but never clears it — the loop spent $274.37 on a slice it had structurally disabled itself from harvesting
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.sh:125: `if [ "${MR_FORCE:-0}" = "1" ]; then log "NOTE disabled-flag overridden (MR_FORCE=1 manual run)"; else` — the override logs and proceeds; nothing removes the flag file. Timeline from mr-native-tick.log: :2632 08-10T08:00:07Z `src=cron SKIP disabled-flag`; :2636 08-10T09:05:29Z `src=manual SPAWN` (flag still armed); :2638 09:08:47Z "DECISION launched M21b-2 (fable@xhigh, hard tier)"; :2665 14:05:13Z "COSTWATCH M21b-2 done-file present, exiting (final-cal=$287.7692 raw=$359.7114)"; :2668 "SPEND-ALERT slice=M21b-2 cost=$274.3706 exceeds single_run_alert_usd=$150"; :2670 14:05:43Z `src=done SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: .../pending-events/M21b-2.done.md)`. That event was not consumed until :2838, 2026-08-14T01:52:31Z (`events=1`) — 83h 46m 48s later. The supervisor prompt contains no rule about clearing, checking, or refusing to arm the flag while a run is live or a .done is pending.
findings.impact: A $274.37 slice (183% of its declared $150 cap) was launched into a disabled loop and could not be merged for 3.5 days. The failure class is already documented in the tree — mr-native-tick.sh:348-352: "until 2026-08-01 nothing in the tree ever wrote rate_limit_resets_at ... That is what made the 2026-07-27 incident a 74h hand-cleared outage instead of a self-clearing standdown." The 2026-07-27 fix was applied to the rate-limit path only; the identical trap on the "nothing launchable" path was left open and recurred at 92.9h.

findings.title: Gate 3 is a single 3,296-character line carrying at least nine unrelated rules
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 measures 3,296 chars / ~824 tokens — 10.1% of the entire prompt on one unbroken line, 2.2x the next-longest (L100, 1,512 chars). Distinct rules packed into it: (1) git remote verification, (2) work-priority ordering, (3) BLOCKER discipline w/ reversible-default, (4) the DONE+disable terminal, (5) mr-ask-drew --blocking procedure, (6) close-the-loop issue hygiene w/ `<!--mr-system-->` marker, (7) repo-routing rule, (8) batch policy + wake_file format, (9) fan-out/N_MAX, (10) decision-space partitioning. Whole-prompt rule density: 75 bold spans, 89 imperative modals (NEVER/MUST/ONLY/ALWAYS), 70 `→` rule arrows, 76 bullet items, 237 sentences across 155 lines.
findings.impact: Ordering ambiguity a tired model resolves wrongly, demonstrated: the clause "Nothing remains → write DONE + disable" sits immediately after "For REVERSIBLE scope/content choices ... take the documented default ... and PROCEED". "Nothing remains" is never defined, and the far more common condition — "I cannot currently identify what to launch" — falls into the terminal-disable clause rather than the proceed-or-ask clause. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-10 (DOCT-01/02).

findings.title: The brief template tells every build session a cost ceiling is mechanical when no enforcement exists anywhere
findings.evidence: mr-brief-template.md:33: "**BUDGET: $<CAP_USD> for this slice (advisory thresholds; only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical).**" — rendered verbatim into every brief (/tmp/mr_pass_14r-g.md:34 "$150 ... only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical", /tmp/mr_pass_13r-d.md:33 "$60 ... only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical"). mr-budget-config.json sets `"costwatch_enforce": false` with `"_costwatch_note": "enforce=false => MONITOR mode (warn flag + logs only; no stop/kill)"`. Confirmed live: mr-native-tick.log:2656 "COSTWATCH M21b-2 HARD-MONITOR 125% (raw $187.7660/$150) — enforce=false or log-stalled" — the run continued to $274.37 (log:2668). The supervisor prompt states this correctly at L33 ("MONITOR until costwatch_enforce=true"); only the build-session-facing brief misstates it.
findings.impact: The one artifact read by the agent that actually spends the money asserts a hard ceiling that does not exist. A build session has no reason to self-limit — the brief promises something else will stop it. This is the direct mechanism behind the 183%-of-cap M21b-2 run, and it is SECONDARY-priority (cost) damage caused by a doctrine defect, not a tooling defect.

findings.title: Tier routing is a fresh judgment call every launch, not the mechanical derivation the prompt claims — and it self-contradicted inside one milestone
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:17: "**HARD criteria (any one):** `touches:` hits server-module schema/reducers · `predictor.ts`/netcode/reconcile paths · security/RLS surfaces · **M20**/M25 slices · resume-after-park · a prior attempt of this slice failed. Derive mechanically from the slice's `touches:` globs." The only mechanical artifact, mr-tier-map.json, is self-described as `"_rules_frozen_2026-07-25"` for "pre-tier-era slices" and covers 0 of the 29 in-window slices (computed: `[s for s in slices if s in tm]` → `[]`). Two misclassifications against the prompt's own "any one" rule: (a) m20b tagged routine — ledger 2026-08-09T01:02:52Z notes "tier=routine; reason=ops/observability config only, ... no schema/reducer/netcode/security surface" — the supervisor applied the touches-based criteria and read straight past the standalone "M20 slices" criterion; m20a/m20c/m20d/m20e in the same milestone were all tagged hard. (b) 13r-c tagged routine (ledger 2026-08-10T02:01:34Z "tier=routine") despite its declared touches (13r spec:88) including `server-module/src/accounts.rs` plus six security evals (currency-integrity, ranking-security, conversation-privacy, wallet-privacy, account-privacy, guest-claim-integrity) — two independent HARD criteria.
findings.impact: The same rule produced different tiers for sibling slices in the same milestone on consecutive ticks. Tier drives model (opus@high vs fable@xhigh), effort, lens battery depth, and the $60-vs-$150 cap — so it is the single highest-leverage decision the supervisor makes, and it is unreproducible. PRIMARY-priority risk: an under-tiered security slice gets a thinner lens battery.

findings.title: The 296-line feedback doctrine is dead: zero ledger activity in 19 days, zero rows ever reached its terminal states — yet it occupies four prompt blocks and a mandatory PR-body field
findings.evidence: $MEM/feedback-ledger.jsonl: 189 rows, mtime Jul 27 07:04; rows with ts>=2026-08-08 = 0. State census: Counter({'CLASSIFIED': 91, 'DISPOSED': 86, 'LOGGED': 5, 'IN-WORK': 4, 'ANSWERED': 3}) — the doctrine §8 terminal states VERIFIED and SHIPPED-VERIFIED have ZERO rows in the file's entire history. The `mr-feedback` script itself is mtime Jul 27 11:16. Still carried in the prompt on every tick: L31 (`mr-feedback brief --episode E`, 185 ch), L34 (`mr-feedback` tool spec, 220 ch), L83 ("**Feedback doctrine (ACTIVE v1.0 — SSOT: `$MEM/mr-feedback-doctrine.md`)**...", 470 ch), L105 ("`mr-feedback set <id> --state IN-WORK` per item at launch, `--state VERIFIED` after the non-author complaint-repro, `--state SHIPPED-VERIFIED --evidence PR#N` at merge adjudication (doctrine §8; first-cycle gap 2026-07-27: items sat DISPOSED while slices ran)", 478 ch). mr-brief-template.md:31 still mandates: "PR description MUST include a line `Items: <feedback-ledger ids, or none>`".
findings.impact: A subsystem whose own prompt text admits it never worked ("first-cycle gap 2026-07-27: items sat DISPOSED while slices ran") is still described as "ACTIVE v1.0" to the supervisor on all 65 paid ticks in the window, and still imposes a required field on every PR body. Labeling dead machinery ACTIVE degrades the trustworthiness of every other ACTIVE label in the prompt.

findings.title: The retro ceremony has produced zero artifacts in its entire existence — its output directory has never been created
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:32: "**retro-request events** (`retro.request.md`): follow `$MEM/mr-retro-playbook.md` exactly, write the report to `$MEM/retros/<utc>.md`, do NOT launch build work in the same run, <=2 sonnet deep-dive agents unless evidence demands more." `ls $MEM/retros/` → "No such file or directory". Supporting artifacts exist and are stale: mr-retro-playbook.md (2,148 B, mtime Jul 26 18:51), mr-retro-request (executable, mtime Jul 27 02:01).
findings.impact: Confirms the dead-weight pattern of DOCT-07 in a second subsystem. Two of the prompt's four described offload ceremonies (retro, feedback) have produced nothing. Small token cost; large signal cost.

findings.title: The weekly review is the only thing that fills the queue and it works — but its cost is invisible to the governor and it is not weekly
findings.evidence: Both in-window milestones came from it: 45b9b6d 2026-08-09T19:56-04:00 "spec(mr): insert M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals (rev13 weekly review @ f9a063d)" and d4e18d5 2026-08-13T21:07-04:00 "spec(rev14): M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals ... (issues mr#313, ch#14)". Those two specs produced 13r-a..h and 14r-a..g — every slice merged in the window after 08-10 traces to them. COST GAP: a scan of all 710 ledger rows for slice matching 'weekly|review-rev|retro' returns exactly ONE row ever — `2026-08-14T01:03:42Z | weekly-review-rev14 | completed | $0.0 | fable`, notes "tier=review visibility-only cost-null row". rev1..rev13, including the rev13 run that produced the 13r spec, have no ledger row at all. CADENCE: rev13 → rev14 was 3 days 21h, not 7. ISOLATION: mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:22-25 "This task runs concurrently with the native `mr-supervisor` loop ... MUST be fully isolated"; :219-220 "NEVER pass `--blocking`: it writes `$MEM/.blocked-on-human`, which gates the RUNNER's cron ticks. A review is never blocked."
findings.impact: The heaviest recurring ceremony in the system (306-line prompt, `fable` model, 13+ runs) contributes $0.00 to the `d7` rolling-7-day sum the budget governor uses — so the 35.6% utilization figure is an undercount by an unknown amount. Also note the near-miss: rev14 wrote a fresh 7-slice milestone into the queue at 2026-08-14T01:07Z while the loop sat disabled, and its prompt (:219) knows about `.blocked-on-human` gating but has no rule to check or clear `.native-supervisor-disabled`. It filled a queue nothing could read; a human 45 minutes later was what closed the loop.

findings.title: The prompt's stated weekly budget calibration is stale by 2.2x against the config that actually governs
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:24: "The LIVE SITUATION bundle computes `budget.state` from the ledger (weekly calibration **$1,250 API-equiv**; recalibrate at the next real park by recording the rolling-7-day ledger sum at trip time)". mr-budget-config.json: `"weekly_limit_usd": 2783`, re-anchored per its own `calibration_anchor.ts` = 2026-07-25T17:00:00Z. Prompt L18 references the same 2026-07-25 recalibration for the fable axis but L24's weekly figure was never updated with it.
findings.impact: A supervisor reasoning about headroom from the prompt rather than the bundle would compute 79% utilization ($989.51/$1,250) instead of the true 35.6% ($989.51/$2,783) — the difference between NORMAL and near-SOFT-PAUSE. It did not misfire in this window (the bundle is authoritative and reported NORMAL), but the prompt carries a number that would cause a spurious launch freeze if ever trusted.

findings.title: The N≤2 vs N≤4 contradiction the prompt claims to have resolved is still on the page
findings.evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81: "N_MAX default = 2; up to 4 is permitted ONLY under the N≥3 LAUNCH PROTOCOL below (Drew-approved 2026-07-26 — **this reconciles the old N≤2-vs-N≤4 contradiction in this doc**)." But the section header at :87 still reads "## Fan-out safety (N ≤ 4; conservative)" and :131 reads "N ≤ 2 runs by default, ≤ 4 under the N≥3 LAUNCH PROTOCOL". Three different framings of the same limit remain across three sections.
findings.impact: Low operational risk — the loop ran at N≤2 all window. It is cited as a marker of the editing pattern: a reconciliation note was appended rather than the contradictory text being edited out, so the contradiction and its resolution now both ship on every tick.

findings.title: The gating-test audit produced 11 flags and 11 false positives; the prompt forces a full-diff human-grade read on every one
findings.evidence: Ledger gating_test_audit census for the window: 11 FLAGGED verdicts, all adjudicated clean, 0 true positives (CLEAN:9, NA/none/n-a:3, FLAGGED-*adjudicated-CLEAN:11). The verdict strings name the grep's failure modes verbatim: "FLAGGED-adjudicated-clean(2 comment-prose false-positives: removed_or_modified_asserts=2 both doc-comment prose edits not test assertions; skip_markers_added=2 both Rust .iter().skip() calls not test-skip markers)" and "FLAGGED->adjudicated CLEAN (1 false-positive: import-line reflow, no real assert removed)". orchestration_audit likewise: "FLAGGED-adjudicated-clean(reviewer+red-team evidenced in commit 39881fd; agent_calls parser gap)". The prompt mandates the expensive path on every flag — L39 "`FLAGGED` or `AUDIT-ERROR` → YOU read the diff/log and adjudicate before merging ... (hard-tier is always FLAGGED: mandatory read)" and L121-122 "Semantic weakening ... is YOUR judgment call on every FLAGGED diff — the grep can only point, not decide." Scale of one such read, from the 13r-c merge row: "diff +1503/-1124 across 12 files."
findings.impact: 100% false-positive rate on the gate protecting the operator's PRIMARY priority (test integrity). A gate that is always wrong trains the adjudicator to rubber-stamp — the eleventh 'FLAGGED→CLEAN' is read far less carefully than the first, so the gate is actively eroding the vigilance it exists to create. The fix is mechanical (exclude comment spans, anchor `skip` to test-framework call sites, ignore import reflow), not prose: the prompt currently pays a sonnet full-diff read to compensate for a grep that cannot tell `.iter().skip()` from `test.skip`.

findings.title: The always-on instruction hierarchy contains a direct cost-vs-thoroughness conflict with no precedence rule
findings.evidence: Harness AGENTS.md Golden rule 5: "**Right-size the effort.** Default to the cheapest model/effort that clears the eval gate; escalate deliberately at high-leverage gates only (see `docs/routing.md`)." mr-brief-template.md:21 (rendered into every brief): "**Budget is ample — favor thoroughness over frugality: prefer more mutation coverage, an added adversarial/red-team lens, and the full eval suite where they catch *distinct* defect classes**". Both are in force in every build session: AGENTS.md is auto-loaded from the cwd walk (mr-launch.sh:18 sets PROJDIR=$HARNESS/projects/monster-realm as cwd, with `--add-dir "$HARNESS"`), and the brief is the user prompt. Neither states which wins.
findings.impact: Resolves de facto by recency/specificity toward the brief, which is the correct call for the operator's stated PRIMARY priority — but it is unstated, so it is luck rather than design. Also note the harness's own authoring doctrine in AGENTS.md: "Keep `AGENTS.md` a lean lookup table, not a brain dump ... Stable rules live here; transient task context does not" — a standard the supervisor prompt violates comprehensively (21 dated incident parentheticals).

findings.title: The brief's TARGET_DESC is the healthiest artifact in the system — a build session can produce from turn one
findings.evidence: Rendered /tmp/mr_pass_14r-g.md (13,544 B) carries a ~2,000-char TARGET_DESC with file:line precision, the correct SSOT predicate AND the wrong one to avoid, EARS criteria, a proof-of-teeth test plan, and decision-hook scoping: "challenge_pvp (pvp.rs:669) and accept_challenge (:820) gate only on a `player` presence row -- guests can enter ranked ... is_account_holder (accounts.rs:190) is the correct SSOT predicate -- NOT has_jwt() (true for every connection) ... EARS: WHEN a guest identity calls challenge_pvp or accept_challenge, THE SYSTEM SHALL reject with a distinct reason ... proof-of-teeth BAD fixture: gate absent -> RED ... Decision-hook: mdrewt/monster-realm#313 governs ONLY the pre-enforcement guest-rating migration sub-step ... build everything else regardless of that issue's open state." mr-spawn:56-70 renders it via python `.replace()` (never sed, per the prompt's own gotcha at L110), and mr-spawn:33-38 resolves CAP_USD from mr-budget-config.json `slice_caps_usd` by tier — mechanical, not judgment.
findings.impact: This is the part of the doctrine that does what doctrine should: it moves derivation out of the expensive session and into cheap prepared text. Zero of the window's 18 slice merges shows evidence of scope re-derivation. Preserve this mechanism; the DOCT-15 defect is a gap in it, not a flaw in the idea.

findings.title: Routine slices — the majority — receive a completely empty quality-tier block
findings.evidence: mr-spawn:59-62 builds tier_block with a hard branch, a content branch, and `else ""` for routine. Verified in rendered output: /tmp/mr_pass_14r-g.md:11 has "QUALITY TIER: HARD — invoke the tester subagent with model opus; depth over speed; this session runs at xhigh effort."; /tmp/mr_pass_13r-d.md (routine) has no QUALITY TIER line at all (grep returns nothing) — the substitution leaves two blank lines at [9]-[13]. Of 22 in-window slices carrying a tier= tag, 13 were routine. The content branch explicitly acknowledges an unresolved upstream conflict it must override: "(THIS OVERRIDES the build-loop prompt bump-one-tier default for this slice)" — meaning routine slices silently inherit build-loop-prompt.md's bump-one-tier default that content slices are told to ignore, with nothing in the brief saying so.
findings.impact: The most common tier gets zero explicit quality signal and an unstated default inherited from a file it must go read. Cheap fix (emit a ROUTINE block); currently it makes tier a two-value signal in practice while the ledger records three.

findings.title: Prompt length is NOT a cost problem — carrying all 155 lines forever costs ~$83/yr, 0.087% of spend
findings.evidence: Prompt = 32,620 chars ≈ 8,155 tok (chars/4). Paid spawns in window (log lines matching `\sSPAWN model=`, UTC 08-08T04..08-15T03) = 65, corroborated by 65 SUPERVISOR ledger rows summing $86.80 (mean $1.335, min $0.2651, max $5.0285). Annualized: 65/7×365 = 3,389 spawns/yr × 8,155 tok = 27.6 M tok/yr; at sonnet input $3/Mtok = $82.92/yr. The identified dead/low-yield subset (L11, L31, L34, L83, L85, L99, L100, L105) = 4,927 chars = 1,232 tok = 15.1% of the prompt = $12.53/yr. Annualized window burn = $1,824.97/7×365 = $95,159/yr, so total prompt carry is 0.087% of spend.
findings.impact: Reported as a correction to the obvious hypothesis. "Trim the prompt to save tokens" is not a defensible recommendation at these numbers — the savings round to zero. The prompt's cost is entirely in decision quality: one clause at char ~1,400 of line 81 cost 92.9 hours of loop availability (DOCT-01/02). Any rewrite should be justified on correctness and retrievability, never on token spend. Note MEDIUM confidence: chars/4 is an approximation and I could not verify whether prompt caching applies to the headless `-p` invocation (1h tick spacing exceeds the 5-min cache TTL, so I assumed cold; if warm, the true cost is ~10x lower still).

findings.title: The accretion loop that built this prompt has stopped — it froze on 2026-08-01 and did not respond to any incident in the window
findings.evidence: 21 dated incident parentheticals across 24 date tokens, spanning exactly seven dates, ALL July 2026: 07-02(×1), 07-21(×2), 07-24(×3), 07-25(×4), 07-26(×9), 07-27(×4), 07-31(×1). Zero August dates anywhere in the file. Representative accretions: L11 "**RESOURCE LOCATIONS (2026-07-21, learned the hard way)**", L81 "(An 88-min stall on a reversible roster question, 2026-07-25.)", L81 "**Close-the-loop (2026-07-27, issues #11/#12 incident)**", L100 "(Origin: two slices independently picked the same affinity, 2026-07-24 — file-disjointness is blind to decision collisions.)". File mtime Aug 1 06:25; last commit touching it is 2026-08-01 "fix(supervisor): cost SSOT (ADR-0011)". mr-brief-template.md and mr-feedback-doctrine.md both mtime Jul 27 12:06; mr-tier-map.json Jul 25 20:05. Meanwhile the window produced a 92.9h outage, a 183%-of-cap run, and 11 false-positive gate flags — and changed not one line of doctrine.
findings.impact: The right question is not "is incident-by-incident accretion sustainable?" — it is that the accretion loop DIED 14 days before this review, and the doctrine no longer learns. The prompt is now a snapshot of what the loop knew on 2026-08-01: it still carries nine separate 2026-07-26 fan-out rulings for an N that never exceeded 2, while containing no rule about the failure that dominated the window. Corroborating signal: mr-native-tick.log CENSUS lines show 63 of 65 ticks ran with `agents: none skills=0 monitor=0` — the supervisor invokes essentially none of the ceremony its prompt describes, so most of the accreted text is never exercised and cannot be falsified by use.

findings.title: The brief forces ~11,900 tokens of mandatory re-reading before a build session can start work
findings.evidence: mr-brief-template.md:1 opens: "Run the Monster Realm v2 build loop in this harness per `specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md`, the project `AGENTS.md`, and `standards/` ... Triage complexity first, then route per `docs/routing.md`." Measured sizes of the referenced-but-not-inlined chain: build-loop-prompt.md 18,838 B (~4,710 tok), standards/*.md ×12 24,481 B (~6,120 tok), docs/routing.md 4,137 B (~1,034 tok) = 47,456 B ≈ 11,864 tok. Already-inlined/auto-loaded at session start: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md 1,642 B + harness CLAUDE.md 842 B + harness AGENTS.md 5,488 B + project AGENTS.md 4,539 B + rendered brief 13,544 B = 26,055 B ≈ 6,514 tok. Combined instruction floor ≈ 18,378 tok before turn 1 of real work.
findings.impact: Reported as MINOR and MEDIUM confidence deliberately: I did not stream the 62 build-session transcripts to verify these files are actually read every time, so the 11,864-tok figure is a ceiling, not a measurement of behavior. The structural point stands regardless — the brief's own excellent TARGET_DESC (DOCT-14) proves that inlining the decision-relevant slice of context works better than pointing at it, and the standards/ pointer is the one place the template still points.

findings.title: mr-cost-watch's PRICE MODEL is accurate (median error 1.1% over 46 runs) but enforcement has never been armed once in its 19-day life; 27 slices blew their cap with zero action
findings.evidence: Joined every `COSTWATCH <slice> done-file present, exiting (final-cal=$X raw=$Y)` line in mr-native-tick.log with that slice's single FINISHED ledger row (n=46 clean pairs): median cal/ledger = 1.011, median raw/ledger = 1.263. Threshold census: 38 distinct slices hit WARN 80%, 27 hit STOP-MONITOR 100%, 13 hit HARD-MONITOR 125%. Every STOP/HARD line carries `enforce=false, no flag` or `enforce=false or log-stalled`. mr-budget-config.json:`"costwatch_enforce": false` with `_costwatch_note`: 'Arm after live-run verification that subagent usage streams in real time (adversarial-review blocking condition F3): compare mr-cost-watch price <log> timeline vs ledger on one completed run.' That blocking condition is now satisfied 46 times over by the data above. Second blocker: 174 `LOG-STALL ... enforcement suspended (blind watcher, review F-A)` lines across 30+ slices (top: m20d 10, M21b-2 10, m20a 7). Corroboration that the price model is the trustworthy party: for uxd2 the watcher said cal=$155.21 while the ledger said $423.65 — the ledger was later corrected to $165.65 by ADR-0011 (README:45), i.e. the watcher was right and the ledger was 2.56x wrong.
findings.impact: M21b-2 reached 183% of its declared $150 cap ($274.37 ledgered) with three mutually inconsistent figures ($274.37 ledger / $287.77 cal / $359.71 raw) and no intervention. The cheapest available win in the whole corpus: arm enforcement on the CALIBRATED sum (cal/ledger=1.011), not the raw sum (1.263, fires ~26% early — the reason it was left on raw is documented in mr-budget-config.json `_stream_factor_note` as 'overcount fires early = safe', which is exactly why nobody dares arm it).

findings.title: The .situation-cache.json HINTS-ONLY layer does not reduce per-tick discovery: 76 ticks still issued 718 gh/git calls, and the 45s cache can hit at most 4 times in 263 tick starts
findings.evidence: Cache TTL is hardcoded at mr-situation:9-11 (`AGE -lt 45`). Tick-process start times extracted from the first `pid=` line per pid in mr-native-tick.log: 966 processes all-time, 263 in-window; consecutive starts <45s apart = 25 all-time (2.6%), 4 in-window (1.5%). Streaming the 79 in-window harness transcripts and classifying by the presence of 'LIVE SITUATION (HINTS-ONLY' in the prompt: 76 tick sessions, mean 23.8 Bash tool calls each (median 21, max 169, total 1,807), of which 718 contain `gh ` or `git ` — ~9.4 live gh/git re-verifications per tick, on top of a bundle that already ships open_prs, master_ci_latest, master_sha_local, locks[], done_files[], pending_events[] and the full budget block. This is by design: SSOT doctrine says the bundle is HINTS-ONLY and to 're-verify anything you are about to mutate'.
findings.impact: The bundle is additive context, not a replacement for discovery — so it costs prompt tokens on every tick without removing the tool calls it was built to remove. The 45s cache is essentially unreachable at hourly/event cadence and saves at most 4 `gh` round-trips per week (LLM cost saved: $0, since mr-situation is pure bash/python). Also noted: the bundle's `recent_blockers` array is populated by a handoff-tail grep and currently contains 5 arbitrary mid-sentence fragments (e.g. '13:Both verified detached (own sessions, setsid)...') — none of which is a BLOCKER.

findings.title: The human-activity probe's documented 'do NOT exclude .codegraph, measured false-trip cost $0' decision is measurably wrong: 90% of in-window trips were the CodeGraph daemon's own writes, costing ~7h of latency
findings.evidence: mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 lists under 'Deliberately NOT done (see ADR-0011)': 'adding `.codegraph` to gate 3's probe (measured false-trip cost $0 — the divergence from `mr-spawn:35` is now documented in-line at both sites instead)'. Actual counts from `STANDDOWN recent-writes: <path>` lines in mr-native-tick.log: 159 trips all-time, of which 129 (81%) name a `.codegraph/` path; 67 trips in-window 2026-08-08..14, of which 60 (90%) are `.codegraph/codegraph.db-wal` (30) or `.codegraph/daemon.log` (30). The remaining 7 in-window trips are ARCHITECTURE.md (4), an ADR (2), README.md (1). Each trip is followed by `RETRY scheduled in 7min`; chains of 3-4 are common (e.g. 2026-08-15T07:37:47Z, 07:45:17Z, 07:52:44Z, then SPAWN at 08:00:07Z = 23 min of pure delay on one done-event).
findings.impact: 60 in-window false trips x 7 min = ~7.0 hours of self-inflicted merge/launch latency in a 7-day window (~4% of wall clock), plus repeated wake/standdown churn. Dollar cost genuinely is ~$0 (standdown happens pre-spawn), which is exactly why the ADR-0011 review dismissed it — the review measured the wrong axis. On the operator's PRIMARY axis this is a responsiveness defect, and it is a one-line fix (exclude `*/.codegraph/*` from the probe, as mr-spawn:35 apparently already diverges).

findings.title: The weekly review is the ONLY generator of launchable work and it works — but it only ever improves the GAME, never the LOOP, and the loop consumes a whole milestone in <24h

Ratchet floors at :120 `const MIGRATED_FLOOR = 10;` — i.e. after two full slices (13r-c $79.31 total, 14r-c $36.66) only 10 of 18 gated evals are migrated.
findings.impact: Seven of the repo's security gates can pass GREEN on code they are supposed to reject. Two are proven to do so. These guard the battle, evolution, raising, recruit, shop, trade and NPC reducer families. $115.97 was spent across 13r-c and 14r-c and the security-critical half of the migration is still open.

findings.title: mr-audit's gating_test_audit has 0% precision in-window (0 true positives on 11 flags) and is structurally incapable of detecting any defect class the residual milestones exist to fix
findings.evidence: WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, from /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/mr-audit (75 lines): line 51 scopes the content diff to test paths only (`git diff base..head -- "*test*" "*spec*" evals ":(glob)**/*_tests.rs" ":(glob)**/*.test.ts"`); line 54 counts any '-' line matching /assert|expect\(|\.toBe|\.toEqual|panic!|prop_assert/ as `removed_or_modified_asserts`; lines 56-57 count added `.skip/.only/xit/xdescribe/#[ignore]/todo!` and `nosemgrep/eslint-disable/@ts-ignore/@ts-expect-error/#[allow(`; lines 58-59 make tier=hard an UNCONDITIONAL FLAG; lines 60-61 flag on any nonzero counter. Line 33-34: the orchestration audit is a string-presence check for `"name":"Agent"` and `subagent_type` values containing 'tester'/'review'/'verif' in the session log. IN-WINDOW VERDICT DISTRIBUTION (computed over ledger rows with ts in window): gating_test_audit = 9 CLEAN, 11 FLAGGED-*-adjudicated-CLEAN (5 'FLAGGED-adjudicated-CLEAN', 2 'FLAGGED-adjudicated-clean', 1 hard-tier-mandatory-read, 1 'hard-tier mandatory read; 70 asserts, all ma...', 1 '2 comment-prose false-positives', 1 'FLAGGED->adjudicated CLEAN (1 false-positive: import-line reflow)'), 3 NA/none/n-a. PRECISION = 0/11 = 0%. At least 2 of the 11 were unconditional hard-tier flags (not detections at all), so discretionary precision is 0/9. DEFECT-THROUGH-THE-GATE PROOF: ledger row 2026-08-09T03:06:33Z, slice m20b: 'PR#302 squash-merged->74f2de0; mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' — that commit shipped the 7-container observability stack whose FIRST REAL BOOT crash-looped four of eight containers (four root-caused config defects, itemised in M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:57-76: tempo bad CLI flag docker-compose.yml:110, alloy uid/cap EACCES :58-71, caddy file-capability EPERM Dockerfile:16,23, grafana 15s alert interval rules.yml:21). mr-audit cannot see any of these by construction — none of them touch a test file.
findings.impact: Every FLAGGED verdict triggers a full-diff LLM read by the supervisor (evidenced in mr-state.json:28, a ~1,200-word adjudication write-up for M21b-2). 11 such reads in-window at supervisor rates, all returning CLEAN. The gate is a pure cost with no demonstrated yield, and it provides false assurance: 'mr-audit CLEAN' appears in the merge record of the slice that shipped a stack which does not start.

findings.title: mr-audit blind spot: suppressions and skip markers added to PRODUCTION source are invisible, because the scanned diff is scoped to test paths only
findings.evidence: memory/projects/mr-audit:51 scopes `r2` to `"*test*" "*spec*" evals **/*_tests.rs **/*.test.ts`; lines 56-57 compute skip_markers_added and suppressions_added from `r2.stdout` only. So `#[allow(...)]`, `@ts-ignore`, `eslint-disable` or `nosemgrep` added to server-module/src/*.rs or client/src/*.ts is never counted. HONEST NEGATIVE: I checked whether it was exploited in-window — `git diff 42c134e..1756653` restricted to non-test production source yields 5 added `/* eslint-disable */` lines, all in auto-generated `client/src/module_bindings/*.ts` (SpacetimeDB codegen output). Zero real suppression abuse occurred in the window.
findings.impact: Latent, not exploited. A slice could silence a clippy lint or a type error in production code and merge CLEAN. Cheap to fix (drop the pathspec for the suppression pass).

findings.title: 30-42% of the server test corpus is regex-over-source-text, concentrated exactly in the security-critical modules; the crate has no reducer-executing harness at all
findings.evidence: Measured over server-module/src/*_tests.rs (637 `#[test]` fns, 44,424 lines). CONSERVATIVE measure (test body references a const/fn bound to `include_str!`): 192/637 = 30%. Per-file: pvp_tests.rs 30/51 = 59%, economy_tests.rs 16/24 = 67%, ranking_tests.rs 13/23 = 57%, npc_tests.rs 17/30 = 57%, battle_tests.rs 25/51 = 49%, accounts_tests.rs 26/55 = 47%, trading_tests.rs 15/38 = 39%. BROAD measure (also counts squash_ws/fn_body_views/block_after helper use): 269/637 = 42%. `grep -c include_str! server-module/src/*_tests.rs` totals 106 occurrences. The reason is stated in the code itself — 14r-d's own test header (server-module/src/battle_tests.rs, added by 0ba8ada): 'SUBSTRATE. Static source-shape scans (ADR-0185 D4 / ADR-0156 P7 — this crate has no reducer-executing harness and no TestDb).' Same pattern client-side: client/src/main.wiring.test.ts is 10,750 lines of `readFileSync`-and-string-match over client/src/main.ts (2,795 lines), a 3.85:1 ratio; its header says 'WHY source-scan (NOT import): main.ts has DOM/wasm side effects'. The 14r-e spec confirms the consequence: 'mvi-e2e parked: no test executes main.ts's frame body'.
findings.impact: Directly against the operator's PRIMARY bar. These tests pin source TEXT, not behaviour: they cannot catch a semantic regression that preserves the text shape, and they FAIL on any innocuous refactor — so they simultaneously under-protect correctness and actively penalise changeability. 14r-d spent 852 test lines to pin a 69-line production change and still cannot prove the reducer behaves correctly. This is also the root cause of the 43% mutation-survivor rate (see QUAL-03).

findings.title: The mutation ratchet was remediated by RAISING the cap 299→324 (43% of server mutants survive), 87% of survivors were never triaged, and the actual root cause — zero nightly alerting — was documented rather than fixed
findings.evidence: justfile:110 `mutate-server cap="324":`. docs/adr/0183-nightly-mutation-gate-rebaseline-and-failure-visibility.md:9 Decision: 'Re-baseline the mutate-server cap 299 → 324 (exact hosted count...) as debt-carrying — 11 killable survivors named'. :41-42 measurement table: hosted nightly @ master 8814416 = 753 mutants, 324 missed, 377 caught, 52 unviable => 43.0% survival. :130-136 states the triage scope honestly: 'The ~282 survivors carried over from the 299 baseline were NOT re-triaged this episode' — so 282/324 = 87% of surviving mutants have never been classified. :113-127: of the 41 newly-classified survivors, 32 legitimate-shell and 9 weak-test; 11 named as killable debt with a successor ratchet to ≤313. :199 D5: 'No issue-creating Action, webhook, or notification step was added' — the fix for five nights of unnoticed red is a comment, blocked on mdrewt/claude-harness#14 which mr-state.json:28 records as still OPEN with 0 comments.
findings.impact: The repo's only semantic quality ratchet now certifies that 43% of mutations to the server module go undetected, and 87% of that population is unexamined. The remediation loosened the gate. The failure-visibility root cause is unfixed, so the identical 5-day-silent-red episode can recur. ADR-0183 is itself rigorous and honest about all of this — the problem is the outcome, not the record.

findings.title: Trace: the `concat!()` scanner-dodge metastasized from one file into two plus a test that pins it, while the slice chartered to delete it spent a whole re-spawn producing a 7-line comment edit
findings.evidence: LINEAGE. (1) m21a (b5bbe1d, 2026-08-08) ships server-module/src/accounts.rs with `pub(crate) const ALLOWED_ISSUERS: &[&str] = &[concat!("https:/", "/auth.monster-realm.invalid/")];` — a production-source contortion existing solely to avoid tripping broken eval scanners. (2) 13r-c's spec charter, M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:104-106, says explicitly: 'then delete the accounts.rs concat!() workaround and write ALLOWED_ISSUERS naturally'. 13r-c merged 2026-08-09 as 0d13923 ($64.86). The concat!() IS STILL THERE — accounts.rs:54, verified today. (3) M21b-2 (4d789bd, 2026-08-13) adds evals/account-e2e.eval.mjs (+2179 lines) whose `ISSUER_NEEDLE` pins the concat!() token exactly, cementing the workaround as a tested contract. (4) 14r-g (f9cd611, 2026-08-14) COPIES it into server-module/src/pvp.rs:63: `const RANKED_PLACEHOLDER_ISSUER: &str = concat!("https:/", "/auth.monster-realm.invalid/");` with the comment 'Assembled with the same concat! split so this file's source text carries no contiguous scheme slashes (server-module source-scan hazard).' findings.impact: A tooling defect is now load-bearing in two production source files and pinned by a test. The dependency runs backwards: production code is shaped to satisfy broken test infrastructure. The 13r-c re-spawn is 100% waste ($14.45 plus a full detached build session and a supervisor merge cycle) caused by stale queue state — the supervisor could not tell that its own queue entry was already satisfied.

findings.title: The `touches:` disjointness discipline — the mechanism that enables slice fan-out — is the direct causal generator of the untracked-residual backlog
findings.evidence: SMOKING GUN: docs/adr/0165-changelog-freshness-nightly-drift-check.md:9, Status Accepted, Date 2026-07-31, Slice 11r-d — 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared `touches:`.' 11r-i merged 2026-08-02 (memory/projects/mr-native-tick.log:1584 'merged PR#278(11r-i)->9debea9; M-postgate-eleventh-review-residuals CLOSED') and did NOT implement it. Consequence per M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:200-205: 'CHANGELOG has re-drifted 18 PRs (#291-#306 absent) one milestone after 12r-f reconciled it — because ADR-0165's Accepted decision ... was assigned to 11r-i and silently never implemented.' Actually implemented 2026-08-15 by 13r-g (6469503), 15 days after Acceptance. SAME PATTERN, in-window: 14r-d's ADR-0185 D6, quoted in commit 0ba8ada's body — 'route through observability::mr_log, not bare log::error! (OBS-2 ratchet would red two gates whose fix files are outside touches:)'; and the m20a perf gate, justfile:35-39 — 'WHY it is wired inside `eval:` rather than as a `ci:` dependency: ci-gate-wiring.eval.mjs pins the ci: dep list against .github/workflows/ci.yml ... and ci.yml is outside m20a's touches.' STRUCTURAL SURFACE: 21 of 165 ADRs carry a 'Residuals / follow-ups' section; `grep -hoE` over docs/adr/*.md finds 78 defer/park phrases ('deferred to' 45, 'a later slice' 11, 'future slice' 10, 'parked to' 8, 'routed to' 2, 'queue it' 1, 'candidate slice' 1). There is no mechanism that converts any of them into queued work.
findings.impact: This is the causal core of the rework rate. Parallelism is bought by forbidding a slice from touching files outside its declared set; the forbidden work is written into an ADR Residuals bullet; nothing reads those bullets; a human-instigated multi-lens review rediscovers them weeks later at the highest possible cost. The review-residual milestone is an expensive LLM-driven garbage collector for a leak the fan-out design creates. Measured disclosure→remediation latency (n=10 traceable items): ADR-0148 nh2 dual-bind 7/25→14r-e 8/14 = 20d (re-disclosed via ADR-0158); ADR-0152 nh5 7/25→13r-f 8/14 = 20d (disclosed twice); ADR-0158 7/27→14r-e 8/14 = 18d; ADR-0165 7/31→13r-g 8/15 = 15d; ADR-0166 R4/R6 7/31→14r-f 8/14 = 14d; ADR-0168 7/31→14r-d 8/14 = 14d; ADR-0170 res.8 8/01→14r-f 8/14 = 13d; ADR-0179 §9 8/08→13r-h 8/15 = 7d; ADR-0180 m20e amendment 8/09→13r-a 8/14 = 5d; OBS-45/46 park 8/09→13r-b 8/14 = 5d. Mean 13.1 days, median 14.

findings.title: Fan-out disjointness derived from declared `touches:` failed in-window — 14r-c and 14r-e both edited client/src/main.wiring.test.ts, forcing a park, rebase and 3-attempt resume
findings.evidence: `git show 9b924f3 --name-only` (14r-c) includes `client/src/main.wiring.test.ts`; `git show 4fd3c6e --name-only` (14r-e) also includes it. 14r-e's declared touches in M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:145 are `client/src/main.ts, client/src/prediction/, client/e2e/` — main.wiring.test.ts is NOT in that set, so 14r-e drifted outside its declaration. Ledger 2026-08-14T14:36:41Z: 'conflict+regression-suspect: PR#318 CONFLICTING vs master 9b924f3 (shared file client/src/main.wiring.test.ts with merged 14r-c) ... park_counters 0->1'. The spec had blessed {14r-e, 14r-f, 14r-g} as a disjoint fan-out group (:238-243) and noted 'mr-disjoint verdicts advisory at spawn time'.
findings.impact: One park + rebase + resume cycle inside a 3-attempt $85.14 slice. The disjointness check is only as sound as the declared touches, and slices routinely exceed them — which is also the reason ADR-0165-class deferrals happen (REWORK-04). The `touches:` field is simultaneously trusted for scheduling and violated in practice.

findings.title: WORKING WELL — the production code the loop emits is genuinely high quality against the operator's PRIMARY bar: pure seams extracted specifically for testability, fail-closed defaults, correct SSOT selection, and honest self-labelling
findings.evidence: 14r-g (f9cd611) server-module/src/pvp.rs:68-115 extracts two PURE functions — `issuers_configured(issuers: &[&str]) -> bool` and `ranked_account_gate(enforced, caller_has_account, opponent_has_account) -> Result<(), &'static str>` — with the rationale written down: 'PURE — no ctx, no I/O — so it is exhaustively unit-testable in-crate (reducer bodies are not)'. It picks the right SSOT and says why: '`is_account_holder` — never `has_jwt`, which is true for every connection'. It re-checks at accept: 'load-bearing, not redundant. Pending rows created before enforcement activation, and any future account-status revocation, must never create a ranked battle'. It fails closed and inert. 13r-f (7e08d36) client/src/prediction/heldKeys.ts introduces `snapshot()`/`restore()` — a pure seam created expressly so an untestable DOM-shell path becomes unit-testable — with a property-shaped observation type `HeldObservation` and the contract stated as an identity law ('`restore(snapshot())` must be the IDENTITY on this observation — that is the whole contract, and expressing it as one comparable value is what makes U-W8 a property rather than a hand-picked pair of assertions'). 14r-f (97d6b6e) server-module/src/movement.rs labels its own change honestly: 'This is DEFENSIVE hygiene, not a reachable-bug fix — the ADR-0168 D1 drain lock above already skipped every battle-locked character'; and client/src/ui/tradeProposeModel.ts documents the cap as 'NOT an SSOT — a MIRROR of server-module/src/trading.rs:37 ... kept honest by evals/trade-cap-parity.eval.mjs' plus 'A VETO, ANDed in — never one more branch of `hasAsset`, which would let a 65-monster offer through as long as it also carried gold.' 14r-d (0ba8ada) battle.rs:737 replaces `?` with log-and-commit and hoists both GC statements above the fallible write with an explicit behaviour-preservation argument.
findings.impact: Per-diff craftsmanship is not the problem. The defect is entirely at the process layer: what gets built, in what order, and whether known problems reach a queue. Any intervention should target routing and backlog integrity, not the code-generation quality.

findings.title: WORKING WELL — the review-residual specs and the proof-of-teeth discipline are exceptionally rigorous; the eval gates that do exist prove they can FAIL before they are trusted
findings.evidence: M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:4-11 pins a review SHA, method ('9 independent sonnet lenses over an isolated --no-hardlinks clone; every reported finding independently re-verified by separate verifier agents given only the claim and location, not the finder's framing or confidence'), and 'All path:line citations are @ f9a063d'. Both specs carry explicit '§5 Explicitly NOT in scope' sections and per-slice 'proof-of-teeth MUST start RED' mandates (13r spec:263-266: '13r-c and 13r-d proofs MUST start RED against the current gates — a green-from-the-start test there means the fix was not actually applied'). The evals honour it: evals/observability-stack-config.eval.mjs:6-11 — 'T-a..T-g (always, FIRST) — PROOF-OF-TEETH over inline fixtures. Every detector below is first shown to REJECT the shape it exists to catch. A gate that has never failed is a decoration.' 14r-d's test header records four red-team defeats of its own first design (S1 return-Err-after-commit, S2 five ways to re-set outcome without the token, S3 seven abort spellings, S4 three GC reorderings) with the lesson written down. 14r-e's commit body records the exact RED evidence and the mutant kill ('narrow-gate mutant 52 sends vs <=12'). 14r-g's records 'RED proven (eval [D/fn-missing], compile-red E0425 x13, structural assert-red x4)'.
findings.impact: This is the strongest asset in the system. The manifest-count tests the 2026-08-14 audit dismissed as 'count-tracking ceremony' are in fact BIDIRECTIONAL: client/src/main.wiring.test.ts:5181-5212 drives the loop domain from a STATIC import of OVERLAY_IDS and asserts count equality in both directions ('A higher count means a 16th entry was smuggled in'). They are weaker than behavioural tests but they are not vacuous — the audit note undersold them.

findings.title: WORKING WELL — ADRs are load-bearing decision records, not after-the-fact paperwork: 143 distinct ADRs are cited 3,729 times in production source, and 14 of the 15 in-window ADRs appear in code
findings.evidence: `grep -rohE 'ADR-0[0-9]{3}' --include=*.rs --include=*.ts server-module/src client/src game-core/src | sort -u | wc -l` = 143 distinct ADRs; total occurrences 3,729. Per in-window ADR (code+config refs): 0179:95, 0180:78, 0181:110, 0182:204, 0183:12, 0184:23, 0185:66, 0186:0, 0187:34, 0188:45, 0189:98, 0190:13, 0191:11, 0192:33, 0193:37. Only ADR-0186 has zero code references. The citations are decision-granular, not just ADR-number name-drops — e.g. pvp.rs cites 'ADR-0189 D6', 'ADR-0189 D2', 'ADR-0189 D8'; battle.rs cites 'ADR-0185 D1', 'ADR-0185 D7'. ADR-0183 is a model triage record: it re-ran the baseline locally and matched it exactly (299/513), diffed hosted-vs-local survivor sets down to a single differing mutant, classified 41 new survivors 32 legitimate-shell / 9 weak-test, and explicitly refused to over-read its own scope.
findings.impact: ADRs earn their cost as navigational anchors — an agent reading pvp.rs:68 can find the exact decision and its rationale. This is a real asset for changeability. The problem is size and the Residuals-as-graveyard pattern (ADR-02), not legitimacy.

findings.title: ADR bloat: mean length grew 3.8x (91→342 lines), 18 ADRs in 8 days = 23% of the whole corpus, and ADR-0180 has become a 1,034-line milestone journal that is exactly where the crash-loop fixes went to be forgotten
findings.evidence: Computed over docs/adr/0*.md (165 files, 27,094 lines): ADR 0001-0049 n=16 mean 91 lines; 0050-0099 n=50 mean 141; 0100-0149 n=49 mean 123; 0150-0178 n=29 mean 198; 0179-0196 n=18 mean 342, total 6,160 lines. Those 18 ADRs are 22.7% of the corpus by line count and were written in 8 days. docs/adr/0180-observability-stack-selection.md is 1,034 lines with five append-only build-note amendments (`## Amendment — 2026-08-08 (m20b build pass...)`, `(m20a build notes...)`, `(m20c build notes...)`, `(m20d build notes...)`, `(m20e build notes: evals tail as shipped)`) — a changelog wearing an ADR's clothes. It is also the file where the observability crash-loop was recorded and parked: M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:57 cites 'ADR-0180's m20e amendment (docs/adr/0180-observability-stack-selection.md:1031), fixes never committed'. Structural surface: 21 ADRs carry a Residuals/follow-ups section; 78 defer/park phrases across the corpus; 29 ADRs carry an `Amended-by:` back-pointer and 7 are Superseded.
findings.impact: The ADR is doing three jobs at once — decision record, build journal, and residual backlog — and it is bad at the third. Every slice pays to read and regenerate the digest against a corpus growing ~770 lines/day. The 'Residuals / follow-ups' section is the single highest-leverage place to intervene: making it emit a queue entry would remove most of class (A) from REWORK-02.

findings.title: Performance — the operator's explicit PRIMARY concern — is gated only by 7 nanosecond-scale pure functions with 20x headroom ceilings; nothing measures reducer latency, DB round-trip, frame time or subscription payload
findings.evidence: game-core/benches/budgets.rs:11-13: 'Ceilings are ~20x the locally measured mean, rounded UP to a clean figure — the gate catches order-of-magnitude regressions, not 5% drift'. The full table (:31-66) is 7 entries, all game-core pure functions: measured 1.87ns→ceiling 40.0; 4.77→100.0; 99.7→2000.0; 14.2→300.0; 14.9→300.0; 8.97→200.0; 134.5→3000.0. All measured 2026-08-08. The gate runs (justfile:30 `just perf-budget` inside `eval:`, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:71 `- run: just eval`), but a 19x regression on any hot path passes GREEN. Its placement is itself a touches:-workaround (justfile:35-39, quoted in REWORK-04). No server-side or client-side latency budget exists: `grep -rn perf-budget justfile .github/workflows` finds no other gate, and evals/baselines/ contains 15 files, none of them perf. m20d ($117.33, 323cee1) delivered sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs (6,053 lines, 187 inline tests, in the cargo workspace so `cargo nextest run --workspace` does run them) and performed a one-off OBS-27 breaking-point measurement — but it is a manual tool, wired into no gate and no baseline.
findings.impact: The operator named performance as a PRIMARY axis. Nothing in the loop can detect a performance regression in the parts of the system where a multiplayer game actually gets slow — reducer execution, subscription fan-out, client frame budget. The one perf gate that exists is a ~order-of-magnitude smoke test over pure combat math. m20d built the instrument to measure the real thing and then did not connect it to anything.

gaps: I could not measure per-slice token/time breakdown INSIDE the detached build sessions. The slice transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-home-mdrewt-projects-ai-apps-claude-harness-projects-monster-realm/ total 442MB across 62 files; streaming and attributing them to slices was out of budget for this lane. So I cannot say how much of a slice's cost went to planning vs testing vs review-wave iteration — only the total from the ledger.

I could not verify the true dollar cost of any individual M20/M21 slice. Most rows carry 'COST-UNKNOWN (no result event; true spend unrecorded)' and were filled by 'mechanical backfill by tick v3 reconcile' (see DATA-01). All cost findings inherit that uncertainty.

I could not determine whether the 282 untriaged mutation survivors (87% of the 324 cap) are legitimate-shell or weak-test. ADR-0183 §D3 explicitly declines to classify them, and re-running cargo-mutants would take tens of minutes of compute plus mutating state, which is out of scope for a read-only lane.

I could not verify that the 13r-a observability fixes actually make the stack boot. The slice's own EARS accepts 'Boot evidence recorded manually per the G11 precedent (runtime container facts are not statically checkable)', so the only in-repo proof is static tripwires in evals/observability-stack-config.eval.mjs. Running docker compose would be a side effect.

I could not measure real runtime performance of any in-window feature. No latency, throughput, or frame-time data exists in the repo for the window — the only committed perf artefacts are the seven nanosecond-scale game-core budgets measured 2026-08-08 (PERF-01). m20d's load driver produced a one-off OBS-27 breaking-point number that is recorded only in an ADR-0180 amendment, with no baseline file to compare against.

I could not compute a dollar figure for CI. monster-realm is a PUBLIC repo, so GitHub Actions minutes are free; the cost of red/flaky CI is wall-clock latency plus the LLM tokens spent diagnosing it, and the latter is not separable in the ledger (it is folded into the slice's total).

I did not audit the ~29 evals outside the KNOWN_UNMIGRATED list for other blindness classes. QUAL-01 reports only what the repo's own SSOT registry (scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs) measures. There may be additional false-GREEN-capable gates that no measurement has yet been pointed at.

I could not establish whether any in-window residual defect was ever reachable by a real player. Several are explicitly labelled unreachable by their own authors (14r-f's movement.rs change: 'DEFENSIVE hygiene, not a reachable-bug fix'); 14r-g is inert until a real OIDC issuer is configured. So 'defects fixed' is not the same as 'player-visible bugs fixed', and I did not attempt to separate the two beyond what the diffs state.

findings.title: The budget governor's "d7_usd" is not a rolling 7-day figure — it resets to $0 on a fixed weekly anchor, and it reset mid-burn on 2026-08-14T00:00Z
findings.evidence: $MEM/mr-situation:63-69 computes `ws = anchor + floor((now-anchor)/7d)*7d` from $MEM/.weekly-reset-anchor (content `1784851200` = 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z), then :70-84 sums cost_usd only for rows with ts>=ws, and :122 emits it under the key "d7_usd". Replaying that exact algorithm against the ledger: 2026-08-10T14:10Z -> window_start=2026-08-07T00:00Z, d7=$1799.64 (64.7% of the $2783 limit); 2026-08-14T00:01Z -> window_start=2026-08-14T00:00Z, d7=$0.00 (0.0%); 2026-08-15T04:00Z -> d7=$728.14 (26.2%). The orchestrator's stated ground-truth value ($989.51 / 35.6%) reproduces at 2026-08-15T14:10Z as $991.56 / 35.6% — i.e. it is spend since 2026-08-14T00:00Z (~38h), not 7 days.
findings.impact: The true 7-day burn of $1,904.45 (68.4% of the $2,783 weekly limit) was never visible to the governor as a single number. After the 2026-08-14T00:00Z reset the loop launched 11 slices (14r-a..g, 13r-a/b/d/f) worth $728.14 in 28h while every tick logged `governor=NORMAL` at a reading that started from zero. SOFT-PAUSE (0.90) and HARD-STOP (0.97) are therefore unreachable in any week whose spend straddles a Friday-00:00Z boundary. Ground-truth item 8 ("d7 = $989.51 ... 35.6% utilization") is technically correct but materially misleading: real utilization for the window was 68.4-70.1%.

findings.title: Cost governor is 100% advisory: 12 WARN, 10 STOP-MONITOR, 4 HARD-MONITOR, 77 LOG-STALL in-window and zero enforcement actions ever taken
findings.evidence: $MEM/mr-budget-config.json:55 `"costwatch_enforce": false`. $MEM/mr-cost-watch:56-57 reads it every poll; :91 `STOP-MONITOR ... enforce=false, no flag`; :108 `HARD-MONITOR 125% ... enforce=false or log-stalled`. Every one of the 23 `started` lines in $MEM/mr-native-tick.log for the window carries `enforce=0` (e.g. L2276, L2637, L3246). In-window COSTWATCH census (167 lines, 2026-08-08T04Z..2026-08-15T04Z): 12 WARN, 10 STOP-MONITOR, 4 HARD-MONITOR (M21b L2327, M21c L2332, 13r-c L2598, M21b-2 L2656), 77 LOG-STALL, 23 started, 24 done-file. Zero STOP flags, zero TERM/KILL, zero `.fired` files. The reason it is off is documented as a deliberate decision: $MEM/mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 "**Deliberately NOT done** (see ADR-0011): arming `costwatch_enforce` (all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0; a kill strands locks and hard-blocks relaunch until a human edits `cap_override`)". The arming precondition is $MEM/mr-budget-config.json:56 (`_costwatch_note`, adversarial-review condition F3: verify subagent usage streams in real time by comparing `mr-cost-watch price <log>` timeline vs ledger on one completed run) — that verification is now trivially satisfiable from the 23 in-window (WARN-time raw, final raw, ledger) triples but has never been run.
findings.impact: 4 of 21 slices exceeded their own declared tier cap in real ledger dollars with no intervention: M21b-2 182.9% ($274.37/$150), M21c 161.0% ($96.60/$60), M21b 130.0% ($77.98/$60), 13r-c 108.1% ($64.86/$60). Counterfactual with enforce=true (HARD at 125% of raw, converted to real dollars by each run's own measured ledger/raw): kills would have landed at $52.75 (87.9% of cap), $75.93 (126.6%), $49.04 (81.7%) and $143.22 (95.5%), preventing $192.85 of spend — $131.15 of it on M21b-2 alone (7% of the whole window). Two of the four kills would have been premature (81.7% and 87.9% of cap) on runs that merged cleanly, which is exactly the README's objection — but that is a calibration defect (COST-03/COST-10), not an argument for permanent disablement.

findings.title: The three M21b-2 figures fully reconcile; the raw estimator has two concrete, measurable pricing bugs (1.75x per-content-block double-count, and 1h cache writes priced at the 5m rate)
findings.evidence: Exact provenance of each number: (1) $359.7114 raw = $MEM/mr-cost-watch:67 calling price_log "$L" raw -> :16-42, a token-price reconstruction of /tmp/mr_pass_M21b-2.log using mr-budget-config.json:17-46 rates. (2) $287.7692 final-cal = the same function without `raw`, :41 `print(f"{tot*F:.4f}")` where F = costwatch_stream_factor = 0.8 (mr-budget-config.json:57). 359.7114 x 0.8 = 287.76912 -> printed 287.7692. Exact. (3) $274.3706 ledger = mr-record:60-73 shelling out to $MEM/mr-cost-sum, which segments the log on `ATTEMPT=`/`ESCALAT` markers and sums per-segment maxima of the CLI's own `total_cost_usd` (mr-cost-sum:70-122). Only (3) is authoritative billing. Bug A — no message-id dedup: mr-cost-watch:29-39 prices EVERY stream line containing `"usage"` with a non-zero output_tokens. Inspection of /tmp/mr_pass_13r-a.log shows the SDK emits one event per content block, each repeating the identical `message.usage` for the same `message.id` (e.g. msg_011Ce3KRiX1JHgYb9mE2aArW appears 3x with identical usage {input 2, cache_creation 29106, cache_read 15894, output 4}). Measured duplication over 15 surviving in-window pass logs: 12,264 usage events vs 7,020 distinct message ids = 1.75 events/message, range 1.38 (M21c) to 2.20 (m20b). Bug B — cache-write tier ignored: mr-cost-watch:39 prices all `cache_creation_input_tokens` at `cache_write_5m`, but the events carry `cache_creation: {ephemeral_5m, ephemeral_1h}` and 17.9% of in-window cache-creation tokens (6.24M of 34.93M) are ephemeral_1h, which mr-budget-config.json:22/29/35/43 prices 1.6x higher. Consequence: the correction factor is not a scalar. Measured ledger/raw per slice ranges 0.6370 (m20b) to 1.0076 (M21c), aggregate 0.7386 across 21 slices — against a hard-coded constant of 0.80.
findings.impact: The SSOT ($274.3706) is trustworthy; the two watcher figures are not, and the config's own note ("Measured: raw overcounts ~25%... ledger/raw=0.80") is wrong in the sense that matters — the error is run-dependent (+-22% band), not a constant. Because enforcement thresholds are applied to `raw` (mr-cost-watch:82, with an explicit comment claiming "overcount fires early = safe direction"), and raw sometimes UNDERCOUNTS (M21c 1.0076, 13r-b 1.0033), the stated safety argument for thresholding on raw is falsified by in-window data.

findings.title: The ledger SSOT systematically under-reports: $46.84 of real, measurable spend in-window is absent, because resume passes append to the same log after the FINISHED row is written and are never re-summed
findings.evidence: 14r-e: /tmp/mr_pass_14r-e.log contains four `ATTEMPT=` markers (12:02:33Z, 13:39:31Z, 13:40:51Z, and a fourth at 15:01:27Z from the post-PARK resume). Segmenting exactly as mr-cost-sum:70-122 does: 73.9980 + 7.7484 + 3.3969 + 40.5831 = $125.7264. The ledger's only costed row (line 637, ts 2026-08-14T13:46:50Z) records $85.1433 = the first three segments only. `mr-cost-sum /tmp/mr_pass_14r-e.log` today returns 125.7264. Missing: $40.5831 (47.7% understatement on that slice). Every subsequent 14r-e row is $0 or null: L645 PARKED (null), L647 launched (null), L649 delegated-ci-watch (0.0), L651 MERGED (0.0). m20c: same pattern — L570 FINISHED $114.5005 (first pass), L571 LAUNCHED (null) for the resume, L576 MERGED (null). `mr-cost-sum /tmp/mr_pass_m20c.log` = $6.2589 for the surviving resume-pass log, unrecorded. Separately, two rows explicitly book real paid work at exactly $0: L573 m20c `REVIEWED-FLAGGED` cost_usd 0.0 with notes "paid review pass (reviewer+red-team+verifier) on PR#304"; L604 `weekly-review-rev14` cost_usd 0.0 with notes "tier=review visibility-only cost-null row". 32 of the 150 in-window rows carry cost_usd = null (COST-UNKNOWN per mr-record:94-96), and mr-situation:81-82 counts null as $0.0.
findings.impact: True window spend is at least $1,951.29, not the $1,904.45 the ledger reports (2.4% understatement, all in the unsafe direction for a governor). The bug class is structural, not a one-off: any slice that is PARKED and resumed, or relaunched under the same slice name, loses its later spend, because mr-record's C1 guard (mr-record:42-58) and the wrapper-reconcile path only fire once per done-event. Also destroys audit trail: /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log is reused across runs, so 13r-c's 2026-08-10 log ($64.86) has been overwritten by its 2026-08-15 rerun (mr-cost-sum now returns $14.4542) and m20c's $114.50 first-pass log is gone.

findings.title: 99.8% of priced token spend is context, not generation: 68.0% cache reads, 31.8% cache writes, 0.1% output tokens — the cost lever is context volume per turn, nothing else
findings.evidence: Re-running mr-cost-watch's own pricing formula (mr-cost-watch:30-39) over 9 surviving in-window pass logs and splitting the four terms reproduces the logged COSTWATCH totals to the cent (13r-a $38.90 vs logged raw $38.8958 at mr-native-tick.log L3156; 14r-g $133.71 vs L3128 $133.7100; m20e $158.22 vs L2534 $158.2201; m20d $154.87 vs L2483 $154.8727). Split of the $928.94 raw across those 9: new input $0.92 (0.1%), output $1.16 (0.1%), cache READ $631.67 (68.0%), cache WRITE $295.18 (31.8%). Per-slice cache-read share 62.6%-72.0%. Average context re-read per distinct assistant message (deduped by message.id): 106,645 tok (14r-d) to 217,639 tok (m20e), mean ~150k. Distinct messages per slice: 230 (m20b) to 762 (14r-e).
findings.impact: Against the operator's SECONDARY priority this is the single largest actionable lever in the system. At ~150k tokens of context re-read per turn and 400-760 turns per slice, halving average context per turn (tighter briefs, narrower touch sets, sub-agent scoping, fewer full-file reads) would roughly halve slice cost — ~$900/week at the observed rate — with no model or scheduling change. Conversely, every prompt-engineering change that adds durable context to the brief is multiplied by ~500 turns before it is paid for.

findings.title: The HARD=fable@xhigh premium costs 2.18x per slice and 1.46x per line changed, and is completely confounded with tier — no clean head-to-head is possible from this window
findings.evidence: Tier and model are 100% collinear in-window: every COSTWATCH `started cap=$150` run is model=fable (M21b-2, m20a, m20c, m20d, m20e, 14r-b, 14r-e, 14r-g, M21a, 13r-f) and every `cap=$60` run is model=opus (M21b, M21c, 13r-a, 13r-b, 13r-c, 13r-d, 14r-a, 14r-c, 14r-d, 14r-f, m20b) — mr-native-tick.log L2276/L2308/L2367/L2426/L2519/L2590/L2637/L2847/L2898/L2969/L3089/L3146/L3183/L3246. Cost (14r-e corrected to $125.7264): fable n=10, $1,234.93, mean $123.49; opus n=11, $623.30, mean $56.66 -> 2.18x per slice. Churn (git show --numstat -M on each merge commit): fable 48,958 lines / 274 files, opus 35,975 / 125 -> $/kline 25.22 vs 17.33 (1.46x), $/file 4.51 vs 4.99 (fable CHEAPER per file). Per-turn: fable mean 547 distinct messages at $0.192/turn, opus 415 at $0.137/turn — a 1.40x per-turn price ratio that closely tracks the 1.5x fable/opus rate ratio configured at mr-budget-config.json:39-46. So the 2.18x slice premium decomposes as ~1.4x price x ~1.32x more turns. Quality signals available in-window are null or adverse: remote_red_fix_cycles = 0 on every single window row (no signal at all); multi-attempt runs are 2/10 for fable (14r-e ATTEMPTS=3, 13r-f ATTEMPTS=3) vs 1/11 for opus (13r-b ATTEMPTS=2); gate flags 7/10 fable vs 4/11 opus, all adjudicated CLEAN.
findings.impact: ~$611 of the window's $1,864 slice spend is the fable-over-opus delta. There is no measurement in this window that would justify or refute it: the confound is total (hard-tier slices genuinely touch schema/reducer/netcode/security, which is why they were routed to fable in the first place), and the only available quality columns are either constant-zero (remote_red_fix_cycles) or recorded before CI concludes (master_ci_after is 'pending'/'in_progress' on 9 of 17 populated rows). Recommendation is a measurement, not a routing change: run one A/B pair of comparable-surface slices on opus@high vs fable@xhigh and record post-merge red cycles, or start populating remote_red_fix_cycles honestly.

findings.title: There is no independent cost source to cross-check the ledger against — mr-usage-daily.jsonl is a derivative of the ledger and ~/.claude/usage-log.csv has no cost or token columns at all
findings.evidence: $MEM/mr-usage-snap:30-38 computes `native_ledger_usd` by re-summing the SAME ledger file over a 24h-ago cut. Verified: the eight daily rows for dates 2026-08-08..2026-08-15 reproduce the ledger EXACTLY over their own 09:35Z windows (375.85/700.30/201.64/274.37/0.00/0.00/208.58/715.97, delta 0.00 on every segment). It is therefore zero independent information. Its `models`/`cowork_est_usd` column measures a different system entirely — mr-usage-snap:8 points at `/mnt/c/Users/mdrewt/AppData/Roaming/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions` (Windows Cowork sessions), not the harness's own transcripts, which is why row 14 shows cowork $0.96 on a day the native loop spent $375.85. Additional defects: the `date` label is the run date while the window starts 24h earlier (row date=2026-08-11 actually covers 2026-08-10T09:35 onward), so naive summation by date over-counts by a day (my sum of the eight rows = $2,476.71 for what is really 08-07T09:35..08-15T09:35); mr-usage-snap:35 has NO upper bound on the window; 2026-07-27 has two rows (window_start 06:01 and 09:35) so any per-date consumer double-counts; and mr-usage-snap:24 prices fable at opus rates by design, so cowork_est_usd is a stated lower bound. ~/.claude/usage-log.csv columns are exactly `timestamp,kind,name,session,project` — no cost, no tokens. Its only in-window content is 196 rows (191 agent + 5 skill invocations across 21 slice projects; reviewer 47, red-team 41, tester 31, planner 20, verifier 16).
findings.impact: Every cost claim in this system traces back to one file written by one code path. When that path drops spend (COST-04) nothing anywhere else notices. The cheapest fix is to make mr-usage-snap read the harness's own ~/.claude/projects transcripts as a genuine second source instead of a Windows directory unrelated to the loop.

findings.title: Supervisor orchestration overhead is small and well-controlled: 4.56% of window spend; the 85h dead period cost $0 in tokens
findings.evidence: 65 SUPERVISOR rows totalling $86.8010 in the stated EDT window (60 rows / $79.7858 on UTC calendar days — see COST-09). Mean $1.3354, median $1.1736, min $0.2651, max $5.0285 (2026-08-09T08:27:13Z, the tick that adjudicated m20c's gate flag). Breakdown by trigger: cron 26 ticks $32.31, done 18 $24.07, ci 15 $22.05, manual 4 $7.26, decision 2 $1.11. $86.80 / $1,904.45 = 4.56% of window spend. Productivity: 21 of 65 ticks (32.3%, $17.66 = 20.3% of tick spend) wrote no launch/merge/fix ledger row within their preceding 30 minutes; a stricter run_id-join gives an upper bound of 58 ticks / $76.13 / 87.7%, but that join is unreliable because slice rows are written under mr-spawn-*/native-*/wrapper-reconcile run_ids rather than the tick's own. In the dead period 2026-08-10T14:05Z..2026-08-14T01:52Z there are zero SUPERVISOR rows and 108 in-window `SKIP disabled-flag` lines in mr-native-tick.log — skipped ticks never spawn a model and cost nothing. mr-ci-watch is a zero-token shell poller (mr-ci-watch:2).
findings.impact: Orchestration is not where the money is. Counterfactual for always-on ticking: 24 ticks/day x 7 days = 168 x $1.3354 = $224.35/week vs $86.80 actual, i.e. +$137.55/week = 4.9% of the $2,783 weekly limit. That is affordable; the 108 skipped ticks saved $137 of a $1,904 spend while forfeiting ~85 hours of throughput. Cutting ticks is the wrong optimization; the ci-triggered ticks (15 for $22.05) are the one place worth trimming, since mr-ci-watch already knows the answer before it wakes a model.

findings.title: Because burn is ~$39/slice-build-hour, the $2,783 weekly limit only funds ~35 wall-hours of 2-way fan-out — the 85h idle window forfeited ~10 slices of achievable work, not the ~22 a naive throughput extrapolation suggests
findings.evidence: From launch->FINISHED ledger timestamps for the 19 slices where both exist: 43.18 measurable slice-build-hours for $1,695.85 = $39.28 per slice-build-hour (range $20.74/h for 13r-a to $55.32/h for M21b-2). Observed fan-out is 2 concurrent slices on every fan-out tick (M21b+M21c, m20a+m20b, m20c+m20d, 14r-b+14r-d, 14r-c+14r-e, 14r-f+14r-g, 13r-b+13r-f), so sustained burn is ~$78.6/wall-hour. $2,783 / $78.56 = 35.4 wall-hours per week at 2-way fan-out = a 21% duty cycle. Window headroom at the end: $2,783 - $1,904.45 = $878.55, and mean all-in cost per merged slice is $88.49 ($1,858.23 corrected slice spend / 21) -> ~10 additional slices affordable. Also flagging a ground-truth discrepancy: the brief states the window is EDT-local 2026-08-08T00:00..2026-08-14T23:59, but the quoted figures ($1,824.97, 60 SUPERVISOR ticks) reproduce exactly on UTC CALENDAR days 2026-08-08..2026-08-14, not on the EDT window (which gives $1,904.45 / 65 ticks). The EDT interpretation adds 12 rows and $79.48.
findings.impact: Reframes the dead-time finding. The 85h outage is a real throughput failure but its cost ceiling is ~10 slices / ~$880, not ~22 slices / ~$1,950 — the budget ceiling binds before the clock does. It also means a 24/7 hourly cron is structurally the wrong shape for this loop: it can only afford to run ~1 day in 5 at current per-slice cost, so cost reduction (COST-05) and idle-recovery are the same problem, not competing ones.

findings.title: Enforcement thresholds are applied to the mis-calibrated `raw` estimate, so the nominal $150/$60 caps actually bite anywhere between 64% and 101% of their stated value in real dollars
findings.evidence: $MEM/mr-cost-watch:82 `COST=$(price_log "$L" raw)` with the in-line justification "threshold on RAW (overcount fires early = safe direction)", and :84 compares that raw figure to 0.8/1.0/1.25 x cap. Measured ledger/raw per slice (final COSTWATCH `done-file` raw vs the ledger row): m20b 0.6370, 13r-c 0.6505, 14r-c 0.6838, M21b 0.6976, M21a 0.7133, 14r-a 0.7437, m20c 0.7440, 13r-f 0.7554, m20d 0.7576, m20e 0.7622, 13r-d 0.7627, M21b-2 0.7628, 14r-g 0.7653, 14r-b 0.7949, 14r-d 0.8479, 14r-f 0.8418, m20a 0.8827, 13r-a 0.9079, 13r-b 1.0033, M21c 1.0076 (median 0.7627, aggregate 0.7386). A $60 routine cap therefore trips at real spend anywhere from $38.22 (m20b's ratio) to $60.46 (M21c's); a $150 hard cap from $95.6 to $151.1. The 125% HARD kill lands at $47.8-$75.6 real for a $60 cap.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism behind the README's stated objection to arming enforcement ("all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0"). The trips were false positives because the estimator over-prices by a run-dependent factor, not because caps are a bad idea. Fixing the two pricing bugs in COST-03 (dedup by message.id; honour ephemeral_1h cache-write rates) would collapse the 0.637-1.008 spread and make the caps mean what they say — at which point arming enforcement would have prevented $131.15 on M21b-2 alone.

findings.title: Exactly one run breached single_run_alert_usd ($150) and the alert fired 4h58m after launch, after every dollar had already been spent
findings.evidence: $MEM/mr-budget-config.json:16 `"single_run_alert_usd": 150`. mr-native-tick.sh:96-105 computes it post-hoc at reconcile time from mr-cost-sum and, on breach, logs SPEND-ALERT and appends a handoff note ("visibility only, not a gate"). Exactly one in-window occurrence: mr-native-tick.log L2668 `2026-08-10T14:05:43Z ... SPEND-ALERT slice=M21b-2 cost=$274.3706 exceeds single_run_alert_usd=$150`. The run launched at 2026-08-10T09:08:06Z (ledger L601) and finished at 14:05:42Z (L603) — the alert post-dates the last dollar by 1 second and the first dollar by 4h58m. No COST-HELPER-FAILED or WATCHER-DEAD lines in the window. In `raw` dollars 3 runs would have breached (m20d $154.87, m20e $158.22, M21b-2 $359.71); in `final-cal` dollars 1 (M21b-2 $287.77).
findings.impact: The only cost control that actually fires is purely retrospective, and the only action it triggered was a handoff line. It did not prevent, throttle, or re-tier anything; the subsequent 3.5-day idle period was caused by the self-disable kill switch, not by this alert. A live version already exists (the WARN flag at 80% of cap, which is set and is honoured by the landing-pattern brief) — the gap is only that the 100%/125% rungs are inert.

findings.title: Cost-efficiency outliers are explained by surface breadth, not by slice size: the cheap slices touched many small files, the expensive ones ground on a few deep behavioural files
findings.evidence: $/kline (ledger cost / total churn from git show --numstat -M against each merge commit): most expensive 14r-e $53.79 (12 files/1,583 ln, client/src/prediction/*, ATTEMPTS=3 + a park/resume), 13r-f $50.06 (9/1,266, held-key warp continuation), M21b $48.37 (6/1,612, auth-kind token guard), 14r-d $41.43 (8/1,264, PvE settle hardening). Cheapest: m20b $9.09 (23/5,024, observability stack config), 13r-b $10.30 (18/5,686, trace-relay integration), M21c $13.57 (7/7,116, eval gates), 14r-f $14.71 (19/4,034), M21b-2 $18.51 (47/14,825). Whole-window aggregates: $88.49 per merged commit, $4.66 per file touched, $21.88 per 1,000 lines of churn. Composition of the 84,933 lines merged: 74.9% test/eval (63,602 ln), 19.0% prod (16,134 ln, and 6,053 of those are m20d's mr_load_driver.rs test tool), 5.7% docs, 0.5% generated. Effective $/kline of production code = $115.18.
findings.impact: The economics reward breadth and punish depth, which is the correct direction for the operator's PRIMARY priority: 75% of everything the loop produced in the window is test and eval code, and the outlier-expensive slices are exactly the ones editing netcode/prediction/auth behaviour — where careful, iterative, expensive work is what you want. The number to watch is not $/kline overall but the $115/kline of production code, which is high enough that any slice producing large prod diffs cheaply should be treated as suspect rather than efficient.

findings.title: 11 of 23 gate audits flagged in-window and all 11 adjudicated CLEAN; the adjudications are paid for out of merge-tick spend and produced the window's single most expensive tick
findings.evidence: gating_test_audit values on in-window ledger rows: 11 FLAGGED-*-adjudicated-CLEAN (m20a, m20c, m20d, m20e, 13r-c, M21b-2, 14r-a, 14r-f, 14r-g, 13r-f, 13r-b), 12 CLEAN/NA. Zero true positives. Where the flag reason is recorded it is explicitly a false positive: 14r-g "1 false-positive: import-line reflow, no real assert removed"; 14r-f "2 comment-prose false-positives: removed_or_modified_asserts=2 both doc-comment prose"; m20e (ledger L589) "1 flagged 'removed/modified assert' was a comment-text false positive (TODO comment replaced...)"; M21b-2 "70 asserts, all manifest-count bumps 15->16/12->13/14->15". The adjudication for m20c ran inside the tick at 2026-08-09T08:27:13Z, which cost $5.0285 — 3.8x the median tick and the most expensive tick of the window.
findings.impact: Confirms ground-truth item 7 with an added cost handle. The gate's precision in this window is 0/11. The dominant flag causes are lexical (comment prose, import reflow, manifest count bumps), all of which are cheaply excludable. Cost of the flag-noise is bounded by the merge ticks that carry it — on the order of $10-20 in the window — so this is a signal-quality problem (the operator's PRIMARY axis: a gate with 0% precision trains its reader to rubber-stamp) far more than a cost problem.
