gaps: I could NOT independently verify any cost figure against a source outside this harness. mr-usage-daily.jsonl reconciles to the cent with the ledger because mr-usage-snap:30-38 re-reads the same file, and ~/.claude/usage-log.csv has columns timestamp,kind,name,session,project with no cost or token fields. There is exactly one cost source in this system.

I could NOT recover true spend for 4 in-window slices whose /tmp/mr_pass_*.log files no longer exist (M21a, m20a, M21b-2, 14r-f). Their ledger values come from wrapper-reconcile rows and are unverifiable now. Two further logs were OVERWRITTEN by later reruns of the same slice name (13r-c's 2026-08-10 log now holds only the 2026-08-15 rerun at $14.4542; m20c's $114.50 first pass is gone, only the $6.26 resume survives).

I could NOT determine the true cost of `weekly-review-rev14` (ledger L604, recorded cost_usd 0.0, notes call it a "visibility-only cost-null row") or of the m20c "paid review pass (reviewer+red-team+verifier)" (L573, cost_usd 0.0). Both consumed model time that is nowhere accounted.

My token-level reconstruction deduped by message.id reproduces only ~70% of billed cost (led/dedup = 1.43 mean). The residual is unexplained and could be any mix of: real output_tokens not present in the streamed per-block usage blocks (they read 3-12 tokens/message, which is implausibly low), fable's true price differing from the configured 1.5x-opus ESTIMATE (mr-budget-config.json:45 says so explicitly), or 1h-cache pricing. I therefore did NOT claim an absolute corrected price — only the two structural bugs (per-block duplication, 5m-vs-1h cache-write rate), both of which are directly observable in the event stream.

I could NOT separate model from tier. Every $150-cap run in the window is fable@xhigh and every $60-cap run is opus@high, with zero crossover, so the 2.18x fable premium cannot be attributed to the model rather than to the surface. The quality columns that would have broken the tie are unusable: remote_red_fix_cycles is 0 on every single window row, and master_ci_after is recorded before CI concludes (9 of 17 populated values read 'pending'/'in_progress').

I did NOT quantify how much of each SUPERVISOR tick's cost is merge/audit work vs. decision work. Tick cost is a single number per tick covering standdown reasoning, gate adjudication, PR merging and ledger writing; separating them would require parsing the per-tick transcripts (/tmp/mr_native_tick_*.log), which are not retained for the window.

I did NOT measure how long enforcement was actually suspended by LOG-STALL. mr-cost-watch:81 logs only at exactly STALL==6 (2 minutes) but mr-cost-watch:94 keeps HARD enforcement suspended for as long as STALL>=6, and no line is emitted when the stall ends, so the 77 logged episodes are a count of stall onsets, not a duration.

findings.title: There is no build-ready-inventory replenishment trigger anywhere in the loop; the only response to an empty queue is a human-only kill switch
findings.evidence: grep -rniE 'replenish|inventory|queue_depth|queue-depth|build.?ready|shovel|slice_count|backlog' over $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh mr-situation mr-spawn mr-launch.sh mr-metrics mr-selfcheck mr-audit mr-record returns ZERO hits. The supervisor doctrine's only empty-queue branch is mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 — 'Nothing remains -> write DONE + disable (create $MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled and note it), exit.' The wrapper honours it at mr-native-tick.sh:124-127 with no auto-clear: `if [ -f "$MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled" ]; then if [ "${MR_FORCE:-0}" = "1" ] ... else ... log "SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: ...)"; exit 0; fi`. No threshold, no low-water mark, no alert, no auto-authored spec, no BLOCKER. The existing anti-starvation guard (consecutive_standdowns>=4 -> BLOCKER, supervisor-archive-full-prompt-2026-07-02.md:106) covers only HUMAN-session starvation and never fires here (mr-state.json consecutive_standdowns=0 after the 85h outage).
findings.impact: This is the root cause of the whole dead-time class. In the window 110 of 168 hourly cron ticks (65.5%) were no-ops on this flag (ground-truth per-day skips 11+7+18+24+24+24+2). At the measured active throughput of 0.300 slices/hour, 98.1 idle hours = roughly 29 slices of forgone throughput, ~$2,800 of forgone build work on a budget that was only 35.6% utilised.

findings.title: The 85-hour outage was NOT caused by empty build-ready inventory — 7 fully specced slices were on the shelf the whole time; ground truth #4 repeats the supervisor's own false explanation
findings.evidence: specs/monster-realm-v2/M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md was committed 45b9b6d3 at 2026-08-09T19:56:31-04:00 (= 2026-08-09T23:56Z) and `git log --follow` shows exactly ONE commit for that file — it has been byte-unchanged since. It contains 8 slices, each with a backticked `touches:` and `after:` line (spec:37,69,88,111,128,157,173,185). 13r-a, 13r-c, 13r-d, 13r-f, 13r-g all carry `after:` none. Only 13r-c was ever launched (mr-native-tick.log:2591, 2026-08-10T02:02:03Z). Then mr-native-tick.log:2623 — '2026-08-10T05:00:52Z ... DECISION standdown -- no mechanical slice launchable (M22-25 design-sketch, 13r-c-2/M21b-2 need heavy-ceremony spec scoping)' -> self-disable. At that instant 13r-a (CRITICAL), 13r-b, 13r-d, 13r-e, 13r-f, 13r-g, 13r-h plus the freshly-elaborated M21b-2 were all build-ready. The loop admitted this itself 4 days later at memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md:1564: 'slices 13r-a ... 13r-h were queued 2026-08-09 and never launched ... This is a genuine backlog gap, not a doctrine no-op — 13r-a in particular is CRITICAL and has sat unaddressed for 5 days.'
findings.impact: CRITICAL slice 13r-a (committed ops/observability stack cannot boot; 4 config defects already live-reproduced in ADR-0180's own m20e amendment with fixes left uncommitted) went 117.1 hours from build-ready (2026-08-09T23:56Z) to launch (mr-native-tick.log:3147, 2026-08-14T21:04:39Z). Diagnostic consequence: every retro that accepts 'no launchable slice' at face value will fund spec-authoring when the actual defect is queue derivation.

findings.title: mr-state.json `queue[]` is an accreted reverse-chronological narrative log, not a forward plan — 58 entries, zero forward-looking items
findings.evidence: json.load($MEM/mr-state.json)['queue'] is a list of 58 STRINGS, every one a past-tense tick summary ('2026-08-15T14:03Z native tick (rid=...): live-reverified master CI SUCCESS...'). Zero entries name a future slice, priority, or readiness state. Entries are not even chronologically ordered (indices 45-47 are 2026-07-31, indices 48-57 are 2026-08-14/15). The weekly-review SSOT states this explicitly: mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:257-258 — 'Do NOT edit `mr-state.json` (its `queue[]` is a narrative journal, not a work queue — scheduling flows through PLAN §9 order).' Priority is therefore re-derived from prose every tick: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 'else first unfinished non-`blocked:` slice per PLAN §9 order + its `M*.spec.md`', where PLAN.md §9 is a 390-line hand-maintained prose block (PLAN.md:202-591) with milestone status encoded in free text ('CLOSED 2026-07-31', 'PARTIALLY RETIRED', 'MERGED with one named partial', 'DE-GATED').
findings.impact: The forward plan exists only as prose a sonnet tick must re-read and re-interpret each hour. That is the mechanism by which PLAN-02 happened: the schema field named `queue` is decorative, so nothing mechanical could contradict the tick's wrong conclusion.

findings.title: The kill switch has no self-clearing path and blocks event ticks, while a sibling gate 20 lines below it in the same script implements exactly the pattern that would fix it
findings.evidence: gate -1 (mr-native-tick.sh:124-127): only `MR_FORCE=1` overrides; an arriving event file is moved to pending-events/ and the tick exits. gate -0.5 (mr-native-tick.sh:144-159) for `.blocked-on-human` does all three things gate -1 does not: (a) self-lifts when a named wake_file appears — `rm -f "$MEM/.blocked-on-human"; log "GATE-LIFTED wake_file present: $WAKE"` (:148); (b) has a 7-day safety expiry — 'NOTE human-gate marker >7d old — proceeding for a fresh look' (:157-158); (c) applies ONLY to `[ "$SRC" = "cron" ]` so event ticks pass through (:144). The script's own comment at :348-352 records the repeat: 'every rate-limit lockout fell through to the human-only .native-supervisor-disabled kill switch. That is what made the 2026-07-27 incident a 74h hand-cleared outage instead of a self-clearing standdown.' That fix armed the rate-limit path only and left the empty-queue path on the hard switch.
findings.impact: Same failure mode, second occurrence, 74h -> 85h. Directly measurable: the M21b-2 completion event was requeued at 2026-08-10T14:05:43Z ('SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: .../pending-events/M21b-2.done.md)', mr-native-tick.log) and sat 83.8h. Under gate -0.5 semantics (event ticks exempt) that merge would have happened within minutes.

findings.title: The only unattended supply channel (weekly review) can produce ONLY fix-up work; forward feature inventory requires an operator-attended ceremony — and the cheap channel is 4-6x cheaper per slice
findings.evidence: Weekly review runs as a Cowork scheduled task ('generate-improvement-plan') per mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7; its Phase 6 authors a spec named '`M-postgate-<review-lineage-name>.spec.md`, continuing the review-residuals naming lineage' (:249-250) — structurally residual-only. Cost attribution via mr-usage-daily.jsonl `cowork_est_usd`, which fits the review windows exactly: rows with a review in-window = $73.88 (2026-08-07, rev12 -> 6 slices), $54.00 (2026-08-10, rev13 -> 8 slices), $54.59 (2026-08-14, rev14 -> 7 slices); non-review rows = $0.96, $0.65, $1.30, $1.55, $1.29 (baseline ~$1.15). Net review cost $52.9-$72.7 -> $6.75-$12.31 per build-ready slice. Forward inventory came only from operator-attended heavy ceremony: measured at $344.15 (Aug-8, M21+M20) and $137.88 (Aug-10, M21b-2) from transcript token sums = $53.56 per build-ready slice, plus 9.2h and 4.1h of operator interactive wall-clock (session spans 2026-08-08T09:11:21Z first human turn -> 18:23:02Z /exit; 2026-08-10T05:33:04Z -> 09:05:06Z).
findings.impact: The window needed FOUR separate human-triggered supply events to cover 168 hours and still ran dry 58% of the time. Automating queue replenishment for forward milestones is the single highest-leverage change available; the review channel already proves unattended spec authoring works and is cheap.

findings.title: Spec-authoring ceremonies are entirely invisible to the ledger and the cost governor — $482.03 measured, $0.00 recorded
findings.evidence: Transcript token-sum (harness's own price table, reverse-derived and validated against mr-usage-daily.jsonl rows: opus $5/$25/$0.50/$6.25 per MTok in/out/cache-read/cache-write; sonnet $3/$15/$0.30/$3.75): session 4244d71c (parent + 71 subagent transcripts under subagents/workflows/wf_4dc55dcc-d52 [39 agents] and wf_bf13293f-ff3 [28 agents] + 3 top-level) = $344.15; session bc3f31de (parent + 17 subagents in wf_8887177b-bfc) = $137.88. Scan of monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl for 2026-08-08/09/10 non-SUPERVISOR rows shows NO row for either session; the closest are $0.00 bookkeeping rows ('issue-301-oq1-resolution', 'master-ci-fix-0179-subsystems'). The weekly review is deliberately zero: ledger line 604 — slice 'weekly-review-rev14', cost_usd 0.0, notes 'tier=review visibility-only cost-null row'. rev3..rev13 have no ledger row at all.
findings.impact: $482.03 of measured ceremony spend + ~$106 of review spend = ~$588 (24.4% of the window's true ~$2,413 spend) is outside the governor's d7 window. The governor read 35.6% utilisation while the real figure was materially higher, and — more damaging for planning — the cost of the loop's INPUT SUPPLY is unmeasurable from the SSOT, so no one can compute the runway-per-dollar ratio that would justify automating it.

findings.title: Both spec-elaboration ceremonies ran on sonnet by accidental session inheritance, while every slice they feed runs opus@high or fable@xhigh
findings.evidence: Session 4244d71c: 569 assistant messages, models Counter = {'claude-sonnet-5': 569} — 100% sonnet; its first user message is verbatim the supervisor prompt ('<!-- SSOT: this file is the single source of truth for Monster Realm supervisor logic...') at 2026-08-08T01:00:11.405Z, i.e. the operator continued a `claude --model sonnet --effort medium` cron tick (mr-native-tick.log:2227 SPAWN model=sonnet effort=medium rid=native-20260808T010010Z-3438269). Subagent spend split: sonnet $219.26 / opus $20.48 (91.5% sonnet). Session bc3f31de identical pattern: supervisor prompt at 2026-08-10T05:00:15Z, human turn 'ultracode Go ahead and begin the heavy-ceremony for spec scoping M21b-2' at 05:33:04Z, spend 100% sonnet ($137.88). Meanwhile mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:16-17 routes 'hard slice = fable@xhigh' for exactly the surfaces these specs cover ('security/RLS surfaces', 'server-module schema/reducers'), and M21a/M21b-2 were both launched fable@xhigh on that rule.
findings.impact: Against the operator's PRIMARY priority (code quality / testability / changeability), the highest-leverage artifact in the pipeline — a spec that 8 downstream opus/fable slices are built from, including the accounts/auth security surface — was authored on the cheapest tier in the fleet, not by decision but as a side effect of reusing the tick's session. The 70-agent adversarial fan-out partly compensates, but the routing doctrine has no rule for spec-authoring at all.

findings.title: M22-M25 are genuinely unauthored, not merely unformatted: 4.2KB sketches with zero slices, zero EARS, and zero real `touches:` declarations
findings.evidence: Measured per file: M22 4,169B/38 lines, M23 4,262B/38, M24 3,931B/35, M25 4,470B/41. Each has `grep -cE '^### '` = 0 (no slice headings), `grep -c SHALL` = 0 (no EARS), and `grep -c 'touches:'` = 4 — but all 4 occurrences are inside the identical boilerplate section 'Fan-out & integration note (for the slicing agent)' (M22 lines 32,34,35,36), which is generic advice, NOT a per-slice path-set. Header of each: '**Status:** design sketch (provisional)'. All four have been byte-unchanged since 2026-06-27 (49 days). Their design ADRs exist but are stubs: adr/0031 1,825B/28 lines, 0032 1,898B/28, 0033 1,793B/27, 0034 2,268B/32 — context + decision only, no implementation design (compare adr/0029 at 9,326B/107 lines, and M20's ceremony additionally produced project ADR-0180). Precedent delta measured at the window boundaries: M20 4,801B -> 75,421B (15.7x), M21 4,267B -> 68,839B (16.1x).
findings.impact: The gap is design work requiring real decisions (M22 alone needs the owner-keyed-table registry, erase-vs-anonymize policy, export format, retention windows), not reformatting. The minimum mechanically-launchable shape is cheaper than the M20/M21 precedent — the 14r spec is only 241 lines for 7 slices (~25 lines/slice: heading + `touches:` + `after:` + Tasks + EARS + Tests + Decision-hook) — so ~180 lines would unblock M22. But no automated path exists to produce even that (see PLAN-01/PLAN-13).

findings.title: The 198KB of per-slice `-plan.md` memos are session-local scratch, not planning inputs — 96% of their I/O is the writing session re-reading itself, and memo size correlates NEGATIVELY with slice cost
findings.evidence: mr-brief-template.md (36 lines, the ONLY thing a build session is launched with) never mentions `-plan.md`; it references `monster-realm-<SLICE>-progress.md` only as a PARK OUTPUT (:13). File mtimes prove they are outputs: monster-realm-13r-a-plan.md mtime 2026-08-14T22:01Z while the 13r-a session ran 21:03:44Z->22:45:29Z. Transcript scan of all 388 in-window session files for Read/Write/Edit tool_use on `monster-realm-*-plan.md`: 159 total operations, of which only 6 (3.8%) are a session reading a DIFFERENT slice's memo (M21b->M21a x2, M21c->M21a x1, m20e->m20b x2, m20e->m20d x1). Total bytes across 13r-a..h + 14r-a..g = 198,201. Correlation of memo bytes vs ledger cost over those 15 slices: Pearson r = -0.417, Spearman rho = -0.257. Extremes: largest memo 13r-a (35,721B) = cheapest slice ($35.31); smallest memo 13r-g (2,463B) = $50.86; 13r-e (3,795B memo) = most expensive at $122.90.
findings.impact: ~198KB of authored prose per two milestones with essentially no downstream reader. Plan-memo size is not a usable planning signal (it does not predict cost or outcome), and the loop's real cross-session planning artifact is the M*.spec.md, not these. Cheap to fix: either wire the memo into the resume/brief path or stop treating its size as evidence of planning rigor.

findings.title: Per-slice `after:` dependency metadata has no mechanical consumer; sequencing is re-derived by hand every tick
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'after:' mr-*.sh mr-situation mr-spawn mr-disjoint mr-metrics` returns zero hits. The weekly-review SSOT states it outright: mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:251-253 — '**`after:` metadata** capturing the real dependency chain per slice (advisory for the supervisor's planning read — no mechanical consumer today, but structured beats prose sequencing)'. mr-spawn's vars.json contract (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:109) is {slice, model, effort, adr, touches, target_desc, resume_block, tier} — no dependency field. Consequence observed live: the 2026-08-14T23:22Z handoff entry (monster-realm-handoff.md:1579) shows the supervisor manually re-deriving 'Serial chains satisfied for 13r-b (after: 13r-a, now merged) and 13r-h (after: 13r-c, now merged); 13r-e still blocked on 13r-d' by hand.
findings.impact: The one structured field that could mechanically answer 'what is launchable right now' is inert. Wiring it (spec -> ready-set) is the smallest change that would have prevented PLAN-02, since 13r-a/c/d/f/g all carry `after:` none.

findings.title: The review-residual spec format IS a good mechanically-launchable contract and it works — this is the part of the pipeline to keep and generalise
findings.evidence: Minimum launchable contract, derived from mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:109 (vars.json fields sourced from the spec) = per slice: (1) a slice ID, (2) a `touches:` path-set, (3) a target description. model/effort/tier are DERIVED mechanically from `touches:` (prompt :17 'Derive mechanically from the slice's `touches:` globs'); ADR comes from mr-state.adr_next_free. The 13r/14r specs supply all of this plus Tasks/EARS/Tests/Decision-hook in ~25 lines per slice (e.g. M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:22-49 for 14r-a). Outcome over the window's 15 review-residual slices: 15/15 merged, 14/15 at ATTEMPTS=1, one park (14r-e), zero failures attributable to spec ambiguity; audits FLAGGED-then-adjudicated-CLEAN in every case. 14r-a..g burned down in 17.5 loop-hours (2026-08-14T02:28Z launch -> 19:56Z last merge).
findings.impact: Positive: the format is not the problem and does not need redesign. The generalisation is to make the SAME format the required output of a forward-milestone elaboration pass, and to make that pass automatable.

findings.title: The Nth-review loop is a flat treadmill, not a converging feedback loop: 13 residual milestones, 85 slices, output not declining while cadence accelerates; 36.9% of window spend is fix-up
findings.evidence: Census of specs/monster-realm-v2/*review-residuals*.spec.md by `git log --diff-filter=A` add-date and `grep -cE '^### '`: 3rd 4 slices, 4th 4, 5th 4, 6th 7, 7th 8, 8th 7, 9th 7, 10th 7, pre-gate 7, 11th(2026-07-31) 9, 12th(2026-08-06) 6, 13th(2026-08-09) 8, 14th(2026-08-13) 7 = 13 milestones / 85 slices. Recent cadence 7d -> 6d -> 3d -> 4d, residual count flat at 6-9. Trigger is a Cowork cron task, not a quality signal (mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7). Window spend split from the ledger (matches ground-truth $1,824.97 exactly): residual/fix-up = 14r-a..g $477.23 + 13r-c $64.86 + 13r-a $35.31 + 12r-e $96.19 = $673.59 (36.9%); forward milestone work = M21a/b/c + M21b-2 + m20a..e = $1,071.59 (58.7%); SUPERVISOR ticks $79.79 (4.4%). Reviews are also self-reporting a recurring class rather than a shrinking one: 14r §1 names 'the recurring disclosed-but-untracked class: six ADR residuals explicitly routed "to a future slice" that never entered any queue' (M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:17-18), and 13r-a/13r-b themselves both spawned NEW undrafted residuals (D1 tempo, D3b caddy, P5-otlp — handoff:67,81,1594).
findings.impact: Roughly $1 in every $2.70 of build spend is fixing work the loop already shipped, and each review reliably manufactures ~7 more slices, so the residual queue is the loop's de facto perpetual fuel supply. That is why nobody noticed the forward-inventory bottleneck for 49 days: fix-up work masked it. Against the operator's PRIMARY quality priority the reviews are earning their keep (13r-a CRITICAL, 14r-a a 5-day-red nightly gate, 14r-b zero dynamic coverage on all four trade reducers) — but a healthy loop would show declining residual counts, and this one does not.

findings.title: The 'elaborate a sketch to a build-ready spec' capability is written into the build-loop doctrine but is structurally unreachable from the supervisor
findings.evidence: specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md:13 and :37 (mirrored at future-prompts.md:120 and :139) make it step 1 of the per-milestone procedure: 'M0–M14 are full; M15–M25 are sketches -> elaborate a sketch to a build-ready spec with full EARS criteria + tasks *before* testing it' and 'If M{N} is a sketch, **elaborate it to a build-ready spec** first', including the full 2026-07-26 SLICING FOR FAN-OUT doctrine (partition-first, contract-first slice-0, per-slice test files, `after:` metadata). The brief template's opening line points every slice run at that document. But a slice can only be launched via `/tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.vars.json` = {slice, model, effort, adr, touches, target_desc, ...} (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:109), and a sketch has no slice ID and no `touches:` to put in it. The supervisor therefore records it as out of scope by policy — ledger row 2026-08-08T01:03:32Z: 'spec-authoring is not a native-tick-assignable action per doctrine'; handoff:1002: 'A single mechanical tick authoring a full milestone spec via heavy ceremony is out of scope for gate+launch+merge+audit+record duties -- did NOT attempt it.'
findings.impact: The fix is small and does not require new capability: define a synthetic slice shape for elaboration (slice='<M>-spec', touches='specs/monster-realm-v2/<M>*.spec.md, specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md', tier=hard) so the existing mr-spawn path can launch the existing build-loop-prompt elaboration procedure unattended, exactly as the weekly review already does for residuals.

findings.title: Peak unbuilt build-ready inventory in the window was 14 slices — reached while the loop was disabled — and end-of-window runway was 3 slices, which the loop burned in 10 hours before disabling again
findings.evidence: Inventory timeline reconstructed from spec commit timestamps + mr-native-tick.log launch/merge DECISION lines. Window start 2026-08-08T04:00Z: 0 (mr-native-tick.log:2228 '2026-08-08T01:03:32Z ... no launchable slice ... loop disabled'; 8 consecutive SKIP disabled-flag lines 02:00Z-09:00Z; :2251 '10:00:11Z ... terminal DONE re-confirmed, no launchable slice, loop re-disabled'). Aug-8 ceremony commit 0724e55 (2026-08-08T09:55:30-04:00) -> +8 (M21a/b/c, m20a-e). Exhausted by 2026-08-09T15:02Z (m20e merge), self-disable #1 at 16:01Z. rev13 spec 2026-08-09T23:56Z -> +8. Self-disable #2 at 2026-08-10T05:00:52Z with 8 build-ready slices in hand. rev14 spec d4e18d5 2026-08-13T21:07:03-04:00 (= 2026-08-14T01:07Z) -> 14 unbuilt build-ready slices (13r a,b,d,e,f,g,h + 14r a-g) WHILE the loop was still disabled (skips at 00:00Z and 01:00Z; human re-enable 01:52Z). Window end 2026-08-15T03:59Z: 13r-e, 13r-g, 13r-h = 3 remaining (13r-a/b/c/d/f merged, last at 03:42:17Z). Throughput: 21 slice-merges / 69.9 active loop-hours = 0.300 slices/hour = 7.2 slices/active-day.
findings.impact: Runway at window end = 3 / 7.2 = 0.42 slice-days. Prediction confirmed: the loop consumed all 3 (plus a 13r-c re-spawn) and self-disabled 10.07 hours later at 2026-08-15T14:03:00Z (mr-native-tick.log:3393). Per-supply-event runway measured: Aug-8 ceremony 22.0 loop-hours (17:02Z Aug-8 -> 15:02Z Aug-9) for $344.15 + 9.2 operator-hours = $15.6/runway-hour; M21b-2 ceremony 5.0 hours for $137.88 = $27.6/runway-hour; rev14 review 17.5 hours for ~$53 = $3.0/runway-hour. The unattended channel is 5-9x cheaper per hour of runway than the attended one.

gaps: Weekly-review cost ($53-74 per review) is ATTRIBUTED, not directly measured. The reviews run as a Cowork/Desktop-Commander scheduled task ('generate-improvement-plan', mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7) and leave no local ~/.claude transcript — I found no session file in either project dir spanning the rev13 (2026-08-09 evening) or rev14 (2026-08-13 evening) execution windows. The figures come from mr-usage-daily.jsonl `cowork_est_usd` rows whose windows contain each review and which are 40-70x the non-review baseline. The fit is tight and consistent across three independent reviews, but it is inference from an aggregate, not a per-session token sum. Confidence MEDIUM.

I could not measure the cost of reviews rev3 through rev11 at all — mr-usage-daily.jsonl only begins carrying per-model call data around 2026-07-27, and the ledger has no review rows before rev14's deliberate $0.00 'visibility-only' row (harness issue #13).

Transcript list-price costing of the whole window totals $3,851.29 across all sessions vs $2,266.99 in the ledger for the same span (my Aug-8..15 ledger sum; the orchestrator's tighter window is $1,824.97). I did NOT reconcile these — they are different accounting bases (ledger uses the CLI's total_cost_usd per ADR-0011; mine is a token-sum at the harness's own price table) and reconciliation belongs to the cost lane. My ceremony figures ($344.15 / $137.88) are on the transcript basis and should be compared like-for-like against other transcript-derived numbers, not against ledger rows.

I cannot measure whether an UNATTENDED elaboration pass would produce a spec of equal quality to the attended heavy ceremony — there is no instance of one in the corpus. The weekly review is the only existing proof that unattended spec authoring works, and it has only ever authored residual milestones, which are derived from verified findings rather than from open design space. The M22 case (which needs genuine design decisions: erase-vs-anonymize policy, the owner-keyed-table registry shape, export format, retention windows) may legitimately need operator input; what is NOT justified is that the DECOMPOSITION of an already-decided milestone (M-postgate-client-coverage, M-postgate-roster-wave-3 — both have PLAN bullets stating exactly what to do) also requires a human.

Operator attention cost is measured only as interactive session wall-clock span (9.2h and 4.1h). I cannot distinguish time Drew was actively engaged from time the session sat idle between his 17 and 5 human turns respectively, so the true operator-hours are an upper bound.

I did not verify whether `ultracode` (the prefix on both ceremony kick-off turns) raises the effort setting above the inherited `--effort medium`. The MODEL is measured beyond doubt (569/569 and 295/295 assistant messages on claude-sonnet-5); the effort level is not.

findings.title: The 85 h halt was self-imposed on a factually false premise: the supervisor disabled itself claiming 'no mechanically-launchable slice' while 7 fully-decomposed slices (one CRITICAL) sat in the spec
findings.evidence: Creating tick: mr-native-tick.log 2026-08-10T05:00:12Z pid=1601679 SPAWN rid=native-20260810T050012Z-1601679, then '2026-08-10T05:00:52Z mr-sup-native-20260810T050052Z-1602929-429 DECISION standdown -- no mechanical slice launchable (M22-25 design-sketch, 13r-c-2/M21b-2 need heavy-ceremony spec scoping); master synced 0d13923 CI green, no locks/PRs/inflight/parked'. Proof the flag was written by that tick: the 05:00Z tick reached gate 3+ (it spawned), the 06:00:05Z tick logs 'SKIP disabled-flag' for the first time. CONTRADICTING GROUND TRUTH: specs/monster-realm-v2/M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md was committed 45b9b6d 2026-08-09T19:56:31-04:00 (= 2026-08-09T23:56:31Z), i.e. 5 h BEFORE that standdown, and carries 8 slices each with explicit `touches:` and `after:` (lines 37, 69-70, 88, 111, 128-129, 157, 173, 185-186); 13r-a is '(CRITICAL, LIGHT)' with NO `after:` line — the exact mechanically-launchable shape. PLAN.md at that commit lists it at line 463 as 'NEW, queued 2026-08-09'. The loop's own later audit agrees: memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md:1564 'M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals is NOT actually closed ... 13r-a in particular is CRITICAL and has sat unaddressed for 5 days'. The resumption DECISION line names it: 2026-08-14T21:04:39Z 'LAUNCHED 13r-a (thirteenth-review-residuals resumed after 5-day skip)'.
findings.impact: 117.1 h from spec-ready (2026-08-09T23:56:31Z) to launch (2026-08-14T21:03:53Z) for a CRITICAL slice ('observability stack cannot boot', 4 live-reproduced config defects). Three fully idle calendar days (08-11/12/13 = 24 cron skips each). Nothing external blocked progress: budget NORMAL, master CI green on 0d13923, no locks/PRs/inflight per the tick's own text. This is the single largest quality-and-throughput loss in the window and it is a work-selection defect, not an infrastructure one.

findings.title: The kill switch has zero provenance: nothing records who created it or why, and one of the two in-window creations has no logged actor at all
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.sh:124-128 only ever READS the flag ('SKIP disabled-flag'); `grep -rn 'native-supervisor-disabled'` over memory/projects/mr-* shows the only other references are reads (mr-ci-watch:9, mr-decision-watch:48). No script writes it; only the LLM (per mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 'Nothing remains -> write DONE + disable') or a human. `grep -n 'recreated .native-supervisor-disabled|Wrote DONE' mr-native-tick.log` returns ZERO hits — the creation is never logged. Second creation, 2026-08-10: the 12:00:05Z cron tick logs 'STANDDOWN live-chain: M21b-2(1771902)', which is gate 1 and therefore PROVES the flag was absent at 12:00:05Z; the 13:00:07Z tick logs 'SKIP disabled-flag', proving it was present. Between those two timestamps there is no tick, no DECISION line, no mr-state.json queue note (queue jumps from 2026-08-10T09:05Z straight to 2026-08-14T02:24Z), no handoff entry, and `find /home/mdrewt/.claude/projects -name '*.jsonl' -newermt '2026-08-10 06:00' ! -newermt '2026-08-10 12:00'` shows no session active in the harness project dir in that hour.
findings.impact: The loop's single most consequential control has no audit trail. A forensic reconstruction of an 85 h outage cannot name the actor or the reason. Because mr-ci-watch:9 also exits on the flag, arming it silently kills in-flight CI watchers too. Recovery is human-only — nothing in the tree can clear it.

findings.title: The human-activity probe was 100% false-positive in the window (72/72); 90% of trips fired on the CodeGraph daemon's own index files
findings.evidence: 72 PROBE-TRIPPED invocations in-window. Trip-file histogram: projects/monster-realm/.codegraph/codegraph.db-wal 25, projects/monster-realm/.codegraph/daemon.log 17, .codegraph/daemon.log 16, .codegraph/codegraph.db-wal 7 (=65, 90.3%, all machine-written index artifacts); projects/monster-realm/ARCHITECTURE.md 4; docs/adr/0180-observability-stack-selection.md 2; docs/adr/README.md 1. The 7 non-codegraph trips are the loop's OWN merge writes — e.g. 2026-08-14T02:00:05Z tripped on ARCHITECTURE.md 7 min after the 01:53Z tick ff-only merged PR#312, and `git show --stat 4d789bd` lists 'ARCHITECTURE.md | 32 +'. Zero human-authored writes appear anywhere in the list. The tick's own inline comment (mr-native-tick.sh:246-252) defends the missing `.codegraph` exclusion with 'The measured cost of the false trips is $0 ... the worst observed case was 15 min of merge latency' — refuted below (SCHED-06).
findings.impact: 13 of these were cron trips, which schedule NO retry (mr-native-tick.sh:263 excludes src=cron/manual), so each burned a whole hourly decision slot. Four are recorded in DECISION lines as having aborted a staged launch: 2026-08-09T04:14:07Z, 2026-08-09T08:27:05Z, 2026-08-09T11:14:45Z, 2026-08-14T05:15:35Z ('staged 14r-b launch but PROBE-TRIPPED on own write'). The loop has begun pre-emptively self-censoring: 2026-08-15T09:17:45Z 'composite launch deferred (own-write probe-trip risk, per doctrine)' cost 105 min.

findings.title: Two divergent copies of the same probe, and the loop's own merge is structurally guaranteed to trip the launch-side copy
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.sh:240-244 (gate 3) excludes .git, node_modules, target, .claude/worktrees, monster-scraper, $HARNESS/memory/* — but NOT */.codegraph/*. mr-spawn:35 excludes the same set PLUS '-not -path "*/.codegraph/*"' but narrows the memory exclusion to $MEM only. Neither excludes the monster-realm working tree, which every ff-only merge writes. Consequence, self-diagnosed 8 times in the ledger: 'PROBE-TRIPPED on docs/adr/README.md -- false positive, that write was MY OWN git merge --ff-only moments earlier, not human', 'PROBE-TRIPPED (ARCHITECTURE.md write, actually this tick's own ff-only merge, 69s old) -- aborted per doctrine, no workaround launch', 'PROBE-TRIPPED(.codegraph WAL, self-caused, no relaunch)'. mr-state.json notes carries the same: '2026-08-14T05:15Z: 14r-b launch probe-tripped on own ff-only write; vars staged at /tmp/mr_pass_14r-b.vars.json for next tick'.
findings.impact: The doctrine's blessed composite action (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:51 'One composite allowed - merge->launch') is self-defeating: performing the merge poisons the probe that gates the launch. Every merge->launch composite is a coin flip, and the loop has adapted by deferring launches an hour rather than fixing the predicate.

findings.title: 1-hour cron granularity plus one-action-per-tick is the dominant serialization cost: mean 59 min of dead wall-clock between every merge and the next launch
findings.evidence: 12 merge->next-launch transitions in-window, computed from ledger MERGED timestamps and mr-native-tick.log DECISION launch lines: 59.1, 65.6, 75.8, 48.6, 49.5, 65.3, 163.5, 50.1, 68.5, 22.1, 20.7, 20.6 min. Total 709.5 min = 11.82 h; mean and median both 59.1 min. 13 of 15 launches in the window occurred at minute :01-:04 of an hour (17:02:52, 21:03:14, 01:03:49, 05:02:01, 12:01:37, 02:02:03, 06:02:33, 12:03:00, 15:01:56, 17:03:09, 21:04:39, 02:03:00, 04:02:34) i.e. gated by the top-of-hour cron, not by an event. The one genuinely event-driven transition — 13r-a merged 2026-08-14T23:01:23Z, 13r-b+13r-f launched 23:23:32Z — took 22.1 min. Excess over that achievable baseline: 443.7 min = 7.40 h/week. Root causes visible in the DECISION lines: 5 'no launch (master CI ... unconfirmed / in_progress)' + 2 'no composite launch' + 4 'deferred to next tick' — master-CI-green has no event source unless the tick explicitly delegates mr-ci-watch, so the loop falls back to the hourly cron.
findings.impact: 7.4 h/week of pure scheduling latency, ~15% of the observed 48 h of productive build time. Against the operator's PRIMARY priority this also degrades feedback speed: a defect found by master CI waits up to 60 min for the next decision opportunity.

findings.title: The durable event queue is defeated by the kill switch: a real completion event sat unprocessed for 83.9 h
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.log: '2026-08-10T14:05:13Z COSTWATCH M21b-2 done-file present, exiting'; '2026-08-10T14:05:42Z pid=2047974 src=done SPEND-ALERT slice=M21b-2 cost=$274.3706 exceeds single_run_alert_usd=$150'; '2026-08-10T14:05:43Z pid=2047974 src=done SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: .../pending-events/M21b-2.done.md)'. The event file's own header reads 'EVENT src=done slice=M21b-2 at=2026-08-10T14:05:10Z'; its filesystem mtime is 2026-08-10 10:05:42 EDT. It was archived (i.e. consumed, mr-native-tick.sh:339) as pending-events/archive/1786672771.M21b-2.done.md = 2026-08-14T01:59:31Z, by the manual tick '2026-08-14T01:52:31Z pid=2797946 src=manual SPAWN ... events=1'. Delay = 83.90 h. Ledger confirms the merge only landed at 2026-08-14T02:26:47Z, giving a FINISHED->MERGED latency of 84.35 h against a median of 0.47 h for the other 20 slices.
findings.impact: A finished, PR-open, locally-green $274 slice (the most expensive run in the window) sat unmerged for 3.5 days. The SPEND-ALERT it triggered was written to the handoff in the same second the loop went blind, so the loop's most expensive anomaly was also its least-observed. Gate -1 requeues the event but nothing re-fires it; only a human restarted the chain.

findings.title: Ollama/Ornith is genuinely used, but the 21 GB warm-up is scheduled before every gate — 86 warm-ups fired inside the 85 h dead span
findings.evidence: USE IS REAL: mr-launch.sh:37-38 calls `mr-ollama summarize-run` and appends '--- LOCAL-MODEL SUMMARY (ornith, ADVISORY ONLY ...) ---' into each done-event; 62 of 66 archived *.done.md carry that block, 23 of them in-window; .ollama-last reads '2026-08-15T13:02:46Z summarize-run OK'. mr-launch.sh:101 also uses `mr-ollama triage` on retries. WASTE IS THE SCHEDULING: the preflight sits at mr-native-tick.sh:30-47, i.e. BEFORE gate -1 at :124, and dispatches a detached generate with keep_alive=30m on every tick. In-window: 263 warm-up lines (151 'hrbrmstr/ornith-35b-fixed', 112 'hrbrmstr/ornith-35b-fixed:latest') against 23 actual summarize-run consumptions = 11.4 warm-ups per use; 86 of them fired between 2026-08-10T13:00:07Z and 2026-08-14T01:52:22Z, a span in which no slice could ever finish and therefore no summary could ever be requested.
findings.impact: No dollar cost, but a 21 GB model is pinned resident for 30 min out of every hour on a box whose own N>=3 launch protocol requires 'free -g >~ one full build EACH' per additional slot (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:99), and mr-ollama's own header warns 'two 21GB variants swapping on a 16GB GPU = thrash' — the log shows the tag alternating between the bare and ':latest' spellings 151/112 times, which is exactly that two-variant condition. Moving the preflight below gate -1/gate 1 costs nothing and removes 86 pointless loads per outage.

findings.title: The event-retry dedup key silently degenerates to the source name, defeating the documented fix at mr-native-tick.sh:258
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.sh:262 sets EVKEY from `basename "${EVFILE:-$SRC}"`, and the comment at :258-261 says the key was moved off $SRC precisely because 'two slices finishing inside the same 7-minute window both carry SRC=done, so the old per-source key silently dropped the second one's retry'. But the retry it schedules at :265 re-execs the script with NO $1 — `MR_EVENT_SRC=${SRC} exec /bin/bash '$MEM/mr-native-tick.sh'` — so on every retry hop EVFILE is empty and EVKEY falls back to $SRC. Measured in-window: of 57 retry schedules, 17 used key=done and 10 used key=ci (the degenerate form), vs 30 that used a real per-event key. Two event probe-trips got no retry at all because the collapsed marker already existed: 2026-08-08T23:37:57Z src=done and 2026-08-14T14:05:55Z src=ci.
findings.impact: Low frequency (2 dropped retries/week) but it is a silent correctness regression against a fix the code believes it has, and each drop pushes an event to the next hourly cron (up to +60 min).

findings.title: Ledger is missing LAUNCHED rows for two fan-out slices, so ledger-only utilization forensics under-report
findings.evidence: 14r-c and 14r-e have no LAUNCHED row anywhere in monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl for their 2026-08-14T12:03Z fan-out; their first rows are 'FINISHED(EXIT=0 ATTEMPTS=3)' 13:46:50Z and 'FINISHED(EXIT=0 ATTEMPTS=1)' 13:53:03Z, both run_id=wrapper-reconcile. Additionally 32 of 150 in-window ledger rows carry 'COST-UNKNOWN (no result event; true spend unrecorded)'.
findings.impact: Recovering those two intervals moved measured build occupancy from 19.5% to 20.6% of the window and added 3.7 h of build time. Any automated duty-cycle/ROI report built on the ledger alone is wrong by that margin, and 21% of rows carry no cost at all.

findings.title: Fan-out was capped at N=2 the entire window; the cap was the binding constraint only on 2026-08-14, work-availability and mr-disjoint bound it elsewhere
findings.evidence: 7 fan-out pairs launched, N never exceeded 2 (concurrency 2 for 13.1 h = 7.8% of the window). mr-disjoint ran on every fan-out decision — 14 in-window ledger mentions, e.g. '14r-b ... disjoint-verified vs 14r-d via mr-disjoint (SAFE)' and '13r-b ... fan-out pair with 13r-f, mr-disjoint SAFE'. It also GATED two launches down to N=1: '13r-a ... 13r-d (SERIAL-REQUIRED-structural per mr-disjoint, hits evals/baselines/table-schemas.json) NOT fanned out alongside it' (2026-08-14T21:03:53Z) and '13r-d ... alone this tick (SERIAL-REQUIRED(structural) vs 13r-h per mr-disjoint -- table-schemas.json is in the always-serial structural set)' (2026-08-15T02:02:27Z). CAP-BOUND moments: at 2026-08-14T12:03Z and 17:03Z, at least 4 further slices were eligible and touches-disjoint (14r-f, 14r-g plus 13r-a..h, all decomposed in their specs). WORK-BOUND moments: 2026-08-10T09:08:47Z 'launched M21b-2 ...; no fan-out' with the handoff explaining 'roster-wave-3 ... has no drafted M*.spec.md yet; M22-25 remain design-sketch'.
findings.impact: On 2026-08-14 the cap left >=4 ready slices queued while 2 ran. Raising N to the already-Drew-approved 4 under the N>=3 protocol on that day would have compressed the 14r+13r tail; on 08-08..08-10 it would have changed nothing, because the queue was genuinely empty of decomposed work.

findings.title: Single-generation log rotation will destroy the only forensic record of the loop
findings.evidence: mr-native-tick.sh:18 — `if [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ "$(stat -c %s "$LOG")" -gt 1000000 ]; then mv "$LOG" "$LOG.1"; fi`. There is no .log.2 and no compression, so each rotation overwrites the previous generation. Current size 444319 bytes covering 2026-07-21T16:12:03Z to 2026-08-15T22:00:01Z (25 days), i.e. ~1 MB every ~56 days. This log is the ONLY record of gate decisions — mr-state.json keeps 58 queue notes, the ledger keeps outcome rows, but neither records SKIP/STANDDOWN/PROBE-TRIPPED, which is where the loop spends 82% of its ticks.
findings.impact: On the next rotation (~2026-10-10 at current rate) every gate-level forensic signal older than one generation is unrecoverable; two rotations erase everything. This entire lane's analysis would have been impossible after that point.

findings.evidence: Aggregated 208 subagent transcripts under <session>/subagents/*.jsonl with agentType from the paired .meta.json, priced per-run by the run's own model mix. tester: 37 runs, 2,389 turns, 507.0M cache-read, $377.20 ($10.19/run, median 58 turns). general-purpose: 11 runs, $134.07 ($12.19/run, median 69 turns). reviewer: 50 runs, $85.71 ($1.71/run, median 29 turns). red-team: 43 runs, $84.52 ($1.97/run, median 42 turns). planner: 21, $62.93. verifier: 17, $30.47. reducer-security-auditor 8 / $14.67; doc-keeper 9 / $11.17; desync-guard 4 / $6.77; claude 3 / $2.41; review-lens 3 / $2.25; researcher 2 / $0.92. Tool mix confirms testers do real work, not review: Read 1,141 + Edit 869 + Grep 558.
findings.impact: The cheap-per-run review roles are not the cost problem — the two implementation-heavy roles (tester, general-purpose) are 63% of subagent spend at 5–7x the per-run cost of a reviewer. If subagent cost is targeted, target tester turn-count (median 58 turns/run) and general-purpose (median 27,743-token preamble — 2.5x any other role's), not the review ceremony.

findings.title: WORKING WELL: the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet catches real merge-blockers that CI does not — this is where the money is earning quality

All work was done in a throwaway copy at /tmp/14rd/repo, where I applied the plan's exact §1 diff ... then ran the real toolchain (cargo 1.96.0, rustfmt 1.9.0, cargo nextest, node v24)'. Independent corroboration in the ledger: 2026-08-09T08:27 'm20c REVIEWED-FLAGGED — paid review pass (reviewer+red-team+verifier) on PR#304 post-CI-green: 1 HIGH (unguarded navigator reads abort main() bootstrap, main.ts:2379-2394)' — found AFTER CI was green.
findings.impact: Against the operator's PRIMARY priority this is the single best-spending part of the loop: ~$171/week (reviewer+red-team, 93 runs) buys verified, reproduced, pre-merge defect discovery on the plan — before code exists, which is the cheapest place to find it. This is emphatically NOT the same gate as the mechanical gating_test_audit that flagged ~8 of 20 merges with zero true positives; do not cut this to fix that.

findings.title: 14r-e forensics: ATTEMPTS=3 is a launcher-spawn counter, not build failures — the real retry was one park + one full resume run, and both root causes were preventable
findings.evidence: Ledger row 2026-08-14T13:46:50Z 'FINISHED(EXIT=0 ATTEMPTS=3) cost 85.1433 ... notes: mechanical backfill by tick v3 reconcile' — EXIT=0, i.e. attempt 1 succeeded at the build level. The real failure sequence is: 14:36 PARKED 'conflict+regression-suspect: PR#318 CONFLICTING vs master 9b924f3 (shared file client/src/main.wiring.test.ts with merged 14r-c); e2e 2nd distinct failure zoneSync.spec.ts:375 inside own touches (prediction/*), not blind-rerun'; 15:01 relaunched as 'RESUME of parked slice (park_counters=1)'; 16:13 MERGED PR#318 -> 4fd3c6e. Transcripts: attempt 1 = 298a8c51 (12:02–13:44 UTC, 127 turns, 9 subagents, $74.47); resume = 11537aee (15:01–15:56, 126 turns, 5 subagents, $36.19), whose edits are confined to client/e2e/zoneSync.spec.ts (x7), client/e2e/movement-input.spec.ts (x4), docs/adr/DIGEST.md. Blocker 1 root cause is CONC-01 (companion-expanded touches collision). Blocker 2 was a genuine e2e regression the loop correctly refused to blind-rerun.
findings.impact: Retry cost $36.19 measured, unrecorded in the ledger (see LEDGER-01). Blocker 1 was fully preventable by fixing the disjointness computation (CONC-01). Blocker 2 was NOT preventable and the loop handled it correctly — the supervisor explicitly declined to blind-rerun a failure inside the slice's own touches, which is exactly the right call. Also worth noting the ATTEMPTS field is misleading as a health signal: it counts spawn attempts, so a clean build with a downstream park reads as ATTEMPTS=3 while a genuinely retried build could read ATTEMPTS=1.

findings.title: The brief is consumed correctly and is not the problem — but its ALWAYS-in-scope companion clause is the mechanism behind CONC-01
findings.evidence: The rendered brief (first user message of 301bf262) is 12,610 chars ≈ 3,152 tokens — 7% of the 44,288-token preamble, so it is not a token sink. Content check: it already supplies the verified defect with file:line (battle.rs:737/:871/:905), the reference implementation (pvp.rs settle funnel, battle.rs:1443), the EARS criterion, the test strategy, the exact touches: set, the ADR number, the worktree rules, and the checkpoint/stop protocol. The session's first planner Agent prompt then restates that same defect nearly verbatim (301bf262 Agent call 1, subagent_type=planner), and the reviewer/red-team prompts restate it again — so the brief's content is re-serialized ~3x into subagent prompts rather than referenced. No instance found of the build session missing a brief instruction; the observed failures were companion-clause scope expansion (CONC-01) and main-checkout writes (ISO-01), both of which the brief states in prose but nothing enforces.
findings.impact: Do not shorten the brief — it is dense, accurate, and cheap. Two targeted changes: (1) make the companion clause machine-readable so mr-disjoint can expand it before declaring SAFE; (2) have subagent prompts reference a written plan file path rather than re-inlining the defect narrative, which would shave a slice of the 592K tokens of Agent-prompt/result traffic.

The SUBAGENT-layer prompt decomposition has 53.6% unattributed (702.3M of 1,309.7M) and should be treated as directional only. The parent decomposition is solid (20.3% slack) because its largest bucket uses exact usage.output_tokens. The subagent slack is almost certainly the chars/4 heuristic underestimating Rust/TypeScript source in Read results (true ratio nearer 2.5-3 chars/token), which would push subagent Read carry from 361.3M toward ~500M+ — but I could not verify that without a token-counting call I was not authorized to make.

I could NOT reliably measure whether individual subagent results were acted upon or discarded. My proxy (repo edits between an Agent result and the next Agent call) returns median 0 for nearly every role, but it is invalid: subagents are frequently spawned back-to-back leaving no window, and testers do their edits INSIDE the subagent (869 Edit calls) rather than in the parent. I am reporting it as a failed measurement, not a finding of waste.

I could NOT quantify how much reviewer/red-team duplication is redundant vs deliberate independent confirmation. In 14r-d both roles independently found the same OBS-2 log-ratchet blocker (~$3.68 combined) — that is by design and arguably worth it, but I have no way to separate valuable corroboration from wasted duplicate effort across all 93 runs.

I could NOT read the build sessions' system prompts directly — transcripts store only messages. The 44,288-token preamble figure is exact (measured as turn-1 context) but its INTERNAL composition (Claude Code system prompt vs MCP instruction blocks vs CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md vs tool schemas vs skill listings) is inferred from what is observable in a comparable session, not measured. The specific claim that unused MCP servers are a meaningful share of it is INFERRED, not proven.
I did not verify the 20.3% parent-decomposition slack empirically. It is consistent with chars/4 underestimating code plus per-turn message framing overhead, but I did not isolate the two.

Wall-clock idle time WITHIN sessions (agent waiting on CI, sleeps, background polls) was not separated from active work. Session spans (55–298 min) therefore overstate compute time, and I make no claims about latency efficiency.

I did not audit the 13 non-window build sessions or the pre-2026-08-08 era, so I cannot say whether any of these patterns (preamble growth, orientation share, compaction absence) are trending better or worse over time.

diagnoses.theme: QUALITY, REWORK AND THE FEEDBACK LOOPS — the quality machinery is inverted. The code this loop writes is genuinely good (pure seams extracted for testability, fail-closed defaults, honest self-labelling, proof-of-teeth discipline). What is broken is everything around it: the loop discloses its own defects in prose nothing reads, then rediscovers them 13 days later using the single most expensive detector it owns (a batched multi-lens review), while the cheap mechanical gates it runs on every merge detect nothing at all (0 true positives in 11 in-window flags, 0 in ~28 lifetime flags). 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend, 46.6% of lifetime spend, and 77.4% of the 13r/14r program went to remediating the loop's own prior output — a rework tax paid disproportionately at the premium fable@xhigh rate, inside a plan week that reached 90% real account utilization. Under the operator's corrected objective function (value per weekly credit, not duty cycle), the disclosure leak is the single largest destroyer of value per credit in the system: ~30 percentage points of a 90-point plan week bought fix-ups of work already shipped, and more than half of those fix-ups were for defects the shipping slice had already written down. The fix is not more review. It is (a) making disclosure mechanically consumable, (b) replacing a lexical assert-counting gate with a diff-scoped mutation gate that is correct by construction, (c) forbidding ratchets from being loosened, and (d) instrumenting the process so the next change to it is falsifiable — which today it is not, because the loop replaced its own measuring instrument in the same commit as its largest intervention.

root_causes.statement: The `touches:` fan-out contract manufactures debt faster than any queue absorbs it, and the only sink for that debt is free-form ADR prose with zero mechanical readers. This is the dominant root cause: 7 of 13 remediation slices (54%) exist solely to re-do work a prior slice already identified, wrote down, and declined to do because it fell outside its declared touch set.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: Root-cause taxonomy over the 15 slices in specs/monster-realm-v2/M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md and M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals.spec.md: (A) DISCLOSED-BUT-UNTRACKED = 7 (13r-a, 13r-b, 13r-f, 13r-h, 14r-d, 14r-e, 14r-f); (B) INCOMPLETE SWEEP = 3 (13r-h#2, 14r-c, 14r-f#1); (C) GATE INSUFFICIENCY = 3 (13r-c, 13r-d, 14r-b); (D) ACCEPTED-ADR-NEVER-IMPLEMENTED = 1 (13r-g); (E) OPERATIONAL BLINDNESS = 1 (14r-a); (F) genuinely new capability inside a residual milestone = 2 (13r-e, 14r-g). Leak surface measured today in projects/monster-realm/docs/adr: 109 deferral phrases (`deferred to` 60, `follow-up slice` 16, `a later slice` 11, `future slice` 10, `parked to` 10, `routed to` 2) plus 19 explicit `outside <slice>'s touches` citations, across 162 ADRs — but only 19 ADRs carry any residual heading, spelled four different ways ('Residuals / flags carried forward' 0180, 'Residuals (named, not done)' 0166, 'Residuals (recorded for the supervisor)' 0170, 'Residuals / follow-ups' 0192). `grep -rn 'after:' memory/projects/mr-*.sh mr-situation mr-spawn mr-disjoint` returns zero hits: the one structured dependency field has no consumer, and mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:251-253 says so verbatim ('no mechanical consumer today'). Smoking gun for class D: docs/adr/0165-changelog-freshness-nightly-drift-check.md:9, Status Accepted 2026-07-31, 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared `touches:`' — 11r-i merged 2026-08-02 without implementing it; actually implemented 2026-08-15 by 13r-g, 15 days after Acceptance. Reproduction proof that the remediation milestone re-emitted its own target class: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124 `const KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7;` parks seven `*-security.eval.mjs` gates to `owner: '14r-c-2'`, a slice that appears in zero file under specs/monster-realm-v2/, zero line of PLAN.md, and zero entry of memory/projects/mr-state.json (verified by scan).
root_causes.mechanism: 1. Fan-out safety requires each slice to declare a `touches:` path set, and mr-disjoint enforces disjointness on it. 2. A slice doing real work finds an adjacent defect whose fix lives outside that set. 3. The correct-by-doctrine move is to NOT touch it and write it into the ADR's Residuals prose — the slice does exactly that, honestly and in detail. 4. Nothing on earth reads that prose: not mr-situation, not mr-spawn, not the supervisor's PLAN §9 read, not mr-state.json (whose `queue[]` is 58 past-tense narrative strings, confirmed by mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:257-258 'a narrative journal, not a work queue'). 5. The residual is invisible until the next batched multi-lens review re-derives it from scratch by reading the codebase, at full review cost. 6. That review authors a residual milestone, whose slices are themselves scoped by `touches:` — so step 2 recurs inside the remediation. The loop is a debt pump with no drain.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The 7 class-A slices cost $415.38 in ledger dollars in-window (13r-a $35.31 + 13r-b $58.54 + 13r-f $63.37 + 13r-h $61.33 + 14r-d $52.36 + 14r-e $85.14 + 14r-f $59.33), plus $36.19 of unrecorded 14r-e resume spend (transcript 11537aee) — ~$452, ~25% of the window's $1,817.65 named-slice spend, entirely on defects already written down. Mean disclosure-to-remediation latency 13.1 days, median 14, max 20 (n=10 traceable items). Two items (ADR-0148 nh2 dual-bind, ADR-0152 nh5) were disclosed TWICE before being fixed.

root_causes.statement: The merge-time gate stack detects a domain disjoint from the domain in which defects actually escape. `gating_test_audit` is a lexical grep over test-path diffs plus an unconditional flag on tier=hard; it has produced 0 true positives in 11 in-window flags and 0 in ~28 lifetime flags, while the slice that shipped a 7-container observability stack in which 4 of 8 containers crash-loop merged with the record 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN'.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: memory/projects/mr-audit, gating pass: line ~51 scopes the content diff to `"*test*" "*spec*" evals ":(glob)**/*_tests.rs" ":(glob)**/*.test.ts"`; line ~54 counts any removed line matching /assert|expect\(|\.toBe|\.toEqual|panic!|prop_assert/ as `removed_or_modified_asserts`; and the verdict block reads `if a.get("tier")=="hard": g["verdict"]="FLAGGED"; g["reason"]="hard-tier: mandatory LLM diff read"` — i.e. hard tier is flagged unconditionally, which is not a detection at all. Its own in-code comment concedes the scope defect: 'NOTE: scoped to test paths only — on hard-tier flags of non-test changes this may be empty; the full diff read is still on the LLM.' In-window verdict census over the ledger: 9 CLEAN, 11 FLAGGED-then-adjudicated-CLEAN, 3 NA — precision 0/11 overall, 0/9 on discretionary flags. Documented flag causes are all lexical: '2 comment-prose false-positives ... skip_markers_added=2 both Rust .iter().skip() calls not test-skip markers', '1 false-positive: import-line reflow', '70 asserts, all manifest-count bumps 15->16/12->13/14->15'. Lifetime: no FLAG has ever survived adjudication in the 710-row ledger. Escape proof: ledger 2026-08-09T03:06:33Z, m20b — 'PR#302 squash-merged->74f2de0; mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' — the commit whose first real boot crash-looped four of eight containers (tempo bad CLI flag docker-compose.yml:110, alloy uid/cap EACCES, caddy file-capability EPERM Dockerfile:16,23, grafana 15s alert interval rules.yml:21, itemised at M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:57-76). None of those four defects touches a test file, so the gate is structurally incapable of seeing them. Blind spot in the same script: `skip_markers_added` and `suppressions_added` are computed only from the test-path-scoped diff, so an `#[allow(...)]` or `@ts-ignore` added to production source is never counted (checked in-window: no exploitation, 5 added eslint-disable lines all in generated client/src/module_bindings/*.ts).
root_causes.mechanism: The gate was designed against the threat 'an agent weakens a test to make CI green'. That threat did not materialize once in 710 ledger rows. The threats that DID materialize are: a shipped config that does not boot (class E/A), a security eval whose scanner swallows its own needle (class C), a fix applied at 3 of 32 sites (class B), and an Accepted ADR never implemented (class D). None of these is a test-file diff, so none is in the gate's detection domain. Meanwhile every FLAG mandates a supervisor full-diff read (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:39, 121-122), so a 0%-precision detector consumes the adjudicator's attention on every merge — the eleventh 'FLAGGED->CLEAN' is read less carefully than the first, so the gate is actively eroding the vigilance it exists to create, and it stamps 'mr-audit CLEAN' onto merge records as false assurance.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Direct credit cost is small and honestly so: adjudication ticks run $1.71 mean (n=7) vs $1.39 for clean merges, ~$3.5 of premium in-window, plus the $5.03 m20c adjudication tick (the window's most expensive, 3.8x median). The real cost is the escape it did not prevent: the m20b crash-loop stack required 13r-a ($35.31) + 13r-b ($58.54) = $93.85 to remediate five days later, and 13r-a was CRITICAL ('observability stack cannot boot') sitting build-ready for 117.1 hours. Seven `*-security.eval.mjs` gates covering the battle, evolution, raising, recruit, shop, trade and NPC reducer families are measurably blind RIGHT NOW, two of them proven to swallow the scan needle (evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190, reasons labelled MEASURED not asserted) — $115.97 across 13r-c and 14r-c has not closed the security-critical half.

root_causes.statement: The test substrate is source-text scanning rather than behaviour execution, so the corpus simultaneously under-protects correctness and actively penalises the changeability the operator names as PRIMARY — and the loop's only semantic ratchet was remediated by loosening it.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: 30% of server tests conservatively (192/637 `#[test]` fns bound to an `include_str!` blob), 42% on the broad measure (269/637), concentrated exactly where risk is: economy 67%, pvp 59%, ranking 57%, npc 57%, battle 49%, accounts 47%. The reason is written into the tests themselves — server-module/src/battle_tests.rs header, added by 14r-d: 'SUBSTRATE. Static source-shape scans (ADR-0185 D4 / ADR-0156 P7 — this crate has no reducer-executing harness and no TestDb).' Client side is the same shape: client/src/main.wiring.test.ts is 10,750 lines of readFileSync-and-string-match over a 2,795-line main.ts (3.85:1), and the 14r-e spec states the consequence: 'mvi-e2e parked: no test executes main.ts's frame body'. Consequence measured by the repo's own ratchet: docs/adr/0183-nightly-mutation-gate-rebaseline-and-failure-visibility.md:41-42, hosted nightly @ master 8814416 = 753 mutants, 324 missed, 377 caught, 52 unviable = 43.0% survival. The remediation raised the gate: justfile:110 `mutate-server cap="324":`, ADR-0183 Decision line 'Re-baseline the mutate-server cap 299 -> 324 ... as debt-carrying — 11 killable survivors named', and :130-136 'The ~282 survivors carried over from the 299 baseline were NOT re-triaged this episode' = 87% of the surviving population unexamined. Note the repo already owns the correct pattern elsewhere: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124 `KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7` with the comment 'EXACTLY the number of KNOWN_UNMIGRATED entries below, so the debt list can only ever shrink: adding an eleventh park requires editing this constant in the same diff, in the open.'
root_causes.mechanism: No reducer-executing harness exists, so a slice that wants to prove a reducer behaves correctly has only one available move: assert on the shape of its source text. Source-shape tests pin TEXT, not BEHAVIOUR. They therefore (a) pass on any semantic regression that preserves the text shape — which is what a surviving mutant IS, hence 43% survival; and (b) RED on any innocuous refactor, which taxes exactly the changeability the operator ranks first. Because the ratchet is a single global integer over the whole crate, a slice cannot be held responsible for its own diff — the only lever available when the number goes up is to raise the number, which is what 14r-a did. A raisable scalar is not a ratchet.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 43.0% of mutations to the server module go undetected and 87% of that population has never been classified. 14r-d spent 852 test lines to pin a 69-line production change and still cannot prove the reducer behaves correctly. In-window diff composition: 82,076 insertions of which 72.2% is test+eval and 16.7% is production source; standing repo ratio 2.79:1 test+eval to source; effective $115.18 per 1,000 lines of PRODUCTION code. The eval corpus is now 93,641 lines across 87 files and has become a maintenance surface generating its own residual milestones — 13r-c, 13r-d, 13r-g, 14r-a, 14r-c are all gate-maintenance slices, $232.34 in-window.

root_causes.statement: Review effort is placed after the fact and in batches, so the residual count is bounded by review CADENCE rather than by defect RATE. The loop is a flat treadmill, not a converging feedback loop — and the cheap inline review that DOES find real defects is not the one being scaled.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: 13 review-residual milestones, 85 slices; the last five produced 7, 9, 6, 8, 7 slices at 7d / 6d / 3d / 4d intervals — output flat while cadence accelerated. The trigger is a Cowork cron task, not a quality signal (mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7), and its Phase 6 authors a spec 'continuing the review-residuals naming lineage' (:249-250) — structurally residual-only, with no loop/process lens anywhere in its 306 lines. The 14th review names the recurrence itself: M-postgate-fourteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:17-18, 'the recurring disclosed-but-untracked class: six ADR residuals explicitly routed "to a future slice" that never entered any queue'; the 13th at :26-38 calls it 'the disclosed-but-untracked class this review process keeps producing — now in its starkest form yet'. 13r-a and 13r-b each spawned NEW undrafted residuals while remediating (handoff:67, 81, 1594). CONTRAST — the inline pre-code gauntlet works and is cheap: reviewer 50 runs $85.71 ($1.71/run), red-team 43 runs $84.52 ($1.97/run); 19 of 50 reviewer results classified BLOCKER. 14r-d's reviewer returned a 15,125-char verdict finding a merge-blocker the plan did not see (3 new bare `log::error!` in battle.rs take the file 7->10 and the grandfathered total 53->56, redding evals/observability-log-wrapper.eval.mjs:1356-1366 and server-module/src/observability_tests.rs:328, with every fix file outside `touches:`), and red-team independently reproduced it in a throwaway clone with the real toolchain. Ledger 2026-08-09T08:27 records a HIGH found by a paid review pass on PR#304 AFTER CI was green.
root_causes.mechanism: Batched-after review is a garbage collector. Its collection rate is set by how often you run it, not by how much garbage exists — so residual counts stay flat at 6-9 regardless of the upstream defect rate, and accelerating the cadence just runs the collector more often. Worse, the collector's own output is scoped by `touches:`, so it re-emits the class it collects (RC-1 step 6). Meanwhile the detector that actually has true positives — reviewer/red-team reading the PLAN before code exists, at $1.71-$1.97/run — is fired per slice and is not given the residual backlog to sweep, so it can only find defects in the slice in front of it, never the ones already written down next door.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 77.4% of the entire 13r+14r program ($770.37 of $995.60) is remediation. Mean 13.1 days from disclosure to remediation. A review costs $54-74 and yields 7-8 slices the loop burns in <24h (14r-a..g: 17.5h; 13r-a..h: 16.3h), a ~7:1 supply/demand mismatch — so the loop is structurally dependent on the treadmill for fuel, which is precisely why nobody noticed that forward inventory (M22-M25, unchanged for 49 days) had run dry.

root_causes.statement: The process cannot measure itself, so no process change is falsifiable and the improvement loop died. There is no unit-of-work denominator anywhere, the fields that would carry quality signal are dead, the orchestration CENSUS reads the wrong log, and the largest intervention in the loop's history replaced its own measuring instrument in the same commit.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: Ledger schema census over all 710 rows (python3 Counter over keys): run_id 707, slice 703, outcome 703, cost_usd 653, gating_test_audit 633, remote_red_fix_cycles 632, attempts 625, orchestration_audit 625, master_ci_after 620 — and NOT ONE field describing the size, shape, or quality of the work (no lines, no files, no EARS count, no test count, no mutants, no residuals). `remote_red_fix_cycles` is populated on 446 v3-era rows and its SUM IS ZERO. `master_ci_after` reads 'pending'/'in_progress' on 9 of 17 populated in-window rows — recorded before CI concludes. memory/projects/mr-native-tick.sh:323 greps `"subagent_type"` out of $TLOG, the SUPERVISOR TICK's own stream log, but build sessions are detached via mr-launch.sh so their Agent spawns never appear there: 159 of 162 CENSUS lines read 'agents: none', against a transcript ground truth of 208 subagent runs (reviewer 50, red-team 43, tester 37, planner 21, verifier 17, ...). CENSUS has never once recorded planner, tester, doc-keeper, reducer-security-auditor or desync-guard. Dormant instrumentation: mr-metrics (6,935 B, the 'judge-approved rollup' the retro playbook §4 mandates) has 0 tick references, 0 SSOT references, 0 log hits, 0 mentions in the 428KB handoff; mr-selfcheck has logged 0 SELFCHECK lines ever and .selfcheck-last is 0 bytes; mr-evidence and mr-retro-request were never wired; $MEM/retros/ has never been created. Zero ledger rows with slice=='SUPERVISOR' exist before the v3 cutover 2026-07-24T15:32Z because that convention was created BY the v3 change (mr-optimization-impl-spec.md:33). Loop-infra commit histogram: 45 of 51 in the four days 2026-07-24..27, last mechanism change 2026-08-01 (7df734d), then ZERO in the 14 days that contained the 5-night nightly red, the 90%-utilization plan week, and 11 false gate flags.
root_causes.mechanism: With no denominator, cost-per-slice comparisons are meaningless (era-A median $14.19 vs era-B $63.16 is confounded entirely by scope, and nothing records scope). With no quality column that ever moves, model/effort/lens-battery choices cannot be evaluated — and because routing makes model perfectly collinear with tier (tier=hard/fable n=22, tier=hard/opus n=1, tier=routine/fable n=0), the fable-vs-opus question is unanswerable from history by construction. With the instrument replaced atomically with the intervention, the v3 push can never have a before/after. So every proposed process change reduces to argument-from-plausibility, the arguments stop being worth having, and the improvement channel dies — which is exactly what the commit histogram shows.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Unmeasurable by definition, which is the finding. Observable proxy: 14 days with zero mechanism changes spanning the worst incidents in the corpus; a documented $250-400/wk routing experiment (mr-native-supervisor-README.md:60) promised for 'about 1wk' three weeks ago and never run; and an enforcement arming precondition (mr-budget-config.json `_costwatch_note`, adversarial-review condition F3) that is now satisfied 46 times over by data sitting in the log and has still never been checked.

root_causes.statement: Operator intent has exactly one consumption path — the weekly review — so answered decisions and reported feedback sit for 4-7 days, while the doctrine still advertises a feedback subsystem that has been frozen for 19 days as 'ACTIVE v1.0' and still imposes a mandatory PR field for it.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: Doctrine is explicit record-and-ignore: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81, decision answers are for 'consumer: weekly generate-improvement-plan run'. Measured latency: issue #284 answered 2026-08-08T09:02:07Z, implemented as 13r-e merged 2026-08-15T06:26:48Z = 7.0 days; issue #13 answered 2026-08-10T00:44:17Z, first weekly-review ledger row 2026-08-14T01:03:42Z = 4.0 days; issue #14 (nightly-red policy — the fix for RC-2's class-E blindness) answered 2026-08-14T12:29:12Z and still OPEN with 0 comments, recorded as still open in mr-state.json. The loop diagnosed the pattern itself: handoff:1021, 'Found 3 answered-but-unclosed DECISION issues sitting in memory/projects/decisions/ (answer transcripts captured by mr-decision-watch, never consumed by a tick)'. The capture side is sound (11/11 answers captured, zero lost). Dead ceremony still declared live: $MEM/feedback-ledger.jsonl has 189 rows, mtime 2026-07-27, zero rows since 2026-08-08, and the doctrine's own terminal states VERIFIED and SHIPPED-VERIFIED have ZERO rows in the file's entire history — yet mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:83 calls it '(ACTIVE v1.0)' on all 65 paid ticks, L105 mandates state transitions through it, and mr-brief-template.md:31 requires every PR body to carry 'Items: <feedback-ledger ids, or none>'. $MEM/retros/ has never been created despite mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:32 specifying it.
root_causes.mechanism: Routing every operator signal through a single weekly batch means the latency floor for acting on operator intent equals the review period, and the review is the most expensive consumer available. Separately, labelling provably dead machinery ACTIVE is not a token problem (the whole prompt costs ~$83/yr to carry, 0.087% of spend — do not trim it for cost) but a signal-integrity problem: once one ACTIVE label is known-false, every other ACTIVE label loses its force, and the required `Items:` PR field trains agents to fill mandatory fields with 'none' as ritual.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 7.0 days on #284, 4.0 on #13, unbounded on #14 — and #14 is the one that would have closed the 5-consecutive-night unnoticed nightly-red that cost 14r-a ($49.24) to discover. A 296-line doctrine, a 15,911-byte script (the largest mr-* tool), a per-tick check, and a mandatory PR field are all servicing a frozen 91-item dataset.

root_causes.statement: Rework is billed at premium rates and against an under-reported meter, so the remediation treadmill consumes the plan allowance roughly 1.4x faster than the loop believes it does.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: Model/tier are perfectly collinear: every $150-cap run in-window is fable@xhigh and every $60-cap run is opus@high, no crossover (mr-native-tick.log COSTWATCH `started cap=$` lines). fable n=10 mean $123.49/slice, $25.22/kline, 547 turns; opus n=11 mean $56.66/slice, $17.33/kline, 415 turns — a 2.18x per-slice premium decomposing as ~1.4x price x ~1.32x more turns. Remediation slices touching schema/reducer/security surfaces route to hard tier by rule (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:17), so the rework tax is paid in the expensive currency: 14r-b $92.17, 14r-e $85.14+$36.19 unrecorded, 14r-g $102.33 are all fable. The meter under-reports: at the operator's manual pause the real account-level `seven_day` utilization read 90% while the internal governor reported 64.7% and NORMAL — a measured 1.39x under-report — and 4 of 21 slices exceeded their own declared tier cap in real ledger dollars (M21b-2 182.9%, M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%) with `costwatch_enforce: false` and zero interventions. The ledger itself loses spend structurally: 32 of 150 in-window rows carry cost_usd=null/'COST-UNKNOWN', and $46.84 of measured resume-pass spend (14r-e $40.58, m20c $6.26) is absent because resume passes append to a log after the FINISHED row is written and are never re-summed.
root_causes.mechanism: Tier routing is a fresh judgment call, not the mechanical derivation the prompt claims (mr-tier-map.json is `_rules_frozen_2026-07-25` and covers 0 of 29 in-window slices), and it self-contradicted inside one milestone (m20b tagged routine despite 'M20 slices' being a standalone HARD criterion; 13r-c tagged routine despite touching accounts.rs plus six security evals). So the most consequential per-slice decision — which sets model, effort, lens depth and cap — is unreproducible, and it systematically sends remediation to the premium tier. Because the governor reasons in synthetic internal dollars that under-report by 1.39x, none of this is visible as pressure until the operator manually intervenes.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$611 of the window's slice spend is the fable-over-opus delta with no measurement in existence that would justify or refute it (remote_red_fix_cycles is constant zero; master_ci_after is recorded pre-conclusion). Remediation was ~34% of window spend inside a plan week that reached 90% real utilization — i.e. roughly 30 percentage points of the weekly plan allowance bought fix-ups of already-shipped work, and the week ended with the operator manually pausing the loop for 3.5 days to protect credits.

recommendations.action: Make ADR residuals machine-readable and mechanically queued. In projects/monster-realm/docs/adr/template.md add a REQUIRED bold field `**Residuals:**` whose value is either the literal `none` or one line per residual with the grammar `id=<ADR>-R<n>; sev=CRITICAL|HIGH|MED|LOW; owner=<slice-id>|UNQUEUED; evidence=<path:line>; claim=<one sentence>`. Extend projects/monster-realm/scripts/adr-digest.mjs (which already does exactly this shape of parsing via extractBoldField/required-field validation for Status, Slice and Subsystems) to (a) parse the field, (b) emit projects/monster-realm/docs/adr/RESIDUALS.md and a `residuals` array in docs/adr/design-corpus.json, and (c) raise ERROR-level issues when: the field is missing; `owner=` names a slice that does not appear in specs/monster-realm-v2/*.spec.md or PLAN.md §9; an `UNQUEUED` residual with sev>=HIGH is older than 7 days; or an ADR with Status=Accepted whose decision is implementation-bearing has no owning slice. Gate it through the existing `just adr-digest-check` (justfile:237) which already runs in CI. Then extend memory/projects/mr-situation to surface `residuals.unqueued_high` in the LIVE SITUATION bundle, and memory/projects/mr-spawn to render the residual rows that intersect the slice's `touches:` into the brief.
recommendations.rationale: RC-1 is the dominant remediation class (7 of 13 slices, 54%) and it is a pure plumbing failure: the information already exists, written honestly and in detail, in prose nothing reads. 109 deferral phrases live in a 162-ADR corpus with only 19 residual headings spelled four different ways. The exact machinery needed already exists and is already CI-gated — scripts/adr-digest.mjs validates required bold header fields today and errors on unknown Status values and out-of-vocabulary Subsystems. This is an extension of a working gate, not a new subsystem. It also closes class D (ADR-0165 Accepted 2026-07-31, implemented 2026-08-15) by making 'Accepted with no owning slice' a build error.
recommendations.expected_effect: Targets $415-452 of in-window spend (25% of named-slice spend) and collapses the measured 13.1-day mean disclosure-to-remediation latency toward one tick, because an UNQUEUED HIGH residual becomes visible in the supervisor's own situation bundle instead of waiting for the next batched review. Immediate concrete catch on day one: `14r-c-2` (seven blind *-security.eval.mjs gates, two proven to swallow their own scan needle) currently exists only inside evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs and in no queue anywhere — the owner-existence check REDs on it.
recommendations.risk: Authors satisfy the field with `none` and keep deferring in prose. Mitigate by adding one line to the per-slice reviewer subagent's charter (memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md): cross-check the diff and ADR body for defer/park/'outside touches' phrases against the Residuals field and treat an unlisted deferral as a BLOCKER. The reviewer already reads the plan and already produces BLOCKER verdicts (19 of 50 in-window), so this is a scope addition to a working detector, not a new one.

recommendations.action: Delete the assert-count / skip-marker / suppression greps and the unconditional hard-tier flag from the gating pass of memory/projects/mr-audit, and replace them with a diff-scoped mutation gate. Add a `mutate-diff base head` recipe to projects/monster-realm/justfile that runs `git diff base..head > /tmp/pr.diff && cargo mutants -p monster-realm-module -D /tmp/pr.diff --test-tool nextest --timeout <bound>` (verified available: `cargo mutants --help` in this repo lists `-D, --in-diff <IN_DIFF>`). mr-audit FLAGS only when a mutant on a line the PR itself added or changed survives, and reports the surviving mutants as the evidence payload instead of diff hunks.
