Keep exactly one of the old greps and move it OUT of the test-path scope: `deleted_test_files` plus suppressions added to PRODUCTION source (the current scoping bug means `#[allow(...)]` in server-module/src is invisible). Retain `orchestration_audit` unchanged but demote it from merge gate to telemetry field — it reads the correct log (the build session's, via a['log']) and its role-presence check is accurate (12 agent calls verified against transcript 301bf262), but it is a did-the-protocol-run probe, not a defect detector.
recommendations.rationale: 0 true positives in 11 in-window flags and 0 in ~28 lifetime flags, with a detection domain (test-file diffs) provably disjoint from the escape domain (config that will not boot, blind scanners, incomplete sweeps, unimplemented ADRs). Two of the 11 flags were the unconditional tier=hard branch, which is not a detection at all. A survived mutant on a line the PR added is by construction an untested change, so the replacement's positives are correct by construction rather than by lexical guess — and it is the only gate that can see RC-3's real failure mode (a test that was added but pins text rather than behaviour).
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes ~11 supervisor full-diff adjudications per week whose measured yield is zero, ending the rubber-stamp erosion (the $5.03 m20c adjudication was the window's most expensive tick, 3.8x median). Replaces them with a signal whose false-positive rate on the class 'this change is not covered by an executing test' is structurally near zero. Honest scope limit: it does NOT cover class A (R1's job) or class E (R9's job), and it covers only Rust; the TypeScript side is handled by R5's TEETH standard.
recommendations.risk: cargo-mutants on a diff can exceed a merge-tick's patience on large PRs. Bound it: run only when the diff touches server-module/src/*.rs, cap with `--timeout`, and on timeout downgrade to AUDIT-DEFERRED and key the run to the merge SHA in the nightly job so the NEXT merge inherits the verdict. This is strictly better than today, where the answer is always CLEAN-or-noise.

recommendations.action: Make nightly red page, and make the supervisor prioritize it. In projects/monster-realm/.github/workflows/nightly.yml add a failure step that creates-or-comments a single deduplicated GitHub issue labelled `nightly-red` carrying the failing job name and the run URL (ADR-0183 §D5 explicitly records 'No issue-creating Action, webhook, or notification step was added', blocked on mdrewt/claude-harness#14 which is still OPEN with 0 comments). In memory/projects/mr-situation, surface `open_nightly_red_issues` in the LIVE SITUATION bundle, and in memory/projects/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md make an open `nightly-red` issue rank ABOVE launching any new slice in the gate-3 work-priority ordering.
recommendations.rationale: Class E, and the cheapest high-value item in this report. mutation-server was RED five consecutive nights (2026-08-09..08-13, runs 31302216601 / 31370098105 / 31471975160 / 31577652043 / 31681643275) with the other three nightly jobs green every single time — maximally diagnosable and still unnoticed. Detection came from the fourteenth human-instigated multi-lens review, i.e. the most expensive detector in the system, applied to a signal that was already sitting in a green/red boolean. Four of those nights fell inside the operator's credit-protection pause, so the loop's only semantic quality gate was failing while the loop was deliberately asleep.
recommendations.expected_effect: Moves detection latency for the only semantic quality ratchet from a measured 5 days (and structurally up to one review cycle, mean 13.1 days) to the next tick. Removes the discovery half of 14r-a's $49.24, and removes ~775 minutes of nightly CI wall-clock spent producing an ignored signal. Costs approximately zero credits: the paging step is a GitHub Action, and the supervisor read is a field in a bundle it already loads.
recommendations.risk: Issue spam if the same failure recurs nightly. Dedupe on a stable title key and comment rather than re-create; auto-close on the first green nightly.

recommendations.action: Convert the mutation ratchet from a raisable scalar into a shrink-only named-debt set. In projects/monster-realm/justfile:110 replace `mutate-server cap="324"` with two independent gates: (a) a frozen allowlist file (generated mechanically from the nightly's own missed.txt) enumerating each carried survivor by file+function+mutant, with an exact-count constant in evals/nightly-smoke-wiring.eval.mjs (which already asserts the cap equals MUTATE_SERVER_CAP_BASELINE) so the list can only ever shrink and adding an entry requires editing the constant in the open; and (b) zero tolerance for any survivor NOT on that list — which, combined with R2's `--in-diff` gate, makes each slice responsible for exactly its own diff. Amend ADR-0050 and ADR-0183 to record that cap-raising is no longer an available remediation.
recommendations.rationale: 14r-a's re-baseline 299 -> 324 was an honest, rigorous ADR that reached the wrong outcome: the response to a failing ratchet was to move the ratchet, certifying that 43.0% of server mutations go undetected with 87% of that population (282 of 324) never triaged. The repo already invented the correct pattern and uses it successfully one directory over — evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124 `KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7` with 'the debt list can only ever shrink: adding an eleventh park requires editing this constant in the same diff, in the open', and each entry self-retires (the gate REDs demanding deletion once a file is migrated). This is not a new idea to import; it is an existing internal exemplar applied to the gate that most needs it.
recommendations.expected_effect: Makes the 43% survival figure permanently visible and structurally non-raisable, and converts an unachievable whole-crate obligation into an achievable per-diff one. Directly enables the successor ratchet ADR-0183 already names (<=313) instead of leaving it as prose. Removes the failure mode where a red ratchet is remediated by loosening it — which is the highest-severity quality-machinery regression in the window.
recommendations.risk: Generating and maintaining a 324-entry allowlist is real work and will churn on refactors. Generate it from the nightly's own missed.txt artifact rather than by hand, key entries on function+mutant text rather than line numbers (line-drift is a known trap in this repo's mutation work), and accept that a refactor may require a regeneration commit — that is the correct cost, and it is bounded.

recommendations.action: Make 'real teeth' mechanically checkable instead of a supervisor judgment call. Require every gate file under projects/monster-realm/evals/ to export a `TEETH` array of `{ name, badFixture, expect: 'REJECT' }`, and extend projects/monster-realm/evals/run.mjs to execute each bad fixture through the gate and assert it FAILS. Add evals/teeth-audit.eval.mjs which REDs when any *.eval.mjs exports zero TEETH entries, or when any TEETH bad fixture passes. This promotes an existing repo doctrine to a mechanism: evals/observability-stack-config.eval.mjs:6-11 already states 'PROOF-OF-TEETH over inline fixtures. Every detector below is first shown to REJECT the shape it exists to catch. A gate that has never failed is a decoration.' Pair it with a standards/ entry stating the rule for tests: a test counts only if it has been observed RED against the unfixed code, and a count/manifest assertion counts only if it is BIDIRECTIONAL (driven from a static import of the domain, asserting equality in both directions).
recommendations.rationale: This is the direct answer to 'are in-window tests real teeth or manifest-count bumps'. The measured answer is: mostly real, but the loop cannot prove it and the audit that tried got it backwards. The gating_test_audit dismissed 70 asserts as 'all manifest-count bumps 15->16/12->13/14->15' — yet client/src/main.wiring.test.ts:5181-5212 drives the loop domain from a STATIC import of OVERLAY_IDS and asserts count equality in BOTH directions ('A higher count means a 16th entry was smuggled in'), which is genuinely load-bearing. Simultaneously, seven *-security.eval.mjs gates are measurably blind right now and two are proven to swallow their own needle. Counting assertions cannot distinguish these cases; executing a bad fixture through the gate can, and does so for exactly the class that escaped (class C, 3 of 13 remediation slices).
recommendations.expected_effect: Turns 'did this slice add real teeth?' from a paid LLM diff read producing 0/11 useful verdicts into a build-time boolean. Would have caught the ADR-0181 blind-scanner class at the moment each gate was written rather than across three slices and $115.97 (13r-c + 14r-c) with the security-critical half still open. Also gives R2's TypeScript-side gap a real answer without importing a mutation framework.
recommendations.risk: Retrofitting TEETH onto 87 existing eval files is a large mechanical diff. Phase it: require TEETH on NEW and MODIFIED gate files immediately (enforced against the PR diff), and carry the existing corpus as a shrink-only named-debt list using the same R4 pattern.

recommendations.action: Move review effort from batched-after to inline-at-plan, and re-scope the batch. Three concrete edits: (1) memory/projects/mr-spawn — render into every brief the RESIDUALS.md rows (from R1) whose `evidence=` path intersects the slice's declared `touches:`, under a new heading 'RESIDUALS IN YOUR BLAST RADIUS — fix in scope, or restate with an owner'. (2) memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md — add to the reviewer/red-team charter: sweep those rows, and treat any deferral in the diff or ADR that is absent from the Residuals field as a BLOCKER. (3) memory/projects/mr-weekly-review-prompt.md — narrow Phase 6 from 'find everything' to 'audit the residual backlog for completeness, severity and staleness, and author a milestone ONLY from UNQUEUED HIGH/CRITICAL rows', and change its trigger from fixed cron to a threshold (open UNQUEUED HIGH count, or oldest UNQUEUED CRITICAL age).
recommendations.rationale: The measured evidence says review is mis-placed in TIME, not mis-sized. The inline pre-code gauntlet has real, reproduced true positives at $1.71-$1.97 per run (14r-d's OBS-2 log-ratchet blocker, found before code existed and independently reproduced by red-team in a throwaway clone with the real toolchain; m20c's HIGH found after CI was green). The batched multi-lens review has true positives too but finds them a mean of 13.1 days after they were disclosed, and its output is bounded by its cadence rather than by the defect rate — 13 milestones, 85 slices, output flat at 6-9 while cadence accelerated 7d->6d->3d->4d. A defect-paced trigger is the mechanism that turns a treadmill into a converging loop.
recommendations.expected_effect: Converts residual generation from cron-paced to defect-paced, which is the only change that makes the residual count capable of converging. Attacks the 13.1-day mean latency at the point of disclosure. Reuses a detector already proven to work rather than funding a new one, so the marginal credit cost is a scope addition to the ~93 reviewer/red-team runs already being paid for (~$171/week total).
recommendations.risk: Overloading the per-slice reviewer degrades its focus on the slice in front of it. Bound the sweep to residuals whose evidence path intersects the declared touches (typically 0-3 rows), not the whole backlog.

recommendations.action: Instrument the process so the next change to it is falsifiable. Extend memory/projects/mr-record's schema to write, at merge, per slice: `plan_ready_ts` (spec commit ts), `launch_ts`, `finished_ts`, `merged_ts`, `attempts`, `parks`, `prod_lines_added/deleted`, `test_lines`, `eval_lines`, `files_touched`, `touches_declared_n`, `touches_actual_n`, `mutants_survived_on_diff` (from R2), `teeth_entries_added` (from R5), `residuals_emitted_n` / `residuals_closed_n` (from R1), `review_blockers_found_precode`, `ci_reds_postmerge`, `flake_reruns`, and — per the operator's corrected cost model — `seven_day_utilization_at_launch` and `_at_finish` parsed from the run log's rate_limit_info objects and PERSISTED out of /tmp. Wire the already-written-but-orphaned memory/projects/mr-metrics (6,935 B, zero call sites anywhere) to emit a weekly memory/projects/mr-process-report-<week>.md carrying exactly six standing numbers: value per utilization point (prod lines + TEETH-bearing evals per plan-percent consumed), remediation share of spend, residual inflow vs outflow, gate precision (flags raised vs flags surviving adjudication), post-merge escape rate, and mean disclosure-to-remediation latency. Adopt one standing rule in memory/projects/mr-native-supervisor-README.md: land the counter one cycle BEFORE the change it is meant to measure.
recommendations.rationale: Every recommendation above is unverifiable without this, and the loop has already proved it will not self-correct blind: 45 of 51 loop-infra commits landed in four days, then zero mechanism changes across the 14 days containing the 5-night nightly red, the 90%-utilization plan week, and 11 false gate flags. The ledger today carries 653 cost values and not one field describing the size, shape or quality of the work; `remote_red_fix_cycles` sums to exactly 0 across 446 rows; `master_ci_after` reads 'pending' on 9 of 17 populated rows; and the v3 intervention can never have a before/after because it created the SUPERVISOR row convention in the same commit as the change it was supposed to measure. `touches_declared_n` vs `touches_actual_n` in particular is a single cheap number that is the leading indicator for BOTH the disjointness failures and the residual leak.
recommendations.expected_effect: Makes 'did change X help?' answerable for the first time. Concretely: R1's effect shows up as residual inflow/outflow crossing; R2's as gate precision moving off 0/11; R4's as mutants_survived_on_diff; R6's as disclosure-to-remediation latency falling from 13.1 days. Also gives the operator the one number the corrected objective function actually needs — durable output per percentage point of the weekly plan allowance — instead of a synthetic internal dollar that under-reports real consumption by a measured 1.39x.
recommendations.risk: Metric theatre: fields recorded and never read. Mitigate by making the weekly report exactly six numbers with a stated decision attached to each, and by deleting any field that goes three weeks without appearing in the report (apply that rule to `remote_red_fix_cycles` immediately — it has never been non-zero).

recommendations.action: Require a repo-wide census with an exact-count cap for any fix that applies a pattern at a site. Add to /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/standards/ a short rule: when a slice fixes a defect of the form 'apply pattern P at site S', it must ship (a) a repo-wide census of every occurrence of P, and (b) an exact-count constant over the unfixed remainder, in the shape evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs already uses (`MIGRATED_FLOOR`, `KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP` equal to the list length, each entry validated to still fail so the gate REDs when one is silently fixed). Reference that file as the normative exemplar. Enforce via the R1 Residuals field: the unfixed remainder is a residual with a real owner.
recommendations.rationale: Class B, 3 of 13 remediation slices: 14r-c fixed 3 of ~32 scanner-migration sites and left 29; 14r-f#1 applied the same fix 12r-d had applied to battle/npc/pvp/content but not evolution; 13r-h#2 re-applied a fix ADR-0179 had already made in pvp_tests.rs for the identical bug class. Every one of these is 'the fix was correct and the sweep was not', and none of them is detectable by any current gate. The correct mechanism already exists in this repo and is the single best-designed quality artifact in it — it is simply not a required practice.
recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates a class worth 3 of 13 remediation slices (14r-c $36.66 + 14r-f $59.33 + 13r-h $61.33 = $157.32 in-window, plus their share of review-cycle cost). Turns an invisible partial fix into a visible, shrink-only debt list at the moment the fix is made, which is when the census is cheapest — the slice already has the pattern in its head.
recommendations.risk: Census cost on very broad patterns. Cap the obligation: if the census exceeds a threshold, the residual row is `sev=HIGH; owner=UNQUEUED` and R1's staleness gate forces it into a queue, rather than requiring the slice to fix everything.

recommendations.action: Expand declared touches by the brief's own companion rules before mr-disjoint renders a verdict. In memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md, make the ALWAYS-in-scope companion clause machine-readable (currently prose: 'sibling test files of any declared code file (e.g. *.test.ts next to a declared .ts)' plus 'docs/adr/**, docs/knowledge/**, CHANGELOG.md, ARCHITECTURE.md'). In memory/projects/mr-disjoint, expand each slice's path list by those rules before computing overlap, and add the always-granted doc set (ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/adr/DIGEST.md) to a new KNOWN_SHARED axis whose verdict is 'EXPECT-CONFLICT: rebase-on-merge' rather than SAFE — since every concurrent slice is granted it, any two are guaranteed to collide there.
recommendations.rationale: mr-disjoint is structurally sound (its header correctly states it is necessary-not-sufficient and may never override toward parallel) but it operates on DECLARED touches while the brief silently grants companions, so it declares SAFE on pairs that are guaranteed to conflict. Measured in-window: 14r-c and 14r-e both edited client/src/main.wiring.test.ts (a *.test.ts sibling of 14r-e's declared client/src/main.ts) after a SAFE verdict, and the park memo says it plainly — '14r-c's fan-out disjointness held on paper, not in practice'. 14r-b's PR#317 conflicted on exactly the clause-(b) doc set (ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md).
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes 3 of ~20 in-window merge conflicts (m20d, 14r-b, 14r-e). Directly recovers 14r-e's $36.19 resume session plus a PARK tick, a relaunch tick and a supervisor adjudication. Also removes a source of ATTEMPTS>1 noise — note the ground-truth correction here: three in-window slices had ATTEMPTS>1 (14r-e=3, 13r-f=3, 13r-b=2), not one.
recommendations.risk: Over-serialization if the doc axis forces N=1. Avoid by treating the doc set as rebase-on-merge rather than as a serialization trigger — the conflicts there are mechanical and auto-resolvable, unlike source conflicts.

recommendations.action: Consume answered operator decisions at the next tick instead of the next weekly review. In memory/projects/mr-decision-watch, on capturing an answer, additionally write a pending-event file so the tick's existing durable event queue picks it up. In memory/projects/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81, replace the 'record-and-ignore -- consumer: weekly generate-improvement-plan run' doctrine with: an answered decision must, within one tick, either launch, or be written into the spec corpus as a slice with a `touches:` set, or be recorded as a Residuals row (R1) with an owner and a severity. Add an open-decisions count to the mr-situation bundle.
recommendations.rationale: The capture side is flawless (11/11 answers captured, zero lost) and the close-the-loop hygiene added after the #11/#12 incident works. The consumption side is the defect: #284 answered 2026-08-08 and implemented 7.0 days later; #13 answered 2026-08-10, consumed 4.0 days later; #14 answered 2026-08-14 and still open — and #14 is the nightly-red policy that would have closed the class-E blindness. The loop diagnosed this itself in its own handoff ('answer transcripts captured by mr-decision-watch, never consumed by a tick') and did not fix it, because the improvement channel was already dead (RC-5).
recommendations.expected_effect: Cuts operator-intent latency from a measured 4-7 days to one tick. Cheapest possible fix for the operator's steering axis: it reuses the existing pending-events bridge, which is the one part of the scheduler that is genuinely sound (37 events archived in-window, every one eventually consumed, zero lost to contention).
recommendations.risk: A tick acting on a decision it only partially understands. Bound it: the tick's permitted actions are launch / write-a-slice / file-a-residual — never a design change; anything else stays a BLOCKER.

recommendations.action: Add a flake registry with a three-strike auto-queue. Create projects/monster-realm/evals/baselines/known-flakes.json recording {spec, symptom, first_seen, occurrences, owner}. In memory/projects/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md, require the supervisor to increment the entry whenever it classifies a red as 'unrelated flake', and on the third occurrence to emit a Residuals row (R1) with sev=HIGH and a real owner rather than another rerun.
recommendations.rationale: wallet-balance.spec.ts flaked four times in seven days — the ledger note for the fourth literally reads 'flake pattern match: wallet-balance.spec.ts quest_001/elder_oak dialogue precondition, 4th occurrence, unrelated to 14r-c touches'. It was diagnosed four separate times, by four separate paid ticks, and never queued. ranked-forfeit.spec.ts, dialogue.spec.ts and zoneSync.spec.ts each flaked twice; 9 of 138 in-window ledger rows (6.5%) are flake/rerun handling. The corrosive cost is not the reruns: it is that the loop is being trained to classify red CI as 'unrelated flake' by pattern-match, which is precisely the mechanism by which a real regression gets waved through. (The loop's counter-example is instructive and worth preserving: 14r-e's supervisor explicitly REFUSED to blind-rerun a failure inside the slice's own touches — that is the correct instinct and the registry should not weaken it.)
recommendations.expected_effect: Converts a recurring per-occurrence tax (~$1.33 supervisor tick + a CI rerun + occasionally a PARK, four times for one spec) into a one-time fix, and removes the 'unrelated flake' classification from being a free action. Also gives R7's escape-rate metric a denominator it can trust.
recommendations.risk: The registry becomes a permission slip to ignore reds. Mitigate by making entries expire: an entry untouched for 14 days is deleted, forcing re-diagnosis rather than permanent amnesty.

recommendations.action: Wire the load driver the loop already built to a committed baseline. projects/monster-realm/sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs (6,053 lines, delivered by m20d for $117.33, 187 inline tests) performed a one-off OBS-27 breaking-point measurement recorded only in an ADR-0180 amendment and is wired into no gate and no baseline. Add a baseline file under projects/monster-realm/evals/baselines/ carrying reducer-latency and subscription-payload figures from that driver, and a nightly job in .github/workflows/nightly.yml that re-runs it and REDs on an order-of-magnitude regression, on the same policy footing as the mutation job.
recommendations.rationale: Performance is named PRIMARY by the operator, and the only performance gate in existence is game-core/benches/budgets.rs — seven nanosecond-scale pure functions whose ceilings are, by their own comment at :11-13, '~20x the locally measured mean ... the gate catches order-of-magnitude regressions, not 5% drift'. A 19x regression on any hot path passes GREEN, and nothing anywhere measures reducer execution, subscription fan-out or client frame budget — the three places a multiplayer game actually gets slow. The instrument to measure the real thing was built and paid for and then not connected. Its gate placement is itself a `touches:` workaround (justfile:35-39 explains perf-budget sits inside `eval:` rather than as a `ci:` dependency because ci.yml was outside m20a's touches) — a class-A residual in the perf gate's own wiring.
recommendations.expected_effect: Gives the operator's stated PRIMARY axis its first real detector, and recovers the value of an already-sunk $117.33. Turns a one-off number recorded in ADR prose into a ratchet — which, per R4, must be shrink-only.
recommendations.risk: Load-driver runs are noisy and long. Run nightly only, use generous order-of-magnitude ceilings initially (same philosophy as budgets.rs, which is defensible for a first gate), and tighten only when R7's data shows the noise band.

recommendations.action: Delete provably dead ceremony so that 'ACTIVE' means something. Remove from memory/projects/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md the four feedback blocks (L31, L34, L83's '(ACTIVE v1.0)' claim, L105's state-transition mandate) and the retro block (L32); remove the mandatory `Items: <feedback-ledger ids, or none>` field from memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md:31; and delete or move under a dated DORMANT heading the scripts memory/projects/mr-feedback (15,911 B, the largest mr-* tool), mr-retro-request, mr-evidence and mr-selfcheck. Separately delete the CENSUS block at memory/projects/mr-native-tick.sh:323 outright — it greps the supervisor tick's own log for build-session subagents that are never there.
recommendations.rationale: $MEM/feedback-ledger.jsonl has 189 rows, mtime 2026-07-27, zero rows since, and the doctrine's own terminal states VERIFIED and SHIPPED-VERIFIED have ZERO rows in the file's entire history — while the prompt calls it 'ACTIVE v1.0' on all 65 paid ticks and the prompt text itself admits the failure ('first-cycle gap 2026-07-27: items sat DISPOSED while slices ran'). $MEM/retros/ has never been created. mr-selfcheck has logged zero SELFCHECK lines ever. CENSUS reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines against a transcript ground truth of 208 subagent runs. State the cost honestly: this is NOT a token saving — the whole 33KB prompt costs roughly $83/yr to carry, 0.087% of spend, and trimming it for tokens would be indefensible. The justification is signal integrity: once one ACTIVE label is known-false, every other ACTIVE label loses its force, and a log line that reads like evidence but is structurally always wrong is worse than no line. Do NOT touch mr-audit's orchestration pass while doing this — it reads the correct log and its role-presence numbers are accurate.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes a required PR field nobody can fill honestly, removes 162 log lines that read like evidence and are not, and restores the meaning of ACTIVE for the doctrine that remains. Prerequisite for R7 being believed: a process report is worthless in a document whose labels are known to lie.
recommendations.risk: Deleting something that was about to be revived. Mitigate by moving rather than deleting the scripts, under a dated DORMANT heading with the measured evidence of dormancy recorded alongside — the same honesty the ADR corpus already practises.

recommendations.action: Fix the human-activity probe's predicate and correct its in-line justification. In memory/projects/mr-native-tick.sh:240-244 add `-not -path '*/.codegraph/*'` (unifying toward mr-spawn:35, which already has it) and exclude paths written by the loop's own most recent ff-only merge by comparing mtime against the merge commit's timestamp. Replace the defending comment at :246-252, which currently reads 'The measured cost of the false trips is $0 ... the worst observed case was 15 min of merge latency'.
recommendations.rationale: 72 of 72 in-window trips were false positives; 65 (90%) named machine-written CodeGraph index artifacts (codegraph.db-wal 25+7, daemon.log 17+16) and the remaining 7 were the loop's own merge writes (e.g. a trip on ARCHITECTURE.md 7 minutes after the tick ff-only merged PR#312, whose --stat shows 'ARCHITECTURE.md | 32 +'). Zero human-authored writes appear anywhere in the list. Be blunt about why this matters more than its size: the in-line comment is a documented instance of the loop measuring the wrong axis ($0 of spend) and then citing that measurement as a settled decision under ADR-0011 — the same error pattern as the doctrine discarding the rate_limit_info utilization gauge because it was only ever read as a binary trip-wire. Under the operator's corrected objective function the latency cost is genuinely near-zero, so this is a LOW-priority item; the reason to fix it is that the loop has begun pre-emptively self-censoring its own blessed composite merge->launch action ('composite launch deferred (own-write probe-trip risk, per doctrine)'), which costs a paid tick to redo the reconciliation.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes ~60 false trips/week and the 4 in-window DECISION lines recording aborted staged launches. Restores the merge->launch composite, saving one supervisor tick (~$1.33) per occurrence. Small, honest, and explicitly ranked last on value-per-credit — do not fund this ahead of R1-R5.
recommendations.risk: Excluding .codegraph removes the only accidental backstop for human edits made inside a worktree, which is the stated reason it was kept. Compensating control: the IDE-session probe at the same gate (`--replay-user-messages`) already covers an attended human session, and worktrees are agent-owned by design per the 2026-07-24 retro.

recommendations.action: Explicitly protect three things from being cut to pay for the above. (1) The per-slice pre-code reviewer/red-team gauntlet in memory/projects/mr-brief-template.md — 93 runs, $171/week, 19 of 50 reviewer results BLOCKER-classified, with reproduced verdicts. (2) The proof-of-teeth and 'MUST start RED' discipline in the residual specs (M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:263-266, 'a green-from-the-start test there means the fix was not actually applied'). (3) The ADR corpus as load-bearing navigation — 143 distinct ADRs cited 3,729 times in production source, at decision granularity ('ADR-0189 D6', 'ADR-0185 D1'), 14 of 15 in-window ADRs referenced in code.
recommendations.rationale: The most likely failure mode of this report is that 'the gate found nothing, cut review' becomes the takeaway. That would be exactly wrong. The mechanical gating_test_audit (0/11) and the LLM pre-code gauntlet (real, reproduced blockers) are different things that happen to both be called review, and only the first is ceremony. Likewise the code quality itself is genuinely high against the operator's PRIMARY bar — 14r-g extracting `issuers_configured` and `ranked_account_gate` as PURE functions with the rationale written down ('reducer bodies are not' exhaustively unit-testable), 13r-f's `snapshot()`/`restore()` seam expressing its contract as an identity law, 14r-f labelling its own change 'DEFENSIVE hygiene, not a reachable-bug fix'. Per-diff craftsmanship is not the problem and must not be traded away to fix the process layer.
recommendations.expected_effect: Preserves the ~$171/week of spend with the highest demonstrated defect yield in the system, and preserves the two disciplines (proof-of-teeth, ADR-as-anchor) that R1, R4 and R5 all build directly on top of. Cutting any of the three would make the rest of this plan unimplementable.
recommendations.risk: None from keeping. The risk is in NOT stating it: an efficiency pass reading only the 0/11 precision number would plausibly cut the wrong review.

diagnoses.theme:
COST EFFICIENCY AND THE ECONOMICS OF THE LOOP — the loop bills itself in a currency that does not exist, spends 99.8% of its money re-reading context it already has, and buys its parallelism with rework.

HEADLINE UNIT ECONOMICS (window 2026-08-08..08-14, corrected):
- $1,904.45 ledger (EDT window) / $1,824.97 (UTC days) + at least $46.84 of unrecorded resume-pass spend + ~$482 of unledgered spec-ceremony + ~$54 of weekly review => true window spend >= ~$2,430.
- Per merged commit $88.49 (ledger) / ~$53.50 (transcript-measured build layer). Per file touched $4.66. Per 1,000 lines churned $21.88. Per 1,000 lines of PRODUCTION code $115.18 (only 19.0% of 84,933 churned lines are prod; 74.9% is test/eval).
- Split of purpose: 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend ($643.73 of $1,817.65) is remediation of the loop's own prior output; 46.6% lifetime.
- Split of tokens: 99.8% of priced spend is context, not generation — 68.0% cache READ, 31.8% cache WRITE, 0.1% output. Mean ~150k tokens of context replayed per turn across 400-760 turns/slice.

WHAT THE LOOP IS ACTUALLY PAYING FOR: it is paying ~$1,013/week to re-read a prefix nothing ever prunes (zero compaction/context-editing events across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts), ~$644/week to fix work it shipped in prior weeks, and ~$166/week to carry its own discarded thinking blocks forward. It is paying almost nothing (0.1%) for the tokens it actually produces, and 4.56% for the orchestration that decides everything.

THE CENTRAL DEFECT, NEWLY MEASURED AND VERIFIED IN THIS PASS: the true binding currency — account-level `seven_day` `utilization` — is emitted by the API into the supervisor tick's OWN stdout on essentially every tick, and is discarded by a single filter line. I reproduced the full pause-week trajectory from tick logs alone (0.29 -> 0.90 over Aug 7-10). The 2026-08-10T05:00:12Z tick that wrote the "no mechanically-launchable slice" standdown read util=0.87. The 2026-08-10T09:05:29Z MR_FORCE tick that LAUNCHED M21b-2 — $274.37, 183% of its $150 cap, the most expensive run of the window — read util=0.90 in its own stream, while its internal governor printed governor=NORMAL at a synthetic 64.7%. The loop launched its single most expensive slice at 90% of the week's allowance with the number 90 in its own output. Everything else in this report is downstream of that one instrumentation error.

root_causes.statement: The loop governs itself with a synthetic internal-dollar model that under-reports real credit consumption by a measured 1.39x, while the true account-level gauge is emitted into the loop's own stdout on every tick and thrown away by one filter line.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: VERIFIED THIS PASS (MEASURED): 188 of 188 surviving /tmp/mr_pass_*.log and /tmp/mr_native_tick_*.log files contain `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{...}}`; 96/188 (51.1%) carry a `seven_day` variant with a `utilization` float, and effectively EVERY supervisor tick log in-window carries one. Reproduced the pause-week trajectory from tick logs alone: 2026-08-07 0.29 -> 08-08 0.53 -> 08-09 0.75/0.83 -> 08-10 0.87 -> 0.90 (mr_native_tick_native-20260810T090529Z-1769875.log). That last tick is the MR_FORCE tick that launched M21b-2 ($274.37 ledger, 183% of its $150 cap); the 05:00:12Z tick that wrote the 'no mechanically-launchable slice' standdown read 0.87. Meanwhile the internal governor reported 64.7% / NORMAL (mr-situation:63-84 over mr-budget-config.json weekly_limit_usd=2783). 90/64.7 = 1.39x under-report. The discard is explicit and intentional: mr-native-tick.sh:379 `if '"resetsAt"' not in l or '"rejected"' not in l: continue`, defended in-line at :354-356 and in mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 ('Trip ONLY on status == "rejected" ... status=="allowed_warning" is routine'). ALSO MEASURED: five_hour events carry utilization too (mr_pass_11r-c.log: `"rateLimitType":"five_hour","utilization":0.99,"surpassedThreshold":0.9`), and a real hard event exists (mr_native_tick_native-20260805T112040Z-1651311.log: `"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true`). The signal is ABSENT from the persisted session transcripts (0 hits across all 62 monster-realm *.jsonl) — it exists only in the ephemeral /tmp stream logs.
root_causes.mechanism: The API streams a continuous account-level gauge. A 2026-08-01 fix needed a binary rate-limit trip, so it wrote an allowlist that keeps only `status=="rejected"` and drops every other event. That was correct for TRIPPING and catastrophic for MEASURING: the loop then had to invent a substitute, so mr-budget-config.json extrapolates a weekly_limit_usd from one operator-reported percentage on 2026-07-25 (1002/0.36=2783) and prices fable by explicit guess ('ESTIMATE 1.5x opus ... CALIBRATE from first fable run' — never done, while fable was ~57% of window spend). Every downstream control — governor state, tier caps, SOFT-PAUSE/HARD-STOP, the d7 window — is computed from that fiction, so all of them read low and none of them ever fired (205 `governor=` occurrences in the tick log, all NORMAL, zero trips in the loop's lifetime). The operator became the pacing controller of last resort, watching real usage by hand and running mr-supervisor-disable at ~90%.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The entire week's plan allowance consumed in ~3.5 active days, followed by a ~85h operator-imposed pause; the prior week (reset 2026-08-06) hit `status:rejected` with `isUsingOverage:true` and burned PURCHASED credits, which the operator names as the true monetary waste. Directly caused the launch of a $274.37 slice at 90% utilization.

root_causes.statement: The loop's unit cost is (context size x turns), and nothing in the loop manages either term: zero compaction, zero context-editing, a 44K-token static preamble replayed every turn, and an orchestrator that navigates by grep despite CodeGraph being indexed and used one layer down.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED (transcript lane, corroborated by cost lane's independent re-implementation of mr-cost-watch:30-39): 99.8% of priced token spend is context — cache read 65.3-68.0% ($1,012.79), cache write 25.6-31.8% ($396.98), output 9.1% ($140.81), fresh input 0.06%. Parent prompt-volume decomposition across 23 sessions / 703.0M turn-tokens: assistant thinking/output carried forward 243.9M (34.7%, ~$166); static preamble x turns 120.4M (17.1%); Bash tool results 69.7M (9.9%); Read results 62.4M (8.9%). ZERO isCompactSummary / compact_boundary events across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts; final contexts reached 295K / 454K / 611K tokens unmanaged. Parent tool census: Bash 2,135 (68.6%), Grep 0, Glob 0, codegraph_explore 0 — against 791 grep/sed/cat/ls calls emitting 2,080,724 chars (~520K tokens) of navigation output; subagents made 47 codegraph_explore + 89 codebase-memory calls, so the tooling works and only the orchestrator abstains, in direct violation of ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. VERIFIED THIS PASS: mr-launch.sh:85 invokes `claude --model "$MODEL" --effort "$EFFORT" --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "$(cat "$B")"` — no --mcp-config, no --strict-mcp-config, no --allowed-tools, so every build session loads all 6 configured MCP servers (3 from ~/.claude.json: spacetimedb-docs-v2-6-0, codegraph, codebase-memory-mcp; 3 from projects/monster-realm/.mcp.json: gitmcp-spacetimedb, gitmcp-wasm-bindgen, gitmcp-pixijs) and every skill listing, on every turn. 32.2% of parent prompt volume (226.1M tokens) is burned BEFORE the first repo-file edit, median at turn 50, with a 6.4x spread across slices (12.0% best, 77.0% worst).
root_causes.mechanism: Every token added to the prefix at turn i is re-billed on all (N-i) remaining turns. With N=400-760 turns per slice, a 12K-token Read at turn 1 costs ~2.4M cache-read tokens; the same Read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M. Because nothing prunes and nothing compacts, the cost of a slice is set almost entirely by how much material enters the context early and how long the session runs — not by what the model writes. Grep-based navigation is the worst possible shape for this: it emits large, low-density text early, and the pre-indexed alternative that would emit small, high-density text is present on disk and ignored.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$1,013/week of pure prefix re-reading (~$52k/yr at run-rate). Addressable sub-buckets measured: carried thinking ~$166/wk; static preamble ~$130/wk across both layers; Bash navigation carry ~$47/wk; orientation-before-first-edit ~$238 of parent spend plus most of planner ($62.93).

root_causes.statement: Parallelism is being purchased with rework: the `touches:` disjointness discipline that enables fan-out forces out-of-scope work into ADR prose that has no mechanical reader, and the only reader is an LLM review that rediscovers it a mean of 13.1 days later at review prices.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED: 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend ($643.73 of $1,817.65) and 46.6% of lifetime named-slice spend ($3,913.21 of $8,394.81) is remediation. 13 review-residual milestones / 85 slices to date; the last five produced 7, 9, 6, 8, 7 slices at 7d/6d/3d/4d intervals — flat output, accelerating cadence. SMOKING GUN for the generator: docs/adr/0165 (Accepted 2026-07-31, slice 11r-d) states 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared `touches:`' — 11r-i merged without implementing it, CHANGELOG re-drifted 18 PRs, and it was finally done by 13r-g on 2026-08-15, 15 days after Acceptance. Same shape in-window: 14r-d's ADR-0185 D6 routes through mr_log because 'OBS-2 ratchet would red two gates whose fix files are outside touches:'; justfile:35-39 wires the m20a perf gate inside `eval:` rather than `ci:` because 'ci.yml is outside m20a's touches'. Corpus surface: 21 of 165 ADRs carry a 'Residuals / follow-ups' section and 78 defer/park phrases exist ('deferred to' 45, 'a later slice' 11, 'future slice' 10, 'parked to' 8), with zero mechanical consumers. The class reproduced itself INSIDE its own remediation: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124-190 parks 7 `*-security.eval.mjs` gates — two of them MEASURED to swallow the scan needle and pass GREEN on code they exist to reject — to a slice `14r-c-2` that `grep -rl` finds in zero spec, PLAN.md, or mr-state.json. Measured disclosure->remediation latency n=10: mean 13.1 days, median 14, max 20.
root_causes.mechanism: mr-disjoint declares two slices SAFE by comparing declared `touches:` sets, which is what permits N=2 fan-out. A slice that discovers an adjacent defect cannot fix it without violating its declaration, so it writes the finding into an ADR Residuals bullet and merges GREEN. Nothing reads ADR Residuals bullets. Weeks later a $54-74 multi-lens weekly review re-derives the same findings from scratch, emits a 7-9 slice residual milestone, and the loop pays full slice price ($36-$126 each) to fix work it already knew about. The compounding term is that each remediation milestone is itself subject to the same rule and therefore emits fresh untracked residuals (13r-a and 13r-b both spawned new undrafted residuals: D1 tempo, D3b caddy, P5-otlp).
root_causes.quantified_cost: $643.73 in-window; $3,913.21 lifetime. Plus a standing safety debt: 7 security gates across battle/evolution/raising/recruit/shop/trade/NPC reducers are measurably blind RIGHT NOW, owned by a slice that exists nowhere.

root_causes.statement: Every gate that could bound cost or protect quality is advisory, and each is advisory because its own estimator is measurably wrong — so the system has trained both the supervisor and the operator to rubber-stamp its signals.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: COST GATE: mr-budget-config.json:55 `costwatch_enforce: false`; all 23 in-window `started` lines carry `enforce=0`; census 12 WARN / 10 STOP-MONITOR / 4 HARD-MONITOR / 77 LOG-STALL / 0 enforcement actions. It is off for a documented and CORRECT reason (mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 — all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0), but the trips were false positives because the estimator is broken in two measurable ways: mr-cost-watch:29-39 prices EVERY stream line containing usage, and the SDK emits one event per content block repeating identical `message.usage` for the same message.id (measured 1.75 events/message over 12,264 events / 7,020 messages, range 1.38-2.20); and mr-cost-watch:39 prices all cache_creation at `cache_write_5m` while 17.9% of in-window cache-creation tokens (6.24M of 34.93M) are ephemeral_1h, priced 1.6x higher in the same config. Result: ledger/raw ranges 0.6370 to 1.0076 across 21 slices (median 0.7627) against a hard-coded constant 0.80 — so a nominal $60 cap actually bites anywhere between $38.22 and $60.46 of real spend, and the in-line justification at mr-cost-watch:82 ('overcount fires early = safe direction') is falsified by the two slices where raw UNDERCOUNTS. QUALITY GATE: gating_test_audit flagged 11 of 23 in-window merges, all 11 adjudicated CLEAN, 0 true positives — and 0 true positives across its entire v3-era life. Documented flag causes are lexical: comment prose, `.iter().skip()` matched as a test-skip marker, import-line reflow, manifest count bumps. Every flag mandates a full-diff supervisor read (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:39, :121-122); the m20c adjudication produced the window's most expensive tick at $5.0285, 3.8x the median. mr-audit:51 also scopes the suppression scan to test paths only, so `#[allow]`/`@ts-ignore`/`nosemgrep` added to production source is invisible by construction. `remote_red_fix_cycles` is populated on 446 v3-era rows and SUMS TO ZERO.
root_causes.mechanism: A gate whose estimator has a run-dependent error cannot be armed without killing good runs, so it is left advisory; a gate with 0% precision cannot be trusted, so its output is adjudicated away. Both then become pure cost with negative signal value: the eleventh 'FLAGGED->adjudicated CLEAN' is read far less carefully than the first, and 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' appears in the merge record of m20b — the slice that shipped a 7-container observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped four of eight containers. The instruments are not merely useless; they manufacture false assurance on the operator's PRIMARY axis.
root_causes.quantified_cost: $192.85 of in-window spend that armed enforcement would have prevented ($131.15 on M21b-2 alone); ~$10-20/week of adjudication ticks; and an unquantifiable but real erosion of gate trust on the quality axis.

root_causes.statement: Model/effort routing is 100% collinear with tier by construction and the only quality columns are constant-zero, so the largest single cost lever in the system — a measured ~$611/week fable premium — is not merely unmeasured but unmeasurable from production data.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED: every `started cap=$150` run in-window is model=fable and every `cap=$60` run is model=opus, with zero crossover (mr-native-tick.log L2276/L2308/L2367/L2426/L2519/L2590/L2637/L2847/L2898/L2969/L3089/L3146/L3183/L3246). fable n=10 mean $123.49/slice, $25.22/kline, $0.192/turn, 547 turns; opus n=11 mean $56.66/slice, $17.33/kline, $0.137/turn, 415 turns. The 2.18x slice premium decomposes as ~1.4x price x ~1.32x more turns. Lifetime cross-tab is worse: tier=hard/model=opus has n=1 (nh2), tier=routine/model=fable has n=0. The quality columns that would break the tie are unusable: remote_red_fix_cycles is 0 on every single window row, master_ci_after reads 'pending'/'in_progress' on 9 of 17 populated rows, gate flags are 7/10 fable vs 4/11 opus but all adjudicated CLEAN. mr-native-supervisor-README.md:60 promised this exact A/B on 2026-07-24 ('A/B hard slices opus-5@xhigh vs fable@xhigh ... frees the 45% fable share ~ $250-400/wk headroom'); three weeks later it has never run. Separately, mr-budget-config.json prices fable by explicit guess (1.5x opus, '_note: CALIBRATE from first fable run') and fable was ~57% of window spend ($1,032.59 of $1,824.97) — the dominant model is the one with the guessed price. The tier decision that drives all of this is itself unreproducible: mr-tier-map.json is self-labelled `_rules_frozen_2026-07-25` and covers 0 of 29 in-window slices, and the rule self-contradicted inside one milestone (m20b tagged routine despite mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:17 making 'M20 slices' a standalone HARD criterion; 13r-c tagged routine despite touching server-module/src/accounts.rs and six security evals).
root_causes.mechanism: The routing rule derives model deterministically from tier, and tier is derived from `touches:`. Hard-tier slices genuinely touch schema/reducer/netcode/security surfaces, which is why they were routed to the premium model — so the premium is perfectly confounded with surface difficulty and no observational analysis can ever separate them. Simultaneously the ledger records no unit-of-work denominator (no LOC, files-changed, EARS-criteria count, or attempts-normalized outcome), so even a like-for-like comparison within a tier is impossible. The question can only be answered by deliberate randomized assignment, which was specified and never executed.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$611 of the window's $1,864 slice spend is the fable-over-opus delta (~21pp of the weekly plan allowance at the measured conversion). If parity holds it is pure waste; if it does not, the loop is currently unable to prove the money is buying anything.

root_causes.statement: Spend is unpaced: there is no reservation, rate-limit, or finish-in-flight mechanism anywhere, so the week's allowance is consumed in ~3.5 days and the only pacing controller is a human running a kill switch that also blocks completion events.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED: sustained burn is ~$39.28 per slice-build-hour and the loop runs 2-way fan-out on every fan-out tick, so ~$78.6/wall-hour; the utilization trajectory I reproduced climbs 0.29 -> 0.90 in ~61 hours of active loop time. There is no pacing code: grep over mr-native-tick.sh / mr-situation / mr-spawn / mr-launch.sh / mr-metrics / mr-selfcheck / mr-audit / mr-record for replenish|inventory|queue_depth|build.?ready|backlog returns ZERO hits, and there is no spend-rate or reservation concept anywhere. The only ceiling that fires is retrospective: mr-native-tick.sh:96-105 computes single_run_alert_usd at reconcile time, and the sole in-window SPEND-ALERT (L2668) post-dates M21b-2's last dollar by one second and its first by 4h58m. When the operator pauses, the mechanism used is `.native-supervisor-disabled`, which mr-native-tick.sh:124-127 evaluates as gate -1, ABOVE the pending-event fastpath at :181 — so the M21b-2 completion event was requeued at 2026-08-10T14:05:43Z and sat 83.9h; the PR merged only at 2026-08-14T02:26:47Z, a FINISHED->MERGED latency of 84.35h against a 0.47h median. The graceful pattern already exists 20 lines below in the same file: gate -0.5 for `.blocked-on-human` (mr-native-tick.sh:144-159) self-lifts on a wake file, has a 7-day expiry, and applies ONLY to src=cron so event ticks pass through.
root_causes.mechanism: With no pace target, the loop treats the weekly allowance as a ceiling rather than a rate. Two-way fan-out at ~$78.6/wall-hour will always exhaust a fixed weekly budget in roughly a third of the week; the loop then either keeps going (into overage-purchased credits, which the operator states are strictly less cost-effective) or is stopped by hand. The hand-stop uses the only lever available, which is a blunt human-only flag ordered above event processing, so pausing NEW work also strands FINISHED work — the precise opposite of the operator's stated scarcity policy (finish in-flight, start nothing new).
root_causes.quantified_cost: A finished, PR-open, locally-green $274.37 slice idle for 3.5 days; recurring manual operator babysitting; and at least one prior week (reset 2026-08-06) that hit `status:rejected` with `isUsingOverage:true` and burned purchased credits.

recommendations.action: Stop discarding the real gauge. In mr-native-tick.sh, replace the drop-filter at :379 (`if '"resetsAt"' not in l or '"rejected"' not in l: continue`) with a two-branch parse: keep the existing earliest-`rejected` arming path EXACTLY as-is, and additionally append every rate_limit_event to a new append-only $MEM/mr-plan-utilization.jsonl as {observed_at, run_id, source_log, rateLimitType, utilization, resetsAt, isUsingOverage, overageInUse, overageResetsAt, surpassedThreshold, status}. Parse from $TLOG at reconcile AND from every /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log the tick already tails in mr-cost-watch. Add the same 4 lines to mr-launch.sh so a detached slice persists its own samples before /tmp is reaped.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED THIS PASS: 188/188 surviving run logs carry rate_limit_event; 96/188 carry a seven_day variant with a `utilization` float; essentially every supervisor tick log in-window carries one, and long slices carry many (m20d emitted 20 samples climbing 0.62->0.75 monotonically). This is the account-level truth — it automatically includes the operator's usage on other machines and unrelated projects, which no local ledger can ever see. It costs zero tokens to read. The signal is ABSENT from the persisted ~/.claude session transcripts (0 hits across all 62 monster-realm *.jsonl), so it exists ONLY in ephemeral /tmp logs and is being deleted; persistence is the whole fix.
recommendations.expected_effect: Replaces a synthetic model measured to under-report by 1.39x (real 90% vs governor 64.7% at the 2026-08-10 pause) with ground truth, at $0/week marginal cost. Enables every governor recommendation below. Sampling caveats to encode explicitly: utilization is quantized to whole percent, is emitted only while a session runs, is account-level (so per-slice attribution is INVALID during fan-out — both concurrent slices see the same climb), and lags; record observed_at and treat any sample older than 2h as stale.
recommendations.risk: None to quality. The only real risk is regressing the existing rate-limit arming logic, which is why the `rejected` branch must be left byte-identical and the new branch must be purely additive/append-only.

recommendations.action: Rewrite the governor to reason in percent-of-allowance. In mr-situation, replace the d7_usd/weekly_limit_usd block (:63-84, :122) with a budget object sourced from the newest $MEM/mr-plan-utilization.jsonl seven_day sample: {utilization, observed_at, staleness_minutes, resets_at, is_using_overage, pace_target, state}. States: <70% NORMAL; 70-85% PACE (routine tier only, N=1, no hard-tier launches); >=85% FINISH-IN-FLIGHT (merge, checkpoint, and park in-flight work; start NOTHING new); is_using_overage||overage_in_use => OVERAGE-STOP (start nothing, finish in-flight, write an operator notification). Delete weekly_limit_usd, fable_allowance_usd, and the calibration_anchor block from mr-budget-config.json; keep the internal dollar model ONLY as a per-run relative signal, never as a governor input.
recommendations.rationale: Operator decision G2 is settled: the governor must reason in percentage of the weekly plan allowance from real telemetry. The dollar model's foundation is one operator-reported observation on 2026-07-25 (1002/0.36=2783), and its dominant model is priced by an explicit guess (fable = 'ESTIMATE 1.5x opus ... CALIBRATE from first fable run', never done, while fable was ~57% of window spend). The 85%/FINISH-IN-FLIGHT state IS operator policy G1 encoded mechanically.
recommendations.expected_effect: Would have moved the loop into PACE at the 2026-08-09 04:02 tick (util=0.74) and FINISH-IN-FLIGHT at the 2026-08-09 10:46 tick (util=0.83), i.e. ~19 hours and roughly $500-600 of spend before the operator had to intervene by hand — and critically before the 2026-08-10T09:05Z MR_FORCE tick that launched M21b-2 ($274.37) at util=0.90. Removes the manual-babysitting requirement (operator goal G3).
recommendations.risk: Staleness between runs is the real hazard: if no session has run for hours, the newest sample is old and the loop could under- or over-estimate. Mitigate by (a) publishing staleness_minutes alongside the value, (b) when stale >2h, extrapolating with the measured burn rate from the last two samples and treating the extrapolation as conservative-only (it may raise the state, never lower it), (c) forcing a cheap ~$0.27 tick spawn purely to refresh the gauge when stale >6h and the queue is non-empty.

recommendations.action: Add a pace target, not just a ceiling. In the same mr-situation budget block, compute pace_target = (seconds elapsed since resets_at-7d)/604800 and pace_delta = utilization - pace_target. Encode in mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md gate order: pace_delta > +0.15 => downgrade to PACE regardless of absolute utilization; pace_delta < -0.15 AND queue non-empty => explicitly permitted to fan out to N=3/4 under the existing N>=3 protocol.
recommendations.rationale: The failure mode is not overspend, it is burst: the week's allowance was consumed in ~3.5 active days at ~$78.6/wall-hour of 2-way fan-out. A ceiling alone cannot prevent that — it only tells you afterwards. Under the operator's reframing (A: idle hours cost nothing; F: overage purchases are the true waste), a pace controller is what converts an unmanaged burst into a week-long even burn that never touches purchased credits. The symmetric under-pace branch matters too: the N>=3 protocol has been Drew-approved since 2026-07-26 and has NEVER been used (85 single launches, 17 pairs, zero triples), so the loop currently has no way to spend a surplus either.
recommendations.expected_effect: Directly targets the measured burst: at the 2026-08-09 04:02 tick, 2.4 days into a 7-day week, pace_target was ~0.34 and utilization was 0.74 — a pace_delta of +0.40, nearly 3x the trigger. Should eliminate overage purchases entirely in a normal week (goal F) and remove the ~85h manual pause as a required operator action.
recommendations.risk: Under-spending the allowance is a real regression risk if the pace band is too tight — a week that ends at 70% has wasted 30% of a paid resource. The symmetric under-pace branch exists specifically to prevent that, and the band should start wide (+/-0.15) and be tightened only on evidence.

recommendations.action: Reorder the gates so a pause never strands finished work. Move the `.native-supervisor-disabled` check (mr-native-tick.sh:124-127) BELOW the pending-event fastpath at :181, and give it the gate -0.5 treatment already implemented 20 lines away for `.blocked-on-human` (:144-159): apply to src=cron only, self-lift on a wake file, and expire after 7 days. Add the same exemption to mr-ci-watch:9. Introduce a distinct, machine-written PAUSE state for the scarcity case so the human kill switch stops being overloaded for it.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: the M21b-2 done-event was requeued at 2026-08-10T14:05:43Z and consumed 83.90h later, giving a FINISHED->MERGED latency of 84.35h against a 0.47h median for the other 20 slices. The loop's most expensive run of the window ($274.37) sat finished, PR-open and locally green for 3.5 days because the pause flag is ordered above event processing. This is a direct violation of the operator's own scarcity policy (G1: finish in-flight work, start nothing new) baked into gate order, and the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
recommendations.expected_effect: Converts an 84.35h merge stall into the observed event-driven baseline of ~22 minutes. Under reframing A this is not a throughput argument — it is a value-preservation argument: $274.37 of already-purchased work was held hostage, and a stranded slice is exactly the outcome operator policy G1 exists to prevent.
recommendations.risk: A pause that still merges is by definition still spending: each merge tick is ~$1.33. That is the correct trade (finishing costs ~$1.33, stranding costs $274 of idle value), but the pause state must forbid LAUNCH unconditionally, and that must be asserted by a test.

recommendations.action: KEEP the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet exactly as it is, and explicitly protect it from every cost cut below. Do not reduce reviewer (50 runs, $85.71) or red-team (43 runs, $84.52) run counts, and do not merge them into one role.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED as the best-spending part of the loop: 19 of 50 reviewer results and 3 of 43 red-team results were classified BLOCKER, with reproduced evidence. On 14r-d the reviewer found a merge-blocker the plan would have shipped (3 new bare log::error! taking battle.rs from 7 to 10 and the grandfathered total 53->56, redding evals/observability-log-wrapper.eval.mjs:1356-1366 and observability_tests.rs:328, with every fix file outside `touches:`); red-team independently reproduced it in a throwaway clone at /tmp/14rd/repo with the real toolchain. On m20c a paid review pass found a HIGH (unguarded navigator reads abort main() bootstrap, main.ts:2379-2394) AFTER CI was green. This is defect discovery on the PLAN, before code exists — the cheapest possible place to find it, and it is the operator's PRIMARY axis.
recommendations.expected_effect: ~$171/week for 93 runs, i.e. ~9% of window spend, buying verified pre-merge blocker discovery that CI demonstrably does not provide. Preserving this is a precondition for every other recommendation: cost cuts that touch it are a quality regression, not a saving.
recommendations.risk: None — this is a do-not-touch instruction. The active risk is that a naive cost-cutting pass conflates this gauntlet with the mechanical gating_test_audit (0/11 precision, R14); they are different gates and must not share a fate.

recommendations.action: Enable context management in build sessions. Add the API context-editing strategy (clear_thinking_20251015 under the context-management beta) to the mr-launch.sh:85/:124 invocations, and set an explicit compaction backstop. Roll out on routine-tier slices first, measure attempts + post-merge red cycles for 2 weeks, then extend to hard tier only on parity.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED as the single largest addressable sink: assistant thinking/output carried forward is 243.9M tokens = 34.7% of all parent prompt volume, computed from exact usage.output_tokens (no estimation). ZERO compaction or context-editing events exist across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts; contexts ran to 295K/454K/611K tokens unmanaged, and 09045af1 (M21b-2, the window's most expensive slice) sat at 611K of a 1M window with no backstop configured — one long slice away from hard failure.
recommendations.expected_effect: At the measured parent blended cache-read rate of $0.6797/M this bucket is $165.79/week. A 60% clear rate saves roughly $100/week (~3.4pp of the weekly plan allowance at the measured conversion of ~$29.5 internal-$ per percentage point; likely more, since that conversion is an upper bound). Also removes a live context-exhaustion risk on hard slices.
recommendations.risk: MARKED: RISKS THE PRIMARY QUALITY BAR. Clearing thinking blocks could degrade long-horizon reasoning precisely on the hard/security slices where careful iterative work is what you want — and COST-12 shows the expensive slices are exactly the netcode/prediction/auth ones where depth is correct. Hence the routine-tier-first rollout with attempts and post-merge red cycles as the falsifier, and no hard-tier extension without measured parity.

recommendations.action: Make the orchestrator use the code index it already has. Add a hard rule to mr-brief-template.md (and mirror it in the QUALITY TIER block emitted by mr-spawn:59-62): before any repo-wide grep/find/sed/cat for orientation, call codegraph_explore or codebase-memory search_code; `grep` is permitted only for literal text that is not a symbol. Additionally pass `--strict-mcp-config` with an explicit --mcp-config naming only codegraph, codebase-memory-mcp and spacetimedb-docs at mr-launch.sh:85/:124, dropping the three unused gitmcp-* servers.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: parent tool census across 23 sessions is Bash 2,135 (68.6%), Grep 0, Glob 0, codegraph_explore 0, cbm 4 — while SUBAGENTS in the same sessions made 47 codegraph_explore + 89 codebase-memory calls. Both .codegraph/ directories exist on disk. So the tooling works, the routing doctrine in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md mandates it, and only the orchestrator abstains — this is a brief-level instruction gap, not a tooling gap. VERIFIED THIS PASS: mr-launch.sh:85 passes no --mcp-config/--strict-mcp-config/--allowed-tools, so build sessions load all 6 configured servers (3 from ~/.claude.json, 3 from projects/monster-realm/.mcp.json).
recommendations.expected_effect: 791 grep/sed/cat/ls calls emitted 2,080,724 chars (~520K tokens); total Bash tool-result carry is 69.7M tokens = 9.9% of parent prompt volume ~ $47/week, of which the navigation share is ~64%. Halving it saves ~$15-25/week directly and more indirectly by shrinking early context (see R8). The MCP trim is honestly small — 3 unused servers of 6, not the 'many unused connectors' hypothesis — so claim it as a minor preamble reduction, not a headline.
recommendations.risk: Low. CodeGraph lags writes by ~1s and can miss very fresh edits, so the rule must permit grep as a fallback when codegraph returns nothing for a symbol the agent just wrote.

recommendations.action: Move orientation out of the expensive session and into prepared text. Extend mr-spawn to render a SLICE CONTEXT PACK into the brief: (a) codegraph_explore output for the symbols named in the slice's `touches:` and TARGET_DESC, (b) the specific ADR decision lines cited (e.g. 'ADR-0185 D6'), never whole ADRs, (c) the 3 most recent handoff entries matching the slice family. Simultaneously stop pointing at un-inlined context: replace mr-brief-template.md:1's reference chain (build-loop-prompt.md 18,838B + standards/*.md 24,481B + docs/routing.md 4,137B ~ 11,864 tokens) with the 3-5 rules that actually bind, and split memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md (428,676 B ~ 107,000 tokens, 1,716 lines, 154 sections) into the archive files that already exist.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 32.2% of all parent prompt volume (226.1M of 703.0M tokens) is consumed BEFORE the first repo-file edit, median at turn 50, with a 6.4x spread (12.0% for 13r-f vs 77.0% for m20d). The top single content blocks by carried cost are all early large reads (a 15,825-token Read at turn 7 of 09045af1 cost ~2.7M carried tokens ~ $1.85 for one Read). Orientation greps against the 107K-token handoff returned 21,481-27,753 chars each at turn 4. DOCT-14 proves the mechanism works: the existing TARGET_DESC already hands the agent file:line defects, the correct SSOT predicate AND the wrong one to avoid, and zero of 18 slice merges show scope re-derivation. This is the same trick applied to the rest of orientation.
recommendations.expected_effect: Closing even a third of the 12%-to-77% spread is ~$75/week of parent spend plus a share of planner ($62.93) and the reviewer/red-team plan-review passes. Compounds with R6 and R7: the tokens saved are early tokens, which are the most expensive kind (a 12K read at turn 1 costs ~2.4M carried tokens; at turn 150, ~0.4M).
recommendations.risk: MARKED: MILD RISK TO THE PRIMARY QUALITY BAR. Pre-loading context can pre-decide the design and suppress the agent's independent verification, which is where several real blockers were found. Rule: the pack carries FACTS (verbatim source, ADR decision text, file:line) and never CONCLUSIONS or a recommended approach. Do NOT shorten the brief itself — at 12,610 chars (~3,152 tokens, 7% of the 44,288-token preamble) it is dense, accurate and cheap.

recommendations.action: Truncate gate output before it enters context. Add `just`-recipe wrappers for the noisy commands (cargo nextest, just eval, playwright e2e, cargo mutants) that emit a fixed-shape summary on PASS (counts + duration only) and the FULL output on FAIL. Point the brief at the wrappers and forbid raw invocation. Pair with a pinned toolchain env file to kill the 43% of Bash calls (912 of 2,135) that re-type an unpinned PATH preamble in two mutually inconsistent forms.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: Bash tool results carry 69.7M tokens (9.9% of parent prompt volume); total Bash result volume is 3,269,548 chars across 2,135 calls. Passing gate output is pure noise that is then re-billed on every remaining turn. The env-preamble repetition is separately a correctness risk the operator has already been bitten by (memory note: 'asdf shebang hook trap: env-python3 hooks exit 126 in unpinned cwds'), and sessions currently guess the node path two different ways.
recommendations.expected_effect: ~$20-30/week of context carry, plus removal of a known toolchain-drift failure class. Small in dollars, cheap in effort, and it is the correct place to attach the local-model summarizer (R12).
recommendations.risk: MARKED: RISKS THE PRIMARY QUALITY BAR IF DONE WRONG. Truncating a FAILING gate would hide the defect the gate exists to surface. The rule must be asymmetric and tested: PASS is summarized, FAIL is never truncated.

recommendations.action: Fix mr-disjoint so it compares what a slice will ACTUALLY touch. Before the SAFE verdict, expand each slice's declared `touches:` by the same companion rules the brief already grants every slice: (a) sibling test files of any declared code file (*.test.ts next to a declared .ts, *_tests.rs next to a declared .rs), and (b) the always-granted doc set docs/adr/**, docs/knowledge/**, CHANGELOG.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/adr/DIGEST.md. Treat (b) as a known shared axis that fan-out must either serialize or auto-merge, since every slice holds it.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 14r-c and 14r-e were declared disjoint on paper and blessed as a fan-out pair (spec :202), then both edited client/src/main.wiring.test.ts — a *.test.ts sibling of 14r-e's declared client/src/main.ts — producing 'PR#318 CONFLICTING vs master 9b924f3'. The 14r-e park memo says it plainly: "14r-c's fan-out disjointness held on paper, not in practice." 14r-b hit the doc axis instead: 'conflict set was ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md' — which EVERY slice is granted, so any two concurrent slices are structurally guaranteed to collide there. 3 of ~20 in-window merges hit sibling conflicts (m20d, 14r-b, 14r-e).
recommendations.expected_effect: Directly prevents the measured 14r-e resume ($36.19 measured, unrecorded in the ledger) plus a PARKED tick, a relaunch tick and a supervisor adjudication — ~$40-50/week at the observed rate of 3 collisions per 20 merges. Also raises the trustworthiness of the SAFE verdict, which is the precondition for ever running N>=3 (R3).
recommendations.risk: Expanding touches makes SAFE verdicts rarer and could suppress legitimate fan-out, reducing throughput. Under reframing A that is acceptable (idle hours are free), but the doc-axis handling should be auto-merge rather than serialize, so the common case does not collapse to N=1.

recommendations.action: Arm cost enforcement, but fix the estimator first and checkpoint instead of killing. Three changes in order: (1) mr-cost-watch:29-39 — dedup usage events by message.id before pricing (measured 1.75 events per message, range 1.38-2.20); (2) mr-cost-watch:39 — price cache_creation.ephemeral_1h at cache_write_1h, not cache_write_5m (17.9% of in-window cache-creation tokens, 6.24M of 34.93M, are 1h and cost 1.6x more); (3) threshold on the corrected sum, not on `raw`, and re-express caps as percentage points of the weekly allowance rather than dollars. Then set costwatch_enforce=true with HARD meaning: write a wip checkpoint commit + park memo + open the PR if possible, then stop — never SIGKILL.
recommendations.rationale: The gate is off for a correct reason (all 4 historical HARD trips merged EXIT=0) but the trips were false positives caused by a run-dependent estimator error, not by caps being wrong: measured ledger/raw spans 0.6370 to 1.0076 (median 0.7627) against a hard-coded 0.80, so a $60 cap actually bites between $38.22 and $60.46 of real spend. The in-line justification at mr-cost-watch:82 ('overcount fires early = safe direction') is falsified by the two slices where raw UNDERCOUNTS (M21c 1.0076, 13r-b 1.0033). The arming precondition in mr-budget-config.json:56 (adversarial-review condition F3) is now satisfied 46 times over by the (WARN-raw, final-raw, ledger) triples already on disk.
recommendations.expected_effect: MEASURED counterfactual with enforce=true: $192.85 of in-window spend prevented, $131.15 of it on M21b-2 alone (7% of the whole window, ~6.5pp of the weekly allowance). Fixing the two pricing bugs should collapse the 0.637-1.008 spread so caps mean what they say, converting two of the four historical trips from premature (81.7% and 87.9% of cap) into correct.
recommendations.risk: MARKED: RISKS THE PRIMARY QUALITY BAR. Killing a run strands locks, hard-blocks relaunch until a human edits cap_override, and discards in-flight work — which is exactly the README's documented objection and the operator's stated position that stranding half-done work is worse than idling (G1). This is why HARD must checkpoint, not kill. Do not arm enforcement before the two pricing fixes land and are validated against at least 10 fresh (corrected-sum, ledger) pairs.

recommendations.action: Adopt this routing table and instrument the one uncertainty. SUPERVISOR TICK: upgrade sonnet@medium -> opus@medium. ROUTINE: keep opus@high unchanged. CONTENT: keep opus@medium unchanged. HARD: hold fable@xhigh but immediately run a randomized A/B — assign the next 8 hard-tier slices 4 fable@xhigh / 4 opus@xhigh by coin flip, and populate remote_red_fix_cycles honestly plus a post-merge-red count taken 24h after merge (not at merge time). SUBAGENTS: keep reviewer/red-team/verifier at current model and run counts (R5); cap the tester role's turn budget (median 58 turns/run) and replace general-purpose (median 27,743-token preamble, $12.19/run) with a scoped role.
recommendations.rationale: TICK: this is the seat with the most consequential decisions (launch/merge/kill) and the least room for error, and it is on the cheapest model in the fleet. Measured tick spend is $86.80 = 4.56% of window spend at $1.34 mean; opus@medium roughly doubles that. Against ~$60-90/week extra, the in-window tick errors were: a standdown that missed 7 spec-ready slices (13r-a CRITICAL, all with `after: none`) buried in a 3,296-char single-line gate — a textbook cheap-model recall failure; 11 rubber-stamped audit adjudications; and a $274.37 launch at util=0.90. A cheap model making a bad merge or launch decision is far more expensive than the model-tier delta, and here that is not theory: one launch decision cost 4.6x the entire annual tick-model delta. ROUTINE: opus@high is measurably right — $56.66/slice mean, 10 of 11 at ATTEMPTS=1, cheapest $/file of any tier ($4.99 vs fable's $4.51 is the only metric where fable wins, and it is within noise). HARD: the 2.18x/slice and 1.46x/kline premium (~$611/window) is bought on a hunch — model is 100% collinear with tier (n=1 at hard/opus lifetime), remote_red_fix_cycles is 0 on every row, and master_ci_after reads 'pending' on 9 of 17 rows. mr-native-supervisor-README.md:60 specified this exact A/B on 2026-07-24 and it never ran.
recommendations.expected_effect: Tick upgrade: NET COST INCREASE of ~$60-90/week (~2-3pp of allowance), justified on quality not cost. HARD A/B: if parity holds on post-merge red cycles and attempts, flipping HARD to opus@xhigh frees ~$611/week (~21pp of the weekly allowance) — by far the largest single lever in the system. FALSIFIERS, stated in advance: revert the tick upgrade if, over 2 weeks / ~130 ticks, standdown-error rate and adjudication depth do not improve; keep fable if the A/B shows opus@xhigh producing more post-merge red cycles or more ATTEMPTS>1 on comparable surfaces.
recommendations.risk: MARKED: THE HARD-TIER A/B DIRECTLY RISKS THE PRIMARY QUALITY BAR — 4 of the 8 A/B slices will touch schema/reducer/netcode/security on a model the loop has not validated there. Mitigate by keeping the full reviewer/red-team gauntlet on both arms and by excluding any slice the supervisor judges irreversible. The tick upgrade risks nothing but money.

recommendations.action: Make ADR residuals mechanically queueable. Add a `just residuals` gate (wired into ci:) that extracts every slice-shaped identifier from (a) '## Residuals / follow-ups' sections in docs/adr/*.md, (b) `owner:` tags in evals/*.eval.mjs, and (c) the 78 defer/park phrases, then fails if any named slice ID appears in no M*.spec.md and no PLAN.md §9 entry. Require the weekly-review Phase 6 spec author to consume that list as its input rather than re-deriving findings from scratch.
recommendations.rationale: This attacks the largest single spend category at its generator. MEASURED: 35.4% of in-window and 46.6% of lifetime named-slice spend is remediation; disclosure->remediation latency is mean 13.1 days / median 14 across 10 traceable items; 21 of 165 ADRs carry a Residuals section and 78 defer/park phrases exist with ZERO mechanical consumers. The failure is live and severe right now: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190 parks 7 *-security.eval.mjs gates — two MEASURED to swallow the scan needle and pass GREEN on code they exist to reject — to a slice `14r-c-2` that grep finds in no spec, no PLAN.md, and no mr-state.json. ADR-0165 is the canonical trace: Accepted 2026-07-31 with implementation deferred out of `touches:`, assigned to 11r-i, silently never done, CHANGELOG re-drifted 18 PRs, finally implemented 15 days later by 13r-g.
recommendations.expected_effect: Converts a $54-74 LLM rediscovery cycle into a free CI grep. Even a 25% reduction in the remediation share is ~$160/week (~5pp of allowance); the realistic ceiling is higher because the review's most expensive function — re-finding what was already written down — disappears entirely. Also closes a live security-gate hole that no queue currently owns.
recommendations.risk: Low mechanically. The real risk is that it makes the residual backlog visible and large, which may look like a regression; treat backlog visibility as the point, not a defect. Note this does NOT fix the underlying `touches:` tension (R10 addresses the collision half); it only guarantees the deferred work reaches a queue.

recommendations.action: Fix the gate-audit grep or delete it. In mr-audit: strip comment spans before counting removed_or_modified_asserts (:54); anchor skip-marker detection to test-framework call sites so `.iter().skip()` no longer matches (:56); ignore pure import-line reflow and manifest count-bump diffs; drop the unconditional tier=hard FLAG (:58-59). Separately, remove the test-path pathspec from the SUPPRESSION pass at :51 so `#[allow]`/`@ts-ignore`/`nosemgrep`/`eslint-disable` added to PRODUCTION source is counted. If those fixes do not produce a true positive within 20 merges, delete the gate.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 11 flags on 23 in-window merges, 11/11 adjudicated CLEAN, 0 true positives — and 0 true positives across the entire v3 era. Every documented flag cause is lexical and cheaply excludable: 'import-line reflow, no real assert removed' (14r-g); '2 comment-prose false-positives ... skip_markers_added=2 both Rust .iter().skip() calls' (14r-f); 'all manifest-count bumps 15->16/12->13' (M21b-2). Meanwhile the gate is structurally blind to the defects the residual milestones exist to fix: 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' appears in the merge record of m20b, the slice that shipped an observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped four of eight containers — none of those defects touch a test file.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes ~11 full-diff supervisor reads per window (~$10-20/week, including the window's most expensive tick at $5.0285). The dominant benefit is on the PRIMARY axis: a gate with 0% precision trains its reader to rubber-stamp, so 'FLAGGED->adjudicated CLEAN' currently reads like a caught defect and is not one. Closing the production-source suppression hole removes a latent (measured unexploited) path to merging a silenced lint.
