recommendations.risk: Deleting the gate outright would remove the only automated check on test-weakening. Prefer the fixes; only delete after the 20-merge trial fails. Do NOT conflate this gate with the reviewer/red-team gauntlet (R5) — they are different mechanisms and must not share a fate.

recommendations.action: Give the ledger a unit-of-work denominator and close its accounting holes. Extend mr-record's row schema with: files_touched, prod_lines, test_lines, doc_lines, attempts, post_merge_red_cycles (populated 24h after merge, not at merge time), and delta_utilization_pp from R1. Fix the resume-pass hole: mr-record must re-sum the FULL log on every done-event including segments appended after a FINISHED row is written. Stop reusing log paths — mr-launch.sh should write /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.<attempt>.<epoch>.log and copy usage + rate_limit lines to $MEM/telemetry/ before /tmp is reaped.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: $46.84 of real in-window spend is absent from the SSOT because resume passes append after the FINISHED row (14r-e's true cost is $125.7264 vs $85.1433 recorded — a 47.7% understatement on that slice); 32 of 150 in-window rows carry cost_usd=null and mr-situation:81-82 counts null as $0.0; two rows book real paid work at exactly $0.0 ('paid review pass (reviewer+red-team+verifier) on PR#304'). Log reuse has already destroyed evidence: 13r-c's 2026-08-10 log ($64.86) was overwritten by its 2026-08-15 rerun, and m20c's $114.50 first-pass log is gone. Separately, the ABSENCE of a work denominator is why COST-06 (fable premium) and PIA-04 (did the optimization push work?) are both permanently unanswerable — cost-per-slice comparisons across eras, tiers and models are all confounded by scope with no way to normalize.
recommendations.expected_effect: No direct dollar saving. It is the precondition for every future economic decision: without it, the R12 A/B cannot be scored, the effect of R6/R7/R8 cannot be measured, and next quarter's version of this postmortem will hit the same wall. Also removes a measured 2.4% systematic under-report, all in the unsafe direction for a governor.
recommendations.risk: None to quality. The one discipline to enforce, learned from PIA-17 (the v3 push changed the system and the instrument in the same commit, permanently destroying its own baseline): land these counters ONE cycle before any change they are meant to measure.

recommendations.action: Ornith/Ornith-35B: kill the scheduling, keep exactly one job, pin one tag. Move the preflight warm-up (mr-native-tick.sh:30-47) from above gate -1 to below gate 1, and fire it only when a .done file is present. Pin a single model tag in mr-ollama:11-24 and delete the currently-LOADED-instance and hermes-.env fallback resolution. Keep exactly one job: the post-done advisory summary already produced at mr-launch.sh:37-38, with its existing hard verification gate (output is appended under 'ADVISORY ONLY', never parsed, never gates a merge/rerun/park decision). Delete the never-fired triage hop at mr-launch.sh:101.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 263 preflight warm-ups against 23 actual summarize-run consumptions = 11.4 warm-ups per use, of which 86 fired inside the 84.87h dead span when no slice could possibly finish. The tag resolution has silently drifted: three 21GB tags coexist (ornith-agent:128k, ornith-agent:65k, hrbrmstr/ornith-35b-fixed:latest), the tick alternates between the bare and ':latest' spellings 151/112 times, and hermes now runs a DIFFERENT tag — which is precisely the 'two 21GB variants swapping on a 16GB GPU = thrash' condition mr-ollama's own header warns against. The triage role has never fired once (0 OLLAMA-UNAVAILABLE in any archived event; the haiku hop it replaced had 0 invocations ever). HONEST ANSWER TO 'KILL OR GIVE IT A REAL JOB': I examined each candidate task named — log classification, diff-stat summarization, lock/state reconciliation, event triage, first-pass brief lint — and every one has a deterministic implementation that is cheaper, exact, and needs no verification gate (diff-stats come from git --numstat; lock/state reconciliation is a file-existence check; brief lint is a grep for touches:/ADR/SHALL/cap; event triage is the exit code). The ONE genuinely model-shaped task is summarizing unbounded novel prose — a 2MB CI log with an unfamiliar failure — where deterministic extraction handles known shapes and the model handles the unknown. That is exactly what it already does, and its verification gate (advisory-only, never parsed) is already correct. So the job is right and only the scheduling and tag hygiene are broken.
recommendations.expected_effect: $0.00 direct dollar saving — state that plainly. Removes an unconditional 21GB GPU load on 803 tick invocations that can evict the operator's interactive Hermes agent, and removes the two-variant thrash condition. Attach it to R9's gate-output wrappers as the FAIL-path summarizer (advisory line only, never replacing the raw failing output).
recommendations.risk: None. The advisory-only contract must not be relaxed — mr-ollama's own history includes confabulating a slice description in test, which is precisely why nothing may ever gate on it.

recommendations.action: Fix the human-activity probe. Add `-not -path "*/.codegraph/*"` to the gate-3 probe at mr-native-tick.sh:240-244 (mr-spawn:35 already has it — reconcile the two divergent copies into one shared predicate), and exclude writes whose mtime post-dates this tick's own ff-only merge commit.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 72 of 72 in-window probe trips were false positives; 65 (90.3%) named machine-written CodeGraph index artifacts (codegraph.db-wal 25+7, daemon.log 17+16) and the remaining 7 were the loop's OWN merge writes (e.g. 2026-08-14T02:00:05Z tripped on ARCHITECTURE.md 7 minutes after the 01:53Z tick ff-merged PR#312, which `git show --stat 4d789bd` confirms touched it). Zero human-authored writes appear anywhere in the list. The in-line defense at mr-native-tick.sh:246-252 ('measured cost of the false trips is $0') measured the wrong axis — the loop has begun pre-emptively self-censoring ('composite launch deferred (own-write probe-trip risk, per doctrine)' cost 105 min), and 4 trips aborted staged launches outright.
recommendations.expected_effect: Under reframing A the latency is not the point; the point is that 13 cron trips lost a whole decision slot with no retry scheduled (mr-native-tick.sh:263 excludes src=cron), and the blessed merge->launch composite is currently a coin flip because performing the merge poisons the probe that gates the launch. Small dollars, near-zero effort, removes a self-inflicted decision-quality defect.
recommendations.risk: The stated reason for keeping .codegraph in scope is that excluding it could mask a genuine human edit inside a worktree. That risk is real but bounded: a human editing source will also touch a non-.codegraph path, and the exclusion is path-scoped to index artifacts only.

recommendations.action: Delete the dead ceremony. Remove from mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md: the feedback-doctrine blocks (L31, L34, L83, L105 — 4,927 chars total with the other dead blocks) and the retro-request block (L32); remove the `Items: <feedback-ledger ids>` mandate from mr-brief-template.md:31; delete or re-point the CENSUS line at mr-native-tick.sh:323; and retire the unwired scripts mr-metrics, mr-evidence, mr-retro-request, mr-selfcheck. Fix the stale weekly-budget figure at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:24 ($1,250, 2.2x off the config's 2783) as part of the same pass — or better, delete it when R2 removes the dollar model.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED as inert: feedback-ledger.jsonl has 189 rows, 0 since 2026-07-27, and its two terminal states (VERIFIED, SHIPPED-VERIFIED) have ZERO rows in the file's entire history — yet the prompt describes it as 'ACTIVE v1.0' on all 65 paid ticks and mr-feedback (15,911 B, the largest script) runs every tick against a frozen dataset. $MEM/retros/ has never been created. mr-metrics/mr-evidence/mr-retro-request/mr-selfcheck have 0 tick refs, 0 SSOT refs, 0 log hits. CENSUS reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines because mr-native-tick.sh:323 greps the SUPERVISOR tick's own log for subagents that only ever appear in the detached build session's log (transcript ground truth: 208 subagent runs in-window, of which CENSUS never once records planner, tester, doc-keeper, reducer-security-auditor, or desync-guard).
recommendations.expected_effect: BE HONEST: ~$13/year in token carry — the dollar saving rounds to zero, and 'trim the prompt to save tokens' is not a defensible recommendation at 0.087% of spend. Justify it entirely on signal integrity: labeling dead machinery ACTIVE degrades every other ACTIVE label in a 155-line prompt where one clause buried at char ~1,400 of a 3,296-char line drove the largest control failure of the window. ~26KB of dead control surface is 26KB of maintenance and misdirection.
recommendations.risk: None — all measured inert. Do NOT delete the weekly review in the same pass: it is the only generator of launchable work ($54-74 per run yielding 7-8 slices, i.e. $6.75-12.31 per build-ready slice, 5-9x cheaper per hour of runway than the attended heavy ceremony) and every milestone the loop built in-window traces to it.

recommendations.action: Restart the improvement loop itself, with a standing rule: land the counter one cycle before the change it measures. Schedule a fortnightly loop-retro whose input is the R1 utilization series + the R15 denominators, and whose output is a change to $MEM/mr-* (not to the game). Add a loop lens to mr-weekly-review-prompt.md, whose 306 lines currently scope it exclusively to 'the monster-realm subproject'.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: 46 of 51 loop-infra commits landed in a single 4-day burst (2026-07-24..27); the last real mechanism change was 2026-08-01; every one of the 20 commits touching memory/projects/mr-* since 2026-08-08 is mr-state.json bookkeeping. The supervisor prompt carries 21 dated incident parentheticals across exactly 7 dates, ALL in July 2026 and zero in August — so the doctrine is a frozen snapshot of what the loop knew on 2026-08-01, carrying nine separate 2026-07-26 fan-out rulings for an N that has never exceeded 2, while containing no rule about the failures that dominated this window. Meanwhile the loop's own self-improvement channel produces only GAME work: no weekly review has ever emitted a loop-improvement recommendation. The counter-before-change rule comes from a measured own-goal: the v3 push introduced the SUPERVISOR ledger row convention in the same commit as the intervention it was meant to measure, so its effect can never be computed (zero SUPERVISOR rows exist before 2026-07-24T15:32Z).
recommendations.expected_effect: No direct dollars. It is the mechanism that makes every recommendation above durable rather than a one-off: without it, this postmortem becomes another frozen July-2026 artifact by September. Cost is ~1 review-equivalent per fortnight (~$27/week amortized, <1pp of allowance).
recommendations.risk: Adds a recurring cost against a binding allowance. Cap it explicitly: fortnightly, <=2 deep-dive agents, and it must produce a diff to $MEM/mr-* or it does not run again.

root_causes.statement: The governor's weekly limit is overstated by 1.52x. Measured against real account telemetry, 1% of the weekly plan allowance costs ~$18.3 internal-ledger dollars, so the true allowance is ~$1,830 internal — not the configured $2,783. The governor week 2026-08-07->2026-08-14 consumed 98.3% of the allowance while reporting 64.7% and governor=NORMAL.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: THREE INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS, all MEASURED. (1) MARGINAL SLOPE: I extracted every seven_day rate_limit_info object from /tmp/mr_pass_*.log and /tmp/mr_native_tick_*.log (256 observations across 3 plan weeks) and joined each to the cumulative ledger sum at its own timestamp. Over 2026-08-08T22:28 (utilization 0.50, ledger $729.64) -> 2026-08-09T14:29 (utilization 0.83, ledger $1,330.27): delta-util 0.33 for delta-ledger $600.63 => $1,820 internal per 100% of allowance => 1 point = $18.20. (2) SINGLE-SLICE CROSS-CHECK: the operator independently states M21b-2 (ledger $274.3706, /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/memory/projects/monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl L603) consumed ~15% of a weekly allowance => 1 point = $18.29. (3) ENDPOINT: at the last pre-pause reading 2026-08-10T05:08, real utilization 0.90 against ledger $1,523.91 => 1 point = $16.93 (a lower bound; the ledger lags slice completion). Band $16.93-$18.29, centre ~$18.3. Applying $18.3: governor-week ledger $1,799.64 (I reproduced this figure exactly by replaying mr-situation:63-84 against the anchor 1784851200 in $MEM/.weekly-reset-anchor) = 98.3% of allowance. The governor reported $1,799.64/$2,783 = 64.7%, state NORMAL. Phase check: the internal anchor 1784851200 (2026-07-24T00:00Z) and the API's own resetsAt values (1786060800 = 2026-08-07T00:00Z, 1786665600 = 2026-08-14T00:00Z) differ by exactly 14 days — the internal week is PHASE-CORRECT; only its magnitude is wrong.
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: $MEM/mr-budget-config.json:2-9 derives weekly_limit_usd from ONE operator-reported observation on 2026-07-25 (internal_total_usd 1002 / drew_total_pct 0.36 = 2783). A single ratio point has no error bars and was never re-anchored despite the config's own instruction 'Re-anchor whenever Drew reports fresh percentages.' Step 2: the numerator of that ratio is itself model-dependent. mr-budget-config.json:39-46 prices fable by explicit guess — '_note: ESTIMATE 1.5x opus (overcount = earlier kill = safe); CALIBRATE from first fable run' — and that calibration never ran. Fable was ~57% of window spend, so the dominant model carries the guessed price. Step 3: the denominator is incomplete. The ledger cannot see spec-elaboration ceremony ($482.03 measured from transcripts, $0.00 in the ledger), weekly reviews (one $0.00 'visibility-only' row ever), resume passes after a FINISHED row is written ($46.84 measured), or the operator's usage on other machines. Step 4: because both numerator and denominator are wrong in the SAME direction (understating consumption), the error compounds into a governor that believes it has 52% more room than it has. Step 5: SOFT-PAUSE (0.90) and HARD-STOP (0.97) are defined as fractions of that inflated limit, so they are unreachable in practice — 205 'governor=' occurrences in $MEM/mr-native-tick.log, all NORMAL, zero trips in the loop's entire life.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The entire weekly allowance (100%) was spent believing 64.7% was spent. Direct consequence: M21b-2 was launched 2026-08-10T09:08:06Z, four hours AFTER the account crossed 90% real utilization (reading at 05:08), and consumed a further ~15% of allowance. The prior plan week (reset 2026-08-07T00:00Z) reached utilization 0.97 and logged a real hard event — {"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true} in /tmp/mr_native_tick_native-20260805T112040Z-1651311.log — i.e. that week actually burned PURCHASED credits.

root_causes.statement: The true, account-wide, self-calibrating telemetry the governor needs is already flowing through two files the loop polls every 20 seconds, and the doctrine explicitly instructs the loop to throw it away.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. Every headless run's stream-json log carries rate_limit_info objects. Verified live: 101 of the 188 surviving /tmp/mr_pass_*.log and /tmp/mr_native_tick_*.log files contain 'seven_day'; 78 of 151 tick logs and slice logs alike (mr_pass_M21c.log 5 occurrences, mr_pass_m20d.log 20, mr_pass_13r-a.log 3). Verified field set: {"status":"allowed_warning","resetsAt":1786060800,"rateLimitType":"seven_day","utilization":0.32,"isUsingOverage":false}. 256 seven_day observations across three plan weeks; per-week max utilization 0.97 / 0.90 / 0.57 with the 0.97 week also carrying rejected=1 and overage=1. resetsAt values decode to Thursday 00:00Z, exactly matching $MEM/.weekly-reset-anchor. THE DISCARD IS EXPLICIT: $MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 enumerates the field set as '{status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage}' — omitting `utilization` from its own schema assertion — and instructs 'Trip ONLY on status == "rejected" ... tripping on it would kill every live slice and park the loop for days over a utilization notice.' The prose uses the word 'utilization' while the rule discards the number. Mechanically, $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh:348-405 does parse rate_limit_info with a proper JSON walker — but ONLY inside the SPAWN-FAIL branch (rc != 0), and its predicate at :364 is `str(o.get("status")) == "rejected"`. On a successful tick nothing is parsed. $MEM/mr-cost-watch:78-100 polls /tmp/mr_pass_$S.log every 20s for the whole life of every slice and already writes to mr-native-tick.log via its own log() — it reads the exact bytes containing utilization and ignores them.
root_causes.mechanism: The design treats a continuous gauge as a binary trip-wire. The reasoning at prompt:116 is CORRECT about not tripping on allowed_warning — an allowlist on 'rejected' is right for a kill decision. But having decided not to TRIP on the event, the doctrine discards the event entirely rather than reading the number inside it. So the loop built a synthetic dollar model (RC-1) to estimate a quantity the API was reporting to it directly, account-wide, every 20 seconds, for free. Compounding this: the logs carrying the signal live in /tmp and are ephemeral — 4 in-window slice logs (M21a, m20a, M21b-2, 14r-f) no longer exist and 13r-c's and m20c's were overwritten by later reruns of the same slice name — so the only accurate record of real consumption is being deleted on a rolling basis.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 100% of the instrumentation failure in RC-1 is attributable here. The signal would also have been free of RC-1's two structural blind spots: being account-level it automatically includes the $482.03 of ledger-invisible ceremony spend, the weekly reviews, the $46.84 of dropped resume passes, and the operator's usage on other machines — none of which any local ledger can ever see. Sampling property that makes it strictly better than the model: mr-cost-watch polls a live slice log every 20s, so readings are near-continuous exactly while credits are burning, and stale only while nothing is running (i.e. while nothing is burning).

root_causes.statement: There is no spend-rate control of any kind. Every cost threshold in the system is advisory, and the only functioning brake on the weekly allowance is the operator personally watching usage and running mr-supervisor-disable.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. $MEM/mr-budget-config.json:55 `"costwatch_enforce": false`. All 23 COSTWATCH 'started' lines in the window carry enforce=0. In-window COSTWATCH census: 12 WARN, 10 STOP-MONITOR, 4 HARD-MONITOR, 77 LOG-STALL, zero enforcement actions, zero .fired files. Four slices exceeded their own declared tier cap in real ledger dollars with no intervention: M21b-2 182.9% ($274.37/$150), M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%. The only cost control that ever fires is retrospective: mr-native-tick.sh:96-105 computes single_run_alert_usd post-hoc at reconcile time; the sole in-window occurrence (mr-native-tick.log L2668, 2026-08-10T14:05:43Z, M21b-2 $274.3706) post-dates the last dollar by one second and the first dollar by 4h58m, and its only action was a handoff note. Meanwhile $MEM/mr-brief-template.md:33 tells every build session '**BUDGET: $<CAP_USD> for this slice (advisory thresholds; only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical).**' — rendered verbatim into every brief (verified in /tmp/mr_pass_13r-d.md:33 and /tmp/mr_pass_14r-g.md:34) — asserting a mechanical ceiling that does not exist. THE OPERATOR IS THE BRAKE: the disabled flag appeared between 2026-08-10T12:01:59Z and 13:00:07Z, during which no supervisor session ran, while M21b-2 was live and COSTWATCH was logging HARD-MONITOR 125%; the operator confirms he runs /home/mdrewt/.local/bin/mr-supervisor-disable when he sees usage approaching the cap. That pause worked: the review week peaked at 0.90 with rejected=0 and overage=0, whereas the unpaused prior week reached 0.97 with rejected=1 and overage=1.
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: enforcement was deliberately disabled and the reason is documented at $MEM/mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 — 'all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0; a kill strands locks and hard-blocks relaunch until a human edits cap_override.' Step 2: that objection is real but is a CALIBRATION defect, not an argument against caps. Thresholds are applied to the `raw` estimate (mr-cost-watch:82) whose measured ledger/raw ratio ranges 0.6370 (m20b) to 1.0076 (M21c) — so a nominal $60 cap actually bites anywhere between $38.22 and $60.46 of real spend. Two of the four historical trips would have fired at 81.7% and 87.9% of cap. The estimator has two directly observable bugs: no dedup by message.id (1.75 usage events per distinct message; msg_011Ce3KRiX1JHgYb9mE2aArW appears 3x with identical usage), and cache-creation priced entirely at the 5-minute rate while 17.9% of cache-creation tokens (6.24M of 34.93M) are ephemeral_1h, priced 1.6x higher. Step 3: because nobody trusted the numbers, nobody armed the caps; because nobody armed the caps, the only brake left is a human. Step 4: the operator's brake works but requires vigilance he has explicitly asked to be relieved of (objective G.3), and it is available only when he happens to be looking.
root_causes.quantified_cost: M21b-2 alone: $274.37 = ~15% of the weekly allowance against a $150 cap, of which ~5% of allowance ($91) is above the 10%-of-allowance ceiling a correctly denominated cap would impose. Counterfactual with enforce=true across the window: $192.85 of spend prevented (~10.5% of allowance). Prior week: one measured overage event (rejected + isUsingOverage=true), i.e. the loop converted plan credits into purchased credits at least once in the three weeks observable — 1 week in 3.

root_causes.statement: 90.9% of build-session spend is cache mechanics, not generation, and no context management of any kind is configured — so every token added to a session's prefix is re-billed on every remaining turn of that session.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED, two independent methods agreeing. Transcript-level (23 build sessions, deduped by message.id): cache_read $1,012.79 (65.3%), cache_creation $396.98 (25.6%), output $140.81 (9.1%), fresh input $0.94 (0.06%), total $1,551.52. Estimator-level (re-running mr-cost-watch's own pricing formula term-by-term over 9 surviving pass logs, reproducing the logged COSTWATCH raw totals to the cent): cache read 68.0%, cache write 31.8%, new input 0.1%, output 0.1%. Parent prompt-volume decomposition (703.0M tokens over 2,718 turns): assistant thinking/output carried forward 243.9M (34.7%, computed exactly from usage.output_tokens as output_i x (N-i)), static preamble x turns 120.4M (17.1%), Bash results 69.7M (9.9%), Read results 62.4M (8.9%), Agent results 48.2M (6.9%). ZERO CONTEXT MANAGEMENT: grep for isCompactSummary / compact_boundary across all 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts returns no matches; final contexts reached 295,092 / 454,481 / 611,322 tokens. I confirmed the cause at the invocation site — $MEM/mr-launch.sh:85, :124, :139 invoke plain `claude --model "$MODEL" --effort "$EFFORT" --dangerously-skip-permissions -p ...` with no context-management flag. Structural asymmetry: parent preamble measures 44,288 tokens vs subagent median 11,103 — 4x — and the launch brief is only 3,152 tokens of that, so ~41K is harness-static. 32.2% of all parent prompt volume (226.1M tokens) is consumed BEFORE the first edit to a repo file (median first edit at turn 50; range 12.0% for 13r-f to 77.0% for m20d).
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: a slice session runs 230-762 turns with an average ~150k tokens of context re-read per turn. Step 2: nothing ever prunes the prefix — no compaction, no thinking-block clearing — so a block added at turn i of N is billed N-i more times. Step 3: the largest single bucket is the model's own thinking, which is pure re-read cost with no downstream consumer once the turn is committed. Step 4: the second largest is a static preamble that by definition never changes. Step 5: the orchestrator compounds this by navigating with 791 Bash grep/sed/cat/ls calls producing 2,080,724 chars of tool output, while making ZERO codegraph_explore calls despite .codegraph/ existing at both repo roots and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md mandating it — subagents comply (47 codegraph + 89 cbm calls), parents do not (0 codegraph, 4 cbm). Step 6: early large reads are the worst shape — a 12K-token read at turn 1 of a 180-turn session costs ~2.4M cache-read tokens; the same read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M. $MEM/monster-realm-handoff.md is 428,676 bytes (~107K tokens, 1,716 lines) and orientation greps against it returned 21,481-27,753 chars at turn 4.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$296/week of the $1,551 build base is structurally re-read text with no new information: carried thinking ~$166 + static preamble ~$130. At $18.3 per allowance point that is ~16.2% of the weekly allowance. Orientation-before-first-edit is a further $238 of parent spend (~13% of allowance), of which the 3.4x spread between best (12%) and worst (77%) slice is the addressable part. Correction to the obvious hypothesis: repeated file reads are NOT the lever — 40 redundant reads of 210 (19%) cost only ~$4.

root_causes.statement: 24.2% of the weekly allowance went to remediating the loop's own prior output, and the mechanism that generates that backlog is structural: the touches: discipline that enables fan-out forbids in-scope fixes, which are then written into ADR 'Residuals' prose that nothing mechanically reads.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. Governor week 2026-08-07->2026-08-14, $1,799.64 across 24 slices, partitioned by milestone lineage: NEW durable capability $1,287.74 (71.6%) = m20a-e $524.26 + M21a/b/c+M21b-2 $547.33 + EG4/EG5 $216.15; REMEDIATION $443.61 (24.6%) = 12r-a..f $378.75 + 13r-c $64.86; ORCHESTRATION (SUPERVISOR ticks) $68.31 (3.8%). Lifetime across the 710-row ledger the remediation share is 46.6% of named-slice spend. SMOKING GUN for the mechanism: /home/mdrewt/projects/ai-apps/claude-harness/projects/monster-realm/docs/adr/0165-changelog-freshness-nightly-drift-check.md:9, Status Accepted, slice 11r-d — 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared `touches:`.' 11r-i merged 2026-08-02 and did not implement it; it was finally built by 13r-g on 2026-08-15, 15 days after Acceptance. Corpus-wide surface: 21 of 165 ADRs carry a 'Residuals / follow-ups' section and grep finds 78 defer/park phrases ('deferred to' 45, 'a later slice' 11, 'future slice' 10, 'parked to' 8). There is no mechanism converting any of them into queued work. Measured disclosure->remediation latency over 10 traceable items: mean 13.1 days, median 14, max 20. THE CLASS REPRODUCED ITSELF INSIDE ITS OWN REMEDIATION: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124 `const KNOWN_UNMIGRATED_CAP = 7;` parks seven *-security.eval.mjs gates to owner '14r-c-2', and `grep -rl 14r-c-2` over specs/monster-realm-v2/*.md, PLAN.md and mr-state.json returns ZERO hits. Two of those seven are documented as reproducibly swallowing the scan needle ('LIVE, REPRODUCIBLE ADR-0181 hazard ... the URL-scheme literal truncates the scan and blinds every ban clause downstream').
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: fan-out safety requires each slice to declare a disjoint touches: path set. Step 2: a slice discovering a defect outside its declared set cannot fix it without breaking disjointness. Step 3: the correct-looking move is to document it in the ADR's Residuals section. Step 4: nothing reads Residuals sections — they are prose in a corpus growing ~770 lines/day whose newest 18 ADRs average 342 lines (3.8x the historical 91). Step 5: the item is rediscovered weeks later by a human-instigated multi-lens weekly review — the most expensive possible detector. Step 6: the review manufactures a fresh 6-9 slice residual milestone, which is the loop's de facto perpetual fuel supply, which is why nobody noticed that forward-milestone inventory had been unauthored for 49 days. Thirteen such milestones now exist (85 slices) with output flat at 6-9 per cycle and cadence accelerating 7d -> 6d -> 3d -> 4d: a treadmill, not a converging loop.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 24.2% of the weekly allowance (~$444) on remediation in the governor week; 35.4% in the review window; 46.6% lifetime. Directly attributable rework inside that: 13r-c re-spawn $14.45 (100% waste — mr-state.json queue[2] records 'found 13r-c's ORIGINAL scope already merged 2026-08-09 as PR#309 -- this was a stale-queue re-spawn'), 14r-e resume leg $36.19, m20c attempt-2 $6.25. Seven security gates are measurably blind right now, two of them provably passing GREEN on code they exist to reject, after $115.97 was spent across 13r-c and 14r-c on exactly that migration.

root_causes.statement: Spec starvation does not waste idle hours (which are free) — it forces queue replenishment through an operator-attended interactive channel that costs 8x more per unit of runway than the unattended channel that already exists and already works.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. Two supply channels with measured cost per build-ready slice. UNATTENDED (weekly review, a Cowork scheduled task per $MEM/mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7): rev12 $73.88 -> 6 slices ($12.31/slice), rev13 $54.00 -> 8 slices ($6.75/slice), rev14 $54.59 -> 7 slices ($7.80/slice), attributed from mr-usage-daily.jsonl cowork_est_usd against a non-review-day baseline of $0.65-$1.55. ATTENDED (heavy ceremony): session 4244d71c (M21+M20 elaboration, 2026-08-08) = $344.15 measured from parent + 70 subagent transcripts, 3,842 assistant messages, plus 9.2h of operator wall-clock; session bc3f31de (M21b-2, 2026-08-10) = $137.88 plus 4.1h operator wall-clock. Per build-ready slice: $53.56 attended vs $6.75-$12.31 unattended — 4-8x. Per hour of loop runway: ~$3.0/h unattended vs $15.6/h and $27.6/h attended. BOTH ceremonies are invisible to the ledger and the governor: $482.03 measured, $0.00 recorded; a scan of all 2026-08-08/09/10 non-SUPERVISOR ledger rows finds no row for either session. BOTH ran on sonnet by accidental session inheritance (4244d71c: 569 of 569 assistant messages claude-sonnet-5; its first user message is verbatim the supervisor prompt, i.e. the operator continued a cron tick) while every slice they feed runs opus@high or fable@xhigh. THE ELABORATION CAPABILITY IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN but structurally unreachable: specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md:13,:37 make 'elaborate a sketch to a build-ready spec' step 1 of the per-milestone procedure, but a slice can only be launched via /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.vars.json = {slice, model, effort, adr, touches, target_desc,...} and a sketch has no slice id and no touches: to put in it. The supervisor records this as policy: ledger 2026-08-08T01:03:32Z 'spec-authoring is not a native-tick-assignable action per doctrine'.
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: the only unattended supply channel is the weekly review, and $MEM/mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:249-250 scopes its output to 'M-postgate-<review-lineage-name>.spec.md, continuing the review-residuals naming lineage' — structurally it can only produce fix-up work. Step 2: forward-milestone inventory therefore requires an attended ceremony. Step 3: no watermark or replenishment trigger exists anywhere — grep for 'replenish|inventory|queue_depth|build.?ready|backlog' over all mr-* scripts returns ZERO hits — so the queue is only refilled after it is already empty. Step 4: refilling under time pressure with the operator present routes to the expensive interactive channel, which has no cost cap, no watcher, and writes no ledger row. Step 5: mr-state.json's `queue` field is 58 free-form past-tense narrative strings, not a forward plan (the weekly-review SSOT says so at :257-258: 'its queue[] is a narrative journal, not a work queue'), and the per-slice `after:` dependency field has no mechanical consumer (grep 'after:' over mr-*.sh, mr-situation, mr-spawn, mr-disjoint returns zero hits) — so 'is anything launchable?' is re-derived from prose by a sonnet tick every hour, and got it wrong on 2026-08-10 while 7 fully-decomposed slices sat in a spec committed 5 hours earlier.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$482 of attended ceremony in the window = ~26% of a weekly allowance, at 4-8x the unattended unit cost. Routing the DECOMPOSITION half of that through the unattended channel would cost ~$60-110 instead. Net redirectable: ~20% of weekly allowance. Note this is spend the governor cannot currently see at all, so it is 20% of allowance being consumed entirely outside the control loop.

root_causes.statement: Every mechanical standdown gate in the tick exits before the merge path, so a credit-driven pause strands finished, paid-for work — violating the operator's own finish-in-flight policy and destroying value already bought.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh gate ordering: gate -1 (disabled flag) at :123-127 exits for all sources, requeueing any event; gate 2 (rate-limit) at :213-236 does `case "$RLGATE" in BLOCKED_UNTIL_*) log ...; exit 0;; esac` with no source exemption. Consequence, measured: 'COSTWATCH M21b-2 done-file present, exiting' at 2026-08-10T14:05:13Z; SPEND-ALERT at 14:05:42Z; then at 14:05:43Z 'src=done SKIP disabled-flag (event requeued: .../pending-events/M21b-2.done.md)'. That event was archived as pending-events/archive/1786672771.M21b-2.done.md = 2026-08-14T01:59:31Z — 83.90 hours later. FINISHED->MERGED latency for M21b-2 was 84.35h against a median of 0.47h for the other 20 slices. So the single most expensive slice of the week ($274.37, ~15% of allowance) sat finished, PR-open and locally-green for 3.5 days. CONTRAST — the fix already exists 20 lines away: gate -0.5 for .blocked-on-human at :144-159 does all three things gate -1 does not: it self-lifts when a named wake_file appears (:148 'GATE-LIFTED wake_file present'), it has a 7-day safety expiry (:157-158), and it applies ONLY to `[ "$SRC" = "cron" ]` so event ticks pass through. The auto-rearm primitive also already exists: $MEM/mr-reset-watch sleeps until a recorded resetsAt +120s then writes pending-events/rate-limit.reset.md and fires a tick. And the checkpoint-not-kill protocol is already fully specified at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 — stop flags, ~10 min grace, fallback-park via 'git add -A && git commit -m "wip(<slice>): supervisor checkpoint" && git push', outcome PARKED with no park-counter bump, never merge a wip branch.
root_causes.mechanism: Step 1: pauses are implemented as tick-level exits rather than launch-level refusals. Step 2: a tick does three separable things — decide/launch, merge/record, and watch — but the gate cannot distinguish them, so pausing launches also pauses merges. Step 3: a finished slice's value is only realised at merge, so pausing at the tick level converts already-spent credits into stranded work. Step 4: mr-state.json currently has rate_limit_resets_at = None and $MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled exists (0 bytes, mtime 2026-08-15 17:58), i.e. the loop is presently held by the human-only switch with no self-clearing path, exactly as it was for 85 hours.
root_causes.quantified_cost: One event, 83.90h stranded, on the window's most expensive slice (~15% of allowance already spent and unrealised). Structurally this converts any future credit pause — including the correct, deliberate one the operator performed — into a value-destroying event rather than a value-preserving one. Zero new machinery is required to fix it: the source-exemption pattern, the auto-rearm watcher, and the checkpoint protocol all already exist in the tree.

recommendations.action: Harvest and persist the real telemetry. Add a ~15-line python block to $MEM/mr-cost-watch's existing 20s poll loop (after the PRICE-ERR case at :80) that JSON-parses each new line of /tmp/mr_pass_$S.log for rate_limit_info objects with rateLimitType=="seven_day" and appends {ts, utilization, resetsAt, status, isUsingOverage, overageInUse, source:slice} to a new append-only file $MEM/mr-plan-usage.jsonl. Add the identical harvest to $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh immediately after the spawn at :308 over $TLOG, on EVERY exit code (not only the SPAWN-FAIL branch at :348) — reuse the existing walk() JSON walker at :356-376 but widen its predicate from status=="rejected" to "any seven_day object carrying utilization". Parse with /usr/bin/python3 over JSON, never grep, per the existing doctrine at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116. Also copy each /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log to $MEM/logs/<slice>.<launch-epoch>.log.zst on the done-event so the record survives /tmp and same-name reruns.
recommendations.rationale: The signal is already flowing through both files and both already have a python parser and a poll loop pointed at them. This is a read, not a model. Being account-level it automatically includes the $482.03 of ledger-invisible ceremony spend, the weekly reviews, the $46.84 of dropped resume passes, and the operator's other-machine usage — every blind spot in RC-1's denominator — and it self-calibrates when the plan changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Enabling, not directly credit-freeing. Replaces a governor that read 64.7% when the truth was 98.3% with one accurate to +/-1 percentage point (the field's quantisation). Unblocks R2-R6, which together de-risk ~15% of allowance and remove the overage exposure that fired in 1 of the 3 observable weeks. Cost to run: $0 — both harvest points are zero-token shell/python.
recommendations.risk: Low. Purely additive and read-only; if the field set drifts the harvest writes nothing and the existing $-model remains as fallback. Do NOT let the harvest trip anything on its own — R3 owns the decisions. One real caveat: log lines can be large, so parse incrementally by byte offset rather than re-reading the whole file every 20s.

recommendations.action: Rewrite the governor to reason in percent of weekly plan allowance. In $MEM/mr-situation, replace the budget() function's d7_usd/weekly_limit_usd computation (:63-84, currently summing ledger cost_usd since the .weekly-reset-anchor) with: read the newest row of $MEM/mr-plan-usage.jsonl; emit {utilization, utilization_ts, resetsAt, stale_minutes, isUsingOverage, projected_utilization, pace_line, state}. Compute projected_utilization = utilization + (ledger spend since utilization_ts / 18.3 / 100) — using the ledger only as a RELATIVE meter between readings, never as an absolute scale. Compute pace_line = elapsed_fraction_of_plan_week. Keep the $-model emitting alongside for one week as a shadow, labelled advisory, then delete it. Update $MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:24-27 to describe utilization states instead of the stale '$1,250 API-equiv' text, and add `utilization` to the field-set assertion at :116.
recommendations.rationale: Operator decision G.2. The synthetic dollar model is wrong by a measured 1.52x in the unsafe direction, is built on one un-repeated 2026-07-25 observation, and prices its dominant model (fable, ~57% of spend) by an admitted uncalibrated guess. No amount of repair fixes a model whose denominator structurally cannot see 20-26% of consumption.
recommendations.expected_effect: Turns SOFT-PAUSE/HARD-STOP from unreachable (205 governor= readings, all NORMAL, zero trips ever) into reachable. Against the measured governor week this alone moves the reported figure from 64.7% to 98.3%, which is the precondition for every pacing decision below.
recommendations.risk: Medium — staleness is the real hazard. utilization is observed only while a session runs, is quantised to whole percent, and lags. Mitigations, in order: (a) mr-cost-watch samples every 20s while any slice is live, so the reading is freshest exactly when credits are burning and stale only when nothing is burning; (b) between readings extrapolate with the ledger delta (a fine relative meter even though its absolute scale is wrong); (c) always round pessimistically; (d) treat a reading older than 90 minutes as stale and add a fixed 3-point safety margin. Do NOT delete the $-model until one full week of shadow agreement.

recommendations.action: Add a launch-selective pacing gate. In $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh insert a new gate 2.5 AFTER the rate-limit gate at :236 and BEFORE the human-activity probe at :238, which never exits the tick — it exports MR_PACE_STATE for the supervisor session and is enforced in $MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md as a launch rule. States, driven by projected_utilization U and pace_line P from R2: NORMAL (U < min(P+10pp, 82%)) launch freely up to N_MAX; PACED (U >= P+10pp) at most 1 concurrent slice and prefer the routine tier; SCARCITY (U >= 82%) FINISH IN-FLIGHT, START NOTHING NEW — merges, reviews, records, CI-watches and parks all still permitted; CHECKPOINT (U >= 93%) touch /tmp/mr_stop_all and each /tmp/mr_stop_<slice>, then run the existing park protocol at prompt:116 verbatim. The 82% SCARCITY threshold is 100% minus an 18-point reserve = (N_MAX 2 x the 8%-of-allowance hard cap from R5) + 2 points of merge/review overhead.
recommendations.rationale: Operator decision G.1 and finding E: the week's allowance was consumed in ~3.5 active days with no rate control. The reserve is sized so that whatever is running when SCARCITY trips can always be finished, reviewed and merged — stranding a half-done slice is worse than idling, and idling is free. The gate must be launch-selective, not tick-selective, because RC-7 shows tick-level gates strand finished work.
recommendations.expected_effect: Applied to the measured week: 82% was crossed ~2026-08-09T14:11. m20e (in flight) finishes and merges normally; M21b-2 — which was actually launched 2026-08-10T09:08, four hours after the account passed 90% — is never launched at that point and instead starts at the 2026-08-14 reset with a full week ahead of it. Directly de-risks the ~15% of allowance that slice consumed, and the week ends at ~90% with the operator never touching mr-supervisor-disable.
recommendations.risk: Medium. Two things to get right: (1) SCARCITY must not block merges, records or CI-watch — if it does it reproduces the 83.9h M21b-2 stall; (2) do not set SCARCITY below ~80% or the loop idles with usable allowance left, which is a pure loss under a use-it-or-lose-it weekly plan. Pick 82% and tune from the mr-plan-usage.jsonl history after two weeks.

recommendations.action: Automatic re-arm at the weekly reset, so the operator never hand-clears a credit pause. On entering SCARCITY or CHECKPOINT, write the seven_day resetsAt into mr-state.json's existing rate_limit_resets_at field (the writer already exists at $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh:399) and spawn $MEM/mr-reset-watch <resetsAt> detached — that script already sleeps until reset+120s, writes pending-events/rate-limit.reset.md and fires a tick. THEN make two one-line gate fixes: (a) gate 2 at :236 must exempt non-cron sources exactly as gate -0.5 does at :144 — change the exit to fire only when [ "$SRC" = "cron" ], so done/ci/reset events still merge, record and park; (b) give the human-only $MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled flag the same wake_file + 7-day expiry treatment gate -0.5 already implements at :148 and :157-158, and have mr-supervisor-disable stamp a reason and an auto-expiry into the file.
recommendations.rationale: Objective G.3. Every primitive needed already exists in the tree and is already proven on the .blocked-on-human path; the credit path just never got them. Credit standdowns are free (a skipped cron tick spawns no model and costs $0 — 108 in-window SKIP lines cost nothing), so a self-clearing standdown is strictly better than a human-cleared one.
recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates the operator's manual disable/enable cycle for credit reasons entirely, and closes the 83.9h stranded-merge class. Recovers the ~15% of allowance already spent on M21b-2 as realised value at the next tick rather than 3.5 days later.
recommendations.risk: Low, but gate ordering is load-bearing: the disabled flag currently sits ABOVE the pending-event fastpath, which is exactly why a real completion event sat 83.9 hours. Verify with a dry-run that a done-event tick reaches the merge path while gate 2 is armed.

recommendations.action: Arm per-slice caps with checkpoint semantics, denominated in allowance percent. In $MEM/mr-budget-config.json replace slice_caps_usd with slice_caps_pct_allowance: {hard: 8, routine: 4, content: 4, absolute_ceiling: 10} and set costwatch_enforce: true. In $MEM/mr-cost-watch:82 threshold on the CALIBRATED sum, not `raw` — and first fix the two measured pricing bugs so calibrated means something: dedup usage events by message.id (measured 1.75 events per distinct message, e.g. msg_011Ce3KRiX1JHgYb9mE2aArW appearing 3x with identical usage), and price cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens at cache_write_1h (17.9% of cache-creation tokens, 6.24M of 34.93M, currently billed at the 5m rate). At 100% of cap set the existing cooperative /tmp/mr_stop_<slice> flag; at the 10% absolute ceiling run the park protocol — NEVER the TERM/KILL path at :106-113. Finally, correct $MEM/mr-brief-template.md:33, which currently tells every build session 'only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical' when nothing is.
recommendations.rationale: Caps set from the MEASURED distribution: fable/hard n=10 mean $123.49 = 6.75% of allowance, opus/routine n=11 mean $56.66 = 3.10%, and the single outlier M21b-2 $274.37 = 15.0%. 8%/4% covers the observed p90 of each tier; the 10% ceiling catches only genuine runaways. The README's documented objection to arming ('all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0') is a calibration defect — measured ledger/raw spans 0.6370 to 1.0076, so a $60 cap actually bites between $38.22 and $60.46 — not an argument against caps. Checkpoint rather than kill satisfies G.1 and reuses the park protocol already specified at prompt:116.
recommendations.expected_effect: M21b-2 checkpoints at ~10% of allowance instead of running to 15%: ~5% of allowance preserved on that one slice. Across the window the enforcement counterfactual is $192.85 prevented = ~10.5% of allowance, and with the two pricing bugs fixed the false-trip rate that justified disablement collapses (the 0.637-1.008 spread narrows toward 1.0).
recommendations.risk: Medium. Arm on ONE routine slice first and verify the checkpoint leaves a clean wip commit that the next tick can resume — the README's fear of stranded locks is legitimate. Keep the LOG-STALL suspension at :94 (77 in-window stall onsets: never take hard action on a blind watcher). Note the pre-existing arming precondition (adversarial-review condition F3, mr-budget-config.json:56) is now satisfied 46 times over by the (WARN-time raw, final raw, ledger) triples already in the tick log.

recommendations.action: Overage tripwire. In the R1 harvest, treat any observation with isUsingOverage==true OR overageInUse==true OR status=="rejected" as an immediate CHECKPOINT regardless of utilization: set /tmp/mr_stop_all, run the park protocol, write a BLOCKER to the handoff, arm rate_limit_resets_at + mr-reset-watch, and send the operator a push notification. Record the event in $MEM/mr-plan-usage.jsonl with a distinct kind so overage weeks are countable afterwards.
recommendations.rationale: Objective F. Auto-purchase is ON, so an uncapped run silently converts cheap plan credits into expensive purchased ones with no local signal whatsoever. This is not hypothetical: the plan week ending 2026-08-07 reached utilization 0.97 and logged {"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true} in /tmp/mr_native_tick_native-20260805T112040Z-1651311.log — the loop bought overage and nothing in the tree noticed or recorded it.
recommendations.expected_effect: Converts overage from silent and unbounded to bounded by one checkpoint cycle (~10 min grace plus the park). Measured base rate: 1 overage week in 3 observable weeks; the review week avoided it only because the operator was watching. Eliminates that dependency on operator vigilance.
recommendations.risk: Low. The one real judgement call belongs to the operator, not the design: whether finishing an in-flight hard slice is ever worth buying overage. Default to never; make it a single config flag so it can be relaxed without a code change.

recommendations.action: Attack context volume per turn — the single largest halvable class. Four changes, in measured-value order: (1) Split $MEM/monster-realm-handoff.md (428,676 bytes, ~107K tokens, 1,716 lines, 154 sections) into the existing archive files and have the brief point orientation at a per-slice memo instead of grepping the rolling log — measured orientation greps against it returned 21,481-27,753 chars at turn 4, each costing ~1.0M carried tokens. (2) Add one line to $MEM/mr-brief-template.md routing the ORCHESTRATOR to codegraph_explore before Bash navigation — parents made 0 codegraph and 4 cbm calls while making 791 grep/sed/cat/ls calls producing 2,080,724 chars; subagents already comply with 47 codegraph + 89 cbm calls, so this is a brief-level fix, not a tooling one. (3) Audit the 44,288-token parent preamble against the 11,103-token subagent preamble and defer unused MCP servers (Postman, Google Drive, Indeed, Audible, ZipRecruiter are loaded in every build session and called in none). (4) SEPARATELY, verify whether the installed CLI exposes context compaction or the context-editing clear_thinking strategy — $MEM/mr-launch.sh:85/:124/:139 invoke plain `claude -p` with no context management and zero compaction events exist across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts. Adopt only if verified; do not assume.
recommendations.rationale: 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics and only 9.1% buys tokens the model produces, so a lever that shrinks per-turn context is ~7x more valuable than one that shrinks output. This is also the only lever that reduces the cost of KEEPING every current behaviour — it does not trade away any quality. Correction to the obvious hypothesis: repeated file reads are NOT the lever (40 of 210, ~$4); size and TIMING are — a 12K-token read at turn 1 of a 180-turn session costs ~2.4M cache-read tokens, the same read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M.
recommendations.expected_effect: Items (1)-(3) target the measured $296/week of pure re-read (carried thinking $166 + static preamble $130) plus the 32.2% of parent volume consumed before the first repo edit. A conservative 30% reduction in that addressable share frees ~5-8% of weekly allowance; the 3.4x spread between the best slice (13r-f, 12.0% orientation) and the worst (m20d, 77.0%) shows the headroom is real. If (4) verifies, thinking-block clearing at a 60% rate adds a further ~$100/week (~5.5% of allowance).
recommendations.risk: Low for (1)-(3) — all are brief and file-layout changes with no behavioural risk. Medium for (4): compaction can drop context an agent still needs mid-slice; gate adoption on one routine slice and compare attempts and audit outcomes. Do NOT shorten the brief itself — at 3,152 tokens it is 7% of the preamble, it is dense and accurate, and its TARGET_DESC is the healthiest artifact in the system.

recommendations.action: Expand touches: by the brief's own companion rules before running mr-disjoint. The brief grants every slice ALWAYS-in-scope companions — '(a) sibling test files of any declared code file (e.g. *.test.ts next to a declared .ts), and (b) docs/adr/**, docs/knowledge/**, CHANGELOG.md, ARCHITECTURE.md'. Make that clause machine-readable and have $MEM/mr-disjoint expand each slice's declared set by it before emitting a SAFE verdict, and treat the clause-(b) doc set (ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/adr/DIGEST.md) as a known shared axis that fan-out either serialises or auto-merges.
recommendations.rationale: The gate is structurally unable to detect the collisions it exists to prevent. 14r-c declared client/src/main.wiring.test.ts; 14r-e declared client/src/main.ts — disjoint on paper, and mr-disjoint returned SAFE. But main.wiring.test.ts is a *.test.ts sibling of main.ts, so both slices legitimately owned it. Outcome: ledger 2026-08-14T14:36 '14r-e PARKED — conflict+regression-suspect: PR#318 CONFLICTING vs master 9b924f3 (shared file client/src/main.wiring.test.ts with merged 14r-c)'. The 14r-e park memo states it plainly: '14r-c's fan-out disjointness held on paper, not in practice.' 14r-b hit the clause-(b) form: 'conflict set was ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md' — which every concurrent pair is guaranteed to collide on.
recommendations.expected_effect: Directly prevents the 14r-e resume leg ($36.19 measured, unrecorded in the ledger) plus its park tick, relaunch tick and supervisor adjudication. 3 of ~20 in-window merges hit sibling conflicts (m20d, 14r-b, 14r-e); eliminating that class frees ~2-3% of weekly allowance and, more importantly, removes a rework source that scales with fan-out width.
recommendations.risk: Low. Expanding the set makes mr-disjoint strictly more conservative, so the failure mode is fewer fan-out pairs, not unsafe ones. Watch for over-serialisation on the doc axis — auto-merge is preferable to serialising there.

recommendations.action: Retire the gating_test_audit grep and replace it with the review gauntlet it is not. In $MEM/mr-audit:51-61, drop the unconditional tier=hard FLAG at :58-59, exclude comment spans and import-line reflow from the removed_or_modified_asserts count at :54, anchor the skip-marker regex at :56 to test-framework call sites so `.iter().skip()` stops matching `test.skip`, and drop the test-path pathspec for the SUPPRESSION pass only so `#[allow(...)]`/`@ts-ignore` added to PRODUCTION source becomes visible (currently invisible by construction). If precision does not exceed 0 after those fixes, delete the gate. Separately re-point or delete the CENSUS line at $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh:323, which greps the supervisor tick's own log for subagent types and therefore reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines while 208 subagent runs actually occurred.
recommendations.rationale: Measured precision is 0/11 in-window and 0 of ~28 across the entire v3 era — not one FLAG has ever survived adjudication. The documented flag causes are all lexical: comment prose, import reflow, manifest count bumps. Meanwhile 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' appears in the merge record of m20b, the slice that shipped the 7-container observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped four of eight containers — a defect class the gate cannot see because none of those files are test files. This is primarily a PRIMARY-axis finding: a gate that is always wrong trains its reader to rubber-stamp, and the eleventh FLAGGED->CLEAN is read far less carefully than the first.
recommendations.expected_effect: Small direct saving (~$8-20/week, ~0.5-1% of allowance, including the $5.03 m20c adjudication tick — the most expensive tick of the window). The real return is removing false assurance from the merge record. Explicitly do NOT touch the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet — that is a different mechanism, it measurably caught merge-blockers CI did not (14r-d's OBS-2 log-ratchet blocker, independently reproduced by red-team in a throwaway clone), and at ~$171/week it is the best-spending part of the loop.
recommendations.risk: Low. Keep the orchestration_audit role-presence check at mr-audit:24-30 — that one reads the build session's own log and is accurate (its '12 agent calls' for 14r-d matches the transcript exactly).

recommendations.action: Make ADR Residuals mechanically consumable. Constrain the 'Residuals / follow-ups' section of every ADR to a fenced machine-readable block (one line per item: id, touches, severity, blocking) and add a nightly job that diffs those blocks against the open slice set in specs/monster-realm-v2/*.spec.md and PLAN.md §9, emitting any unmatched item as a queue candidate. Seed it with the seven *-security.eval.mjs gates currently parked to owner '14r-c-2' in evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190 — a slice id that appears in ZERO spec, PLAN or state file.
recommendations.rationale: This is the generator of the remediation treadmill. 21 of 165 ADRs carry a Residuals section, 78 defer/park phrases exist corpus-wide, and nothing reads any of them — so items surface only via a human-instigated multi-lens review, the most expensive possible detector, at a measured mean latency of 13.1 days. ADR-0165 is the clean proof: Accepted 2026-07-31 with implementation 'deferred to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared touches:', 11r-i merged without it, and it was finally built 15 days later by 13r-g. The touches: discipline that enables fan-out is what creates these orphans, so the fix belongs at the hand-off point, not in the fan-out rule.
recommendations.expected_effect: Targets the 24.2%-of-allowance remediation class at its source. Even a 25% reduction in rediscovery cost frees ~6% of weekly allowance, and it converts the weekly review from the sole detector into a backstop. Immediate safety return: seven security gates guarding the battle, evolution, raising, recruit, shop, trade and NPC reducer families are measurably blind right now, two of them provably passing GREEN on code they exist to reject.
recommendations.risk: Low mechanically. The real risk is the queue filling faster than the allowance can drain it — which is FINE under a credit-bound regime (idle is free, and inventory is not a cost), but the supervisor must then prioritise by severity rather than by spec order. Pair with R11.

recommendations.action: Inventory watermark, denominated in credits rather than hours. Add a build-ready slice count to $MEM/mr-situation (derived mechanically: a slice is ready if it has a slice id, a touches: set, and its after: chain is satisfied — the after: field already exists in every 13r/14r spec and currently has ZERO mechanical consumers). When the ready count falls below 10, fire a replenishment event rather than a self-disable. Route it to the CHEAP unattended channel by defining a synthetic elaboration slice shape — slice='<M>-spec', touches='specs/monster-realm-v2/<M>*.spec.md, specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md', tier=hard — so the existing mr-spawn path can run the elaboration procedure already written at specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md:13,:37. Scope it to DECOMPOSITION of already-decided milestones only (M-postgate-client-coverage and M-postgate-roster-wave-3 each have a PLAN bullet stating exactly what to do); leave genuine open-design milestones (M22-M25) attended.
recommendations.rationale: Justified strictly on credits, per the reframing. Idle hours are free, so the throughput argument is worthless — but starvation is not free, because it forces replenishment through the 4-8x more expensive attended channel: $53.56 per build-ready slice attended (plus 9.2h and 4.1h of operator time) versus $6.75-$12.31 unattended. Worse, that attended spend is invisible to the ledger AND to the governor ($482.03 measured, $0.00 recorded), so ~26% of a weekly allowance was consumed entirely outside the control loop. The watermark of 10 is credit-denominated: at $18.3 per allowance point and a mean all-in $88.49 per merged slice, one week's allowance buys ~20 slices, so 10 ready slices is a half-week reserve — enough to never hit the expensive channel under time pressure, and cheap to hold because inventory costs nothing.
recommendations.expected_effect: Redirects the decomposition half of ~26% of allowance from the attended channel to the unattended one: ~15-20% of weekly allowance freed or redirected. Secondary: makes 'is anything launchable?' a mechanical query rather than a prose re-derivation, which is the error that produced the 2026-08-10 'no mechanically-launchable slice' standdown while 7 fully-decomposed slices (one CRITICAL, spec-committed 5 hours earlier) sat unbuilt.
recommendations.risk: Medium, and I will not overstate the evidence: there is NO instance in the corpus of an unattended pass elaborating a FORWARD milestone. The weekly review is the only proof that unattended spec authoring works, and it has only ever authored residual milestones derived from verified findings. Scope strictly to decomposition of already-decided work and require an operator sign-off on the first two before trusting the channel. Also fix the routing accident while here: both measured ceremonies ran 100% on sonnet purely by session inheritance from a cron tick, while every slice they feed runs opus@high or fable@xhigh.

recommendations.action: Preserve, and explicitly protect from cost-cutting: (1) the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet — ~$171/week across 93 runs, measurably catching merge-blockers CI does not; (2) the ADR corpus as navigation — 143 distinct ADRs cited 3,729 times in production source, decision-granular (pvp.rs cites 'ADR-0189 D6', battle.rs cites 'ADR-0185 D1'); (3) the review-residual spec format — 15/15 slices merged, 14/15 at ATTEMPTS=1, ~25 lines per slice, zero failures attributable to spec ambiguity; (4) the brief's TARGET_DESC, which supplies file:line defects, the correct SSOT predicate and the wrong one to avoid, EARS criteria and proof-of-teeth plans; (5) the proof-of-teeth discipline ('a gate that has never failed is a decoration'); (6) lock/mutex/orphan hygiene and the durable event queue, both clean in-window. Separately, retire genuinely dead weight for signal reasons only, not token reasons: the feedback doctrine (189 rows, zero since 2026-07-27, zero VERIFIED or SHIPPED-VERIFIED ever, still labelled ACTIVE v1.0 on all 65 paid ticks and still mandating an 'Items:' field in every PR body) and the retro ceremony ($MEM/retros/ has never been created).
recommendations.rationale: Two guardrails. First, the credit pressure will tempt cuts to ceremony, and the measured evidence says the review gauntlet and the ADR corpus are where the money is earning quality — they serve the operator's PRIMARY axis directly and are NOT the same mechanism as the 0-precision gating_test_audit that R9 retires. Second, prompt length is emphatically not a cost problem: the full 155-line supervisor prompt costs ~$83/year to carry, 0.087% of spend, so dead doctrine should be removed for decision-quality reasons (labelling dead machinery ACTIVE degrades the trustworthiness of every other ACTIVE label) and never justified as a token saving.
recommendations.expected_effect: Protects ~10% of weekly allowance of demonstrably high-value spend from being cut in pursuit of the other recommendations. The dead-doctrine removal frees ~0% of allowance and is proposed purely for signal integrity.
recommendations.risk: Low. The one thing to watch: R3's SCARCITY state must not be allowed to erode the review gauntlet by tempting thinner lens batteries near the ceiling — the correct scarcity response is fewer slices at full rigour, never more slices at reduced rigour.

diagnoses.theme: RECURRING-ISSUE TAXONOMY, RANKED BY VALUE DESTROYED PER WEEKLY PLAN CREDIT. Nine issue CLASSES with measured recurrence, ranked by (frequency x credit-cost) against the operator's corrected objective function (maximize durable capability per weekly allowance; idle hours are free). The window's plan week was consumed to 90% real account utilization by 2026-08-10T05:08Z while the internal governor read 64.7% and NORMAL; the prior plan week reached 97% and burned purchased credits (measured: {"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true}). Conversion anchor used throughout: $1,799.65 internal-ledger dollars in the governor week corresponded to ~90% real utilization, so 1% of the plan allowance is worth ~$20 internal-dollars. Top classes: (1) BLIND GOVERNOR / PACING FAILURE — the true account-level gauge exists in every run log and is discarded by doctrine; (2) THE RESIDUAL LEAK — 35.4% in-window / 46.6% lifetime of slice spend is remediation of the loop's own prior output, generated by a records-are-not-queues defect; (3) CONTEXT RE-READ AMPLIFICATION — 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics, 65.3% cache-read, with zero compaction across 230 transcripts; (4) ZERO-PRECISION AND BLIND GATES — 0 true positives in 11 in-window flags and across the entire v3 era, while 7 security evals are measurably blind and the mutation ratchet was loosened to certify 43% survival; (5) MEASUREMENT SELF-REFERENCE — one cost source, 21% COST-UNKNOWN rows, resume passes never re-summed, no unit-of-work denominator; (6) DECLARED-SCOPE UNSOUNDNESS — fan-out disjointness computed on touches: that the brief itself silently expands; (7) DEAD DOCTRINE — the improvement loop froze 2026-08-01 and did not respond to any incident in the window; (8) SUPPLY MONOCULTURE AND SPEC MISROUTING — the only unattended work generator produces remediation exclusively, and both forward-spec ceremonies ran on sonnet by session inheritance while their downstream slices ran fable@xhigh; (9) SELF-COLLISION — 72/72 false probe trips, 90% caused by the loop's own indexer, now demoted to low rank because its cost is latency, not credits. NEGATIVE RESULTS (candidates the evidence does not support, dropped): stale locks/mutexes/orphaned done-files (0 ORPHAN-RUN, 0 WATCHER-DEAD, 0 CRASHED rows in-window — the 2026-08-01 fixes held); repeated file reads (19% of Reads, ~$4); prompt length as a token cost (~$83/yr, 0.087% of spend); duty cycle (explicitly not a goal). GROUND-TRUTH CORRECTIONS: fact 9 is wrong — three in-window slices had ATTEMPTS>1 (14r-e=3, 13r-f=3, 13r-b=2), and ATTEMPTS is a spawn counter rather than a failure counter, so it is unusable as a health signal in either direction; facts 3/4 conflate two distinct causes that must never again be merged — the 85h halt was a deliberate operator credit-protection pause (mr-supervisor-disable confirmed at /home/mdrewt/.local/bin/mr-supervisor-disable), while the supervisor's own empty-queue self-disables are a separate, shorter (~21h) and genuinely defective class.

root_causes.statement: BINARY-TRIPWIRE THINKING: the loop systematically converts continuous measurements into booleans at the earliest possible moment and discards the magnitude, so it can detect that a limit was crossed but can never pace against it.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. The account-level weekly gauge is present in every headless run log: 255 seven_day rate_limit_info samples survive in /tmp/mr_pass_*.log and /tmp/mr_native_tick_*.log, e.g. {"status":"allowed_warning","resetsAt":1786060800,"rateLimitType":"seven_day","utilization":0.32,"isUsingOverage":false}. Doctrine at $MEM/mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 enumerates the field set as '{status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage}' — utilization is MISSING FROM ITS OWN FIELD LIST — and instructs 'Trip ONLY on status == "rejected"'. The only occurrence of the word 'utilization' in $MEM/mr-native-tick.sh is a comment at line 355; grep -ln utilization over all $MEM/mr-* matches only the prompt and that comment. No script parses it. Same pattern elsewhere: mr-audit collapses a diff to a FLAGGED bit (0 true positives in 11 in-window flags); the cost governor collapses spend to a cap flag that is then disabled (mr-budget-config.json costwatch_enforce:false); the human-activity probe collapses filesystem mtime to a trip (72/72 false positives).
root_causes.mechanism: Doctrine is authored as a list of gates. A gate needs a boolean, so each signal is thresholded at the point of ingestion and the underlying number is never persisted. The rejection reasoning at :116 is correct on its own terms — tripping on allowed_warning would kill live slices — but having decided not to TRIP on the event, the design discards the whole event rather than reading the number inside it. The failure compounds because utilization is present on allowed/allowed_warning events and ABSENT on rejected events (verified: both rejected samples carry overageStatus/overageInUse but no utilization), so the only moment the binary fires is the exact moment the gauge disappears and purchased credits begin.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The entire pacing failure. Plan week ending 2026-08-14: real utilization reached 0.90 by 2026-08-10T05:08Z while the governor reported 64.7% and NORMAL — a measured 1.39x under-report — forcing a manual operator pause and ~3.5 days of stranded capacity. Prior plan week (resets 2026-08-07) reached 0.97 and logged a genuine rejected+isUsingOverage event, i.e. that week bought overage credits, which operator objective F names as the true monetary waste. Also the direct driver of the 4 slices that exceeded their declared cap in real dollars (M21b-2 182.9%, M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%).

root_causes.statement: RECORDS ARE NOT QUEUES: every disclosure channel in the system writes prose into a file that no mechanical consumer reads, so known work is reliably recorded and reliably forgotten until an expensive review rediscovers it.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED, and the class reproduced itself while being remediated. docs/adr/ carries 78 defer/park phrases across 21 ADRs with a 'Residuals / follow-ups' section, with no mechanism converting any into queued work. Smoking gun: docs/adr/0165-*.md:9 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared touches:' — 11r-i merged and did not implement it; actually implemented 15 days later by 13r-g. mr-state.json queue[] is 58 past-tense narrative strings, zero forward items, and mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:257-258 confirms 'its queue[] is a narrative journal, not a work queue'. The per-slice after: field has zero mechanical consumers (grep 'after:' over mr-*.sh/mr-situation/mr-spawn/mr-disjoint = no hits) and mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:251-253 admits 'no mechanical consumer today'. VERIFIED REPRODUCTION: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190 parks seven blind *-security.eval.mjs gates to owner '14r-c-2'; I confirmed 14r-c-2 appears in progress memos and the handoff but returns 0 hits in specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md, 0 in mr-state.json, and no file under specs/ — it exists in narrative only, in the very milestone chartered to eliminate this class. Same for feedback-ledger.jsonl (frozen since 2026-07-27, still polled every tick) and decisions/ (answers consumed 4-7 days later).
root_causes.mechanism: Fan-out parallelism is bought by forbidding a slice to touch files outside its declared touches:. Work discovered mid-slice but out of scope is therefore structurally un-doable, and the only available action is to write it down. The written form is free prose inside an ADR, a progress memo, or a code comment — none of which any launcher, gate, or scheduler parses. The backlog therefore leaks at exactly the rate the discipline succeeds, and the only recovery mechanism is a human-instigated multi-lens review, which is the most expensive detector available.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend ($643.73 of $1,817.65, ~32% of the plan week) and 46.6% of lifetime named-slice spend ($3,913.21 of $8,394.81). Mean disclosure-to-remediation latency 13.1 days (median 14, max 20, n=10). 13 review-residual milestones / 85 slices to date, with residual count flat at 6-9 per cycle and cadence accelerating 7d->6d->3d->4d — a flat treadmill, not a converging loop. Live quality exposure: 7 reducer-security gates blind right now, 2 of them measured to swallow the scan needle.

root_causes.statement: MEASUREMENT SELF-REFERENCE: every cost number traces to one file written by one code path, with no independent source and no unit-of-work denominator, so the loop cannot tell whether any intervention improved value per credit.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. mr-usage-snap:30-38 computes native_ledger_usd by re-summing the SAME ledger (eight daily rows reproduce it with delta 0.00), and its models/cowork column points at /mnt/c/.../local-agent-mode-sessions, a different system entirely; ~/.claude/usage-log.csv has columns timestamp,kind,name,session,project — no cost, no tokens. The ledger under-reports structurally: 32 of 150 in-window rows are COST-UNKNOWN, and resume/retry legs are never re-summed ($46.84 measured missing: 14r-e $40.58 + m20c $6.26; 14r-e true $125.73 vs recorded $85.14). One run carries three mutually inconsistent figures ($274.37 ledger / $287.77 cal / $359.71 raw) because mr-cost-watch has two verified pricing bugs: it prices every content block rather than deduping by message.id (1.75 events per message, range 1.38-2.20) and prices all cache-creation at the 5m rate when 17.9% of tokens are ephemeral_1h. Ledger/raw therefore ranges 0.637-1.008 against a hard-coded 0.80. No slice-size field exists anywhere (no LOC, files, or EARS count). remote_red_fix_cycles is populated on 446 rows and sums to 0. CENSUS greps the tick's own log instead of the build session's, so 159 of 162 lines read 'agents: none'. The /tmp logs holding the only real telemetry are ephemeral and already overwritten for 13r-c and m20c.
root_causes.mechanism: Instrumentation was repeatedly replaced in the same commit as the intervention it was meant to measure (the v3 push created the SUPERVISOR row convention, so no pre-v3 baseline exists and never will). Combined with a single self-referential source, any regression in accounting is invisible, and the errors all run in the unsafe direction because a missing row reads as $0.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Makes the headline question unanswerable: cost per merged slice rose 4.5x across the v3 cutover (median $14.19 -> $63.16) and has been flat for four weeks, but cannot be normalized for scope. The named $250-400/wk model-routing lever (README:60) has sat unexercised for three weeks and is now unmeasurable retroactively because routing made model perfectly collinear with tier (n=1 at hard/opus). Fable was 57% of window spend at a price the config itself labels a guess.

root_causes.statement: UNBOUNDED CONTEXT ACCUMULATION: nothing ever prunes a build session's prefix, so every token added at turn i is re-billed on every remaining turn, making cost scale with the square of session length rather than with work done.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts. Cost structure: cache-read $1,012.79 (65.3%), cache-write $396.98 (25.6%), output $140.81 (9.1%), fresh input $0.94 — 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics. Zero compaction and zero context-editing events across all 230 transcripts (no isCompactSummary, no compact_boundary; every literal 'compact' hit verified as prose/code). Final contexts 295,092 / 454,481 / 611,322 tokens — the last is M21b-2 at 611K of a 1M window. Largest proven sink is assistant thinking/output carried forward: 243.9M tokens = 34.7% of all parent prompt volume, computed exactly from usage.output_tokens as output_i x (N-i). Static 44,288-token preamble x 2,718 turns = 120.4M (17.1%), against a subagent preamble of only 11,103 median — the parent carries 4x. 32.2% of all parent prompt volume is consumed before the first repo-file edit (median turn 50; worst 77.0% at turn 134/157). Orchestrator navigation is 791 Bash grep/sed/cat/ls calls producing 2.08M chars, with 0 codegraph and 0 Grep calls despite two .codegraph/ directories and an explicit global doctrine to prefer it; subagents comply (47 codegraph calls) but the parent does not.
root_causes.mechanism: The API replays the whole prefix each turn and bills it as cache-read. With no compaction strategy configured and no context budget in the brief, an early 12K-token Read costs ~2.4M carried tokens while the same Read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M. Orientation habits (grep over a 428,676-byte handoff, full-file reads, re-inlining the brief into every subagent prompt) all land at the front of the session where the multiplier is largest.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Cache-read alone is ~$1,013 of $1,551 measured build spend, roughly 50% of a full plan week. Carried-forward thinking is ~$166/week; static preamble across both layers ~$130/week; Bash navigation carry ~$47/week. Headline efficiency: 24,125 prompt tokens re-read per line of code added.

root_causes.statement: DECLARED SCOPE IS TRUSTED FOR SCHEDULING BUT SYSTEMATICALLY INCOMPLETE, so the safety property fan-out depends on is routinely violated by the loop's own rules.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. The brief grants every slice an ALWAYS-in-scope companion set — '(a) sibling test files of any declared code file (e.g. *.test.ts next to a declared .ts), and (b) docs/adr/**, docs/knowledge/**, CHANGELOG.md, ARCHITECTURE.md' — while mr-disjoint compares only the declared touches:. Consequence: 14r-c and 14r-e were declared disjoint and blessed as a fan-out pair (spec:202), then collided on client/src/main.wiring.test.ts (a *.test.ts sibling of 14r-e's declared client/src/main.ts), producing 'PR#318 CONFLICTING vs master 9b924f3', a park, and a $36.19 resume run. The 14r-e park memo states it directly: '14r-c's fan-out disjointness held on paper, not in practice.' Clause (b) is worse: it is granted to EVERY slice, so any two concurrent slices are guaranteed to collide there — 14r-b's conflict set was exactly ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md. 3 of ~20 in-window merges hit sibling conflicts. Related unenforced invariant: session af23a7f8 (14r-c) issued two Edits against the MAIN checkout at 13:19:39Z and 13:19:46Z while sibling 14r-e was live, self-reverting 7 seconds later — the brief prohibits this in prose and nothing blocks it.
root_causes.mechanism: Two different definitions of a slice's file set exist in two artifacts written for different purposes: the spec's touches: (used by the scheduler) and the brief's companion grants (used by the build session). Nothing reconciles them, and the scheduler's verdict is computed from the narrower one, so mr-disjoint returns SAFE on pairs that are provably not disjoint.
root_causes.quantified_cost: One park + rebase + resume cycle at $36.19 unrecorded spend, plus supervisor park/relaunch/adjudication ticks, on 3 of ~20 merges. Also the mechanism behind RC2's deferrals: touches: is simultaneously the thing that makes parallelism safe and the thing that forces known work to be written down instead of done.

root_causes.statement: THE IMPROVEMENT LOOP HAS NO OWNER OR TRIGGER: it ran as a 4-day human burst, froze on 2026-08-01, and did not respond to a single incident in the review window.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED. 45 of 51 loop-infra commits landed 2026-07-24..27; the last real mechanism change is 7df734d (2026-08-01). Every one of the 20 commits touching memory/projects/mr-* since 2026-08-08 is mr-state.json bookkeeping. The supervisor prompt carries 21 dated incident parentheticals spanning exactly seven dates, ALL July 2026, zero August — while the window produced a 97%-utilization overage week, 4 cap-blowing runs, and 11 false gate flags, and changed no doctrine. Retros 1-5 are all July; $MEM/retros/ has never been created. The only surviving automated generator, the weekly review, is scoped by its own Goal section exclusively to 'the monster-realm subproject' and has never produced a loop-improvement recommendation.
