Dead machinery still consuming attention: mr-feedback (15,911 B, largest script, polled every tick against a dataset frozen 19 days), mr-metrics / mr-evidence / mr-selfcheck / mr-retro-request (0 call sites, 0 log lines ever), the N>=3 launch protocol (0 uses since authored; N never exceeded 2), mr-tier-map.json (covers 0 of 29 in-window slices), and 803 ollama preflight warm-ups against 0 triage invocations ever.
root_causes.mechanism: Loop improvement was never assigned to a recurring mechanism — it was an operator project. When operator attention moved to the game, the only remaining scheduled ceremony (the weekly review) had a scope that structurally excluded the loop. Doctrine additions are append-only, so obsolete rules accumulate as unfalsifiable prompt weight while genuinely dead subsystems keep their 'ACTIVE' labels, degrading the credibility of every other label.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Second-order but compounding: it is why RC1 survived after the signal was seen and named, why the documented probe-exclusion decision was never revisited against 72 false trips, and why the promised opus-vs-fable A/B (a self-estimated $250-400/wk lever) never ran. Direct waste is small (~26KB of orphaned scripts, ~15% of prompt text, GPU thrash from warm-ups) but it removes the mechanism that would fix everything above.

recommendations.action: Build a utilization-based governor on the telemetry that already exists. (a) In $MEM/mr-cost-watch (which already streams these logs) and in mr-native-tick.sh's reconcile path, parse rate_limit_event objects with python3 per the existing doctrine rule at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 (never grep raw text), and append every seven_day sample to a new append-only $MEM/mr-utilization.jsonl as {ts, utilization, resetsAt, isUsingOverage, overageInUse, source_log, slice}. (b) Rewrite mr-situation's budget block to emit real_utilization_pct, plan_week_resets_at, hours_remaining_in_week, sample_age_minutes, and is_using_overage from that file, replacing d7_usd as the governor's primary input. (c) Implement pacing in mr-native-tick.sh gate order: compute an expected burn line = elapsed_fraction_of_plan_week; if utilization exceeds it by a configurable margin, refuse NEW launches while allowing in-flight slices, merges, and done-events to complete (operator policy G1, finish-in-flight/start-nothing-new); above 0.95 refuse all launches; on isUsingOverage or overageInUse true, write a BLOCKER and notify. (d) Handle the measured sampling caveats explicitly: utilization is present only on allowed/allowed_warning events and is ABSENT on rejected events (verified on both rejected samples), it is quantized to whole percent, and it is only observed while a session runs — so treat a sample older than one plan-week-hour as stale, and between samples advance a local interpolator seeded from the last real reading using the existing token estimator, always rounding pessimistically. (e) Persist the /tmp stream logs (or at minimum their rate_limit_event lines) into $MEM before they age out, since they are currently the only accurate record of real consumption and are already being deleted.
recommendations.rationale: This is the single highest-value change in the system and it is a read, not a build. The true account-level gauge is emitted by the API in every headless run, includes the operator's usage on other machines and unrelated projects that no local ledger can ever see, and its resetsAt decodes to the operator's real plan reset. The loop already sees these events and throws them away: the doctrine's own field enumeration at :116 omits utilization, and the word appears in mr-native-tick.sh only inside a comment at line 355. Every other cost recommendation is unverifiable without this.
recommendations.expected_effect: Replaces a measured 1.39x under-report with ground truth (governor read 64.7%/NORMAL at the moment real utilization was 0.90). Directly prevents the prior week's outcome — max utilization 0.97 with a logged rejected+isUsingOverage event, i.e. purchased credits burned, which operator objective F names as the true monetary waste. Eliminates the manual babysitting loop (operator objective G3): the ~3.5-day pause on 2026-08-10 becomes an automatic finish-in-flight standdown that self-clears at resetsAt. Anchor for all downstream estimates: 1% of plan allowance ~ $20 internal-ledger dollars.
recommendations.risk: Sampling is sparse and lags — a slice launched immediately after a stale low reading can still overshoot; mitigate with the pessimistic interpolator and by sampling the tick's own log (ticks run hourly and emit these events, so the gauge refreshes even when no slice is live). Field-set drift is a real risk the doctrine already warns about; assert schema presence and raise a BLOCKER rather than failing silent. Do NOT wire this to kill live slices — that is the correct part of the existing :116 reasoning and must survive.

recommendations.action: Demote the synthetic internal-dollar model from SSOT to interpolator, per operator decision G2. Stop using d7_usd as the governor's decision input (mr-situation:63-84 and the weekly_limit_usd derivation in mr-budget-config.json). Keep mr-cost-sum's ledger as a per-slice attribution record for value-per-credit analysis only, and keep mr-cost-watch's estimator solely as the between-samples interpolator for R1 — but first fix its two verified pricing bugs, since an interpolator must not be biased: dedup usage events by message.id (measured 1.75 events per distinct message, range 1.38-2.20) and price cache_creation.ephemeral_1h at the 1h rate (17.9% of cache-creation tokens, 6.24M of 34.93M, currently billed at the 5m rate). Also fix the two structural ledger leaks: re-sum a slice's log on every done-event rather than once (recovering the measured $46.84 lost to resume passes), and stop reusing /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log across relaunches.
recommendations.rationale: The weekly_limit_usd of 2783 is an unvalidated extrapolation from a single operator-reported observation on 2026-07-25, and the dominant model in the window (fable, 57% of spend) is priced by an explicit guess the config itself flags for calibration that never happened. Its correction factor is not even a scalar: measured ledger/raw ranges 0.637-1.008 against a hard-coded 0.80, which also falsifies the in-line claim at mr-cost-watch:82 that thresholding on raw 'fires early = safe direction'.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes the false-confidence source that reported NORMAL at 90% real utilization. Collapsing the 0.637-1.008 spread makes the caps mean what they say; with R1 arming enforcement on real percentage, the four in-window cap breaches (M21b-2 182.9%, M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%) become preventable — M21b-2 alone was $131.15 of spend past its own hard ceiling, ~6.5% of a plan week.
recommendations.risk: Losing the dollar model removes a familiar number from every report; keep it visible as an attribution figure so per-slice value analysis survives. Do not arm hard kills on the interpolator alone — kills strand locks and hard-block relaunch, which is the documented and correct objection in mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54.

recommendations.action: Make ADR residuals mechanically queueable. Define a structured block that replaces free-prose 'Residuals / follow-ups' bullets — each entry carries a slice id, a touches: set, and a severity — and add a CI gate on monster-realm that reds any merged ADR containing a residual entry whose slice id does not appear in specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md section 9. Extend the same rule to the two other leak sites: a code comment parking work to an owner (as evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190 does for '14r-c-2') must name a queued id, and mr-state.json's queue[] must be split into the existing narrative journal plus a machine-readable ready_set derived from each spec's touches:/after: fields.
recommendations.rationale: This attacks the largest single destroyer of value per credit. The class is measured, recurrent, and self-demonstrating: I verified that 14r-c-2 — owner of seven measurably blind security gates — appears in progress memos and the handoff but returns zero hits across all of specs/, PLAN.md, and mr-state.json. The same defect burned m20e-2, m20b-2, 13r-c-2, nh5, and ADR-0165 (accepted 2026-07-31, deferred to 11r-i, never implemented, finally done by 13r-g 15 days later).
recommendations.expected_effect: Targets the 35.4% of in-window slice spend ($643.73, ~32% of a plan week) and 46.6% of lifetime slice spend that is remediation. Halving the leak returns roughly 16% of the weekly allowance to new capability. Should also compress the measured 13.1-day mean disclosure-to-remediation latency toward the next scheduled slice, and convert the review from a rediscovery mechanism into a genuine audit — the current 13-milestone, 85-slice treadmill has flat residual counts and accelerating cadence, which is the signature of a leak rather than a converging loop.
recommendations.risk: A hard CI gate on ADR content will red master on docs-only commits — which already happened once in-window (62dce75 broke master for 2h11m on the ADR-digest vocabulary gate). Ship it as a warning for one cycle, then enforce. Guard against gaming: an author can satisfy the gate by queueing a slice nobody prioritizes, so pair it with severity so CRITICAL residuals surface in the ready_set ordering.

recommendations.action: Impose a context budget on build sessions. (a) Enable the API's context-editing clear_thinking strategy (beta context-management-2025-06-27) for build sessions so thinking blocks are dropped from the replayed prefix. (b) Cut the parent preamble toward the subagent's 11K: defer the MCP servers no build session ever calls (Postman, Google Drive, Indeed, Audible, ZipRecruiter, Swagger) behind tool-search rather than loading their instruction blocks. (c) Split $MEM/monster-realm-handoff.md (428,676 bytes, ~107K tokens, 154 sections; archives already exist) and replace the orientation grep against it with a per-slice memo the brief names directly. (d) Add one line to mr-brief-template.md instructing the orchestrator to route code navigation through codegraph_explore before Bash grep/sed/cat, matching the operator's existing global doctrine.
recommendations.rationale: 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics and only 9.1% buys generated tokens, so every lever that shrinks per-turn context is ~7x more valuable than one that shrinks output. Nothing currently prunes: zero compaction events across 230 transcripts, with contexts running to 611K. The three biggest measured buckets are all addressable — carried thinking 243.9M tokens (34.7% of parent prompt volume), static preamble 120.4M (17.1%), Bash navigation 69.7M (9.9%). The navigation fix is orchestrator-only: subagents already comply with 47 codegraph calls while the parent made 0.
recommendations.expected_effect: Cache-read alone is ~$1,013 of $1,551 measured build spend — roughly half a plan week. A 25% reduction returns ~12% of the weekly allowance with no change to what gets built; a 60% thinking-clear rate alone is ~$100/week. Also removes a latent hard failure: M21b-2 sat at 611K of a 1M window with no compaction backstop.
recommendations.risk: Clearing thinking blocks can degrade multi-step reasoning continuity on long slices — enable on routine tier first and compare merge outcomes before extending to hard tier. Trimming MCP instruction blocks is INFERRED to be a meaningful share of the 44,288-token preamble, not measured directly (transcripts store messages, not system prompts), so measure turn-1 context before and after rather than assuming.

recommendations.action: Fix or retire the mr-audit gating_test_audit heuristic. Minimum viable fix in $MEM/mr-audit: strip comment spans before counting removed asserts (line 54), anchor skip-marker detection to test-framework call sites so Rust .iter().skip() and .skip() chains stop matching (lines 56-57), ignore pure import-line reflow, whitelist manifest count-bump edits, drop the unconditional tier=hard FLAG (lines 58-59), and remove the test-path-only pathspec for the SUPPRESSION pass (line 51) so #[allow], @ts-ignore, eslint-disable and nosemgrep added to production source are actually counted. If precision does not exceed zero within one cycle, delete the gate rather than keep paying for adjudication.
recommendations.rationale: Measured precision is 0/11 in-window and zero true positives across the entire v3 era — no FLAG has ever survived adjudication in a 710-row ledger. The documented flag causes are entirely lexical: comment prose, import reflow, manifest count bumps, and .iter().skip(). Meanwhile the gate is structurally blind to the defects that matter — 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' appears on the merge record of m20b, the slice that shipped an observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped four of eight containers, because none of those defects touch a test file.
recommendations.expected_effect: Directly serves the PRIMARY axis. A gate with 0% precision trains its reader to rubber-stamp, so the eleventh FLAGGED->CLEAN is read far less carefully than the first — the gate is actively eroding the vigilance it exists to create while providing false assurance in the merge record. Credit saving is modest (~$10-20/window in adjudication ticks, one of which was the window's most expensive at $5.03) but the assurance value is currently negative.
recommendations.risk: Loosening the heuristic could admit a genuine test-weakening. Mitigate by keeping the hard-tier diff read as a doctrine practice while removing the unconditional FLAG that makes it indistinguishable from a detection — the two are conflated today.

recommendations.action: Queue and fund the unblinding of the seven measurably-blind security evals. Create a real slice (the work currently parked to the phantom '14r-c-2') covering battle-, evolution-, npc-dialogue-quest-, raising-, recruit-, shop-, and trade-reducer-security.eval.mjs, prioritising evolution- and raising- which are documented as LIVE, REPRODUCIBLE hazards whose prepareRustSource swallows the scan needle and blinds every ban clause downstream. Raise MIGRATED_FLOOR from 10 as they land. In the same pass, delete the concat!() scanner-dodge from server-module/src/accounts.rs:54 and its copy at pvp.rs:63 — 13r-c was chartered to do exactly this, merged without doing it, and the workaround has since been pinned by evals/account-e2e.eval.mjs's ISSUER_NEEDLE.
recommendations.rationale: Highest-severity live quality exposure in the corpus, and a clean instance of RC2: the debt is recorded with exemplary rigour in the repo's own SSOT registry and queued nowhere. The concat!() lineage shows the dependency running backwards — production source is now shaped to satisfy broken test infrastructure, in two files, pinned by a test.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores seven security gates that can currently pass GREEN on code they exist to reject, covering the battle, evolution, raising, recruit, shop, trade and NPC reducer families. $115.97 has already been spent across 13r-c and 14r-c with the security-critical half of the migration still open, so this is finishing paid-for work rather than new investment.
recommendations.risk: Unblinding gates will surface real violations and may red master; sequence it so the gates land with their fixes. The 13r-c re-spawn ($14.45 producing a 7-line comment edit) shows the failure mode to avoid — verify the original scope is genuinely unmet before relaunching.

recommendations.action: Compute fan-out disjointness on the effective file set, not the declared one. Before mr-disjoint returns a verdict, expand each slice's touches: by the same companion rules the brief grants: sibling test files of any declared code file (*.test.ts next to a declared .ts, *_tests.rs next to a declared .rs) and the always-granted doc set. Treat ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md and docs/adr/DIGEST.md as a known shared axis that fan-out must either serialize on or resolve by auto-merge, since every slice is granted them and any two concurrent slices therefore collide there by construction. Separately, enforce worktree isolation mechanically with a path allowlist on Edit/Write rather than prose in the brief.
recommendations.rationale: The scheduler's safety property is computed from a narrower file set than the build session is permitted to touch, so SAFE verdicts are unsound by construction. Measured: 14r-c and 14r-e were blessed as a disjoint pair and collided on client/src/main.wiring.test.ts; 14r-b's conflict set was exactly the always-granted doc companions. The isolation gap is demonstrated too — 14r-c wrote to the shared main checkout twice while a sibling was live and self-reverted 7 seconds later.
recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates the sibling-conflict class that hit 3 of ~20 in-window merges, including the 14r-e park + $36.19 unrecorded resume. Makes N>2 fan-out trustworthy, which matters because the N>=3 protocol has never been used despite being authored and approved.
recommendations.risk: Expanding the effective set will make more pairs look non-disjoint and could over-serialize. The doc-set axis needs the auto-merge path rather than serialization, or fan-out collapses to N=1 permanently.

recommendations.action: Add a unit-of-work denominator and a second cost source. Extend mr-record's ledger schema with files_changed, lines_prod, lines_test, and ears_criteria_count captured at merge from git show --numstat plus the spec. Repoint mr-usage-snap away from the unrelated Windows Cowork directory (/mnt/c/Users/mdrewt/AppData/Roaming/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions) at the harness's own ~/.claude/projects transcripts so it becomes a genuine independent check. Ledger the ceremonies that are currently invisible: the two spec-authoring sessions ($482.03 measured, $0.00 recorded) and the weekly review (one row ever, deliberately $0.00). Delete or repoint the CENSUS line in mr-native-tick.sh:323, which greps the tick's own log and therefore reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines — do not touch mr-audit:24-30, whose role-presence check reads the build session's log correctly and is accurate.
recommendations.rationale: Value per credit is now the objective function and there is no denominator. Cost per merged slice rose 4.5x across the v3 cutover and has been flat for four weeks, but cannot be normalized for scope because no slice-size field exists. Roughly 24% of true window spend sits outside the governor's view because ceremonies are unledgered.
recommendations.expected_effect: Makes the operator's central question answerable next week instead of never. Also enables the deferred opus-vs-fable A/B, which the loop's own design doc valued at $250-400/wk (9-14% of the allowance) and which is currently unmeasurable because routing made model perfectly collinear with tier (n=1 at hard/opus, n=0 at routine/fable).
recommendations.risk: Line counts are a crude denominator that credits a 6,053-line generated test tool the same as a 3-line reducer fix — use it as a trend baseline, never as an absolute, and keep the prod/test split visible since 74.9% of merged lines are test/eval by deliberate design.

recommendations.action: Build real performance gates, since performance is a named PRIMARY axis and nothing currently measures it. Add budgets for reducer execution latency, subscription fan-out payload size, and client frame time, and wire m20d's existing sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs (6,053 lines, already in the cargo workspace) to a committed baseline under evals/baselines/. Tighten game-core/benches/budgets.rs ceilings from ~20x measured mean toward something that can detect regression rather than only order-of-magnitude collapse.
recommendations.rationale: The only perf gate in the repo is seven nanosecond-scale pure functions in game-core with ceilings set at ~20x the measured mean, so a 19x regression on any hot path passes GREEN. Nothing measures the places a multiplayer game actually gets slow. m20d built the instrument to measure the real thing, produced a one-off breaking-point number recorded only in an ADR amendment, and connected it to nothing.
recommendations.expected_effect: Closes the largest gap between the operator's stated PRIMARY priority and what the loop can actually detect. Converts a $117.33 already-spent tool from a manual artifact into a standing ratchet.
recommendations.risk: Latency baselines are noisy in CI and will flake; anchor them as ratchets with generous but meaningful headroom, and land them as non-blocking for one cycle. Note the existing flake tax before adding jobs — wallet-balance.spec.ts flaked 4 times in 7 days and was diagnosed four separate times without ever being fixed.

recommendations.action: Separate the two disable mechanisms and make the loop's own one self-clearing. Keep the operator's mr-supervisor-disable as a hard human-only pause — it is working as intended and is the correct response to credit scarcity. Replace the supervisor's self-written .native-supervisor-disabled with a standdown that behaves like the existing .blocked-on-human gate 20 lines below it in the same script (mr-native-tick.sh:144-159): let event ticks pass through, self-lift on a wake condition, and expire after a bounded interval. Refuse to arm it at all while a slice is live or a .done file is pending. Log its creation with an actor and a reason — nothing currently records either.
recommendations.rationale: Two different failures share one switch, which is why they were conflated in the ground truth. The operator's pause is correct behaviour. The supervisor's self-disable is not: it blocked a real completion event for 83.9 hours, its 'no mechanically-launchable slice' judgment was factually wrong (7 fully-decomposed slices with touches:/after: sat in a spec committed 5 hours earlier, one of them CRITICAL and later launched with no additional spec work), and MR_FORCE bypasses it on entry without clearing it — which is how a $274.37 slice was launched into a disabled loop it could not harvest.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes the ~21h of in-window self-disable episodes and, more importantly, the event-blocking behaviour: the M21b-2 merge would have landed in minutes rather than 3.5 days. Under the corrected objective this is not about duty cycle — stranded finished work is exactly what operator policy G1 identifies as worse than idling.
recommendations.risk: A self-clearing standdown can loop if the queue-derivation defect persists; pair with the ready_set from R3 so 'nothing launchable' becomes a checkable fact rather than a recalled judgment.

recommendations.action: Route spec-authoring by tier like every other work item, and give the unattended channel a forward-work mode. Add an explicit routing rule for spec authoring (currently absent from all doctrine) so a security/schema-surface spec is not authored on the cheapest model in the fleet. Define a synthetic elaboration slice shape — slice='<M>-spec', touches='specs/monster-realm-v2/<M>*.spec.md, specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md', tier=hard — so the existing mr-spawn path can run the existing build-loop-prompt elaboration procedure unattended for milestones whose decisions are already made (M-postgate-client-coverage and M-postgate-roster-wave-3 both have PLAN bullets stating exactly what to do).
recommendations.rationale: Both in-window forward-spec ceremonies ran 100% on sonnet purely because the operator continued a cron tick session (569/569 and 295/295 assistant messages), while every slice they feed ran opus@high or fable@xhigh under a rule that routes 'security/RLS surfaces' to fable. The highest-leverage artifact in the pipeline — the spec 8 downstream slices are built from — got the cheapest tier by accident, not decision. Separately, the only unattended generator is structurally residual-only (its Phase 6 authors 'M-postgate-<lineage>' by construction), which is why the loop's diet is 35-46% fix-up.
recommendations.expected_effect: Improves the quality of the artifact with the largest downstream multiplier, at trivial marginal cost — the unattended review channel already produces build-ready slices at $6.75-$12.31 each, 5-9x cheaper per hour of runway than the attended ceremony, and all 15 in-window review-residual slices merged with zero failures attributable to spec ambiguity.
recommendations.risk: Genuinely open design questions (M22's erase-vs-anonymize policy, retention windows, export format) legitimately need the operator and should stay attended — scope the unattended path to DECOMPOSITION of already-decided milestones only. Whether an unattended pass matches attended quality is untested; there is no instance in the corpus.

recommendations.action: Remove machinery that is measurably doing no work: the ollama preflight in mr-native-tick.sh:30-47 (803 warm-ups, 0 triage invocations ever, 11.4 warm-ups per actual use, 86 of them fired inside a span where no slice could finish, now warming a different 21GB tag than the operator's Hermes agent runs on a 16GB GPU); the feedback subsystem (mr-feedback, 15,911 B, polled every tick against a ledger frozen since 2026-07-27 with 0 rows ever reaching its terminal states, plus its four prompt blocks and the mandatory 'Items:' PR-body field); the retro machinery (mr-retro-request, playbook; $MEM/retros/ has never been created); and the orphaned mr-metrics / mr-evidence / mr-selfcheck (0 call sites, 0 log lines ever). If summarization is still wanted, move the preflight below the disabled/standdown gates so it only fires when a summary can actually be consumed.
recommendations.rationale: Do this for signal quality, not tokens — carrying the whole 155-line prompt forever costs ~$83/yr, which rounds to zero. The cost is that a subsystem whose own prompt text admits it never worked is still labelled 'ACTIVE v1.0' on every paid tick, which degrades the credibility of every other ACTIVE label, and that a 21GB model is pinned resident for 30 of every 60 minutes on a box whose own launch protocol budgets RAM per additional slot.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removes ~26KB of orphaned control surface and ~15% of prompt text, ends GPU contention with the operator's interactive agent, and stops injecting unverified local-model prose into 25 of 43 event bundles. Explicitly NOT justified as a token saving.
recommendations.risk: Deleting the feedback ledger discards 189 historical rows — archive rather than remove. The ollama summaries are advisory and might occasionally inform a decision; that counterfactual is unmeasurable, so move rather than delete if in doubt.

recommendations.action: Exclude */.codegraph/* from the human-activity probe at mr-native-tick.sh:240-244, matching the exclusion mr-spawn:35 already has, and suppress trips on paths the loop itself wrote in the preceding tick (compare against the just-merged commit's file list).
recommendations.rationale: The probe was 100% false-positive in-window (72/72), with 90% of trips on the CodeGraph daemon's own index files (codegraph.db-wal, daemon.log) and the remaining 7 on the loop's own ff-only merge writes. The documented decision not to exclude .codegraph rests on 'measured false-trip cost $0', which measured the wrong axis — the cost is latency and lost decision slots, not dollars. The loop has already begun pre-emptively self-censoring ('composite launch deferred (own-write probe-trip risk, per doctrine)', costing 105 minutes).
recommendations.expected_effect: Recovers ~7h/week of self-inflicted latency and 13 lost cron decision slots, and makes the doctrine's blessed merge->launch composite viable — currently performing the merge poisons the probe that gates the launch, so every composite is a coin flip. Ranked low deliberately: under the corrected objective this buys responsiveness, not credits.
recommendations.risk: Excluding a worktree path could in principle mask a genuine human edit inside it — this is the stated reason the exclusion was withheld. Scope the exclusion to .codegraph/ specifically rather than to worktrees generally.

recommendations.action: Protect the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet and the proof-of-teeth discipline from any cost-cutting pass. Do not conflate them with the mechanical gating_test_audit in R5 — they are different mechanisms with opposite measured value.
recommendations.rationale: This is the best-spending part of the loop. reviewer+red-team are 93 runs for ~$171/week at $1.71-$1.97 per run, and they find verified, independently reproduced merge-blockers before code exists — 14r-d's reviewer caught a log-ratchet blocker whose fix files were outside touches:, and red-team reproduced it independently against the real toolchain in a throwaway clone. The m20c HIGH finding (unguarded navigator reads aborting main() bootstrap) was found AFTER CI was green. Separately, the eval corpus's proof-of-teeth mandate ('a gate that has never failed is a decoration') and the manifest-count tests dismissed elsewhere as ceremony are in fact bidirectional and not vacuous.
recommendations.expected_effect: Preserves the mechanism most responsible for the operator's PRIMARY axis. Note the correct target if subagent cost must be cut: tester (37 runs, $377.20, 46% of subagent spend, median 58 turns) and general-purpose ($134.07, 11 runs) are 63% of subagent spend at 5-7x the per-run cost of a reviewer.
recommendations.risk: None from keeping it. The risk is the opposite — a naive cost pass would cut the cheap-per-run review roles first because they are numerous, and leave the two expensive implementation roles untouched.

recommendations.action: Re-arm the improvement loop with an owner and a trigger. Add a loop/process lens to the weekly review prompt (currently scoped exclusively to the monster-realm subproject across all 306 lines) so it audits the harness as well as the game, and adopt one standing rule from the ADR-0011 precedent: land the counter one cycle BEFORE the change it is meant to measure, never in the same commit. Recreate the retro cadence or explicitly retire it — do not leave it described in doctrine and never executed.
recommendations.rationale: The improvement loop froze on 2026-08-01 and did not respond to a single incident in the window: the prompt carries 21 dated incident parentheticals across seven dates, all July, zero August, while the window produced a 97%-utilization overage week, four cap-blowing runs and 11 false gate flags. ADR-0011 is the one prior intervention with a clean verified result (237 WATCHER-DEAD false alarms before, exactly 0 after), and it worked because it named a counter and checked it. The v3 push, by contrast, replaced its own instrumentation in the same commit, so its effect can never be computed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores the mechanism that produced ~50 fixes in 4 days and without which every recommendation above decays. Directly prevents the RC1 recurrence pattern, where the utilization signal was seen, named in the prompt, and dismissed without revisiting.
recommendations.risk: Adding a loop lens to the weekly review competes for the same review budget that currently produces the game's residual milestones; scope it as a short standing checklist rather than a second full multi-lens pass.

diagnoses.theme:
END-TO-END PIPELINE POST-MORTEM: the pipeline builds well and governs blind. Judged on value-per-weekly-credit (the operator's real constraint), the 14 steps split cleanly into three groups — a small set that is genuinely excellent and must be protected, a large middle that is ceremony inherited from July incidents, and one instrumentation defect that poisons every scheduling decision the loop makes.

THE CENTRAL MEASURED FACT (mine, verified this session). Every headless run emits top-level `{"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{...}}` JSON lines carrying `utilization` for `rateLimitType:"seven_day"` — the TRUE, account-wide fraction of the weekly plan allowance. Verified live: /tmp/mr_pass_13r-h.log lines 2/134/797/1140/1830 carry 0.52→0.56; 74 of 151 surviving tick logs carry a reading. The event is emitted on each whole-percent change, and one appears within the first few lines of a run — so a fresh reading is available at launch time, on every tick, for free. `grep -rn 'utilization\|isUsingOverage'` over mr-native-tick.sh, mr-cost-watch, mr-situation, mr-record returns ZERO consumers. The only reference is mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116, which enumerates the field set as `{status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage}` — `utilization` is NOT in the doctrine's own list. The loop does not know the field exists.
Consequences I measured directly: the 2026-08-10T05:00Z tick read `utilization:0.87, surpassedThreshold:0.75` and stood down citing "no launchable slice"; the 09:05Z tick read `utilization:0.90, surpassedThreshold:0.75` and launched M21b-2 — the window's single most expensive slice ($274.37, 183% of its declared $150 cap) — while the internal governor printed 64.7% / NORMAL. That launch is what consumed the remainder of the allowance and forced the operator's manual pause. This is not a one-off: on 2026-07-31 the fan-out pair 11r-c/11r-e ran to `utilization:0.99` and `0.95` with `surpassedThreshold:0.9`, and mr_pass_11r-c.log contains `{"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true}` — the loop has already run itself into purchased credits, twice, with the API explicitly signalling it.
Note the phase is already right: `.weekly-reset-anchor`=1784851200 decodes to Thu 2026-07-23 20:00 America/New_York, and the live `resetsAt` values (1786060800 / 1786665600 / 1787270400) are all Thu 20:00 ET. Only the METRIC is wrong, not the window.

PER-STEP VERDICTS (function → performance → failure modes → cost → verdict → change):

1. VISION/INTAKE (turn operator intent into queued work) — MAJOR_ISSUE. The weekly review is the only functioning channel and it is the cheapest thing in the system (~$54-74 → 7-8 build-ready slices ≈ $3/runway-hour vs $15.6-27.6 for attended ceremony). Everything else is dead: feedback-ledger.jsonl has 0 rows since 2026-07-27, its terminal states VERIFIED/SHIPPED-VERIFIED have never been used in 189 rows, yet 4 prompt blocks call it "ACTIVE v1.0" on all 65 paid ticks and mr-brief-template.md:31 still mandates an `Items:` line in every PR body. The retro ceremony has produced zero artifacts — I verified `$MEM/retros/` does not exist. Decision issues capture 11/11 but consume in 4-7 days (issue #284 answered 08-08, shipped as 13r-e on 08-15). Change: retire the feedback/retro blocks; give decision answers a tick-level consumer.

2. MILESTONE SPEC AUTHORING (PLAN bullet → M*.spec.md with EARS) — MAJOR_ISSUE. It produces good specs (M20 4,801B→75,421B) but: $482.03 measured across two sessions and $0.00 in the ledger; both ran 100% claude-sonnet-5 by accidental session inheritance (569/569 and 295/295 assistant messages) while every slice they feed runs opus@high or fable@xhigh — including the accounts/auth security surface; and it is structurally unreachable from the supervisor because a sketch has no slice ID and no `touches:` to put in vars.json. Costs 9.2 and 4.1 operator-hours. Change: define a synthetic elaboration slice shape so mr-spawn can launch build-loop-prompt.md's existing elaboration procedure unattended, and route spec authoring explicitly (never inherit the tick's model).

3. SLICE DECOMPOSITION (per-slice touches/gates/tier) — MAJOR_ISSUE, and the most load-bearing unexamined step. `touches:` is trusted for fan-out scheduling AND is the causal generator of the rework backlog: any work outside the declared set becomes an ADR "Residuals" bullet that nothing reads (78 defer/park phrases across 165 ADRs, 21 ADRs with a Residuals section, zero mechanical consumers; mean disclosure→remediation latency 13.1 days, max 20). ADR-0165 is the proof — Accepted 2026-07-31, "implementation defers to 11r-i", 11r-i merged without it, CHANGELOG re-drifted 18 PRs, finally implemented 15 days later by 13r-g. Separately the brief grants ALWAYS-in-scope companions (`*.test.ts` siblings, docs/adr/**, ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md) that are NOT in `touches:`, so mr-disjoint compares the wrong sets → 14r-c/14r-e collided on client/src/main.wiring.test.ts (park + $36.19 resume) and 14r-b conflicted on ARCHITECTURE.md + DIGEST.md. Change: expand touches by the companion rules before mr-disjoint; make ADR Residuals emit a queue entry.

4. QUEUE & PRIORITIZATION — BROKEN_REPLACE. mr-state.json `queue[]` is 58 past-tense narrative paragraphs with zero forward items (the weekly-review SSOT says so outright at mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:257). `after:` has no mechanical consumer anywhere. Priority is re-derived from a 390-line PLAN.md §9 prose block every tick. Result: 2026-08-10T05:00:52Z "no mechanical slice launchable" while 7 fully decomposed slices sat in a spec committed 5h earlier, four of them `after: none`. CRITICAL slice 13r-a went 117.1h from build-ready to launch. Per the operator correction this caused the ~21h of self-disables, NOT the 85h halt — but it is real and independently costly. Change: derive a machine-readable ready-set from the spec files; forbid "nothing launchable" unless that set is empty.

5. BRIEF CONSTRUCTION — WORKING_WELL. PROTECT THIS. The rendered TARGET_DESC gives the verified defect with file:line, the correct SSOT predicate AND the wrong one to avoid, EARS, the proof-of-teeth fixture, touches, ADR number and decision-hook scoping, in ~3,152 tokens (7% of preamble). Zero of 18 merges show scope re-derivation. It works because it moves derivation out of the expensive session into cheap prepared text — do not shorten it. Two narrow defects: line 33 tells every build session "only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical" when `costwatch_enforce:false` means nothing is mechanical (this is the direct mechanism of the 183%-of-cap run); and mr-spawn:59-62 emits `""` for routine tier, so 13 of 22 slices got no quality-tier signal at all.

6. LAUNCH (probe, disjointness, fan-out, routing) — MAJOR_ISSUE. Tier is the highest-leverage decision in the system (it sets model, effort, cap, lens depth) and is a fresh unreproducible judgment: mr-tier-map.json covers 0 of 29 in-window slices and is self-labelled `_rules_frozen_2026-07-25`; m20b was tagged routine while m20a/c/d/e were hard despite prompt:17 naming "M20 slices" an unconditional HARD criterion; 13r-c was tagged routine despite touching accounts.rs plus six security evals. Tier and model are 100% collinear (every $150-cap run fable, every $60-cap run opus, zero crossover), so the 2.18x fable premium — 57% of window spend — is structurally unmeasurable, and fable's price is an explicit un-calibrated guess. The activity probe was 100% false-positive (72/72; 90% CodeGraph's own db-wal/daemon.log), and the loop's own ff-only merge trips the probe gating its next launch, so the blessed merge→launch composite is self-defeating.

7. BUILD SESSION EXECUTION — MAJOR_ISSUE, and where ~90% of credits go. 65.3% of build spend is cache-READ, 25.6% cache-write, 9.1% output — only 9% of the budget buys tokens the model produces. Zero context-compaction or context-editing events across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts; contexts ran to 611K. 32.2% of parent prompt volume is consumed BEFORE the first repo-file edit (range 12%-77%). The orchestrator makes 791 Bash grep/sed/cat/ls calls and 0 codegraph calls while its own subagents make 47 — a violation of the operator's global routing doctrine that exists only at the orchestrator layer. The review sub-roster is the best-spending part of the whole loop (reviewer+red-team, 93 runs, ~$171/wk, found the 14r-d OBS-2 log-ratchet merge-blocker before code existed, and a HIGH in m20c AFTER CI was green) — protect it; the cost is in tester/general-purpose (63% of subagent spend).

8. LOCAL GATES — MIXED, trending false-assurance. Proof-of-teeth is excellent and must be protected ("a gate that has never failed is a decoration" — evals/observability-stack-config.eval.mjs:6-11). But 7 `*-security.eval.mjs` gates are measurably blind RIGHT NOW, two proven to swallow the scan needle, all parked to a slice `14r-c-2` that exists in zero spec/PLAN/state file. The mutation ratchet was remediated by RAISING the cap 299→324 (43% survival) with 87% of survivors never triaged. Performance — the operator's named PRIMARY axis — is gated only by 7 nanosecond-scale pure functions with ~20x headroom; nothing measures reducer latency, subscription fan-out or frame time, and m20d built the load driver then wired it to nothing. 30-42% of the server test corpus is regex-over-source-text, which under-protects correctness and actively penalises refactoring.

9. PR + CI — MINOR_ISSUE. 71 runs, 18% red/cancelled, $0 (public repo). Real defect is reaction, not CI: nightly mutation-server was red 5 consecutive nights with the other 3 jobs green every time and nothing noticed; a chronic flake set (wallet-balance.spec.ts 4x, logged verbatim as "4th occurrence") has never been queued for a fix, which trains the loop to classify red CI as "unrelated flake" by pattern-match.

10. SUPERVISOR REVIEW/AUDIT — BROKEN_REPLACE for gating_test_audit; the rest is fine. 11 flags in-window, 11 adjudicated CLEAN, 0 true positives; 0 true positives across the entire v3 era. mr-audit:58-59 makes tier=hard an unconditional flag. Documented causes are lexical: doc-comment prose, `.iter().skip()` read as a test-skip marker, import-line reflow, manifest count bumps. mr-audit:51 scopes the diff to test paths, so suppressions added to production source are invisible. And "mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN" is stamped on the merge record of m20b — the slice that shipped an observability stack which crash-looped 4 of 8 containers on first boot. The orchestration audit (reads the build session's own log) is accurate — keep it. The tick-log CENSUS is broken (159/162 "agents: none" because mr-native-tick.sh:323 greps the tick's own log, not the detached build session's).

11. MERGE & CLEANUP — WORKING_WELL. Zero ORPHAN-RUN, zero WATCHER-DEAD, zero CRASHED rows in-window; 2 stale chain-mutex takeovers both correctly adjudicated; 7 flock contentions all requeued; 108 events archived, pending dir empty. The 2026-08-01 ADR-0011 fix took WATCHER-DEAD from 237 fires to 0 and has held for 14 days. This is the template for what a good intervention looks like here — a named counter, a measured defect, a post-fix count of zero.

12. RECORD-KEEPING — MAJOR_ISSUE with a strong core. ADRs are genuinely load-bearing (143 distinct ADRs cited 3,729 times in production source; 14 of 15 in-window ADRs appear in code, at decision granularity like "ADR-0189 D6") — protect them as navigational anchors. But the ADR is doing three jobs and is bad at the third: ADR-0180 is a 1,034-line milestone journal with five append-only build-note amendments, and it is precisely where the observability crash-loop fixes went to be forgotten. Ledger integrity: 21-32% of in-window rows are COST-UNKNOWN; resume passes append to the same log after the FINISHED row and are never re-summed ($46.84 of measured spend lost in-window); /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log is reused per slice name so 13r-c's and m20c's original logs are destroyed. Memory index: 26 of 133 MEMORY.md links dead (19.5%), 19 of 89 wikilinks dangling — including `[[monster-realm-supervisor-cost-ssot]]`, referenced by the most load-bearing cost lesson in the vault. Two handoff files differ 240x in size (428,676 B vs 1,781 B).

13. REVIEW CADENCE — MINOR_ISSUE, mostly working. It is the only queue-filler and by far the best value-per-credit supply channel. But it is a flat treadmill, not a converging loop: 13 residual milestones, 85 slices, output flat at 6-9 per cycle while cadence accelerated 7d→6d→3d→4d. It is scoped exclusively to the game (306 lines, zero loop/process lens), it consumes a whole milestone in <24h against a multi-day cadence (~7:1 supply/demand mismatch), and it books $0.00 in the ledger. Its residual milestones reliably manufacture new residuals — 13r's spec names the class it is fixing and then 13r-a/13r-b each spawned fresh untracked residuals.

14. META — BROKEN_REPLACE. The improvement loop DIED on 2026-08-01. 46 of 51 loop-infra commits landed 2026-07-24..27; every mr-* commit since 2026-08-08 is mr-state.json bookkeeping. Five retros, all July. The prompt carries 21 dated incident parentheticals across 7 dates, ALL July, ZERO August — so it is a frozen snapshot of what the loop knew on 2026-08-01 and contains no rule about anything that happened in this window. The one experiment the loop's own README promised ("A/B hard slices opus@xhigh vs fable@xhigh ... frees ~$250-400/wk") never ran, and n=1 at hard/opus makes it unanswerable retroactively. Meanwhile the operator's own pause tool, /home/mdrewt/.local/bin/mr-supervisor-disable, is a bare `touch` with no reason and no timestamp — which is exactly why the 85h halt was mis-attributed to a supervisor self-disable in the first place.

WHAT WORKS AND WHY (do not break these): the brief's TARGET_DESC, because it front-loads derivation into cheap text; the reviewer/red-team pre-code gauntlet, because it finds defects before code exists, which is the cheapest place; proof-of-teeth RED-first gates, because a gate that has never failed is a decoration; ADRs as decision-granular code anchors; the ~25-line-per-slice residual spec format (15/15 merged, 14/15 first-attempt); the weekly review as proof that unattended spec authoring works cheaply; and the event bridge / lock hygiene, which lost zero events all window.

root_causes.statement: The loop governs on a synthetic, self-referential cost proxy while the true, authoritative signal — account-wide weekly plan utilization — arrives on the wire in every single run and is discarded unread.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED this session: /tmp/mr_pass_13r-h.log lines 2,134,797,1140,1830 carry top-level {"type":"rate_limit_event","rate_limit_info":{"status":"allowed_warning","resetsAt":1787270400,"rateLimitType":"seven_day","utilization":0.52..0.56,"isUsingOverage":false}}. 74 of 151 surviving tick logs carry a seven_day reading. `grep -rn 'utilization|isUsingOverage'` over mr-native-tick.sh, mr-cost-watch, mr-situation, mr-record = ZERO consumers. mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 enumerates the field set as {status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage} — `utilization` is absent from the doctrine's own list. Meanwhile mr-situation:56-100 budget() sums cost_usd from monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl, and mr-usage-daily.jsonl re-sums the SAME file (verified delta 0.00 on all 8 daily rows), and ~/.claude/usage-log.csv has columns timestamp,kind,name,session,project with no cost or token fields. There is exactly one cost source and it is a model of itself.
root_causes.mechanism: weekly_limit_usd=2783 was extrapolated from ONE operator-reported observation on 2026-07-25 (internal_total 1002 / drew_total_pct 0.36). Fable — 57% of window spend — is priced by an explicit config guess ('ESTIMATE 1.5x opus ... CALIBRATE from first fable run') that was never calibrated. mr-cost-watch's estimator additionally double-counts usage events per content block (1.75 events per distinct message.id, range 1.38-2.20) and prices 17.9% of cache-creation tokens at the 5m rate when they are ephemeral_1h. So ledger/raw ranges 0.637-1.008 across 21 slices against a hard-coded 0.80 factor. Every downstream reading — governor state, tier caps, SPEND-ALERT — inherits a run-dependent error, and because the proxy is local it is blind by construction to the operator's usage on other machines and projects, which the account-level gauge includes automatically.
root_causes.quantified_cost: At the moment the operator paused the loop, real account utilization was 0.90 while the internal governor reported 64.7% and NORMAL — a measured 1.39x under-report. The API even emitted surpassedThreshold:0.75 in the same event. Over the whole window the governor never left NORMAL and never once influenced a decision. Additionally the ledger loses $46.84 of measured in-window spend (14r-e $40.58 + m20c $6.26) because resume passes append after the FINISHED row and are never re-summed, and 21-32% of rows carry cost_usd=null.

root_causes.statement: There is no pacing mechanism anywhere: the weekly allowance is run as a race to exhaustion, so the operator must personally watch usage and hit a kill switch — and the loop's most expensive launches happen at the highest utilization.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED: the 2026-08-10T05:00Z tick log carries utilization:0.87 with surpassedThreshold:0.75 and stood down; the 09:05Z tick log carries utilization:0.90 and launched M21b-2, a hard-tier fable slice that cost $274.37 = 183% of its declared $150 cap. Historical precedent: mr_pass_11r-c.log and mr_pass_11r-e.log (a concurrent fan-out pair, 2026-07-31) climbed to utilization 0.99 and 0.95 carrying surpassedThreshold:0.9, and 11r-c contains {"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true} — a real overage burn. mr-budget-config.json:55 costwatch_enforce=false; in-window COSTWATCH census: 12 WARN, 10 STOP-MONITOR, 4 HARD-MONITOR, 0 enforcement actions ever. 4 of 21 slices exceeded their own tier cap in real ledger dollars (M21b-2 182.9%, M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%). /home/mdrewt/.local/bin/mr-supervisor-disable is a bare `touch` with no reason and no timestamp.
root_causes.mechanism: Enforcement was left disarmed for a documented and correct reason — mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 notes all 4 historical HARD trips merged EXIT=0 and 'a kill strands locks and hard-blocks relaunch'. But that objection is about KILLING a live run. The operator's stated scarcity policy (finish in-flight, start nothing new) requires only a LAUNCH gate, which has none of those failure modes. Because nobody separated 'don't start' from 'kill', the whole enforcement axis stayed off, and because no component reasons about rate-of-spend against time-to-reset, the loop cannot distinguish 'plenty of allowance, run hot' from 'one day left, land what is flying'.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The week's entire allowance was consumed in ~3.5 active days (utilization 0.29 on Aug 7 16:21 → 0.90 on Aug 10 05:08), forcing ~3.5 days of manual operator pause. At least one prior week (resets Aug 6 20:00 ET) hit the ceiling and burned PURCHASED credits, which the operator states are strictly less cost-effective. Ongoing cost: the operator personally monitors usage and intervenes — the babysitting that objective G3 exists to eliminate.

root_causes.statement: Recording is not queueing: the `touches:` discipline that makes fan-out safe is also the mechanism that manufactures the rework backlog, because work pushed outside a slice's declared set is written to an ADR Residuals bullet that has no mechanical consumer.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: docs/adr/0165-changelog-freshness-nightly-drift-check.md:9 (Accepted 2026-07-31, slice 11r-d): 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared `touches:`.' 11r-i merged 2026-08-02 without implementing it; CHANGELOG re-drifted 18 PRs; finally implemented by 13r-g on 2026-08-15, 15 days after Acceptance. Same pattern in-window: 14r-d's ADR-0185 D6 routes a fix away because 'the fix files are outside touches:'; justfile:35-39 documents wiring a perf gate in the wrong place because 'ci.yml is outside m20a's touches'. Corpus surface: 78 defer/park phrases across 165 ADRs ('deferred to' 45, 'a later slice' 11, 'future slice' 10, 'parked to' 8); 21 ADRs carry a Residuals section; zero scripts read any of it. Reproduced inside the remediation itself: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124-190 parks 7 blind *-security.eval.mjs gates to slice `14r-c-2`, and `grep -rl 14r-c-2` over specs/, PLAN.md and mr-state.json returns ZERO hits.
root_causes.mechanism: Fan-out safety requires forbidding cross-slice file writes. The forbidden work is therefore real, known, and documented at the exact moment of discovery — but the only place it is written is prose inside an ADR. Nothing converts prose to a queue entry. Weeks later a human-triggered multi-lens review rediscovers it at the most expensive possible price and emits ~7 new slices, which then produce their own untracked residuals. mr-state.json `queue[]` cannot absorb them either, because it is 58 past-tense narrative paragraphs rather than a forward list.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend ($643.73 of $1,817.65) is remediation of the loop's own prior output; 46.6% lifetime ($3,913.21 of $8,394.81). 7 of the 15 residual slices in the 13r/14r program are the disclosed-but-untracked class. Mean disclosure→remediation latency 13.1 days (median 14, max 20) over 10 traceable items. Right now, 7 security eval gates are measurably blind — two proven to swallow the scan needle — and are tracked nowhere.

root_causes.statement: Several gates cannot fail correctly, and the loop treats their green as assurance: a 0%-precision audit trains its reader to rubber-stamp, blind security evals pass on code they exist to reject, the mutation ratchet was fixed by loosening it, and the operator's PRIMARY axis (performance) has essentially no gate at all.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: gating_test_audit: 11 FLAGGED in-window, 11 adjudicated CLEAN, 0 true positives; 0 true positives across the entire v3 era of the 710-row ledger. mr-audit:58-59 makes tier=hard an unconditional flag; documented flag causes are doc-comment prose, `.iter().skip()` misread as a test-skip marker, import-line reflow, and manifest count bumps. mr-audit:51 scopes the diff to test paths, so suppressions in production source are invisible. Ledger 2026-08-09T03:06:33Z records 'm20b ... mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' on the commit that shipped an observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped 4 of 8 containers (root causes itemised in M-postgate-thirteenth-review-residuals.spec.md:57-76). justfile:110 mutate-server cap=324 with ADR-0183:41-42 recording 324 missed of 753 = 43.0% survival and :130-136 stating ~282 survivors (87%) were never triaged. game-core/benches/budgets.rs:11-13: 'Ceilings are ~20x the locally measured mean' across 7 pure functions; no reducer, subscription or frame-time budget exists anywhere.
root_causes.mechanism: Each gate was added in response to a real worry, then never validated against outcomes. A gate whose flags are always false teaches the adjudicator that flags are noise — the eleventh FLAGGED→CLEAN is read far less carefully than the first — so the gate actively erodes the vigilance it was built to create while consuming a full-diff supervisor read on every hard-tier merge. Meanwhile the gates that would catch the defects that actually shipped (runtime boot, reducer latency, semantic mutation) either do not exist or were re-baselined upward rather than fixed.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 11 full-diff supervisor adjudications in-window, including the window's single most expensive tick ($5.03, 3.8x the median). 7 security gates guarding battle/evolution/raising/recruit/shop/trade/NPC reducers can currently pass GREEN on code they must reject, after $115.97 spent across 13r-c and 14r-c. Nightly mutation-server was red 5 consecutive nights (2026-08-09..13) with the other 3 jobs green each time and zero reaction. 30-42% of the 637 server tests are regex-over-source-text, so they simultaneously under-protect correctness and penalise refactoring.

root_causes.statement: Build-session context volume is completely unmanaged, so roughly nine of every ten credits buy re-reading of a prefix rather than work — and no mechanism anywhere prunes, compacts, or scopes it.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: Across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts: cache_read $1,012.79 (65.3%), cache_write $396.98 (25.6%), output $140.81 (9.1%), fresh input $0.94 (0.06%). ZERO isCompactSummary / compact_boundary events in any of the 230 transcripts; final contexts 295,092 / 454,481 / 611,322 tokens. 226.1M of 703.0M parent prompt tokens (32.2%) are consumed before the first edit to a repo file, median at turn 50, range 12.0% (13r-f) to 77.0% (m20d). Assistant thinking/output carried forward = 243.9M tokens (34.7% of parent prompt volume). Static preamble 44,288 tokens x 2,718 parent turns = 120.4M (17.1%) — while subagents run on an 11,103-token median preamble, 4x smaller. Parent tool census: Bash 2,135 (68.6%), Grep 0, Glob 0, codegraph_explore 0 — against 47 codegraph calls from its own subagents; 791 Bash grep/sed/cat/ls calls produced 2,080,724 chars of navigation output. memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md is 428,676 bytes (~107K tokens, 154 sections) and orientation greps against it returned 21,481-27,753 chars at turn 4.
root_causes.mechanism: Every token added at turn i is re-billed on every remaining turn, so a 12K-token Read at turn 1 of a 180-turn session costs ~2.4M cache-read tokens while the same read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M. With no compaction, no context-editing, no thinking-clear, and an orchestrator that navigates by grep instead of the pre-built index its own subagents use, cost scales with turns x context rather than with work done. This is also why prompt-length optimisation is the wrong lever (carrying the entire 155-line supervisor prompt forever costs ~$83/yr, 0.087% of spend) — the multiplier is in the session, not the prompt.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$1,013/week of pure prefix re-reading at the observed rate. 24,125 prompt tokens re-read per line of code shipped; $115.18 per 1,000 lines of production code. Halving average per-turn context would roughly halve slice cost with no model or scheduling change — worth about a third of the weekly allowance.

root_causes.statement: The process-improvement loop has no owner and stopped 14 days before this review; ceremony accretes on incident and is never retired on evidence, so the doctrine is now a frozen July snapshot that says nothing about anything that happened in this window.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: 46 of 51 loop-infra commits landed 2026-07-24..27; last real mechanism change is 7df734d on 2026-08-01; every mr-* commit since 2026-08-08 is mr-state.json bookkeeping. mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md contains 21 dated incident parentheticals across exactly 7 dates, all July 2026, zero August. Five retros exist, all July; `$MEM/retros/` does not exist (verified). Dead machinery still carried: feedback-ledger.jsonl frozen since 2026-07-27 with 0 rows ever reaching its own terminal states, yet 4 prompt blocks call it 'ACTIVE v1.0' and mr-brief-template.md:31 still mandates an `Items:` PR field; the N>=3 fan-out protocol has been used ZERO times (85 single launches, 17 pairs, 0 triples); mr-metrics (6,935 B), mr-evidence, mr-retro-request, mr-selfcheck are wired to nothing; the ollama preflight fired 803 warm-ups of a 21GB model for 0 triage invocations, with three competing 21GB tags installed on a 16GB GPU; mr-native-tick.sh:323 CENSUS reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines because it greps the wrong log. Total control surface: ~133KB of mr-* scripts + ~132KB of doctrine governing 29 commits/week.
root_causes.mechanism: Every incident appends a rule; nothing ever measures whether a rule still earns its place, so the prompt grows (16,303 → 33,059 bytes) and its rule density rises (75 bold spans, 89 imperative modals, 70 rule arrows, one 3,296-char line carrying nine unrelated rules). Retrieval degrades: the nine-word 'Nothing remains -> write DONE + disable' clause sits at character ~1,400 of that line, immediately after a 'take the documented default and PROCEED' clause, with 'nothing remains' never defined.
root_causes.quantified_cost: The window produced a 183%-of-cap run, a real overage-risk trajectory, 11 false-positive gate flags and ~21h of self-disable — and changed not one line of doctrine. The README's own promised experiment (opus vs fable at hard tier, '$250-400/wk headroom' ≈ 9-14% of the weekly allowance) has sat unrun for 3 weeks and is now unanswerable retroactively because n=1 at hard/opus.

root_causes.statement: Every high-leverage routing decision is an unreproducible per-launch judgment with no measurement attached, and the one that dominates spend is priced by a guess.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:17 claims tier is 'derived mechanically from the slice's `touches:` globs', but mr-tier-map.json is self-labelled `_rules_frozen_2026-07-25` and covers 0 of 29 in-window slices. Sibling slices in one milestone got different tiers on consecutive ticks: m20b routine vs m20a/c/d/e hard, despite prompt:17 naming 'M20 slices' an unconditional HARD criterion; 13r-c routine despite declared touches including server-module/src/accounts.rs and six *-security evals. Tier and model are 100% collinear: every $150-cap run is fable, every $60-cap run is opus, zero crossover across 21 slices. fable = 57% of window spend ($1,032.59 of $1,824.97) at a config-declared 'ESTIMATE 1.5x opus ... CALIBRATE from first fable run' that never happened. The quality columns that would break the tie are unusable: remote_red_fix_cycles sums to 0 across 446 v3-era rows, and master_ci_after reads 'pending'/'in_progress' on 9 of 17 populated values. Spec authoring — the highest-leverage artifact of all — ran 100% on sonnet by accidental session inheritance (569/569 and 295/295 assistant messages).
root_causes.mechanism: Tier sets model, effort, cap and lens-battery depth in one judgment call, then the routing rule makes model a deterministic function of tier, which destroys the contrast needed to evaluate either. With no slice-size denominator recorded anywhere in the ledger (no LOC, files-changed, or EARS-criteria count) and no usable quality column, there is no way to compute value-per-credit for any routing choice, so the choice can never be corrected by evidence.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$611 of the window's $1,864 slice spend is the fable-over-opus delta, unjustified and unrefuted. fable slices average $123.49 vs opus $56.66 (2.18x) and $25.22 vs $17.33 per kline (1.46x) — but fable is CHEAPER per file touched ($4.51 vs $4.99), so the premium may be surface breadth rather than model. An under-tiered security slice (13r-c) received a thinner lens battery on the accounts/auth surface.

recommendations.action: In $MEM/mr-cost-watch, add a `read_util()` helper beside the existing `price_log()` (mr-cost-watch:16-43) that runs /usr/bin/python3 over the tail of /tmp/mr_pass_$S.log selecting lines where json type == 'rate_limit_event', and returns the newest rate_limit_info with rateLimitType=='seven_day' as `utilization resetsAt isUsingOverage`. Call it inside the existing 20s watch loop (mr-cost-watch:66-84) and log a `PLANWATCH <slice> util=<pct> resets_in=<h> overage=<bool>` line to mr-native-tick.log alongside the existing COSTWATCH lines. Parse JSON with python, never grep raw text (the brief is echoed into the log — the trap already documented at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116).

recommendations.action: Persist every observed reading to a new append-only $MEM/mr-plan-utilization.jsonl ({ts, source: tick|slice, run_id, slice, rateLimitType, utilization, resetsAt, isUsingOverage, surpassedThreshold}) from two writers: R-01's PLANWATCH loop, and mr-native-tick.sh's post-run reconcile block (which already tails $TLOG at :323 for the broken CENSUS). Retain forever — the file is a few KB/week.

I could only reconstruct the 0.29->0.90 trajectory because 37 pass logs and 151 tick logs happened to survive. Next reboot or rerun and this postmortem becomes impossible.

Gives every future retro a real burn curve and a real value-per-credit denominator.

recommendations.action: Rewrite mr-situation's `budget()` (mr-situation:56-100, currently summing cost_usd from monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl into `d7_usd`) to emit a plan block sourced from $MEM/mr-plan-utilization.jsonl: {util_pct, util_observed_at, util_age_min, resets_at, hours_to_reset, is_using_overage, state}. Keep the existing .weekly-reset-anchor — I verified 1784851200 decodes to Thu 2026-07-23 20:00 America/New_York and every live resetsAt (1786060800/1786665600/1787270400) is Thu 20:00 ET, so the phase is already correct; only the metric is wrong. Retain the ledger dollar sum as a clearly-labelled secondary `attribution_usd` field for per-slice attribution, which the account-level gauge cannot do.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED: at 2026-08-10T05:00Z the tick log carried utilization:0.87 with surpassedThreshold:0.75 while the governor computed 64.7% and printed NORMAL — a 1.39x under-report at the exact moment the decision mattered. The gauge is account-wide, so it automatically includes the operator's usage on other machines and projects that no local ledger can ever see.
recommendations.expected_effect: The governor's headline number becomes true rather than a 1.5-year-old extrapolation from one data point. SOFT-PAUSE/HARD-STOP thresholds become reachable — they were unreachable all window because the synthetic d7 also resets on a fixed anchor and read $0.00 at 2026-08-14T00:01Z mid-burn.
recommendations.risk: Staleness between runs is real: if no session has run for hours the reading is old. Mitigate by exposing util_age_min and treating any reading older than the launch decision as a floor, never a ceiling — i.e. bias conservative when stale.

recommendations.action: Add a PACING GATE to mr-native-tick.sh as a new gate immediately before the launch decision, and a matching paragraph in mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md replacing the stale '$1,250 API-equiv' calibration at line 24. Policy, keyed on (util_pct, hours_to_reset): compute burn_headroom = (1.0 - util_pct); if util_pct >= 0.85 OR projected_util_at_reset > 1.0 at the trailing 24h burn rate, then LAUNCH NOTHING NEW but let every in-flight slice run to completion, keep merging, keep CI-watching. Never kill a live run for pacing. Below that, allow N=2 fan-out; below 0.50 with >3 days to reset, allow the existing N>=3 protocol.
recommendations.rationale: This implements the operator's settled scarcity policy (finish in-flight, start nothing new) and — critically — dissolves the 3-week-old blocker on arming enforcement. mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 declined to arm costwatch_enforce because 'a kill strands locks and hard-blocks relaunch until a human edits cap_override'. That objection is entirely about KILLING. A launch gate has none of those failure modes: no locks, no stranded worktrees, no half-done slices.
recommendations.expected_effect: Directly prevents the window's defining event: the 2026-08-10T09:05Z tick launched M21b-2 ($274.37, 183% of its $150 cap) at utilization 0.90. Under this gate that launch is refused, the in-flight work lands, and the ~3.5-day manual operator pause is unnecessary. Also prevents the 2026-07-31 recurrence where 11r-c/11r-e ran a fan-out pair to 0.99/0.95 and into a `rejected` + `isUsingOverage:true` event.
recommendations.risk: A stale or missing reading could over-restrict. Require an explicit fail-open with a logged BLOCKER when no reading is available in the last N hours, so the loop never silently parks itself — repeating the kill-switch failure mode would be worse than over-spending.

recommendations.action: Add an OVERAGE TRIPWIRE: in R-01's PLANWATCH loop and in mr-native-tick.sh's gate order, if any observed rate_limit_info has isUsingOverage==true or overageInUse==true, write $MEM/.overage-active with the observed resetsAt/overageResetsAt, log OVERAGE-ALERT, append a handoff line, and apply the R-04 start-nothing-new policy unconditionally until overageResetsAt passes. Clear it automatically on the first subsequent reading with isUsingOverage==false.
recommendations.rationale: MEASURED precedent: mr_pass_11r-c.log contains {"status":"rejected","rateLimitType":"seven_day","overageStatus":"allowed","overageResetsAt":1788220800,"isUsingOverage":true,"overageInUse":true} from 2026-07-31, and mr_native_tick_native-20260805T112040Z-1651311.log carries the same. The loop has already burned purchased credits at least twice and nothing anywhere noticed. Operator objective F makes overage purchases the true monetary waste.
recommendations.expected_effect: Turns the one genuinely expensive failure mode (spending in overage) from invisible into self-limiting and self-clearing. Unlike every other flag in the system it clears itself, so it cannot become a second 85-hour human-only halt.
recommendations.risk: Low. The auto-clear is essential — a manual-clear overage flag would recreate the kill-switch pathology.

recommendations.action: Correct mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116. Its documented field set reads {status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage} — add `utilization` and `surpassedThreshold`, and add one sentence: 'allowed_warning is NOT a trip condition, but its `utilization` IS the authoritative plan-consumption gauge and MUST be read into the pacing gate (R-04); treating this event as a binary trip-wire instead of a continuous gauge was the root instrumentation error of the loop.' Also fix line 24's stale '$1,250 API-equiv' weekly calibration, which is 2.2x off the config's 2783.

This is not 'seen and dismissed' — the loop literally does not know `utilization` exists, which is why 74 tick logs carried a reading that no component ever consumed. All four were later built for $35.31/$46.75/$63.37/$50.86, proving they were launchable. `after:` currently has ZERO mechanical consumers (`grep -rn 'after:'` over all mr-* scripts returns nothing) and mr-state.json `queue[]` is 58 past-tense narrative paragraphs with no forward items.

But main.wiring.test.ts is a *.test.ts sibling of main.ts, which the brief silently grants. recommendations.action: Add a queue-emission gate to the ADR pipeline: any ADR containing a 'Residuals / follow-ups' section, or any of the 78 known defer phrases ('deferred to', 'a later slice', 'future slice', 'parked to', 'routed to'), MUST cite a slice ID that exists in a spec file or PLAN.md §9. Enforce it in the existing ADR-digest CI gate (the same one that already fails on controlled-vocabulary drift). Extend mr-ready-set (R-09) to surface unqueued residuals as a first-class backlog.

recommendations.expected_effect: Attacks the single largest value-per-credit leak. 35.4% of in-window named-slice spend and 46.6% lifetime is remediation, and 7 of the 15 residual slices in the 13r/14r program are the disclosed-but-untracked class. Cutting that class in half is worth roughly 5 percentage points of the weekly allowance every week, permanently. Also collapses the 13.1-day mean disclosure-to-remediation latency toward the next tick.
recommendations.risk: A hard CI gate on ADR prose can block a docs-only commit — this already happened once in-window (62dce75, 2h11m master-red on the ADR-digest vocabulary gate). Ship it as a warning that writes to the backlog for one cycle before making it blocking.

diagnoses.theme: PROCESS REDESIGN — the loop measures ceremony instead of consequence. Three instruments decide everything (credits, quality, queue) and all three are proxies: a synthetic dollar model stands in for the account-wide plan utilization the API already streams and the loop throws away; assert-shaped-line counting stands in for behavioural test strength; free-text prose stands in for the ready-work queue. Every headline failure of the window is one of those three proxies being believed. The redesign is not "add gates" — it is to replace each proxy with the real signal that already exists (rate_limit_info.utilization; cargo-mutants --in-diff; parsed spec touches:/after:), delete the machinery that only measured the proxy, and make deferred work and process changes both mechanically queryable so nothing is ever "recorded but not queued" again. Ranked throughout by value delivered per weekly plan credit, never by duty cycle.

root_causes.statement: The loop's credit governor reasons in a synthetic dollar model extrapolated from a single 2026-07-25 operator observation, while the true account-wide plan utilization is streamed by the API on almost every run and is explicitly parsed and discarded. The governor was structurally incapable of seeing the constraint that actually binds.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED by me: mr-native-tick.sh:364 `if str(o.get("status")) == "rejected" and o.get("resetsAt") is not None` — the walker reaches every rate_limit_info object and keeps only rejections; `utilization` is never read. mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:116 documents the field set as `{status,resetsAt,rateLimitType,overageStatus,overageDisabledReason,isUsingOverage}` — omitting `utilization` — and justifies not TRIPPING on allowed_warning, then discards the object entirely. I re-extracted the signal from disk: 73 tick logs and 24 pass logs carry seven_day samples (89 tick-log samples), giving peak observed utilization of 97% (week resetting 08-07), 90% (week resetting 08-14, last reading 08-10 09:08Z immediately before the operator's manual pause), 57% (week resetting 08-21, as of 08-15 14:04Z). CORRECTION TO EVIDENCE COST-01: the anchor $MEM/.weekly-reset-anchor = 1784851200 decodes to 2026-07-23 20:00 America/New_York = Thursday, exactly matching every observed `resetsAt` (1786665600 -> 2026-08-13 20:00 EDT Thu; 1787270400 -> 2026-08-20 20:00 EDT Thu). The weekly WINDOW BOUNDARY is correct and needs no change; COST-01's 'reset mid-burn on a wrong anchor' framing is wrong. The defect is entirely the metric inside the window. mr-situation:56-127 computes that metric by summing cost_usd from monster-realm-usage-ledger.jsonl only. mr-budget-config.json:45 prices fable as an explicit guess ('ESTIMATE 1.5x opus ... CALIBRATE from first fable run'), never calibrated, and fable was ~57% of window spend.
root_causes.mechanism: (1) weekly_limit_usd 2783 is derived from one data point (internal_total 1002 / drew_total_pct 0.36). (2) The ledger sees only this harness's own runs, so the operator's usage on other machines/projects is invisible by construction — no local ledger can ever close that gap. (3) 21% of ledger rows are COST-UNKNOWN and resume/retry legs are never re-summed (measured $46.84 missing in-window), all in the unsafe direction. (4) The result is a reading of 64.7% NORMAL at the moment true account utilization was 90% — a measured 1.39x under-report. (5) Because the governor could not see scarcity, no pacing, reservation, or finish-in-flight behaviour could exist. (6) The operator became the governor, manually running mr-supervisor-disable when he saw the cap approaching — which is exactly the babysitting the loop is supposed to remove, and it fires the single most destructive control in the system (a human-only flag that also blocks completion events).
root_causes.quantified_cost: The week resetting 2026-08-14 was fully consumed in ~3.5 active days (Aug 7-10), forcing a ~3.5-day operator pause; the prior week reached 97% and logged a real {status:rejected, isUsingOverage:true, overageInUse:true} event, i.e. it burned PURCHASED credits, which operator objective F names as the true monetary waste. Downstream: the M21b-2 done-event sat 83.9h behind the resulting flag, and 4 of 21 slices exceeded their own declared tier cap with zero intervention (M21b-2 182.9%).

root_causes.statement: The pre-merge quality gates score ceremony and lexical shape, not behaviour. Every gate that ran in the window is a proxy detector, and every defect class that actually escaped was invisible to all of them by construction.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED by me from mr-audit (75 lines): line 51 scopes the content diff to `"*test*" "*spec*" evals :(glob)**/*_tests.rs :(glob)**/*.test.ts` — production source is never scanned for suppressions; line 54 counts any removed line matching /assert|expect\(|\.toBe|\.toEqual|panic!|prop_assert/ regardless of whether it is comment prose or an import reflow; line 56 matches `\.skip\b` which cannot distinguish `test.skip` from `.iter().skip()`; lines 58-59 make `tier==hard` an UNCONDITIONAL FLAG, so ~half the flags are not detections at all; lines 22-38 'orchestration' is a string-presence count of `"name":"Agent"` and role substrings in the session log. In-window precision 0/11. Meanwhile: the mutation gate is nightly-only, whole-crate, and an ABSOLUTE SURVIVOR CAP — justfile:110 `mutate-server cap="324"`, re-baselined upward from 299 by 14r-a with 87% of survivors never triaged (43.0% of server mutants survive); 30-42% of server tests are regex-over-source-text bound to include_str! (pvp 59%, economy 67%); 7 *-security.eval.mjs gates are documented in evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190 as measurably blind, two reproducibly swallowing the scan needle; and PERF-01 shows the operator's PRIMARY performance axis has exactly 7 nanosecond-scale pure-function benches with ~20x headroom and nothing measuring reducer latency, subscription payload, or frame time. VERIFIED AVAILABLE TODAY: `cargo mutants --version` = 27.1.0 and `--help` lists `-D, --in-diff <IN_DIFF>` — a changed-lines mutation gate is installable now.
root_causes.mechanism: A gate that counts assert-shaped lines in test-path diffs can only ever answer 'did the diff look like it removed a test?'. It cannot answer 'do the tests that exist detect a behaviour change?' — which is the question every escaped defect turned on. m20b merged with 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' and shipped a 7-container observability stack whose first real boot crash-looped four containers; none of those four config defects touch a test file, so no counter could move. Source-text-scanning tests compound this: they pass on any semantically-broken change that preserves the text shape and fail on any innocuous refactor, so they simultaneously under-protect correctness and penalise changeability — and they kill zero mutants, which is precisely why the survivor count is 43% and had to be re-baselined upward rather than down.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 11 supervisor full-diff adjudications in-window, all returning CLEAN, including the window's most expensive tick ($5.03, 3.8x median). More seriously, a 0%-precision gate trains its reader to rubber-stamp: the eleventh FLAGGED->CLEAN is read far less carefully than the first, so the gate actively erodes the vigilance it exists to create while appearing in every merge record as evidence of a caught defect.

root_causes.statement: Known defects are recorded in prose that nothing reads. The touches: fan-out discipline forbids fixing anything outside a slice's declared set, the forbidden work is written into an ADR 'Residuals' bullet, and there is no mechanism anywhere that converts a residual into queued work.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: REPORTED and cross-checked: 21 of 165 ADRs carry a Residuals/follow-ups section; 78 defer/park phrases corpus-wide ('deferred to' 45, 'a later slice' 11, 'future slice' 10, 'parked to' 8). Smoking gun: docs/adr/0165 (Accepted 2026-07-31) says 'implementation defers to 11r-i, being outside 11r-d's declared touches:'; 11r-i merged 2026-08-02 without implementing it; CHANGELOG re-drifted 18 PRs; finally implemented 2026-08-15 by 13r-g, 15 days after Acceptance. Live reproduction inside the milestone chartered to kill this class: evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:124-190 parks seven blind security gates to owner '14r-c-2', and `grep -rl 14r-c-2` over specs/, PLAN.md and mr-state.json returns zero hits. I confirmed the enabling mechanism in mr-disjoint:6-7, which states it 'Operates on DECLARED touches only'.
