root_causes.mechanism: Parallelism is bought by forbidding out-of-scope edits. The prohibition is correct; the missing half is a sink for what it forbids. Because the sink is an ADR bullet in a 27,094-line corpus rather than a queue entry, the only thing that ever re-finds the work is a human-instigated multi-lens review weeks later — the most expensive detector available. The review then manufactures ~7 new slices, which is why the residual milestone reads as the loop's fuel supply rather than as debt.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 46.6% of lifetime named-slice spend ($3,913 of $8,395) and 35.4% of in-window spend ($643.73) is remediation of the loop's own prior output. Measured disclosure->remediation latency mean 13.1 days, median 14, max 20 (n=10), with two items disclosed twice before being fixed.

root_causes.statement: Review effort sits after ~20 merges instead of inside the slice, and the batch is triggered by a cron cadence rather than by a quality signal. Residual counts are flat across 13 milestones, so this is a treadmill, not a converging feedback loop.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: REPORTED: 13 review-residual milestones, 85 slices; the last five produced 7, 9, 6, 8, 7 slices at 7d/6d/3d/4d intervals — flat output, accelerating cadence, triggered by a Cowork cron task (mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:1-7), not by a defect-rate threshold. Contrast the in-slice gauntlet, which is the best-spending thing in the system: reviewer 50 runs $85.71 ($1.71/run) and red-team 43 runs $84.52 ($1.97/run) found real merge-blockers BEFORE code existed (14r-d's reviewer caught the OBS-2 log-ratchet blocker whose fix files were outside touches:; red-team independently reproduced it in a throwaway clone with the real toolchain), and a paid post-CI-green review on m20c found a HIGH that CI had passed.
root_causes.mechanism: Findings generated at the end of a 20-merge batch cannot be fixed in the slice that caused them (that slice is merged and its touches: window is closed), so 100% of batch findings become residuals by construction — the batch cadence mechanically manufactures the RC-3 backlog. Findings generated inside the slice are fixed in the same PR at ~$2/run and never enter a queue at all.
root_causes.quantified_cost: $770.37 of the $995.60 13r+14r program (77.4%) is remediation. The batch review costs ~$54-74 and yields ~7-8 slices which the loop burns in <24h, so the supply/demand mismatch is roughly 7:1 and the residual arrival rate is not declining.

root_causes.statement: The only unattended work-supply channel can produce fix-up work exclusively; forward capability requires an operator-attended ceremony, because spec elaboration is doctrinally declared non-mechanical. The loop therefore self-disables rather than replenishing.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: REPORTED: mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:249-250 scopes its Phase 6 output to 'M-postgate-<review-lineage-name>.spec.md, continuing the review-residuals naming lineage' — structurally residual-only, and its 306 lines contain no loop/process lens at all. specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md:13,37 DOES specify 'elaborate a sketch to a build-ready spec' as step 1, but a slice can only launch via /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.vars.json = {slice, model, effort, adr, touches, target_desc, resume_block, tier} (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:109) and a sketch has no slice id and no touches:, so the capability is structurally unreachable. Ledger 2026-08-08T01:03:32Z records the policy: 'spec-authoring is not a native-tick-assignable action per doctrine'. M22-M25 are 4.2KB sketches with 0 slice headings and 0 SHALL, byte-unchanged for 49 days. Separately I confirmed `after:` has zero mechanical consumers (grep over all mr-* scripts returns nothing), and mr-state.json queue[] is 58 past-tense prose paragraphs — mr-weekly-review-prompt.md:257-258 says so explicitly: 'its queue[] is a narrative journal, not a work queue'.
root_causes.mechanism: There is no machine-readable ready-set. Priority is re-derived every tick by a sonnet session reading 390 lines of PLAN §9 prose plus M*.spec.md files. A recall failure inside that prose is indistinguishable from an empty queue, and the doctrinal response to an empty queue is the terminal human-only kill switch (mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81, nine words mid-paragraph on a 3,296-char line). So a derivation error becomes an outage, and the correct response (author more inventory) is forbidden to the only actor that is awake.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Separating the two causes per operator correction D: the 85h halt was a DELIBERATE operator credit-protection pause and is a symptom of RC-1, not starvation. The genuine supervisor self-disables are ~21h in-window (Aug08 02:00-09:13Z, Aug08 11:00-14:00Z, Aug09 17:00Z-Aug10 01:04Z, Aug10 06:00-09:05Z). Their cost under operator correction A is not idle hours but forgone CHOICE: with no ready-set, the loop cannot preferentially spend scarce credits on the highest-value available work, and 13r-a (CRITICAL, 'observability stack cannot boot') waited 117.1h from spec-ready to launch while lower-value work ran.

root_causes.statement: The instruction surface accreted incident-by-incident, froze on 2026-08-01, and now encodes rules a model must re-interpret hourly that could be executed mechanically — including rules that are factually false and subsystems labelled ACTIVE that have been dead for weeks.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED: mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md is 155 lines / 32,620 chars, of which line 81 alone is 3,296 chars (10.1% of the prompt) carrying at least nine unrelated rules including the kill-switch terminal. 21 dated incident parentheticals span seven dates, ALL July 2026; zero August dates, while the file's own window contained a 92.9h flag arming, a 183%-of-cap run and 11 false-positive flags. I verified the brief template directly: mr-brief-template.md:33 states 'BUDGET: $<CAP_USD> for this slice (advisory thresholds; only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical)' while mr-budget-config.json sets costwatch_enforce:false — the single artifact read by the agent that spends the money asserts a ceiling that does not exist. Dead-but-ACTIVE: feedback-ledger.jsonl has zero rows since 2026-07-27 and zero rows ever reached its terminal states, yet the doctrine occupies prompt lines 31/34/83/105 and mandates an `Items:` line in every PR body (mr-brief-template.md:31); $MEM/retros/ has never been created. Tier routing claims to 'Derive mechanically from the slice's touches: globs' (L17) but mr-tier-map.json covers 0 of 29 in-window slices and produced contradictory tiers for sibling slices in one milestone (m20b routine vs m20a/c/d/e hard, despite 'M20 slices' being a standalone HARD criterion; 13r-c routine despite touching accounts.rs and six security evals).
root_causes.mechanism: Token cost is negligible (~$83/yr, 0.087% of spend) — the cost is decision quality. Rules that live in prose are re-interpreted every tick by a sonnet session under context pressure; rules that live in code execute identically every time. Because nothing expires, resolved-incident text and live rules are typographically indistinguishable, so the model cannot tell which of 89 imperative modals binds now. And because the accretion loop died, the prompt is a snapshot of what the loop knew on 2026-08-01 — carrying nine 2026-07-26 fan-out rulings for an N that never exceeded 2, and no rule at all about the failures that dominated the window.
root_causes.quantified_cost: One nine-word clause at char ~1,400 of line 81 is the entire specification of the loop's most consequential control. Tier is the highest-leverage decision the supervisor makes (it selects model, effort, lens depth and cap) and it is unreproducible. 15.1% of the prompt is measurably dead.

root_causes.statement: Process interventions are unfalsifiable by construction: there is no unit-of-work denominator, the instrumentation is replaced in the same commit as the intervention it should measure, and the reporting tools built to close the loop were never wired to anything.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: REPORTED and consistent across two lanes: zero ledger rows with slice=='SUPERVISOR' exist before the v3 cutover, because that row convention was created BY the v3 change (mr-optimization-impl-spec.md:33) — so the loop's largest intervention can never have a before/after. The ledger records cost_usd, attempts and audit verdicts but nothing about slice size (no LOC, files-changed, EARS count, test count), so no cost comparison can be normalised — median cost per merged slice rose 4.5x across the cutover and nobody can say whether that is regression or scope. remote_red_fix_cycles is populated on 446 rows and SUMS TO ZERO. mr-metrics (6,935 B, the 'judge-approved rollup' the retro playbook mandates), mr-evidence, mr-retro-request and mr-selfcheck have zero call sites and zero log lines. Five retros ran 2026-07-24..27 and produced ~50 fixes; retro 6 does not exist; $MEM/retros/ has never been created.
root_causes.mechanism: Without a denominator, every measurement is confounded by scope, so every disagreement about whether a change helped is unresolvable and defaults to intuition. Without a change log joined to per-slice outcomes, the question 'did change X help?' has no query that answers it. The two known-good interventions (ADR-0011 cost SSOT; the rate-limit gate arming) are exactly the two that shipped with a named counter whose post-fix value is zero — that is the template, and it was not generalised.
root_causes.quantified_cost: Three weeks of a documented $250-400/wk model-routing experiment (fable vs opus at hard tier) never ran, and can no longer be answered retrospectively: routing makes model perfectly collinear with tier (hard/fable n=22, hard/opus n=1, routine/fable n=0). The one quality column that would have broken the tie sums to zero across 446 rows.

root_causes.statement: Credits are consumed by context volume, not by generation. 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics and a third of all prompt volume is burned before the first repo file is edited, with no compaction configured anywhere.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: REPORTED (measured from 23 build transcripts, deduped by message.id): cache_read $1,012.79 (65.3%) + cache_creation $396.98 (25.6%) = 90.9%; output $140.81 (9.1%); fresh input $0.94. Largest decomposed bucket is assistant thinking/output carried forward: 243.9M tokens = 34.7% of parent prompt volume. Static preamble x turns = 120.4M (17.1%) at a measured 44,288-token parent preamble vs an 11,103-token subagent preamble — the harness already proves a 4x smaller preamble works one layer down. Orientation: 226.1M of 703.0M parent tokens (32.2%) consumed before the first edit to a repo file, median first edit at turn 50, range 12.0% (13r-f) to 77.0% (m20d). ZERO compaction or context-editing events across 23 parent + 207 subagent transcripts; final contexts 295K/454K/611K. Parent tool census: Bash 2,135 (68.6%), Grep 0, Glob 0, codegraph_explore 0 — despite .codegraph/ existing and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md mandating it; subagents comply (47 codegraph calls), the orchestrator does not.
root_causes.mechanism: Nothing prunes the prefix, so a token added at turn i is re-billed on every one of the remaining turns. A 12K-token Read at turn 1 of a 180-turn session costs ~2.4M cache-read tokens; the same read at turn 150 costs ~0.4M. This makes early, large, unstructured orientation the dominant credit sink, and it makes every prompt-engineering change that adds durable brief context multiply by ~500 turns before it pays for itself.
root_causes.quantified_cost: ~$1,013/week of pure prefix re-reading at window rates. Under operator correction A this is the single largest lever on value-per-credit: halving average context per turn roughly halves slice credit cost with no model or scheduling change, i.e. it converts directly into more slices per identical weekly allowance.

root_causes.statement: The fan-out safety check models a narrower scope than the brief actually grants, so it certifies SAFE for slice pairs that are guaranteed to collide.
root_causes.supporting_evidence: MEASURED by me: mr-disjoint:6-7 states 'Operates on DECLARED touches only' and :30-33 intersects the declared path lists verbatim. But mr-brief-template.md:1 grants every slice ALWAYS-in-scope companions: '(a) sibling test files of any declared code file (e.g. foo_tests.rs next to foo.rs, *.test.ts next to a declared .ts), and (b) the standard doc outputs docs/adr/**, docs/knowledge/**, CHANGELOG.md, ARCHITECTURE.md'. Clause (b) is granted identically to every slice, so ANY two concurrent slices share a guaranteed collision axis. Outcome in-window: 14r-c and 14r-e both edited client/src/main.wiring.test.ts (a clause-(a) sibling of 14r-e's declared client/src/main.ts) after being launched with 'mr-disjoint SAFE', forcing PR#318 CONFLICTING, a park, a rebase and a $36.19 resume run; 14r-b's PR#317 conflict set was ARCHITECTURE.md + docs/adr/DIGEST.md, i.e. pure clause (b). The 14r-e park memo states it plainly: "14r-c's fan-out disjointness held on paper, not in practice."
root_causes.mechanism: The check is sound for the input it is given and the input is wrong. Because the companion grant lives in English prose in the brief and the disjointness computation lives in Python over a comma-separated string, there is no place where the two definitions of 'this slice's file set' are reconciled.
root_causes.quantified_cost: 3 of ~20 in-window merges hit sibling conflicts (m20d, 14r-b, 14r-e); the measurable direct cost is the 14r-e resume ($36.19 / 126 turns / 55 min) plus a park tick, a relaunch tick and supervisor adjudication. Under RC-1 scarcity that is credits spent re-doing merges rather than shipping capability.

recommendations.action: Create $MEM/mr-util-sample (new ~40-line python/bash): stream a stream-json log, walk every object for `.rate_limit_info`, and append the max `seven_day` sample to a NEW durable file $MEM/mr-plan-utilization.jsonl as {ts, source_log, utilization, resets_at, is_using_overage, overage_in_use, status}. Call it from THREE existing sites that already hold these logs open: (a) mr-native-tick.sh immediately after the tick's claude invocation returns, on $TLOG (defined at :301) — on EVERY exit path, not only the SPAWN-FAIL branch that currently owns the rate-limit parse at :350-405; (b) mr-cost-watch's existing poll loop (:56-91), which already tails each live /tmp/mr_pass_<slice>.log; (c) mr-launch.sh's reconcile step, on the finished pass log. Reuse the proven JSON-walk from mr-native-tick.sh:363-377 verbatim — never grep raw text (the brief is echoed into the log).
recommendations.rationale: The true, account-wide, cross-machine weekly plan utilization is already being streamed by the API into logs the loop already opens, and is being deleted. It is the only signal that includes the operator's usage on other machines and projects, which no local ledger can ever see. It costs zero API calls and zero model tokens to capture. /tmp logs are ephemeral, so persistence is part of the fix.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 0 utilization samples retained anywhere; governor blind to a measured 1.39x under-report (read 64.7% NORMAL at true 90%). After: a durable hourly-resolution series. I verified sampling density on disk today — 73 tick logs carry 89 seven_day samples and 24 pass logs carry more, so even with zero slices running the hourly cron alone yields ~1 sample/hour. Week-1 check: mr-plan-utilization.jsonl exists, contains >=100 rows, and its max value for the current plan week is within 2 percentage points of what /usage shows the operator.
recommendations.risk: Very low — pure read/append, no control flow touched. Only real risk is field drift in the API payload; mitigate by asserting the walk found >=1 seven_day sample per tick and logging UTIL-SAMPLE-ABSENT (never silently) so the governor can distinguish 'no data' from 'low utilization'.

recommendations.action: Replace the budget block in mr-situation:56-127 (`WEEKLY,SOFT,HARD,FGUARD,FALLOW` + `def budget()`) with a `plan` block computed from mr-plan-utilization.jsonl: {utilization, sample_age_min, resets_at, hours_to_reset, week_elapsed_frac, pace_delta_pp (= utilization - week_elapsed_frac), burn_pp_per_hour (from the last 6h of samples), projected_util_at_reset, is_using_overage, state}. Demote the entire dollar model — d7_usd, weekly_limit_usd, fable_allowance_usd — to a `diagnostics` sub-object explicitly labelled ADVISORY-ESTIMATE-ONLY, and delete `soft_pause_frac`/`hard_stop_frac`/`fable_guard_frac` as decision inputs. Keep .weekly-reset-anchor as-is: I verified 1784851200 decodes to Thu 20:00 America/New_York and matches every observed API resetsAt exactly, so the window boundary is already correct.
recommendations.rationale: Operator decision G2: the governor must reason in percentage of the weekly plan allowance read from real telemetry, not a synthetic internal-dollar model. Percentage is also the correct denominator for value-per-credit (operator correction H), which dollars can never be because the dollar model's dominant term (fable) is a guess that was never calibrated.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: governor reported 64.7% / NORMAL at true 90%, and reported NORMAL on all 205 occurrences in the log's history — it has never once fired. After: the situation bundle carries the same number the operator sees. Week-1 check: on any tick, `jq .plan.utilization` from the bundle matches the latest telemetry sample, and pace_delta_pp is non-zero and moves. Second check: at least one tick logs a non-NORMAL state, proving the code path is reachable at all (it never has been).
recommendations.risk: Sampling staleness is the real hazard and must be handled explicitly, not hidden: utilization is observed only while a session runs, is quantized to whole percent, and lags. Design rule — if sample_age_min > 90, the governor MUST treat the reading as a floor and add burn_pp_per_hour * age to it before comparing to any threshold, and must never treat a stale low reading as headroom. State UNKNOWN (no sample this plan week) must behave as the most conservative band, not as NORMAL.

recommendations.action: Add a mechanical pacing gate to mr-native-tick.sh as a new gate between gate 2 (reset-time) and gate 3 (activity probe), reading the R2 `plan` block, implementing the operator's settled scarcity policy (G1) in code rather than prose. Bands, keyed on staleness-adjusted utilization vs the pace line: (a) util <= pace+10pp -> NORMAL, no restriction; (b) util > pace+10pp -> THROTTLE: N_MAX=1 and routine tier only, no new hard-tier launches; (c) util >= 85% OR projected_util_at_reset >= 100% -> FINISH-IN-FLIGHT: launch NOTHING new; merges, CI watches, audits, ledger writes and park/resume of in-flight slices all continue unimpeded; (d) is_using_overage OR overage_in_use true -> OVERAGE-STOP: same as (c) plus write a decision issue via mr-ask-drew (non-blocking) and log OVERAGE-TRIPPED. Mirror the band names into mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md replacing the stale L24 '$1,250 API-equiv' text, as a 4-line table, not prose.
recommendations.rationale: Operator objectives E, F and G1: there is no automatic pacing anywhere in the loop; stranding a half-done slice is worse than idling; overage purchases are the true monetary waste. The bands are deliberately asymmetric — they restrict STARTING, never FINISHING, which is exactly G1. Idle hours cost nothing (operator correction A), so a conservative pause is nearly free while an overage purchase is not.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: the week resetting 2026-08-14 was fully consumed in ~3.5 days with the loop launching 11 slices after a reading it believed was 0%; the prior week hit 97% and logged a real rejected+isUsingOverage event, i.e. bought credits. After: at the measured burn of ~1 percentage point per wall-clock hour during 2-way fan-out (30pp between 08-09 03:06Z at 60% and 08-10 09:08Z at 90%), band (c) would have engaged around 08-09 19:00Z and prevented the last ~4 launches while still merging everything already running. Week-1 check: zero OVERAGE-TRIPPED events, and utilization at reset lands in 90-100% rather than either hitting the ceiling early or finishing under 70% (both are failures — the goal is to consume the allowance fully but not overflow).
recommendations.risk: MARKED AS A QUALITY TRADE-OFF ONLY IN THE MILD SENSE: band (b) forces routine tier under pace pressure, which routes a would-be hard slice to opus@high with a thinner lens battery. Mitigate by making tier demotion FORBIDDEN for slices whose touches: hit security/RLS/schema surfaces — those defer instead of demote. Second risk: a mis-set pace line idles the loop while credits go unused, which wastes the allowance in the other direction; mitigate by making band (a)'s +10pp margin a config value and reviewing it in the R23 standing report after two plan weeks.

recommendations.action: Fix the two measured pricing bugs in mr-cost-watch before touching enforcement: (1) at :29-39, dedupe usage events by message.id — the SDK emits one event per content block, each repeating identical usage, measured at 1.75 events/message (range 1.38-2.20) across 15 logs; (2) at :39, price cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens at the cache_write_1h rate from mr-budget-config.json:22/29/35/43 instead of pricing everything at cache_write_5m — 17.9% of in-window cache-creation tokens (6.24M of 34.93M) are 1h. Then delete the `costwatch_stream_factor: 0.8` scalar (mr-budget-config.json:57) and its `_stream_factor_note`, and switch the threshold input at mr-cost-watch:82 from `raw` to the corrected sum.
recommendations.rationale: The estimator is the reason enforcement has never been armed: mr-native-supervisor-README.md:54 objects that 'all 4 historical HARD trips were on runs that merged EXIT=0'. Those were false positives caused by a run-dependent over-price, not by caps being a bad idea. The measured ledger/raw ratio spans 0.6370 to 1.0076 — a 22% band around a hard-coded 0.80 constant — and because raw sometimes UNDERCOUNTS (M21c 1.0076, 13r-b 1.0033), the in-line comment's 'overcount fires early = safe direction' justification is falsified by in-window data.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: nominal $150/$60 caps actually bite anywhere between 64% and 101% of their stated value; 27 slices lifetime hit STOP-MONITOR with zero action. After: the spread should collapse toward 1.0. Week-1 check: over the week's completed slices, |corrected_estimate / ledger - 1| < 0.10 on at least 80% of runs (baseline: median 0.7627, i.e. 24% error). Do not arm anything until that check passes.
recommendations.risk: Low in isolation (the estimator is advisory today). The residual ~30% of billed cost my token reconstruction could not explain remains unexplained, so the corrected figure may still carry a systematic offset; treat the week-1 accuracy check as a hard precondition and report the residual honestly rather than tuning a second fudge factor to hide it.

recommendations.action: Two coupled edits. (a) mr-brief-template.md:33: replace 'BUDGET: $<CAP_USD> for this slice (advisory thresholds; only the 125% hard ceiling is mechanical).' with the truth for whatever state enforcement is actually in — while costwatch_enforce=false, state 'BUDGET: $<CAP_USD> advisory. NOTHING will stop you — self-limit; blowing the cap is a sizing failure recorded against this slice.' (b) After R4's accuracy check passes, set mr-budget-config.json:55 costwatch_enforce=true and update the brief line to match, keeping the existing WARN-at-80% landing-pattern rung as the first action so the run converges rather than dying.
recommendations.rationale: DOCT-05 is a doctrine defect with a direct causal line to a 183%-of-cap run: the only artifact read by the agent that actually spends the money asserts that something else will stop it, so the agent has no reason to self-limit. Fixing the sentence costs nothing and is independent of whether enforcement is ever armed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 4 of 21 slices exceeded their declared tier cap (M21b-2 182.9%, M21c 161.0%, M21b 130.0%, 13r-c 108.1%); one SPEND-ALERT fired 4h58m after launch, one second after the last dollar was spent. After (a) alone: expect fewer than 2 of ~20 slices over cap. After (b): counterfactual on in-window HARD trips is $192.85 of spend prevented, $131.15 of it on M21b-2. Week-1 check: count slices exceeding 100% of declared cap, and count how many WARN flags were followed by an actual scope reduction in the transcript rather than by continued fan-out.
recommendations.risk: Part (b) IS A QUALITY TRADE-OFF and must be marked: killing a run mid-flight strands work, hard-blocks relaunch until a human edits cap_override, and two of the four in-window counterfactual kills would have landed at 81.7% and 87.9% of real cap on runs that merged cleanly. Do not ship (b) until R4's accuracy gate passes, and make the 125% rung fire the cooperative stop-flag path (which the brief already implements at :36) rather than a SIGKILL, so the run checkpoints and pushes.

recommendations.action: Replace mr-audit's gating-test block (mr-audit:39-70) as the primary quality gate with a real behavioural detector: add a `mutate-diff` recipe to the monster-realm justfile using `cargo mutants --in-diff <slice.diff> -p monster-realm-module -p game-core --test-tool nextest` with ZERO-TOLERANCE on survivors, run in PR CI (not nightly) against the slice's own diff vs merge-base. I verified cargo-mutants 27.1.0 is installed and `-D, --in-diff <IN_DIFF>` is available today. Make it a required check; a survivor on a changed line is a merge blocker with the survivor listed in the PR.
recommendations.rationale: This is the detector for the class that actually escapes. A source-text-scanning test (30-42% of the server corpus, pvp 59%, economy 67%) kills zero mutants on the lines it pretends to cover, so a changed-lines mutation gate makes that weakness visible AT THE PR, on exactly the code the slice touched, instead of six weeks later as a 43%-survival aggregate. It is also cheap by construction — it mutates only the diff, not the 753-mutant crate — which is what makes it viable in PR CI where the nightly whole-crate run is not.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: the gating_test_audit produced 11 flags and 0 true positives in-window while m20b merged 'mr-audit CLEAN/CLEAN' shipping a stack that crash-looped 4 of 8 containers, and the nightly aggregate gate was re-baselined UPWARD 299->324 (43.0% survival, 87% of survivors never triaged). After: every merged slice carries a zero-survivor proof on its own changed lines. Week-1 check: run it retroactively against the last 5 merged slices' diffs — I predict it finds survivors in at least 2, and each survivor is a concrete, nameable missing assertion. If it finds zero across all 5, the gate is mis-wired (verify by mutating a line deliberately).
recommendations.risk: Runtime is the main risk: cargo-mutants must rebuild per mutant, so a large diff could exceed CI budget. Mitigate with a per-slice mutant ceiling (skip-and-report above N mutants rather than time out) and by scoping to Rust first — the TypeScript half needs a separate tool (Stryker) and should be a follow-on slice, not a blocker on shipping the Rust gate. Second risk: this raises per-slice CI credit cost; that is a deliberate trade of credits for the operator's PRIMARY axis and should be measured in the R23 report as pp-of-plan per slice before/after.

recommendations.action: Retune mr-audit's remaining lexical tripwires from a merge gate into a cheap recorded signal, and fix its three measured defects: (1) DELETE lines 58-59 (`if a.get("tier")=="hard": verdict=FLAGGED`) — the unconditional hard-tier flag is not a detection and accounts for at least 2 of the 11 in-window flags; (2) at :53-57, strip comment spans and import lines before matching, and anchor the skip pattern to test-framework call sites (`\b(it|test|describe|context)\.(skip|only)\b`, `#\[ignore\]`) so `.iter().skip()` and doc-comment prose stop matching; (3) at :51, run the suppression pass over the WHOLE diff, not the test pathspec — `#[allow(...)]`/`@ts-ignore`/`nosemgrep` added to production source is currently invisible (GATE-02, latent, unexploited in-window). Emit the result into the ledger as a field; require a supervisor diff read ONLY when deleted_test_files is non-empty or suppressions_added > 0.
recommendations.rationale: Once R6 provides a real behavioural gate, the lexical scan's job shrinks to catching the two things mutation testing genuinely cannot see: a test file deleted outright, and a suppression silencing a linter. Those are cheap, high-signal, and currently either unchecked (production suppressions) or drowned in noise.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 11 flags / 20 merges, 0 true positives, each costing a full supervisor diff read (the m20c adjudication tick cost $5.03, 3.8x median). After: expect <=1 flag per 20 merges, and any flag that does fire is actionable. Week-1 check: flags-per-merge < 0.1, and every flag raised names either a deleted test file or a real suppression — if a flag still fires on comment prose or import reflow, the filter is wrong.
recommendations.risk: Low, but genuinely reduces one class of coverage: removing the unconditional hard-tier read means nobody automatically eyeballs every security-surface diff. That is acceptable ONLY because R6 covers the same slices with a stronger signal — do not ship R7 before R6 is green.

recommendations.action: Keep the orchestration check (mr-audit:22-38) but demote it from a FLAG that forces adjudication to a recorded ledger field, EXCEPT when agent_calls==0 on a non-doc slice (which stays a hard blocker). Fix the parser gap the ledger already documents ('reviewer+red-team evidenced in commit 39881fd; agent_calls parser gap'), and separately DELETE the CENSUS line at mr-native-tick.sh:323 — it greps $TLOG, the supervisor tick's own log, for subagent_type, so it structurally cannot see detached build sessions and reports 'agents: none' on 159 of 162 lines.
recommendations.rationale: The role-presence check is measuring the ceremony that QUALITY-01 shows is the best-spending part of the system (reviewer $1.71/run, red-team $1.97/run, catching merge-blockers before code exists), so it should not be deleted — but three flags in the v3 era, all adjudicated CLEAN, do not justify a mandatory supervisor read. CENSUS is different: it is pure log noise that reads like evidence, and it is measuring the wrong process entirely.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 159/162 CENSUS lines report 'agents: none' while transcript ground truth is 208 subagent runs across 12 roles. After: CENSUS gone, orchestration recorded not adjudicated. Week-1 check: zero 'agents: none' lines in the tick log; ledger orchestration field still populated on every merge; no non-doc slice merges with agent_calls==0.
recommendations.risk: Very low. Do not touch mr-audit's role-presence logic itself — the ledger note for 14r-d ('12 agent calls') matches the transcript exactly, so that half is accurate and load-bearing.

recommendations.action: Two fixes to the activity probe in mr-native-tick.sh:240-252. (1) Add `-not -path "*/.codegraph/*"` to the find predicate, aligning it with mr-spawn:35 which already has it, and DELETE the in-line comment at :246-252 defending the omission ('The measured cost of the false trips is $0') — it is refuted by measurement. (2) Make the probe ignore the loop's own writes by recording the tick's own last git-mutation timestamp and file set in mr-state.json at merge time, and excluding paths whose mtime falls within that window; that removes the ARCHITECTURE.md / docs/adr/** self-trips that make the doctrine's blessed merge->launch composite self-defeating.
recommendations.rationale: 72 of 72 in-window probe trips were false positives; 90% named .codegraph/codegraph.db-wal or .codegraph/daemon.log, which are machine-written index artifacts, and the remaining 7 were the loop's own ff-only merge writes. The loop has begun pre-emptively self-censoring ('composite launch deferred (own-write probe-trip risk, per doctrine)', costing 105 min), which is a doctrine adapting around a bug instead of fixing it.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 72/72 false positives; 13 cron trips lost a whole hourly decision slot each (mr-native-tick.sh:263 schedules no retry for src=cron). After: expect <5 trips/week and every one of them a genuine human edit. Week-1 check: count PROBE-TRIPPED lines and histogram the trip path — zero .codegraph paths, zero paths matching the loop's own last merge file set. Note under operator correction A the benefit is NOT recovered hours; it is that the loop stops declining the composite merge->launch action, which is a correctness/ordering win.
recommendations.risk: Low. The stated reason for keeping .codegraph in the probe is that excluding it could mask a genuine human edit inside a worktree — but the daemon writes those files continuously regardless, so the probe is saturated and detects nothing there today; excluding them strictly increases the probe's information content.

recommendations.action: Change mr-disjoint to expand each slice's declared touches by the SAME companion rules the brief grants, before computing overlap. Concretely: at mr-disjoint:18, after parsing each path list, add (a) sibling-test expansion — for every declared `X.rs` also claim `X_tests.rs`, for every `X.ts` also claim `X.test.ts` and `X.wiring.test.ts`; and (b) add the always-granted doc set (`docs/adr/**`, `docs/knowledge/**`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/adr/DIGEST.md`) to the STRUCTURAL list at :13, so any fan-out that would touch them is either serialized or explicitly routed through the supervisor's existing serial doc-reconcile step. Make the companion rules a single shared JSON constant read by BOTH mr-disjoint and mr-spawn's brief renderer so the two definitions cannot drift again.
recommendations.rationale: The check is sound for its input and the input is wrong: clause (b) of the brief's companion grant is identical for every slice, so any two concurrent slices are guaranteed to collide there. Encoding the rule once, in data, is what stops prose and Python from disagreeing about what 'this slice's file set' means.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 3 of ~20 merges hit sibling conflicts; 14r-e cost a park + rebase + $36.19 resume after being certified SAFE. After: expect 0 sibling-file conflicts on declared-disjoint pairs. Week-1 check: zero ledger rows containing 'CONFLICTING' with a shared-file cause; and confirm mr-disjoint now returns SERIAL-REQUIRED for the exact 14r-c/14r-e input that it previously called SAFE (a direct regression test worth adding as a fixture).
recommendations.risk: Low. It will return SERIAL-REQUIRED more often, reducing fan-out opportunities — but under operator correction A, serialized-but-correct beats parallel-then-rework, since rework spends credits twice for the same capability.

recommendations.action: Make deferred work mechanically queryable. (1) Define a structured residual block that ADRs and slice PRs MUST emit instead of prose: a fenced `residual:` YAML block with {id, severity, statement, touches, evidence_path_line, blocks_milestone}. (2) Add an eval gate (evals/residual-registry.eval.mjs) that fails CI if an ADR contains a defer/park phrase ('deferred to', 'a later slice', 'future slice', 'parked to') outside a structured block — the phrase list is already measured (78 occurrences corpus-wide). (3) Add $MEM/mr-residuals: scans docs/adr/**, open PR bodies and evals for residual blocks, and emits $MEM/mr-residual-registry.jsonl; mr-situation surfaces open_residuals count and the highest-severity open item. (4) Seed it by back-filling the known orphans, starting with the seven blind security evals currently owned by the non-existent slice '14r-c-2' (evals/scanner-migration-audit.eval.mjs:135-190).
recommendations.rationale: This is the direct fix for the loop's single largest value-per-credit leak. The touches: prohibition is correct and should stay; what is missing is a sink for what it forbids. A residual that is a queue row is picked up by the next tick at slice cost; a residual that is an ADR bullet is picked up by a multi-lens review 13 days later at review cost plus a whole remediation milestone.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 46.6% of lifetime named-slice spend is remediation; disclosure->remediation latency mean 13.1 days / median 14 / max 20; 78 unstructured defer phrases; the flagship orphan '14r-c-2' (seven measurably blind security gates, two proven to swallow the scan needle) appears in zero spec, PLAN or state file. Target: median disclosure->queued latency < 1 day (it becomes a row the moment the PR merges), and remediation share of spend falling below 30% within three milestones. Week-1 check: mr-residual-registry.jsonl is non-empty, contains the seven 14r-c-2 gates, and the CI gate has rejected at least one prose defer.
recommendations.risk: Low mechanically; the real risk is gaming — authors writing vaguer prose to dodge the phrase list. Mitigate by making the reviewer/red-team lenses explicitly responsible for asserting 'every deferral in this PR is structured', which is a check they are already well-placed to make.

recommendations.action: Rebalance review from batched-after to inline-plus-thin-batch, with an explicit stopping rule. (1) INLINE (grow): keep the reviewer/red-team/verifier pre-code gauntlet exactly as-is — it is the best-spending machinery in the system — and extend its remit with one instruction: any finding it raises that falls outside touches: MUST be emitted as an R11 residual block in the PR body rather than described in prose. (2) BATCH (shrink): reduce the periodic multi-lens review from ~9 independent lenses over a full clone to a targeted pass whose input is the R11 registry plus the diff since the last review, and whose job is to PRIORITISE and DECOMPOSE existing residuals, not to re-discover them. (3) STOPPING RULE, written into mr-weekly-review-prompt.md: trigger the batch review when open_residuals crosses 12 OR a severity=CRITICAL residual has been open > 72h, whichever first — NOT on a cron cadence; and declare the residual program converged (stand the batch review down to monthly) when new-residuals-discovered-per-merged-slice stays below 0.3 for two consecutive milestones.
recommendations.rationale: Diagnosis: this is a treadmill, not convergence — 13 milestones, 85 slices, last five producing 7/9/6/8/7 residuals at accelerating cadence (7d/6d/3d/4d) with flat output. The batch cadence mechanically manufactures residuals, because a finding raised after a slice has merged cannot be fixed inside that slice's closed touches: window, so 100% of batch findings become queue items by construction. Moving finding-generation inside the slice converts them into same-PR fixes at ~$2/run.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 77.4% of the 13r+14r program was remediation; batch review costs $54-74 and yields 7-8 slices consumed in <24h. Target: new-residuals-per-merged-slice trending down for the first time across a milestone boundary (measurable directly from the R11 registry). Week-1 check: the registry shows residuals arriving from IN-SLICE reviewers (a new source) rather than only from batch reviews; and at least one finding that would previously have become a residual was instead fixed in its originating PR.
recommendations.risk: MARKED QUALITY TRADE-OFF: shrinking the batch review's independent-lens count reduces the chance of catching a defect class no in-slice lens is looking for — and the batch review's track record is genuinely strong (13r-a CRITICAL, 14r-a's 5-day-red nightly gate, 14r-b's zero dynamic coverage on four trade reducers). Mitigate by keeping ONE full-breadth review per month with unchanged lens depth, and by making the R23 report track 'defects first found by batch review that no in-slice lens could have seen' — if that number stays high, reverse this recommendation.

recommendations.action: Make the ready-set machine-readable. Add $MEM/mr-ready: parse every specs/monster-realm-v2/M*.spec.md for `### <slice>` headings plus their backticked `touches:` and `after:` lines, join against merged slices (from the ledger and git log), and emit ready_slices[] = slices whose `after:` dependencies are all merged and which are not already in-flight. Surface it in mr-situation as {ready_count, ready_slices[], blocked_slices[], runway_slice_days}. Then change mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81's work-selection clause from 'first unfinished non-blocked: slice per PLAN §9 order' to 'select from situation.ready_slices'.
recommendations.rationale: `after:` currently has ZERO mechanical consumers (verified: grep across all mr-* scripts returns nothing) and mr-state.json's queue[] is 58 past-tense prose paragraphs that the weekly-review SSOT itself calls 'a narrative journal, not a work queue'. Priority is therefore re-derived every hour by a sonnet session reading 390 lines of prose, and a recall failure in that prose is indistinguishable from an empty queue. This single change is what makes the 2026-08-10 'no mechanical slice launchable' standdown impossible: 13r-a, 13r-d, 13r-f and 13r-g all carried `after: none` at that moment.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 13r-a (CRITICAL) waited 117.1h from spec-ready to launch; four supervisor self-disable episodes totalling ~21h in-window each claimed no launchable work. Under operator correction A the value is not recovered hours but recovered CHOICE — with scarce credits, the loop must be able to rank available work by severity, which it currently cannot do at all. Week-1 check: situation.ready_count is non-zero whenever any spec slice has satisfied dependencies; zero DECISION lines claiming 'no mechanical slice launchable' while ready_count > 0.
recommendations.risk: Low. Parsing risk if a spec drifts from the `### slice` + `touches:` convention — mitigate by having mr-ready report PARSE-GAP loudly (naming the file) rather than silently returning a short list, since a silently-short ready-set reproduces exactly the failure being fixed.

recommendations.action: Make spec elaboration a first-class launchable slice. Define a synthetic slice shape the existing mr-spawn path can already carry: slice='<M>-spec', touches='specs/monster-realm-v2/<M>*.spec.md, specs/monster-realm-v2/PLAN.md', tier=hard, target_desc='elaborate <M> from design sketch to build-ready spec per specs/monster-realm-v2/build-loop-prompt.md:13,37 SLICING FOR FAN-OUT doctrine; output the review-residual spec format'. Its terminal state is a SPEC PR — never a merge — for ASYNC operator review. Add an inventory watermark to the R3 gate: when situation.runway_slice_days < 1.5 AND the plan band is NORMAL, the tick launches an elaboration slice instead of standing down.
recommendations.rationale: The capability is already written into build-loop-prompt.md:13,37 as step 1 of the per-milestone procedure and is structurally unreachable only because vars.json requires a slice id and a touches: set that a sketch does not have — a 3-field gap, not a missing capability. The weekly review already proves unattended spec authoring works and produces launchable slices. Answering the operator's question directly: the 'interactive heavy-ceremony' constraint is CALCIFIED CONVENTION for DECOMPOSING an already-decided milestone (M-postgate-client-coverage and M-postgate-roster-wave-3 each have a PLAN bullet stating exactly what to do), and ESSENTIAL only where genuine open design decisions remain (M22's erase-vs-anonymize policy, retention windows, export format). The guardrail that makes relaxation safe is that the output is a PR, not a merge.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: forward inventory required four separate human-triggered supply events to cover 168 hours; M22-M25 have been byte-unchanged 4.2KB sketches for 49 days; measured cost per build-ready slice was $53.56 via attended ceremony vs $6.75-$12.31 via the unattended channel. Target: the operator's involvement in replenishment becomes reviewing a spec PR asynchronously instead of running a 9.2-hour interactive session. Week-1 check: at least one <M>-spec PR opened without an interactive session, and the operator's review of it takes minutes rather than hours.
recommendations.risk: MARKED QUALITY TRADE-OFF: an unattended pass may make a design decision the operator would have made differently, and there is no instance in the corpus of unattended elaboration on genuinely open design space — the weekly review has only ever decomposed verified findings. Mitigate with three guardrails: (1) terminal state is a PR, never a merge, so nothing is built on an unreviewed spec; (2) the pass MUST emit an explicit 'OPEN DESIGN DECISIONS' section listing every choice it made and its alternative, and any decision it flags as irreversible blocks the PR pending operator sign-off; (3) restrict the first two runs to milestones with an existing PLAN bullet (decomposition-only), and only extend to open-design sketches after reviewing how those went.

recommendations.action: Judge the ceremony weight down. Replace the 38-agent ideation-and-judge pass (measured at 70 subagent transcripts / $344.15 for the Aug-8 M21+M20 pass and 17 subagents / $137.88 for M21b-2) with a fixed lighter shape: 1 planner + 3 divergent design agents + 1 judge + 1 red-team, targeting the PROVEN contract — the review-residual format at ~25 lines per slice (slice heading, touches:, after:, Tasks, EARS, Tests, Decision-hook), which is what mr-spawn actually consumes. Also fix the routing accident: both ceremonies ran 100% on claude-sonnet-5 purely because the operator continued a cron tick's session, while every slice they feed runs opus@high or fable@xhigh. Add an explicit spec-authoring routing rule to mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md's Model & effort section (there is currently none) pinning elaboration to the hard-tier model.
recommendations.rationale: Answering the operator's question with evidence: the heavy ceremony is NOT buying proportionate value. The unattended weekly review produces 7-8 equally launchable slices for $54-74 using the same output format, versus $344 plus 9.2 operator-hours — a 5-9x difference in cost per hour of resulting loop runway. And the measured quality differentiator is not agent count: it is that both channels emit the same 25-line-per-slice contract. Meanwhile the single highest-leverage artifact in the pipeline was authored on the cheapest model in the fleet by accident, which is the actual quality defect in this area.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: $482.03 of measured ceremony spend, $0.00 of it recorded in the ledger, at $53.56 per build-ready slice. Target: <=$120 per elaboration pass at the same slices-per-pass yield, with the model pinned deliberately. Week-1 check: an elaboration pass produces >=5 slices that mr-ready parses successfully and mr-spawn launches without hand-editing vars.json — that is the only quality bar that matters for a spec, and it is directly falsifiable.
recommendations.risk: MARKED QUALITY TRADE-OFF: fewer divergent lenses may produce a less-explored design. The mitigation is the same falsifiable bar as above plus R14's OPEN DESIGN DECISIONS section — and note the countervailing evidence that raising the MODEL (from the accidental sonnet to the hard-tier model) plausibly buys more design quality than 38 sonnet agents did, at a fraction of the credits.

recommendations.action: Split the kill switch in two and remove the supervisor's ability to arm the terminal one. (1) Keep $MEM/.native-supervisor-disabled as an OPERATOR-ONLY flag (the deliberate credit-protection pause Drew already uses via /home/mdrewt/.local/bin/mr-supervisor-disable), but make it event-exempt like gate -0.5 already is: mr-native-tick.sh:124-127 should apply it only when SRC=cron, so completion events, CI events and merges still land. (2) Introduce a separate self-clearing $MEM/.supervisor-standdown for the 'I see no work' case, copying gate -0.5's proven pattern at :144-159 verbatim — a named wake_file that self-lifts, plus a 7-day expiry ('proceeding for a fresh look'). (3) DELETE the 'Nothing remains -> write DONE + disable' clause from mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:81 and replace it with 'ready_count==0 -> launch an elaboration slice per R14, else write .supervisor-standdown'. (4) Log flag creation with actor and reason — nothing currently writes any provenance, which made an 85h outage forensically unattributable.
recommendations.rationale: The routine, recurring, expected condition ('I cannot currently see work') is routed to the most severe terminal state in the system, while the exceptional condition (blocked on a human) gets the graceful self-clearing one. Worse, the terminal flag sits ABOVE the durable event queue in gate order, so arming it strands completed, PR-open, locally-green work — the M21b-2 done-event sat 83.9h behind it and the loop had spent $274.37 on a slice it had disabled itself from harvesting. Under operator correction A the fix is not about uptime; it is that a deliberate credit pause must never also block the merging of work whose credits are already spent, because that is pure value destruction.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: a done-event blocked 83.9h; FINISHED->MERGED latency 84.35h for M21b-2 against a 0.47h median for the other 20 slices; zero provenance recorded for either in-window flag creation. After: an operator pause halts spending while still harvesting everything in flight, which is exactly operator policy G1 expressed in gate order. Week-1 check: arm the operator flag deliberately with a live slice finishing; confirm the done-event is processed and the PR merged while no new launch occurs.
recommendations.risk: Low, but requires care that 'merges still land' cannot smuggle in new spend — merges, CI watches and ledger writes cost a tick (~$1.33 mean), which is negligible against stranded slice cost. Make the event-exempt path explicitly refuse any launch action so it cannot be widened later.

recommendations.action: Delete measurably dead weight from mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md in one pass: the feedback-doctrine blocks (L31, L34, L83, L105) and the corresponding mandatory `Items:` line in mr-brief-template.md:31 (feedback-ledger.jsonl has zero rows since 2026-07-27 and zero rows ever reached its terminal VERIFIED/SHIPPED-VERIFIED states); the retro-request block (L32) ($MEM/retros/ has never been created); the stale weekly calibration figure at L24 ('$1,250 API-equiv', superseded and 2.2x wrong against the config that governs, replaced by R3's bands); and the duplicated N-limit framings at L87 and L131 that the reconciliation note at L81 claims to have resolved while leaving both contradictory statements on the page. Also stop running mr-feedback from mr-native-tick.sh:134 every tick against a 19-day-frozen dataset.
recommendations.rationale: Not a token-cost argument — carrying the whole prompt forever costs ~$83/yr, 0.087% of spend, and that argument would be indefensible. It is a signal-integrity argument: labelling dead machinery 'ACTIVE v1.0' in text whose own parenthetical admits it never worked degrades the trustworthiness of every other ACTIVE label, and a model under context pressure cannot distinguish resolved-incident text from binding rules when 89 imperative modals are typographically identical.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 15.1% of the prompt (4,927 chars) measurably dead; 155 lines with 21 dated incident parentheticals, all July, zero August. Target: <=120 lines, zero blocks referencing subsystems with no activity in 14 days. Week-1 check: grep the prompt for every named artifact and assert each has had activity within 14 days — this becomes the standing R19 maintenance query.
recommendations.risk: Low. Risk is deleting something dormant-but-correct; mitigate by moving deleted blocks to an archive file (the repo already has supervisor-archive-full-prompt-2026-07-02.md as precedent) rather than destroying them, so a resurrected subsystem can restore its doctrine.

recommendations.action: Move mechanical rules out of prose and into the tick script or small scripts. Specifically: (1) tier derivation — create $MEM/mr-tier that takes the slice's touches: globs and returns hard|routine|content per the criteria currently written at mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md:17, and have mr-spawn call it instead of accepting a tier the LLM judged; retire mr-tier-map.json (self-labelled '_rules_frozen_2026-07-25', covering 0 of 29 in-window slices). (2) N_MAX and the fan-out protocol — enforce in the tick gate from the R3 band, delete the prose rulings. (3) Split the 3,296-char line 81 into named sections with one rule each: WORK SELECTION, BLOCKER DISCIPLINE, STANDDOWN, ASK-DREW, ISSUE HYGIENE, REPO ROUTING, BATCH POLICY, FAN-OUT.
recommendations.rationale: Tier is the highest-leverage decision the supervisor makes — it selects model, effort, lens battery depth and cap — and the prompt claims it is derived mechanically while the only mechanical artifact covers none of the actual slices. The measured consequence is sibling slices in one milestone receiving different tiers on consecutive ticks (m20b routine while m20a/c/d/e were hard, despite 'M20 slices' being a standalone HARD criterion; 13r-c routine while touching accounts.rs and six security evals). A rule executed by code is identical every time; a rule re-read hourly is not.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 0 of 29 in-window slices covered by the mechanical tier map; two demonstrable misclassifications, both under-tiering security-adjacent work (which routes it to a thinner lens battery — a direct PRIMARY-axis risk). Target: 100% of launches carry a tier produced by mr-tier, with any LLM disagreement logged as an explicit override plus reason. Week-1 check: re-run mr-tier over the last 29 slices' touches: sets and confirm it reproduces the intended tier, flagging m20b and 13r-c as the known-bad cases it must now get right.
recommendations.risk: Low. A mechanical rule can be wrong in a new way (over-tiering everything to hard, wasting credits); keep the LLM override path but require it to be recorded, so R23 can measure how often the mechanism and the judgment disagree.

recommendations.action: Institute a prompt maintenance discipline so the instruction surface cannot silently regrow. Every rule added to mr-supervisor-prompt-native.md or mr-brief-template.md must carry two inline machine-parsable tags: `owner-incident:<date|id>` and `falsifier:<a query or counter that would show this rule is no longer needed>`. Add $MEM/mr-prompt-audit (a pure-read script) that lists every rule whose falsifier has not fired in 30 days and every rule referencing an artifact with no activity in 14 days. Run it as a cheap monthly slice whose deliverable is deletions. Enforce a hard ceiling of 120 lines in the prompt: adding a rule beyond it requires deleting one.
recommendations.rationale: The accretion loop that built this prompt did not become unsustainable — it DIED on 2026-08-01, and the prompt has not responded to a single incident since, including a 92.9h flag arming, a 183%-of-cap run and 11 false-positive flags. A maintenance discipline with no forcing function decays to zero; a line budget plus a falsifier per rule makes deletion the default rather than an act of courage.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 155 lines, 21 dated parentheticals all from July, 15.1% measurably dead, zero edits in 14 days spanning the worst incidents of the period. Target: prompt <=120 lines and every rule carrying a falsifier within one month. Week-1 check: mr-prompt-audit runs and produces a non-empty deletion candidate list — if it produces an empty list on the current prompt, the falsifier tags are not being written honestly.
recommendations.risk: Low. Real risk is that a falsifier is written vacuously ('this rule is needed because the loop works'); mitigate by requiring the falsifier to name a specific counter, log line or ledger field, which is the same standard the two known-good interventions (ADR-0011, rate-limit arming) already met.

recommendations.action: Move async operator interaction onto the critical path and off the weekly-review-only consumption path. (1) Change decision-issue consumption from 'record-and-ignore, consumer: weekly generate-improvement-plan' to: every tick reads $MEM/decisions/ for answered-but-unconsumed transcripts and acts on them, with the existing reversible-default rule ('for REVERSIBLE scope/content choices take the documented default and PROCEED') unchanged. (2) Keep mr-ask-drew --blocking strictly for irreversible decisions only, and make the non-blocking path the default in the prompt. (3) Route the new async surfaces through the same channel: R14's spec PRs, R11's CRITICAL residuals, and R3's OVERAGE-TRIPPED events.
recommendations.rationale: The channel itself works — 11 of 11 answers captured, zero lost — but the operator answers in seconds and the system consumes in 4-7 days (issue #284 answered 2026-08-08, implemented 2026-08-15; issue #13 answered 2026-08-10, first effect 2026-08-14; issue #14 still open). That latency is what makes the loop feel like it needs babysitting when what it actually needs is a faster read.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: mean answered->consumed latency 4-7 days; the loop's own handoff records finding 'three answered-but-unclosed DECISION issues sitting in memory/projects/decisions/, never consumed by a tick'. Target: < 2h (next tick). Week-1 check: zero answered decision transcripts older than 2h remain unconsumed at any point in the week.
recommendations.risk: Low. Slight risk of a tick acting on a decision it misreads; mitigate by requiring the tick to echo its interpretation into the ledger note and to close the issue with the existing <!--mr-system--> marker, so a misread is visible to the operator immediately rather than at the next review.

recommendations.action: Define the minimum per-slice instrumentation set and make mr-record write it. Extend the ledger schema (mr-record) with exactly these fields per slice, chosen because each is cheaply obtainable and each falsifies a specific belief: plan_util_delta_pp (from R1's samples at launch and finish — the true credit denominator), turns (distinct message.id in the pass log), prompt_tokens_total, first_repo_edit_turn, files_changed / prod_lines / test_lines, mutate_diff_survivors (from R6), residuals_emitted (from R11), review_findings_precode, park_count, attempts_real (distinguished from the current ATTEMPTS spawn counter, which is misleading — 14r-e read ATTEMPTS=3 on a clean EXIT=0 build), and escaped_defect_backrefs (populated later when a residual or review names this slice as the origin). Store in the existing ledger plus a derived $MEM/mr-slice-metrics.jsonl.
recommendations.rationale: The absence of a unit-of-work denominator is why four weeks of cost optimization cannot be evaluated, why the fable-vs-opus question is unanswerable, and why every past intervention was unmeasurable. plan_util_delta_pp is the single most important addition: it is the real currency, it needs no price model, and I confirmed it is derivable today — per-slice deltas of 1-13pp are directly readable from the existing logs (13r-b+13r-f pair 7pp, m20d 13pp, 14r-g 6pp, 13r-h 4pp).
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: cost_usd only, 21% of rows COST-UNKNOWN, remote_red_fix_cycles summing to zero across 446 rows, no size metric of any kind. Target: a headline value-per-credit number — percentage points of weekly plan per merged slice, whose current measured value is ~3.5-4.3pp (from ~21 merged slices consuming a full ~100pp week). Week-1 check: every merged slice has a non-null plan_util_delta_pp and mutate_diff_survivors; the week's slices sum to within 15pp of the week's observed utilization change.
recommendations.risk: Low. The main hazard is repeating RC-7's cardinal error — changing the instrument and the system together. Land this recommendation FIRST, before R6/R12/R15, so those changes have a baseline to be measured against. That sequencing constraint is itself the lesson from the v3 cutover and should be written into R19's discipline as a standing rule.

recommendations.action: Create $MEM/mr-changes.jsonl: an append-only log of process interventions, one row per change, {id, date, description, files_touched, hypothesis, metric, predicted_direction, review_after_n_slices}. Every recommendation from this postmortem that is implemented gets a row at implementation time, with its predicted effect stated BEFORE the change lands.
recommendations.rationale: 'Did change X help?' is currently unanswerable because there is no record of when X landed or what it was supposed to do. Recording the prediction before the fact is what converts a process change from an opinion into a falsifiable claim, and it is the discipline the two successful interventions (ADR-0011, rate-limit arming) happened to follow by accident.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 51 loop-infra commits with no hypothesis recorded for any; five retros producing ~50 fixes whose individual effects were never checked. Target: every future intervention has a stated prediction and a date. Week-1 check: mr-changes.jsonl contains a row for each shipped recommendation, each naming a metric that exists in mr-slice-metrics.jsonl (a change whose metric does not exist yet is not ready to ship).
recommendations.risk: Very low. Risk is the log becoming write-only like feedback-ledger.jsonl; R23 is the forcing function that reads it.

recommendations.action: Re-point the orphaned $MEM/mr-metrics (6,935 B, currently zero call sites, zero log lines, zero references in the 428KB handoff, despite being the rollup the retro playbook mandates) to produce a standing one-page weekly report joining mr-slice-metrics.jsonl to mr-changes.jsonl. Fixed sections: (1) PLAN CREDITS — utilization trajectory, peak, whether overage was touched, pp-per-merged-slice vs prior weeks; (2) VALUE — merged slices, prod vs test lines, residuals closed vs opened, escaped defects traced back to a prior slice; (3) QUALITY GATES — mutate_diff survivors found, gate flags and their precision, nightly status; (4) DID CHANGE X HELP — for each mr-changes row whose review_after_n_slices has elapsed, the metric before and after with the predicted direction, and a verdict of CONFIRMED / REFUTED / INCONCLUSIVE. Deliver it as an artifact/markdown the operator reads asynchronously, and DELETE mr-evidence, mr-retro-request and mr-selfcheck (zero call sites, zero output, never wired).
recommendations.rationale: This is the mechanism that makes process change falsifiable and closes the meta-loop that died on 2026-08-01. Section (4) is the whole point: it is the query that has never existed, and its absence is why the operator's intuition that past work 'helped only a little' could neither be confirmed nor refuted.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: five retros, none since 2026-07-27; $MEM/retros/ never created; three rollup tools built and never wired; zero interventions ever evaluated. Target: a report that renders REFUTED at least once — a process that never refutes anything is not measuring. Week-1 check: the report generates, section (4) is non-empty, and its pp-per-merged-slice figure is reproducible from the raw telemetry by hand.
recommendations.risk: Low. Real risk is the report becoming ceremony nobody reads — mitigate by keeping it to one page, delivering it in the same async channel as the spec PRs and decision issues (R20), and letting section (4) recommend reversals, which gives it teeth.

recommendations.action: Attack context volume, the largest lever on value-per-credit, with four targeted changes and no brief-shortening. (1) Enable context editing on build sessions — the API's clear_thinking strategy drops thinking blocks from the replayed prefix; zero of 23 sessions used any compaction and contexts ran to 611K unmanaged, while carried thinking/output is the single largest measured bucket at 243.9M tokens (34.7% of parent prompt volume). (2) Add ONE line to mr-brief-template.md's opening paragraph directing the orchestrator to use codegraph_explore for code navigation — the parent made 0 codegraph and 0 Grep calls versus 2,135 Bash calls (791 of them grep/sed/cat/ls producing ~520K tokens), while its own subagents comply with 47 codegraph calls; this is an orchestrator-only doctrine gap. (3) Split $MEM/monster-realm-handoff.md (428,676 bytes ~107K tokens, 1,716 lines, 154 sections) into the existing archive files and have orientation read a per-slice memo instead of grepping the rolling log — orientation greps against it returned 21-27K chars at turn 4, costing ~1.0M carried tokens each. (4) Have subagent prompts reference a written plan file path rather than re-inlining the defect narrative ~3x. Do NOT shorten the brief itself — at 12,610 chars it is 7% of the preamble, dense and accurate.
recommendations.rationale: 90.9% of build spend is cache mechanics and 32.2% of parent prompt volume is consumed before the first repo file is edited (range 12.0% to 77.0% — a 6.4x spread that is the addressable part). Under operator correction A this is the highest-value change in the whole postmortem: it converts directly into more slices per identical weekly allowance without touching model, schedule, or quality gates.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 44,288-token parent preamble vs 11,103 for subagents; median first repo edit at turn 50; ~150K tokens re-read per turn across 400-760 turns per slice; measured ~3.5-4.3pp of weekly plan per merged slice. Target: a 25-40% reduction in plan_util_delta_pp per merged slice, i.e. roughly 5-8 additional slices from the same weekly allowance. Week-1 check: plan_util_delta_pp per merged slice (from R21) falls versus the prior week's baseline, and first_repo_edit_turn median drops below 35.
recommendations.risk: Context editing can drop reasoning a later turn needed, causing rework — introduce it on routine-tier slices first and watch attempts_real and park_count in the R23 report before extending to hard tier. Change (2) is near-zero risk and should ship immediately. Note the asymmetry from RC-8: any change that ADDS durable brief context is multiplied by ~500 turns before it pays for itself, so every future prompt addition must be justified against this metric.

recommendations.action: Give the operator's PRIMARY performance axis an actual detector. Wire m20d's existing sim-harness/src/bin/mr_load_driver.rs (6,053 lines, already in the cargo workspace, currently a manual tool connected to no gate and no baseline) into a nightly perf job that records reducer latency percentiles, subscription payload sizes and settle throughput into evals/baselines/perf-*.json, with a ratchet that fails on regression beyond a stated band. Separately, replace the ~20x headroom ceilings in game-core/benches/budgets.rs:31-66 with ratchets tied to the recorded baseline rather than order-of-magnitude smoke.
recommendations.rationale: Performance is named PRIMARY by the operator and is currently gated only by 7 nanosecond-scale pure functions with ~20x headroom, where a 19x regression passes green. Nothing measures reducer latency, DB round-trip, frame time or subscription payload — the places a multiplayer game actually gets slow. The instrument to measure the real thing was already built and paid for ($117.33 for m20d) and then not connected to anything, which is the RC-3 pattern showing up in the perf domain.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: zero runtime performance data exists in the repo for the window; m20d's OBS-27 breaking-point number lives only in an ADR-0180 amendment with no baseline file to compare against. Target: a committed baseline plus a ratchet. Week-1 check: evals/baselines/ contains a perf baseline; deliberately regress one reducer locally and confirm the gate reds — a perf gate that has never failed is a decoration, exactly as the repo's own proof-of-teeth doctrine states.
recommendations.risk: Nightly perf measurements are noisy on shared hardware and a flaky perf gate would train the loop to ignore red — which is precisely how the 5-night silent mutation red happened. Mitigate by ratcheting on a percentile over N runs rather than a single measurement, and by wiring R26's notification so a red is never silent.

recommendations.action: Fix nightly failure visibility and the mutation ratchet direction. (1) Close the ADR-0183 D5 gap ('No issue-creating Action, webhook, or notification step was added', blocked on the still-open mdrewt/claude-harness#14): have mr-ci-watch or a small poller convert a red nightly into a pending-event so the next tick sees it, giving the loop the same reflex for nightly as it has for PR CI. (2) Change justfile:110 `mutate-server cap="324"` from a single crate-wide absolute cap to per-module caps that can only ratchet DOWN, and forbid raising any cap in the same slice that discovers the survivors. (3) Queue the 282 untriaged survivors (87% of the 324) as R11 residuals with severity, so they enter the queue rather than sitting as a number.
recommendations.rationale: The only semantic quality ratchet in the repo was red for five consecutive nights with zero reaction, the other three nightly jobs green each time (maximally diagnosable and still unnoticed), and the eventual remediation LOOSENED the gate 299->324 while leaving the failure-visibility root cause documented rather than fixed. A gate that can be re-baselined upward by the slice that trips it is not a ratchet.
recommendations.expected_effect: Baseline: 5 silent red nights; 43.0% server mutant survival; 87% of survivors never triaged; detection came only from a human-instigated multi-lens review — the most expensive detector available. Target: nightly red produces a tick reaction within one hour, and the cap never rises again. Week-1 check: deliberately red the nightly and confirm a pending-event appears and a tick acts on it; confirm the ratchet script rejects a cap increase.
recommendations.risk: Low. Per-module caps require a one-time triage pass to set honestly; do that as a queued slice rather than guessing, and mark the interim caps as provisional in the ADR so they are not mistaken for a measured baseline.

reviews.reasoning: The measured half is correct — mr-situation:63-84 does compute d7_usd from a fixed weekly anchor rather than a rolling 7 days, and it did read $0.00 just after 2026-08-14T00:00Z. But the IMPACT framing is wrong and is superseded by theme-3's RC-1. I verified the anchor arithmetic: 1784851200 is exactly divisible by 86400, so it is 2026-07-24T00:00:00Z = Thursday 20:00 America/New_York — which is the operator's REAL plan reset boundary and matches every observed API resetsAt (1786060800/1786665600/1787270400). The window boundary is therefore correct, not defective.
reviews.correction: Rewrite the impact: the reset at 2026-08-14T00:00Z was CORRECT behaviour (a real plan-week rollover), not a governor bug. The defect is entirely the metric inside the window — the synthetic dollar sum under-reports true account utilization by a measured ~1.39x — not the phase of the window. Drop the claim that 'SOFT-PAUSE and HARD-STOP are unreachable in any week whose spend straddles a Friday-00:00Z boundary'; they are unreachable because the metric is wrong and costwatch_enforce=false, and any fix must not 'correct' the anchor, which R-03 rightly preserves.
reviews.severity_adjustment: MAJOR_ISSUE -> MINOR_ISSUE for the anchor framing; the d7-is-not-rolling observation remains valid as a description.

reviews.reasoning: Confirmed and under-diagnosed. The lane calls the worktree-isolation guard 'prose in the brief, with nothing blocking a write outside the session's own worktree' and proposes 'a hook or path-allowlist on Edit/Write'. I found the actual mechanism, which changes what the fix has to be: mr-launch.sh:18 sets PROJDIR="$HARNESS/projects/monster-realm" — the SHARED main checkout — and :85 runs `( cd "$PROJDIR" && claude --model ... --dangerously-skip-permissions -p ... --add-dir "$HARNESS" ... )`. The session's cwd IS the shared checkout, every permission gate is disabled, and the whole harness is added as a writable dir. The session never enters its worktree at all; it has to navigate there by path.
reviews.correction: The invariant is not merely unenforced, it is structurally inverted by the launcher. Any fix must change mr-launch.sh's cwd or add a path allowlist, and it must confront the documented tradeoff in the inline comment at mr-launch.sh:18 ('project-level .claude (31 domain skills, desync-guard, reducer-security-auditor) is only discovered from inside PROJ'), i.e. cd-ing into the worktree may lose skill discovery. See OMISSION-3.

reviews.reasoning: The 44,288-token turn-1 preamble measurement is sound and the parent-vs-subagent 4x asymmetry is a real, actionable signal. But the load-bearing recommendation that follows from it ('deferring unused MCP servers ... is the obvious first cut') rests on an inference the lane itself flags as unproven, and it is directly measurable by an experiment nobody ran.
reviews.correction: Before any recommendation trims MCP instruction blocks, measure it: launch one throwaway headless session with the current config and one with a trimmed MCP scope and diff turn-1 context (cache_read+cache_creation+input on the first assistant message) — the same method that produced the 44,288 figure. Until that runs, the MCP share of the preamble is unquantified and the 'obvious first cut' framing is not supported. See OMISSION-7.
reviews.severity_adjustment: Keep MAJOR_ISSUE for the preamble sink; downgrade the MCP-specific attribution to INFERRED/unquantified.

reviews.reasoning: Accurate for the window as measured (zero ORPHAN-RUN, zero WATCHER-DEAD, zero CRASHED rows), but the lane generalises to 'this lane costs nothing' and 'remediation effort should not be spent here' without examining the one failure path that never occurred in-window: machine reboot mid-slice.
reviews.correction: Scope the WORKING_WELL verdict to steady-state operation. The reboot path is untested and has a latent liveness bug — see OMISSION-4. crontab does carry `@reboot sleep 60 && mr-native-tick.sh`, and mr-native-tick.sh:114-119 writes CRASHED(no-done, dead leader) for a dead session_leader, so recovery partly exists; but the liveness test is a bare `kill -0 "$PIDL"` with no age bound (contrast the chain-mutex, which does have one at :276), and PID reuse after a reboot can pin a dead slice as permanently 'live'.

reviews.reasoning: UNIMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN. The recommendation says to 'turn on automatic compaction and, where the API surface allows it, the context-editing clear_thinking_20251015 strategy ... Set it in the launch path (mr-launch.sh) so every detached slice inherits it.' I read the launch path: mr-launch.sh:85 is `( cd "$PROJDIR" && claude --model "$MODEL" --effort "$EFFORT" --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "$(cat "$B")" --add-dir "$HARNESS" --output-format stream-json --verbose )`, with the same flag set repeated at :124 (resume) and :139 (cost-cap wrap). That is the Claude CLI, not the Anthropic API. `clear_thinking_20251015` and the `context-management-2025-06-27` beta are request-body features of the API; there is no flag in this invocation that sets them, and the recommendation names none. An engineer told to 'set it in mr-launch.sh' tomorrow has nothing to set.
reviews.correction: Rewrite as one of three concrete options and pick one: (a) verify and name an actual CLI flag or settings.json key that enables auto-compaction for headless `-p` runs, citing it — if none exists, say so; (b) move the build-session launch path off the CLI onto the SDK, which is an L-effort change to mr-launch.sh and its stream-json/lock/reconcile contract, not the M claimed; or (c) achieve the same effect inside the surface that already exists — cap turns per session and checkpoint/relaunch, for which mr-launch.sh already has the machinery (the --resume path at :124 and the cost-cap wrap prompt at :138-140 that instructs the session to commit WIP, push, and write a handoff). Option (c) is the only one executable tomorrow. This defect applies identically to theme-2's R4(1) and theme-3's R24(1), which propose the same unreachable mechanism.

reviews.reasoning: Parts (a), (b) and (d) are concrete and executable. Part (c) — 'split memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md into the existing archive files and have orientation read a per-slice memo' — is executable but incomplete in a way that would lose data, because it assumes one handoff file.
reviews.correction: Before splitting, reconcile the two files. I verified they hold DIVERGENT content, not merely different sizes: memory/monster-realm-handoff.md (untracked, 1781 B) contains two supervisor tick entries — '## 2026-08-14T15:59Z — native tick: delegated 14r-e CI-wait' and '## 2026-08-15T11:02Z — native tick: launched 13r-h' — and grepping the canonical memory/projects/monster-realm-handoff.md for those timestamps, and for the phrases 'delegated 14r-e CI-wait' and '13r-h solo (HARD tier', returns 0 hits for all four. A split that reads only the canonical file will silently discard both. See OMISSION-2.

reviews.reasoning: Item (2) (a codegraph line in the brief) is the strongest and cheapest item in the whole postmortem and should ship first. Item (4) is concrete. Item (1) is unimplementable for the reason given under R-16. Item (3) is incomplete for the reason given under R-15.
reviews.correction: Split this recommendation: ship (2) and (4) immediately; replace (1) with the turn-cap/checkpoint-relaunch approach that the existing CLI launch path can actually execute; and make (3) conditional on first reconciling the two divergent handoff files (OMISSION-2). Also note the internal tension the recommendation itself creates: RC-8's own rule is that 'every prompt-engineering change that adds durable context to the brief is multiplied by ~500 turns before it is paid for', yet R-5 and R-13 both propose ADDING text to the brief (a corrected budget sentence, plus live plan-utilization context). Those additions are small but the report should state the rule once and apply it consistently rather than leaving both instincts on the page.

reviews.reasoning: Concrete and executable — parsing '### <slice>' headings plus backticked touches:/after: out of specs/monster-realm-v2/M*.spec.md is a clearly specified script, and I confirmed the enabling gap (no mr-* script consumes `after:`). But it collides with R-04 and nobody resolved the collision. R-09 forbids the self-disable branch whenever the ready-set is non-empty; R-04 forbids new launches whenever utilization exceeds the pace line. In a week like the one under review, both conditions are true simultaneously for days: ready-set non-empty AND utilization at 0.90. R-09 as written would have the tick refuse to stand down while R-04 refuses to launch.
reviews.correction: State the precedence explicitly: the pacing gate WINS over the ready-set rule. The correct composite behaviour is a third state — 'work available, credits exhausted, deliberately deferring' — which must be logged distinctly from both 'nothing launchable' (a bug) and 'operator paused' (correct).
